<CHAPTER id="rthw:domains-of-dread" title="Domains Of Dread">

# Introduction: Domains of Dread {#rthw:domains-of-dread:IntroductionDomainsofDread}

## Introduction Domains of Dread {#rthw:domains-of-dread:IntroductionDomainsofDread}

The Mists reach from the darkest shadows of the multiverse, condemning the wicked and the brave to endless nightmares as prisoners of the Domains of Dread. These grim netherworlds compose the Ravenloft setting and are horrific backdrops for Dungeons & Dragons adventures steeped in fear. In these haunted realms, adventurers might oppose villainous Darklords, seek escape from the Mists, or experience any terrifying adventure you can imagine.

[![(Artist: Dustin Panzino)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/00-001.domains-of-dread.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/00-001.domains-of-dread.png)

## Using This Book {#rthw:domains-of-dread:UsingThisBook}

This book explores the Domains of Dread and helps you create frightful adventures and heroes ready to confront horrors. It requires the [Player’s Handbook](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024), [Dungeon Master’s Guide](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/dmg-2024), and [Monster Manual](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/mm-2024).

**This introduction** provides an overview of Ravenloft and its mysteries.

[**Chapter 1**](#rthw:character-options "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/character-options") presents subclasses, backgrounds, species, feats, and more for characters preparing to face nightmarish adventures.

[**Chapter 2**](#rthw:domains-of-ravenloft "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/domains-of-ravenloft") details prominent Domains of Dread, along with their Darklords and adventures within.

[**Chapter 3**](#rthw:ravenloft-adventures "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/ravenloft-adventures") provides tools for Dungeon Masters running horror adventures, including ways to develop frightful campaigns and rules for Haunted Bastions.

[**Chapter 4**](#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/creating-domains-of-dread") explores how Dungeon Masters can create their own Domains of Dread.

[**Chapter 5**](#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/denizens-of-the-mists") reveals allies and enemies that might appear in terrifying tales in the Mists or beyond.

[**The appendix**](#rthw:tarokka-deck "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/tarokka-deck") details the tarokka deck and how to use it in your adventures.

## Secrets of Ravenloft {#rthw:domains-of-dread:SecretsofRavenloft}

Untold mysteries pervade the [Domains of Dread](#rthw:domains-of-dread:domains "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/domains-of-dread#domains"), but these truths underpin the setting:

**1: Ravenloft Is Malleable.** The domains of Ravenloft are disconnected demiplanes. They don’t share a world or a certain reality. Few truths connect them, and even inviolate facts—such as time or death—might change. The only constant is fear.

**2: The Dark Powers Reign.** Sinister forces known as the [Dark Powers](#rthw:domains-of-dread:thedarkpowers "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/domains-of-dread#thedarkpowers") manipulate the Domains of Dread. Unknowable and omnipotent, the Dark Powers torment their captives for unfathomable reasons.

**3: Domains Imprison Darklords.** Each of Ravenloft’s demiplanes imprisons a [Darklord](#rthw:domains-of-dread:darklords "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/domains-of-dread#darklords"), a villain tormented by the Dark Powers. Domains ironically twist Darklords’ desires, trapping these villains in cycles of dread and despair.

**4: The Mists’ Clutches.** Constant fogs known as the [Mists](#rthw:domains-of-dread:themists "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/domains-of-dread#themists") encircle each domain and might rise anywhere within. The Mists trap individuals within domains and make travel between domains uncertain. They sometimes drag inhabitants of other worlds into the Domains of Dread.

**5: Heroes Are Few.** Few oppose the villainy of the Darklords. The domains don’t contain benevolent nations or untarnished heroic orders. Those who oppose evil can rely only on themselves, and they might inspire others or attract greater terrors.

**6: Isolated Islands.** The Domains of Dread are isolated from one another and the rest of the multiverse. Magic that facilitates travel between planes doesn’t function unless the Dark Powers allow it, and most inhabitants know little of realms beyond. Nevertheless, anything from across the multiverse might appear in Ravenloft, albeit with an unsettling twist.

**7: Rule of Fear.** The mysteries of the Dark Powers and the Mists facilitate frightful adventures. Whatever inspires terror and aids your horror adventures is the will of the Dark Powers.

## The Land of the Mists {#rthw:domains-of-dread:TheLandoftheMists}

[![(Artist: Sylvain Sarrailh)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/00-002.weeping-in-graveyard.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/00-002.weeping-in-graveyard.png)

This section provides you, the DM, an overview of Ravenloft. For details on specific Domains of Dread, see [chapter 2](#rthw:domains-of-ravenloft "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/domains-of-ravenloft").

### Nightmare Logic {#rthw:domains-of-dread:NightmareLogic}

Ravenloft cultivates dread in defiance of logic. Domains don’t abut one another, historians don’t record coherent pasts, and communities cloak ignorance in strange traditions. The Domains of Dread operate on the same logic as nightmares: Whatever is the most terrifying is true. The Dark Powers, the Mists, and the nature of domains are purposefully mysterious. Mundane details and the lives of domain inhabitants are constructed on illusions and impossibilities. Should characters realize the surreality of the setting, those revelations only create a stronger sense of existential dread and suggest greater questions. Ultimately, none can ever fully understand the Domains of Dread.

### The Dark Powers {#rthw:domains-of-dread:TheDarkPowers}

The Dark Powers are faceless, godlike forces that manipulate reality within the Domains of Dread. Few even suspect their existence. These enigmatic forces help you create horror adventures and serve two complementary roles:

**Narrative.** The nature and goals of the Dark Powers are mysteries behind the scenes of the setting. Most adventures won’t engage with these forces, but that doesn’t prevent characters and Darklords from seeking to learn about them, particularly as a means to escape the Domains of Dread.

**Practical.** The Dark Powers provide a narrative veneer for DM intervention. They are why characters appear in Ravenloft, why the Mists can’t be escaped, and why reality-defying strangeness occurs. The desires of the Dark Powers correspond with your needs in creating horror adventures.

### The Mists {#rthw:domains-of-dread:TheMists}

The Mists of Ravenloft appear without warning and move with eerie intention. Areas within the Mists are [**Heavily Obscured**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#heavilyobscured). No amount of wind can disperse the Mists.

The Mists serve the following roles:

**Dark Clutches.** The Mists serve the Dark Powers. They might steal residents of other worlds or entire locations from elsewhere in the multiverse and trap them in the Domains of Dread. Whether the Mists ever return what they claim depends on the whims of the Dark Powers.

**Domain Borders.** The Mists surround and isolate every Domain of Dread, preventing easy or predictable travel between them.

**Transportation.** The Mists can appear anywhere, claim individuals, and spirit them elsewhere in the Domains of Dread.

[![Few claimed by the Mists escape the horrors within (Artist: Pauline Voss)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/00-003.party-faces-mist.jpg)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/00-003.party-faces-mist.jpg)

#### Mysteries of the Mists {#rthw:domains-of-dread:MysteriesoftheMists}

The inhabitants of the Domains of Dread ascribe sinister stories to the Mists but accept the Mists as a natural part of their homeland. Those who travel between domains refer to their world as the Land of the Mists. Any supernatural happening or malicious force might be blamed on the Mists. Those who interact with the Mists—or who come from beyond—are typically met with suspicion.

#### Mist Talismans {#rthw:domains-of-dread:MistTalismans}

Mist talismans are nonmagical objects that resonate with certain domains. They might be any object, and some might be aligned with multiple domains. By holding or wearing a Mist talisman and focusing on the domain it’s associated with, a creature in the Mists can reach the intended domain after 1d6 hours of travel. Creatures following within 30 feet of a Mist talisman’s bearer reach the same destination. Mist talismans associated with domains are detailed in [chapter 2](#rthw:domains-of-ravenloft "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/domains-of-ravenloft").

Mist talismans don’t allow their bearers to escape domains with closed borders (see “[Darklords](#rthw:domains-of-dread:darklords "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/domains-of-dread#darklords")”). Similarly, if the borders of the destination domain are closed, roll on the Wandering the Mists table to determine what happens.

#### Wandering the Mists {#rthw:domains-of-dread:WanderingtheMists}

So long as a Darklord hasn’t closed their domain’s borders, creatures that enter the Mists might travel to other domains. When characters without a Mist talisman enter the Mists surrounding a domain, they emerge elsewhere after 1d6 hours of travel. Roll on or take inspiration from the Wandering the Mists table to determine where the Mists relocate characters.

**Wandering the Mists**

| 1d100 | Characters Emerge from the Mists …                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ----- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 01–20 | In a domain of your choosing.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| 21–40 | After wandering for another 1d6 hours and rolling again on this table.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| 41–65 | 1d100 feet from where they entered.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| 66–75 | A mile from where they entered at midnight of the following night.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| 76–85 | Inside a structure within the domain they tried to leave, perhaps a cave, crypt, shed, or closet.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| 86–95 | After encountering creatures within the Mists. Roll any die. If you roll an even number, a terrified [**Commoner**](#ref:monster:5194951-commoner "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5194951-commoner") appears. If you roll an odd number, a [**Mist Horror**](#ref:monster:6491374-mist-horror "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491374-mist-horror") (see [chapter 5](#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:misthorror "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/denizens-of-the-mists#misthorror")) appears. Roll again on this table. |
| 96–99 | Where they entered, only to find the domain changed. Perhaps someone the characters knew is gone and no one remembers the person.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| 100   | On a world on the Material Plane. After 1d6 hours, the Mists rise around them once more and return them to the domain they departed.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |

### Domains {#rthw:domains-of-dread:Domains}

The Domains of Dread are untold numbers of individual demiplanes hidden in the Shadowfell. Some are created entirely by the [Dark Powers](#rthw:domains-of-dread:thedarkpowers "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/domains-of-dread#thedarkpowers"), while others the Mists claimed from elsewhere in the multiverse and bear evidence of other worlds. Domains might change as the Dark Powers find new ways to torment their captives, with domains changing shape, merging, fading away, reappearing, and even repeating events.

The Domains of Dread share these features:

**Domains Are Finite.** Domains vary in size from countries or regions to a single city or structure.

**Domains Are Isolated.** Each domain is bordered by the [Mists](#rthw:domains-of-dread:themists "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/domains-of-dread#themists"). Generally, domains don’t share geography, and the residents and cultures of different domains don’t influence one another.

**Domains Hold Darklords.** Each domain exists to contains a Darklord. Darklords exert some control over their domains, but they are tormented by their imprisonment. A domain without a Darklord has no purpose; if a domain’s Darklord escapes or is permanently defeated, it might cease to exist.

[Chapter 2](#rthw:domains-of-ravenloft "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/domains-of-ravenloft") describes some of the most notorious Domains of Dread, while [chapter 3](#rthw:ravenloft-adventures "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/ravenloft-adventures") explores how to use domains in horror adventures. Use the methods in [chapter 4](#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/creating-domains-of-dread") to create domains of your own.

### Darklords {#rthw:domains-of-dread:Darklords}

[![(Artist: Helge C. Balzer)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/00-004.sea-monster.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/00-004.sea-monster.png)

Every domain torments a Darklord, a villain whose depravity attracted the attention of the [Dark Powers](#rthw:domains-of-dread:thedarkpowers "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/domains-of-dread#thedarkpowers") and led to their imprisonment in the [Domains of Dread](#rthw:domains-of-dread:domains "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/domains-of-dread#domains"). A Darklord might be anyone in a domain, from a national leader to an unassuming resident. Darklords share these qualities:

**Darklords Are Evil.** Each Darklord is the ultimate villain of a domain and the root of its terrors.

**Darklords Are Prisoners.** Darklords can’t leave their domains. If a Darklord enters the [Mists](#rthw:domains-of-dread:themists "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/domains-of-dread#themists") or uses another method to attempt escape, the Dark Powers return them to their domain. Even death rarely allows a Darklord to escape for long.

**Darklords Are Tormented.** Every domain torments its Darklord in an ironic way tied to their crimes, failures, or ambitions.

**Darklords Influence Domains.** Darklords have supernatural influence over their domains. A Darklord can close their domain’s borders (see “Closing Domain Borders” below) and create other effects.

**Darklords Are Active.** Darklords might brood over their failures, but their attempts to achieve their depraved goals fuel their conflicts with characters. Liberally use Darklords in your adventures rather than saving them for climactic plots.

**Darklords Don’t Realize They’re Darklords.** Darklords generally don’t realize they occupy a special place in the world. Their obsessions make them oblivious to the strangeness of their circumstances. Most don’t suspect the nature of the Domains of Dread or the Dark Powers.

**Closing Domain Borders.** Darklords can close the borders of their domains at will. When this occurs, the Mists become dangerous (see the Darklord descriptions in [chapter 2](#rthw:domains-of-ravenloft "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/domains-of-ravenloft")), and no matter how far a creature travels in the Mists, it eventually finds itself back in the domain it left. This makes leaving a domain impossible until the Darklord opens the borders or is defeated.

Chapter 2 presents stat blocks for numerous Darklords. [Chapter 3](#rthw:ravenloft-adventures "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/ravenloft-adventures") explores how to use Darklords in your horror adventures, while [chapter 4](#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/creating-domains-of-dread") aids in creating your own Darklords.

### People of the Mists {#rthw:domains-of-dread:PeopleoftheMists}

[![(Artist: Romain Kurdi)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/00-005.haunted-toy.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/00-005.haunted-toy.png)

The inhabitants of the [Domains of Dread](#rthw:domains-of-dread:domains "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/domains-of-dread#domains") fall into these categories:

**Soulless Shells.** Some domain inhabitants are creations of the [Dark Powers](#rthw:domains-of-dread:thedarkpowers "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/domains-of-dread#thedarkpowers"). These beings are indistinguishable from normal creatures, living unremarkable lives and existing to reinforce whatever status quo the Dark Powers impose. At the will of the Dark Powers, these inhabitants might reappear in a domain even after being slain.

**Bright Souls.** Some beings are like those who populate other worlds in the multiverse. Some live unremarkable lives, while others awake to their homes’ wrongness and fight their domains’ evils.

**Strangers.** Those whom the [Mists](#rthw:domains-of-dread:themists "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/domains-of-dread#themists") abduct from other worlds likely suspect the surreal nature of the Domains of Dread. These individuals often seek ways to escape the Mists and return home.

#### Death and Rebirth {#rthw:domains-of-dread:DeathandRebirth}

The spirits of those who die in the Domains of Dread or the Mists don’t travel to the afterlife. Those magically returned to life after being dead for at least 24 hours return with the grim realization that they’re trapped within the Mists.

The souls of those who die and aren’t returned to life are trapped within the Domains of Dread. The Dark Powers might eventually reincarnate these souls. Individuals who inherit a soul often look like their predecessor and might recall memories of their past lives.

### Magic in the Mists {#rthw:domains-of-dread:MagicintheMists}

Some magic functions differently in the [Domains of Dread](#rthw:domains-of-dread:domains "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/domains-of-dread#domains"). Characters who receive spells from otherworldly forces or patrons do so as normal, but the magic noted here functions in distinct ways:

**Banishment.** Aberrations, Celestials, Elementals, Fey, or Fiends aren’t transported to different planes after the [**Banishment**](#ref:spell:2618906-banishment "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618906-banishment") spell ends. Rather, they appear in a random different domain.

**Escape.** No spell allows escape from Ravenloft.

**Etherealness.** Magic that accesses the Border Ethereal, such as the [**Etherealness**](#ref:spell:2619193-etherealness "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619193-etherealness") spell, functions as normal, but a creature that enters the Border Ethereal from a domain is pulled back into the domain it left on leaving the Ethereal Plane.

**Extradimensional Spaces.** Extradimensional spaces function as normal, but spells cast within them are subject to the same restrictions as magic cast within a domain.

**Otherworldly Contact.** Magic that allows contact with beings from other planes, such as the [**Commune**](#ref:spell:2618987-commune "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618987-commune") spell, functions normally, but the domain’s Darklord senses when someone in their domain casts such a spell. The Darklord can make themself the spell’s target so that they become the one who is contacted and answer as they please.

**Planar Boundaries.** For the purposes of spell effects that change across or are blocked by planar boundaries (such as the [**Sending**](#ref:spell:2619015-sending "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619015-sending") spell), each domain is considered its own plane.

**Planar Travel.** Magic that allows travel to other planes, such as the [**Astral Projection**](#ref:spell:2618878-astral-projection "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618878-astral-projection") and [**Plane Shift**](#ref:spell:2618867-plane-shift "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618867-plane-shift") spells, fails in the Domains of Dread. [**Gate**](#ref:spell:2618932-gate "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618932-gate") can conjure beings into the Domains of Dread, but it doesn’t allow them or others to escape. Magic that creates or sends creatures to demiplanes—such as the [**Demiplane**](#ref:spell:2619088-demiplane "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619088-demiplane"), [**Maze**](#ref:spell:2619030-maze "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619030-maze"), and [**Imprisonment**](#ref:spell:2619175-imprisonment "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619175-imprisonment") spells—functions as normal.

**Summoning.** Magic that summons creatures or objects functions as normal, but whatever is summoned is a creation of the [Dark Powers](#rthw:domains-of-dread:thedarkpowers "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/domains-of-dread#thedarkpowers") and might appear or behave in eerie ways.

#### Cosmetic Magic Effects {#rthw:domains-of-dread:CosmeticMagicEffects}

Magic effects produced in Ravenloft appear more sinister than they do elsewhere in the multiverse. For example, a creature conjured by [**Find Familiar**](#ref:spell:2618877-find-familiar "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618877-find-familiar") or [**Find Steed**](#ref:spell:2618879-find-steed "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618879-find-steed") might appear unnatural or deathly, or the [**Find the Path**](#ref:spell:2618881-find-the-path "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618881-find-the-path") spell might cause a silent, childlike spirit to guide the caster to their destination. Describe such effects in whatever way reinforces a horrific atmosphere, drawing inspiration from the domain where your adventure takes place.

### Life in the Mists {#rthw:domains-of-dread:LifeintheMists}

[![(Artist: Leroy Steinmann)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/00-006.trapped-in-mirror.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/00-006.trapped-in-mirror.png)

The [Domains of Dread](#rthw:domains-of-dread:domains "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/domains-of-dread#domains") might seem surreal to individuals from other worlds, but for the residents of the [Mists](#rthw:domains-of-dread:themists "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/domains-of-dread#themists"), Ravenloft’s bizarre qualities are normal parts of reality.

#### Shared Delusion {#rthw:domains-of-dread:SharedDelusion}

Domain residents don’t see incongruities in their existence. Societal pressure and soulless individuals controlled by the [Dark Powers](#rthw:domains-of-dread:thedarkpowers "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/domains-of-dread#thedarkpowers") encourage inhabitants to embrace ignorance, dismiss coincidences, or doubt their senses. Residents of the Domains of Dread are no less perceptive than people elsewhere in the multiverse, but their home domains manipulate them into believing everything is as it should be, must be, and always was.

Those who call domain residents’ reality into question are likely to be dismissed, distrusted, or worse. Individuals who speak of other worlds are broadly considered to be liars or delusional. Few individuals are open-minded to such concepts.

#### Adventurers {#rthw:domains-of-dread:Adventurers}

Ravenloft rarely gives rise to heroes. For the inhabitants of most domains, survival is the only act of courage they pursue. Those willing to confront the terrors of the [Mists](#rthw:domains-of-dread:themists "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/domains-of-dread#themists") are typically strangers from other worlds or domain residents jarred from their apathy by traumatic events.

Adventurers find few peers in the Land of the Mists. Guilds of adventurers and shops catering to their needs generally don’t exist. As a result, the challenge of confronting evil rests squarely with a few rare souls. [Chapter 3](#rthw:ravenloft-adventures "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/ravenloft-adventures") provides details on wanderers who might aid adventurers across domains.

#### Culture and Technology {#rthw:domains-of-dread:CultureandTechnology}

Each domain has a distinct culture. Such cultures might be inspired by societies elsewhere in the multiverse or fantasies manufactured to torment a [Darklord](#rthw:domains-of-dread:darklords "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/domains-of-dread#darklords"). Traditions are purportedly based on history, but few domains have coherent records of the past. Details of ages before a Darklord’s arrival are usually vague or absent.

Similarly, every domain has its own level of technological advancement, the details of which are up to you. In some domains, firearms and clockwork devices are common, while others might feature cutting-edge weird science.

No cultural exchange occurs between the [Domains of Dread](#rthw:domains-of-dread:domains "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/domains-of-dread#domains"). While evidence of one domain might appear in another, such things are viewed with suspicion.

#### Currency {#rthw:domains-of-dread:Currency}

Some domains mint their own gold, silver, and copper coins. Though these currencies bear different markings, merchants aren’t particular about the designs stamped on their currency. Platinum and electrum coins rarely circulate through the domains, but they appear often enough—originating from hidden troves or ancient vaults—that no trader questions their value.

[![(Artist: Andrey Kuzinskiy)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/00-007.haunting-shadow.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/00-007.haunting-shadow.png)

#### Language {#rthw:domains-of-dread:Language}

Common is the shared language of the Domains of Dread. Some domains might have unique words, and speakers from different domains might have distinctive accents, but individuals from different domains are understandable to one another. Other [languages](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/creating-a-character#standardlanguages) from the [Player’s Handbook](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024) are also known among the domains, but their rarity varies between domains as you see fit.

#### Religion {#rthw:domains-of-dread:Religion}

In many domains, residents worship stern but vague gods, and clergy have scant supernatural powers. Any deity, patron, or philosophy from anywhere in the multiverse might have followers in the [Domains of Dread](#rthw:domains-of-dread:domains "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/domains-of-dread#domains"), though these followers’ beliefs might be unconventional. The [Dark Powers](#rthw:domains-of-dread:thedarkpowers "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/domains-of-dread#thedarkpowers") also breathe power into the faith of delusional zealots. Whether otherworldly forces or the Dark Powers empower faithful spellcasters is up to you.

**_Ezra._** Mysteriously, worship of one god has its origins in the [Mists](#rthw:domains-of-dread:themists "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/domains-of-dread#themists"). The god Ezra is depicted as a vaporous figure with dark, billowing hair and is believed to be able to manipulate the Mists. Ezra’s holy symbol is a sprig of belladonna atop a silver kite shield. Ezra’s followers across domains view the deity in contradictory ways. For some, Ezra is a stalwart guardian, while others perceive the god as a soul-stealing embodiment of the Mists. The truths of Ezra’s existence and nature are mysteries.

#### Time and Dates {#rthw:domains-of-dread:TimeandDates}

The Domains of Dread don’t share a calendar. However, in most domains, locals measure time by “moons” rather than months. Each moon begins on the first night of a full moon and lasts a full lunar cycle. A year consists of twelve moons.

Although domains don’t subscribe to a shared history, the populace of all domains inexplicably accept the current year as 735. Some local histories cleave to anomalous dates and methods of tracking years, but these are considered obsolete. No such irregularities exist in [Barovia](#rthw:barovia "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/barovia"), though, where year 1 corresponds with the founding of Barovia by the von Zarovich family.

#### Travel {#rthw:domains-of-dread:Travel}

Most domain residents have little interest in domains beyond their own, and the nature of the Mists makes mercantile ventures and military conquests between domains essentially impossible. Nevertheless, rare individuals travel between the domains either at random, using [Mist talismans](#rthw:domains-of-dread:misttalismans "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/domains-of-dread#misttalismans") (see “[The Mists](#rthw:domains-of-dread:themists "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/domains-of-dread#themists")”), or by engaging mist-wandering guides. Those who enter the Mists by road, river, or sea usually emerge in a new domain by the same method. This means that domains with no coastline must be reached by methods other than ship, but also that travelers following roads rarely emerge from the Mists on the sea—though they might arrive inland within a domain surrounded by water.

<CHAPTER id="rthw:character-options" title="Character Options">

# Chapter 1: Character Options {#rthw:character-options:Chapter1CharacterOptions}

## Chapter 1 Character Options {#rthw:character-options:Chapter1CharacterOptions}

[![The Weathermay-Foxgrove Twins, Gennifer and Laurie, along with Savra Sunstar and Ez d’Avenir, explore the infamous House on Gryphon Hill (Artist: Sean A. Murray)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/01-001.house-on-gryphon-hill.jpg)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/01-001.house-on-gryphon-hill.jpg)

Whether for a night or an eternity, the Mists of Ravenloft pit heroes against their greatest nightmares. This chapter presents resources for players creating and playing characters in horror adventures, including new [subclasses](#rthw:character-options:Subclasses "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/character-options#Subclasses"), [backgrounds](#rthw:character-options:Backgrounds "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/character-options#Backgrounds"), [species](#rthw:character-options:Species "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/character-options#Species"), and [feats](#rthw:character-options:Feats "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/character-options#Feats"). These character options supplement the rules presented in the [Player’s Handbook](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024).

## Haunted Heroes {#rthw:character-options:HauntedHeroes}

This section highlights ways you can create a character prepared to participate in horror adventures.

### Before You Begin {#rthw:character-options:BeforeYouBegin}

Who is a horror adventure supposed to be scary for: you as the player or your character? Is it suspenseful like a mystery story or frightening like a slasher movie? What do you not want to see in a horror adventure? Align with your group’s DM and other players on topics like these before participating in fear-focused adventures. Horror tales cover broad swaths of content. What some might find unsettling, others might shrug off. If you are the DM, consult the “[Ensuring Fun for All](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/dmg-2024/the-basics#ensuringfunforall)” section of the [Dungeon Master’s Guide](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/dmg-2024) for guidance on setting expectations about your game.

### Building a Horror Hero {#rthw:character-options:BuildingaHorrorHero}

[![Characters in horror adventures are often haunted by greater terrors than the monsters they face (Artist: Ignatius Budi)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/01-002.haunted-adventurer.jpg)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/01-002.haunted-adventurer.jpg)

While playing a horror adventure, you participate in building a sense of dread. If your character laughs in the face of every danger, they undermine the adventure’s atmosphere. Consider how past events might haunt your character and contribute to the mood of horror adventures.

### Prepare to Be Scared {#rthw:character-options:PreparetoBeScared}

Knowing what frightens your character provides insight into their past and can motivate their behavior. A character’s fear of cats might stem from a terrible sight they witnessed at their grandmother’s home, while a fear of earthquakes might tie back to the experience of being trapped after a tremor. Consider two or three things that unsettle your character and how those fears shape your character’s past and present.

Courage isn’t the absence of fear, but how one deals with and overcomes it. Consider this in the context of your character. How might they react to a startling scene before rallying to overcome it? Does your character scream and flee, freeze in place, or jump recklessly into battle? Record a default fear reaction on your character sheet to help you respond when shocking events occur.

### Fear Stays in the Game {#rthw:character-options:FearStaysintheGame}

Understand the difference between scaring characters and scaring players. For example, if you know another player has a fear of spiders, never employ that knowledge when contributing to a creepy scene. The [Dungeon Master’s Guide](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/dmg-2024) offers guidance (see “[Hard and Soft Limits](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/dmg-2024/the-basics#hardandsoftlimits)”) to ensure your group has a method for raising concerns mid-game, in the event that things become too intense or go in directions you don’t want to explore. If something in the game leads you to consider scaring or otherwise involving another player’s character, ask that player’s permission before acting. Their enjoyment is more important than shock value.

### Sinister Secrets {#rthw:character-options:SinisterSecrets}

Many characters in horror adventures have shadowy pasts: a harrowing experience that haunts their dreams, a bargain with sinister forces they keep hidden from others, or some other nefarious secret. How a character engages with such internal darkness can make for exciting conflicts. Be sure that your choices allow your character to remain a reliable part of your adventuring group, though, and not a near-villain other heroes only tolerate.

If you’d like your character’s secret to have mechanical implications, Dark Gifts (detailed later in [this chapter](#rthw:character-options:darkgifts "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/character-options#darkgifts")) grant characters supernatural abilities in return for sinister consequences.

### Enjoying the Struggle {#rthw:character-options:EnjoyingtheStruggle}

Not everyone can escape a horror story unscathed. While your character should do everything they can to triumph over challenges, any scars they gain along the way are part of what makes the horror meaningful and memorable.

Consider your goals as a participant in a horror adventure. Are you aiming to ensure the party’s survival or just your character’s? Or do you simply want to create a memorable experience for the other players? Let your goals evolve during an adventure. If these goals lead to greater tension, drama, or sacrifice in ways that echo your favorite horror tales—and that don’t undermine other players’ enjoyment of the game—embrace them. Your character’s actions have great influence in creating exciting and impactful horror adventures.

---

## Subclasses {#rthw:character-options:Subclasses}

This section presents seven new subclasses: the [Reanimator (Artificer)](#rthw:character-options:reanimatorartificer "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/character-options#reanimatorartificer"), [College of Spirits (Bard)](#rthw:character-options:collegeofspiritsbard "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/character-options#collegeofspiritsbard"), [Grave Domain (Cleric)](#rthw:character-options:gravedomaincleric "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/character-options#gravedomaincleric"), [Hollow Warden (Ranger)](#rthw:character-options:hollowwardenranger "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/character-options#hollowwardenranger"), [Phantom (Rogue)](#rthw:character-options:phantomrogue "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/character-options#phantomrogue"), [Shadow Sorcery (Sorcerer)](#rthw:character-options:shadowsorcerysorcerer "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/character-options#shadowsorcerysorcerer"), and [Undead Patron (Warlock)](#rthw:character-options:undeadpatronwarlock "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/character-options#undeadpatronwarlock"). The Artificer class is detailed in [Eberron: Forge of the Artificer](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/efota).

### Reanimator (Artificer) {#rthw:character-options:ReanimatorArtificer}

Reassemble Corpses and Raise the Dead

[![Reanimator Artificer (Artist: Ignatius Budi)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/01-003.reanimator-artificer.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/01-003.reanimator-artificer.png)

Reanimators defy the laws of nature in pursuit of gruesome experiments. These grim Artificers stitch together servants from disparate corpses, use foul magic to strengthen the living, and transform the art of necromancy into a terrifying science.

#### Level 3: Reanimator Spells {#rthw:character-options:Level3ReanimatorSpells}

When you reach an Artificer level specified in the Reanimator Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

**Reanimator Spells**

| Artificer Level | Spells                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| --------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 3               | [**False Life**](#ref:spell:2618866-false-life "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618866-false-life"), [**Spare the Dying**](#ref:spell:2619067-spare-the-dying "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619067-spare-the-dying"), [**Witch Bolt**](#ref:spell:2619215-witch-bolt "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619215-witch-bolt") |
| 5               | [**Blindness/Deafness**](#ref:spell:2618938-blindness-deafness "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618938-blindness-deafness"), [**Enhance Ability**](#ref:spell:2619165-enhance-ability "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619165-enhance-ability")                                                                                |
| 9               | [**Animate Dead**](#ref:spell:2618853-animate-dead "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618853-animate-dead"), [**Lightning Bolt**](#ref:spell:2618999-lightning-bolt "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618999-lightning-bolt")                                                                                                     |
| 13              | [**Blight**](#ref:spell:2618934-blight "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618934-blight"), [**Death Ward**](#ref:spell:2619085-death-ward "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619085-death-ward")                                                                                                                                   |
| 17              | [**Antilife Shell**](#ref:spell:2618856-antilife-shell "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618856-antilife-shell"), [**Raise Dead**](#ref:spell:2618922-raise-dead "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618922-raise-dead")                                                                                                           |

#### Level 3: Reanimator’s Skill Set {#rthw:character-options:Level3ReanimatorsSkillSet}

You gain the following benefits.

**_Jolt to Life._** When you cast [**Spare the Dying**](#ref:spell:2619067-spare-the-dying "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619067-spare-the-dying"), you can modify the spell so that it sends a jolt of electricity through the target, reviving it. The target regains a number of Hit Points equal to your Artificer level, and each creature of your choice in a 10-foot [**Emanation**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#emanationareaofeffect) originating from the target makes a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC, taking 2d4 Lightning damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

You can modify the spell this way a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest. The Lightning damage of this feature increases by 1d4 when you reach Artificer levels 11 (3d4) and 17 (4d4).

**_Reanimator’s Tools._** You gain proficiency with [**Alchemist’s Supplies**](#ref:equipment:397-alchemists-supplies "https://www.dndbeyond.com/equipment/397-alchemists-supplies"). If you already have this proficiency, you gain proficiency with one other type of Artisan’s Tools of your choice.

#### Level 3: Reanimated Companion {#rthw:character-options:Level3ReanimatedCompanion}

Using [**Tinker’s Tools**](#ref:equipment:441-tinkers-tools "https://www.dndbeyond.com/equipment/441-tinkers-tools") or another type of Artisan’s Tools with which you have proficiency, you can take a [**Magic**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#magicaction) action to create a **Reanimated Companion** (see the stat block) through the power of necromancy and science. The companion manifests in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of you. You determine the companion’s appearance; your choices don’t affect the companion’s game statistics.

The companion is [**Friendly**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#friendlyattitude) to you and your allies and obeys you. It lasts until you finish a Long Rest or until you take a Magic action to dismiss it early, at which point it harmlessly collapses into a pile of viscera. It immediately drops to 0 Hit Points and dies (triggering its Death Burst trait) if you die.

Once you create a companion, you can’t do so again until you finish a Long Rest or expend a spell slot to create one. You can have only one companion at a time and can’t create one while your companion is present.

**_The Companion in Combat._** In combat, the companion acts during your turn. It can move and take its Reaction on its own, but the only action it takes is the [**Dodge**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#dodgeaction) action unless you take a Bonus Action to command it to take an action. If you have the [**Incapacitated**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#incapacitatedcondition) condition, the companion acts on its own and isn’t limited to the Dodge action.

##### Reanimated Companion {#rthw:character-options:ReanimatedCompanion}

Medium Undead, Neutral

**AC** 10 plus your Intelligence modifier

**HP** 5 plus five times your Artificer level (the companion has a number of Hit Dice [d8s] equal to your Artificer level)

**Speed** 30 ft.

**STR** 11 (+0) | **DEX** 10 (+0) | **CON** 16 (+3) | **INT** 4 (–3) | **WIS** 10 (+0) | **CHA** 6 (–2)

**Resistances** Necrotic, Poison

**Immunities** Lightning; [**Charmed**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#charmedcondition), [**Exhaustion**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#exhaustioncondition), [**Poisoned**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#poisonedcondition)

**Senses** [**Blindsight**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#blindsight) 60 ft.; Passive Perception 10

**Languages** Understands the languages you know

**CR** None (XP 0; PB equals your Proficiency Bonus)

#### Traits {#rthw:character-options:Traits}

**_Death Burst._** The companion explodes when it dies. _Dexterity Saving Throw:_ DC equals your spell save DC, each creature in a 10-foot [**Emanation**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#emanationareaofeffect) originating from the companion. _Failure:_ 2d4 Necrotic damage. _Success:_ Half damage.

**_Lightning Absorption._** Whenever the companion is subjected to Lightning damage, it regains a number of Hit Points equal to the Lightning damage dealt.

#### Actions {#rthw:character-options:Actions}

**_Dreadful Swipe._** _Melee Attack Roll:_ Bonus equals your spell attack modifier, reach 5 ft. _Hit:_ 1d4 plus your Intelligence modifier Necrotic damage, and the target can’t take [**Opportunity Attacks**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#opportunityattack) until the start of its next turn.

#### Level 5: Strange Modifications {#rthw:character-options:Level5StrangeModifications}

Whenever you create a **Reanimated Companion**, it gains one of the following options of your choice; choose when you create the companion.

**_Arcane Conduit._** You can cast spells as though you were in the companion’s space, but you must use your own senses. Once per turn, when you cast an Artificer spell from the Evocation or Necromancy school and deal damage while your companion is within 120 feet of you, you can add your Intelligence modifier to one damage roll of that spell.

**_Ferocity._** The damage die of the companion’s Dreadful Swipe increases to 1d6.

#### Level 9: Improved Reanimation {#rthw:character-options:Level9ImprovedReanimation}

The damage of your [**Reanimated Companion**’s](#rthw:character-options:reanimatedcompanionstatblock "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/character-options#reanimatedcompanionstatblock") Death Burst increases to 4d4. Necrotic damage dealt by your companion ignores Resistance.

#### Level 9: Macabre Modifications {#rthw:character-options:Level9MacabreModifications}

You experiment and alter your companion further. Whenever you create a [**Reanimated Companion**](#rthw:character-options:reanimatedcompanionstatblock "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/character-options#reanimatedcompanionstatblock"), the companion now gains two options for [Strange Modifications](#rthw:character-options:level5strangemodifications "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/character-options#level5strangemodifications"), instead of one. Additionally, when picking options for Strange Modifications, you can also choose from the following options.

**_Bloated._** The companion becomes Large. Whenever it hits a Large or smaller creature with its Dreadful Swipe action, that creature is pushed up to 10 feet away from the companion. Additionally, you can add your Intelligence modifier to the damage dealt by the companion’s Death Burst.

**_Gaunt._** The companion’s Speed increases to 45 feet, and it gains a Climb Speed equal to its Speed. It can climb difficult surfaces, including along ceilings, without needing to make an ability check. In addition, whenever a creature of your choice starts its turn within a 10-foot [**Emanation**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#emanationareaofeffect) originating from your companion, the creature must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or have the [**Frightened**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#frightenedcondition) condition until the start of its next turn.

**_Moist._** The companion gains a Swim Speed equal to its Speed, and it can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch without expending extra movement to do so. In addition, whenever the companion is hit by an attack roll from a creature within 10 feet of itself, the attacker takes Acid damage equal to your Intelligence modifier.

#### Level 15: Refined Reanimation {#rthw:character-options:Level15RefinedReanimation}

You have mastered the science of revivification, granting you the following benefits.

**_Facilitated Revival._** You can cast [**Raise Dead**](#ref:spell:2618922-raise-dead "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618922-raise-dead") once without expending a spell slot and without Material components, provided you use [**Tinker’s Tools**](#ref:equipment:441-tinkers-tools "https://www.dndbeyond.com/equipment/441-tinkers-tools") or another type of Artisan’s Tools with which you have proficiency as the Spellcasting Focus. Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

**_Life Transfer._** You can siphon the animating magic of your [**Reanimated Companion**](#rthw:character-options:reanimatedcompanionstatblock "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/character-options#reanimatedcompanionstatblock") to bolster yourself. When you or your companion takes damage, you can take a Reaction to gain a number of Hit Points equal to your companion’s current Hit Points. The companion then immediately drops to 0 Hit Points and dies (triggering its Death Burst trait).

**_Superior Modifications._** Whenever you create a **Reanimated Companion**, the companion now gains three options for [Strange Modifications](#rthw:character-options:level5strangemodifications "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/character-options#level5strangemodifications").

### College of Spirits (Bard) {#rthw:character-options:CollegeofSpiritsBard}

Call Forth Spirits from Beyond the Grave

[![College of Spirits Bard (Artist: Ignatius Budi)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/01-004.college-of-spirits-bard.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/01-004.college-of-spirits-bard.png)

Bards of the College of Spirits conjure legendary spirits to change the world. But such entities are capricious, and what a Bard summons isn’t always entirely under their control.

#### Level 3: Channeler {#rthw:character-options:Level3Channeler}

You learn how to contact spirits beyond the grave, letting their power and knowledge flow through you. You gain the following benefits.

**_Guiding Whispers._** You know the [**Guidance**](#ref:spell:2618971-guidance "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618971-guidance") cantrip. It has a range of 60 feet when you cast it.

**_Spiritual Focus._** You employ tools that aid you in channeling spirits. You gain a Gaming Set ([**playing cards**](#ref:equipment:455-playing-cards "https://www.dndbeyond.com/equipment/455-playing-cards")). You have proficiency with this Gaming Set, and you can use it or one of the following items as a Spellcasting Focus for your Bard spells: Arcane Focus ([**crystal**](#ref:equipment:523-crystal "https://www.dndbeyond.com/equipment/523-crystal") or [**orb**](#ref:equipment:526-orb "https://www.dndbeyond.com/equipment/526-orb")), [**Candle**](#ref:equipment:501-candle "https://www.dndbeyond.com/equipment/501-candle"), or [**Ink Pen**](#ref:equipment:502-ink-pen "https://www.dndbeyond.com/equipment/502-ink-pen").

#### Level 3: Spirits from Beyond {#rthw:character-options:Level3SpiritsfromBeyond}

You can call forth spirits of the dead to empower you and your allies. When you take a Bonus Action to give a creature a Bardic Inspiration die, you can call forth the powers of a random spirit. To determine the spirit you channel, roll the Bardic Inspiration die and refer to the Spirits from Beyond table. The spirit remains channeled until you unleash it or until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

**_Controlled Channeling._** As a Bonus Action, you can expend a use of your Bardic Inspiration and channel a specific spirit. When you do so, choose the spirit from the Spirits from Beyond table rather than rolling. The chosen spirit’s corresponding number must be less than or equal to the highest number on your Bardic Inspiration die; for example, if your Bardic Inspiration die is a d8, you can choose to channel any spirit up to (and including) the Shade.

**_Unleashing a Spirit._** As a [**Magic**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#magicaction) action, you can unleash one of your channeled spirits. Choose one creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself as the spirit’s target. The spirit then takes effect; if a spirit’s effect requires a saving throw, the DC equals your Bard spell save DC.

**Spirits from Beyond**

| Bardic Insp. Die | Spirit and Unleash Effect                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| 1                | **Beloved.** The target regains Hit Points equal to a roll of your Bardic Inspiration die plus your Charisma modifier.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| 2                | **Sharpshooter.** The target takes Force damage equal to a roll of your Bardic Inspiration die plus your Charisma modifier.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| 3                | **Avenger.** Until the end of your next turn, any creature that hits the target with a melee attack roll takes Force damage equal to a roll of your Bardic Inspiration die.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| 4                | **Renegade.** The target can immediately take a Reaction to teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space it can see.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| 5                | **Fortune Teller.** The target has [**Advantage**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#advantage) on [**D20 Tests**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#d20test) until the start of your next turn.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| 6                | **Wayfarer.** The target gains [**Temporary Hit Points**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#temporaryhitpoints) equal to a roll of your Bardic Inspiration die plus your Bard level. While the target has these Temporary Hit Points, its Speed increases by 10 feet.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| 7                | **Trickster.** The target makes a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the target takes Psychic damage equal to two rolls of your Bardic Inspiration die and has the [**Charmed**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#charmedcondition) condition until the start of your next turn. On a successful save, the target takes half as much damage only.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| 8                | **Shade.** The target has the [**Invisible**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#invisiblecondition) condition until the end of its next turn or until the target makes an attack roll, deals damage, or casts a spell. When the invisibility ends, each creature in a 5-foot [**Emanation**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#emanationareaofeffect) originating from the target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or take Necrotic damage equal to two rolls of your Bardic Inspiration die.                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| 9                | **Arsonist.** The target makes a Dexterity saving throw, taking Fire damage equal to four rolls of your Bardic Inspiration die on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |

While a creature is Frightened, its Speed is halved (round down), and it can take either an action or a Bonus Action, not both.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
