<CHAPTER id="rthw:domains-of-ravenloft" title="Domains Of Ravenloft">

# Chapter 2: Domains of Ravenloft {#rthw:domains-of-ravenloft:Chapter2DomainsofRavenloft}

## Chapter 2 Domains of Ravenloft {#rthw:domains-of-ravenloft:Chapter2DomainsofRavenloft}

[![By the light of the full moon, villagers in Kartakass undergo a terrifying transformation (Artist: Sean A. Murray)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/02-001.kartakass-transformation.jpg)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/02-001.kartakass-transformation.jpg)

At the unfathomable edge of the Shadowfell liethe Domains of Dread, realms bound by Mists where magic and reality twist into nightmare. This chapter for DMs explores the most terrifying of the Domains of Dread. Among other tools, each featured domain includes the following details:

**Domain.** This initial section introduces the domain, its unique horrors, and notable locations.

**Darklord.** The domain’s Darklord, their stat block, effects they create within their domain, how they close their domain’s borders (see the [introduction](#rthw:domains-of-dread:darklords "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/domains-of-dread#darklords")), and details of their lair appear here.

**Adventures.** This section provides guidance on creating adventures in the domain, a campaign outline, and short adventures.

This chapter concludes with an overview of [additional domains](#rthw:other-domains-of-dread "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/other-domains-of-dread").

## Tarokka and the Mists {#rthw:domains-of-ravenloft:TarokkaandtheMists}

Tarokka fortune-telling cards (detailed in the [appendix](#rthw:tarokka-deck "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/tarokka-deck")) have special relationships with domains and their Darklords.

### Tarokka Mist Talismans {#rthw:domains-of-ravenloft:TarokkaMistTalismans}

Each Domain of Dread is aligned with a tarokka card. A character with a tarokka deck can use it to travel between domains. While in the Mists, the deck’s bearer can draw a random card from the deck; that card serves as a Mist talisman (see the [introduction](#rthw:domains-of-dread:misttalismans "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/domains-of-dread#misttalismans")), allowing travel to the domain it is aligned with. A tarokka deck can be used in this way once every 24 hours. A list of domains and their aligned tarokka cards appears later in [this book](#rthw:other-domains-of-dread:randomdomainsofdreadtable "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/other-domains-of-dread#randomdomainsofdreadtable").

### Darklords and the Tarokka {#rthw:domains-of-ravenloft:DarklordsandtheTarokka}

Every Domain of Dread has a tarokka card that opposes it—one hinting at the truth of the domain’s Darklord. If a domain’s opposed tarokka card is drawn during a tarokka reading in that domain, that domain’s Darklord becomes aware of the reading and its participants. When this occurs, the Darklord can choose to see through the eyes of the tarokka user and speak through them for 1 minute. The Darklord might make their presence known, level a threat, or misinterpret the cards. A tarokka reader has no memory of what a Darklord uses them to say.

<CHAPTER id="rthw:barovia" title="Barovia">

# Barovia {#rthw:barovia:Barovia}

Domain of the First Vampire

> #### **Darklord:** [Strahd von Zarovich](#rthw:barovia:StrahdvonZarovich "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/barovia#StrahdvonZarovich") {#rthw:barovia:StrahdvonZarovich}
>
> **Genre:** [Gothic horror](#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:gothichorror "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/creating-domains-of-dread#gothichorror")
>
> **Hallmarks:** Undead despot, notorious haunted stronghold, tragic resurrection
>
> **Mist Talismans:** Barovian wine bottle, von Zarovich crest, Mark of the Raven talisman
>
> **Aligned Tarokka Card:** Darklord
>
> **Opposed Tarokka Card:** Mists

[![(Artist: Pam Wishbow)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/03-001.darklord-tarokka.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/03-001.darklord-tarokka.png) [![](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/03-002.mists-tarokka.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/03-002.mists-tarokka.png)

In Barovia, the night is a curse. As darkness falls, wicked souls slip from the spires of Castle Ravenloft to work the will of an immortal overlord. This is the realm of the vampire [**Count Strahd von Zarovich**](#ref:monster:6491390-strahd-von-zarovich "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491390-strahd-von-zarovich"), whose depravities have doomed him and his land to endless cycles of obsession and despair.

The howls of wolves and shrieks of ravens echo through the dismal valleys and oppressive forests of Barovia. In isolated communities, superstitious villagers find the brightness in their lives smothered by dread of their aloof overlord and other festering evils. These Barovians fear the night, as agents of the devil Strahd watch in the dark and claim whatever he desires. Yet few in Barovia realize their torments have played out again and again. In every generation, echoes of Strahd’s past reemerge, compelling and confounding the Darklord as he endlessly obsesses over the one victim who’s eluded him for centuries.

## Domain Features {#rthw:barovia:DomainFeatures}

Barovia is known for the following features:

**The Devil Strahd.** Few have seen [Count von Zarovich](#rthw:barovia:StrahdvonZarovich "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/barovia#StrahdvonZarovich"), but all know he dwells in Castle Ravenloft, a citadel from which few visitors return. Strahd is infamous for viciously executing any who flagrantly break his laws, but otherwise he rarely interferes in the lives of his people. Some whisper that he is a vampire.

**Haunted Tales.** The stories of Barovia’s people are full of hidden evils: accursed ruins, portentous ravens, secretive cults, treacherous witches, vicious werewolves, and worse.

**Isolation and Suspicion.** Barovia is a realm of wolf-prowled forests and treacherous mountains where the sun is obscured. The land’s superstitious people live in scattered villages. They distrust strangers, fearing they’re agents of the count.

## Locations in Barovia {#rthw:barovia:LocationsinBarovia}

Barovia is a land of long shadows where ancient wildernesses strangle the ruins of a near-forgotten empire. Mysteries pervade the domain, and those who leave the relative safety of Barovia’s dismal settlements enter perilous lands where mortals aren’t welcome.

The village of Barovia is described below, and other notable locations are summarized on the [Barovia Locations table](#rthw:barovia:barovialocations "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/barovia#barovialocations").

### Village of Barovia {#rthw:barovia:VillageofBarovia}

Lying in the shadow of Castle Ravenloft, the village of Barovia teeters on the brink of ruin. Its few residents rarely venture from their homes, suspecting their neighbors of wickedness and fearing evils in the night. Their dread is largely justified, as wolves, ghosts, and vampire spawn haunt the town, and many locals have been consumed by callousness or wicked temptations.

A rare exception to the village’s cold desperation can be found at the local tavern, the Blood of the Vine. Those few who oppose Strahd’s evil congregate here—under the covert oversight of the count’s agents.

[![Map 2.1: Barovia View Player Version (Artist: Damien Mammoliti)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/map-03-01.barovia.jpg)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/map-03-01.barovia.jpg)

**Barovia Locations**

| Location                             | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Amber Temple                         | A society of mages constructed the Amber Temple long ago to imprison vestiges of malevolent entities. The mages are long dead; mighty evil forces now obsess over the temple’s secrets.                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Argynvostholt                        | The fortified Argynvostholt mansion lies in ruins haunted by the restless spirits of a knightly order destroyed by Strahd. A statue of a regal silver dragon stands before the manor’s entrance.                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Balinok Mountains                    | Barovia spans valleys among the Balinok Mountains. Snow crowns the highest peak, Mount Baratok, while the smaller Mount Ghakis is riddled with deep caves.                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| [Castle Ravenloft](#rthw:barovia:castleravenloft "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/barovia#castleravenloft") | The grim castle of Count Strahd von Zarovich looms over the village of Barovia. The haunted castle contains Strahd’s supernatural servants and the secrets of the Darklord’s origins.                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Gates of Barovia                     | Mighty gates flanked by decapitated statues of soldiers stand along the Old Svalich Road. They open mysteriously for travelers but allow only Vistani to leave the domain to the east.                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Krezk                                | Above the fortified, wooded village of Krezk rises the Abbey of Saint Markovia. Here, a mysterious abbot tends to patients but, in doing so, leaves them permanently changed.                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Old Bonegrinder                      | An ominous windmill called Old Bonegrinder is home to a coven of night hags that create magical pastries. Those who consume the pastries enter a stupor filled with vivid, joyful dreams.                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Ruins of Berez                       | Moldering ruins are all that remain of Berez, a village that denied Strahd’s will and earned his wrath. Nearby stands a statue of a kneeling peasant clutching a rose.                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Svalich Woods                        | Packs of wolves, dire wolves, and werewolves prowl the Svalich Woods, hunting those who oppose Strahd. Strange hermits and witches lurk within the deepest reaches.                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Tser Pool                            | The Vistani who camp near the Tser Pool lake are often joined by other wanderers. This is also the home of the seer [**Madam Eva**](#ref:monster:6491372-madam-eva "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491372-madam-eva") (see [chapter 5](#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:madameva "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/denizens-of-the-mists#madameva")), who knows much of Strahd and the Mists. |
| Vallaki                              | The walled town of Vallaki hosts regular festivals to lift the spirits of its despondent inhabitants. Those who don’t participate risk being punished as malcontents.                                                                                                                                                                                            |

The Mists nearby reflect a vision of the count’s ancestral home in the distance.                                                                                                                                                                               |

## Strahd von Zarovich {#rthw:barovia:StrahdvonZarovich}

First of the Darklords

[![(Artist: Anna Podedworna)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/03-003.strahd-von-zarovich.jpg)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/03-003.strahd-von-zarovich.jpg)

> “I am the Ancient. I am the Land. My beginnings are lost in the darkness of the past. I am not dead. Nor am I alive. I am undead, forever.”
>
> —Strahd von Zarovich

Count Strahd von Zarovich has lost all he ever desired—over and over again. Tormented by the Dark Powers, Strahd is haunted by visions of his lost family and tarnished nobility. The count spends long years brooding in the depths of Castle Ravenloft, but a reincarnation of his obsession appears every generation: Tatyana. Each time Tatyana’s reincarnation emerges, Strahd seeks to undo the failures of his past and find a way to win her love. Time and time again, Strahd’s heartless, domineering nature causes his bloody history to repeat itself and drives Tatyana beyond his clutches.

A severe, aristocratic figure, the count has the bearing of a former soldier and the impatience of one used to being obeyed. He feels little but occasionally embraces the novelty of toying with amusing strangers or breaking the spirits of his enemies. During his unnaturally long existence, he has learned many occult secrets and mysteries of the Domains of Dread. Strahd’s dignified bearing crumbles when someone breaks his laws or denies him what he desires. In such cases, Strahd makes bloody examples of his opponents, drawing out his vengeance into campaigns of terror.

### [Strahd von Zarovich](#ref:monster:6491390-strahd-von-zarovich "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491390-strahd-von-zarovich") {#rthw:barovia:StrahdvonZarovichrefmonster6491390strahdvonzarovichhttpswwwdndbeyondcommonsters6491390strahdvonzarovich}

Medium Undead (Vampire), Lawful Evil

**AC** 16 **Initiative** +9 (19)

**HP** 204 (24d8 + 96)

**Speed** 40 ft., Climb 40 ft.

|     |     | Mod | Save |
| --- | --- | --- | ---- |
| STR | 18  | +4  | +4   |
| DEX | 18  | +4  | +9   |
| CON | 18  | +4  | +4   |

|     |     | Mod | Save |
| --- | --- | --- | ---- |
| INT | 20  | +5  | +5   |
| WIS | 15  | +2  | +7   |
| CHA | 18  | +4  | +9   |

**Skills** [**Arcana**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#skills) +15, [**Perception**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#skills) +12, [**Religion**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#skills) +10, [**Stealth**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#skills) +14

**Resistances** Necrotic

**Senses** [**Darkvision**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#darkvision) 120 ft.; Passive Perception 22

**Challenge** 15 (XP 13,000, or 15,000 in domain; PB +5)

#### Traits {#rthw:barovia:Traits}

**_Darklord Restoration._** If Strahd dies, he revives with all his Hit Points in 1d10 weeks somewhere in Barovia.

**_Legendary Resistance (3/Day, or 4/Day in Domain)._** If Strahd fails a saving throw, he can choose to succeed instead.

**_Misty Escape._** If Strahd drops to 0 Hit Points outside his resting place, he uses Shape-Shift to become mist (no action required). If he can’t use Shape-Shift, he is destroyed. While Strahd has 0 Hit Points in mist form, he can’t return to his vampire form, and he must reach his resting place within 2 hours or be destroyed. Once in his resting place, Strahd returns to his vampire form and has the [**Paralyzed**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#paralyzedcondition) condition until he regains any Hit Points, and he regains 1 Hit Point after spending 1 hour there.

**_Spider Climb._** Strahd can climb difficult surfaces, including ceilings, without making an ability check.

**_Vampire Weakness._** Strahd has these weaknesses:

**Forbiddance.** Strahd can’t enter a residence without an invitation from an occupant.

**Running Water.** Strahd takes 20 Acid damage if he ends his turn in running water.

**Stake to the Heart.** If a weapon that deals Piercing damage is driven into Strahd’s heart while Strahd has the [**Incapacitated**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#incapacitatedcondition) condition in his resting place, Strahd has the [**Paralyzed**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#paralyzedcondition) condition until the weapon is removed.

**Sunlight.** Strahd takes 20 Radiant damage if he starts his turn in sunlight. While in sunlight, he has [**Disadvantage**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#disadvantage) on attack rolls and ability checks.

#### Actions {#rthw:barovia:Actions}

**_Multiattack._** Strahd makes two Death Strike attacks. He can replace one of these attacks with a use of (A) Bite or (B) Spellcasting to cast [**Fireball**](#ref:spell:2618887-fireball "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618887-fireball") if available.

**_Death Strike._** _Melee Attack Roll:_ +9, reach 5 ft. _Hit:_ 8 (1d8 + 4) Slashing damage plus 14 (4d6) Necrotic damage. If the target is a Large or smaller creature, it has the [**Grappled**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#grappledcondition) condition (escape DC 14) from one of two hands.

**_Bite (Bat or Vampire Form Only)._** _Constitution Saving Throw:_ DC 17, one creature within 5 feet that is willing or that has the [**Grappled**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#grappledcondition), [**Incapacitated**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#incapacitatedcondition), or [**Restrained**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#restrainedcondition) condition. _Failure:_ 7 (1d6 + 4) Piercing damage plus 10 (3d6) Necrotic damage. The target’s Hit Point maximum decreases by an amount equal to the Necrotic damage taken, and Strahd regains Hit Points equal to that amount. A Humanoid reduced to 0 Hit Points by this damage rises the following night as a [**Vampire Spawn**](#ref:monster:5195249-vampire-spawn "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195249-vampire-spawn") under Strahd’s control, unless the Humanoid is restored to life or its body is destroyed.

**_Spellcasting._** Strahd casts one of the following spells, using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 18):

**At Will:** [**Detect Thoughts**](#ref:spell:2619099-detect-thoughts "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619099-detect-thoughts"), [**Fog Cloud**](#ref:spell:2618910-fog-cloud "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618910-fog-cloud"), [**Mage Hand**](#ref:spell:2619008-mage-hand "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619008-mage-hand")

**2/Day Each:** [**Animate Dead**](#ref:spell:2618853-animate-dead "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618853-animate-dead"), [**Fireball**](#ref:spell:2618887-fireball "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618887-fireball"), [**Gust of Wind**](#ref:spell:2619137-gust-of-wind "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619137-gust-of-wind"), [**Mirror Image**](#ref:spell:2619060-mirror-image "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619060-mirror-image"), [**Nondetection**](#ref:spell:2619122-nondetection "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619122-nondetection")

**1/Day Each:** [**Greater Invisibility**](#ref:spell:2618958-greater-invisibility "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618958-greater-invisibility"), [**Polymorph**](#ref:spell:2618876-polymorph "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618876-polymorph"), [**Scrying**](#ref:spell:2619007-scrying "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619007-scrying")

#### Bonus Actions {#rthw:barovia:BonusActions}

**_Charm._** Strahd casts [**Charm Person**](#ref:spell:2618964-charm-person "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618964-charm-person"), requiring no spell components and using the same spellcasting ability as Spellcasting. When the spell is cast this way, its duration is 24 hours, and the [**Charmed**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#charmedcondition) target is a willing recipient of Strahd’s Bite, the damage of which doesn’t end the spell. When the spell ends, the target is unaware it was Charmed by Strahd.

**_Shape-Shift._** If Strahd isn’t in sunlight or running water, he [**shape-shifts**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#shapeshifting) into a Tiny bat (Speed 5 ft., Fly Speed 30 ft.), a Medium wolf (Speed 40 ft.), or a Medium cloud of mist (Speed 5 ft., Fly Speed 20 ft. [hover]), or he returns to his vampire form. Anything he is wearing transforms with him.

While in bat or wolf form, Strahd can’t speak. His game statistics, other than his size and Speed, are unchanged.

While in mist form, Strahd can’t take any actions, speak, or manipulate objects. He is weightless and can enter an enemy’s space and stop there. If air can pass through a space, Strahd can do so, but he can’t pass through liquid. Strahd has Resistance to all damage, except the damage he takes from sunlight.

#### Legendary Actions {#rthw:barovia:LegendaryActions}

Legendary Action Uses: 3 (4 in Domain). Immediately after another creature’s turn, Strahd can expend a use to take one of the following actions. Strahd regains all expended uses at the start of each of his turns.

**_Count’s Command._** Strahd casts [**Command**](#ref:spell:2618985-command "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618985-command") (level 2 version), requiring no spell components and using the same spellcasting ability as Spellcasting.

**_Striding Strike._** Strahd moves up to half his Speed, and he makes one Death Strike attack.

### Strahd’s Tale {#rthw:barovia:StrahdsTale}

Count Strahd von Zarovich was a ruthless conqueror. Retiring after years of war, Strahd settled in the beautiful valley where he’d won his greatest victory. There, in the way of his ancestors, he spilled his blood into the earth, sealing a pact between himself and the land. In honor of his parents, King Barov and Queen Ravenovia, he named the valley Barovia and constructed his home, Castle Ravenloft.

Strahd invited his few remaining family members to live with him at Castle Ravenloft and eventually was joined by his younger brother, Sergei. Sergei was everything Strahd wasn’t—youthful, empathic, and warm. Soon after he arrived, the younger von Zarovich and a local villager named Tatyana fell in love. Strahd resented his brother, even more so after meeting Tatyana and being charmed by her pure kindness. Obsessed, Strahd sought to woo her but was rebuffed. Unwilling to accept her wishes or the idea of Sergei as his better, Strahd made a pact with ancient evil forces to regain his vitality and ensnare Tatyana’s heart.

The day of Sergei and Tatyana’s wedding, Strahd murdered Sergei and, to seal his pact, drank his brother’s blood. He revealed his new might to Tatyana, expecting to enthrall her. Instead, horrified by Sergei’s murder, Tatyana fled Strahd, ultimately leaping from the height of Castle Ravenloft and vanishing into the Mists. At the same time, traitors from among the castle’s guards and wedding’s guests rose up to assassinate Strahd. Despite countless wounds, Strahd didn’t die. His bargain with the Dark Powers had made Strahd the multiverse’s first vampire. A night of slaughter followed; when dawn touched the parapets of Castle Ravenloft, no living soul survived within. But Strahd remained.

Strahd’s villainy and his connection to his land drew all of Barovia into the grip of the Dark Powers, which transplanted the vampire and his realm into the Shadowfell. This began a succession of torments that plague the count still. The Dark Powers’ attentions have spilled forth to drag others into the Mists as well, giving rise to the Domains of Dread.

### Strahd’s Domain {#rthw:barovia:StrahdsDomain}

Barovia is altered by Strahd’s presence, creating the following effects:

**Closing the Borders.** While in his domain, Strahd can close or open the borders to Barovia at will. While the borders are closed, noxious fog suffuses the Mists surrounding Barovia. A creature that enters the Mists for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there must succeed on a DC 20 Constitution saving throw or gain 1 [**Exhaustion**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#exhaustioncondition) level. A creature makes this save only once per turn.

**Dreadful Darkness.** While in an area of [**Darkness**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#darkness), creatures other than Strahd and creatures of his choice have [**Disadvantage**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#disadvantage) on saving throws to end or avoid the [**Frightened**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#frightenedcondition) condition.

**Jealous Heart.** When a character receives [**Heroic Inspiration**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#heroicinspiration) but already has it, that character can’t give it to another character in the group.

If Strahd dies, these effects end immediately.

### Strahd’s Lairs {#rthw:barovia:StrahdsLairs}

While the notorious Castle Ravenloft is Strahd’s home, it isn’t his only redoubt in Barovia. Multiple bastions of evil serve as sanctuaries for the count and his servants, should fate demand.

[![Nightly the village of Vallaki bars its gates against attacks from wolves and deadlier predators (Artist: Richard Wright)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/03-004.village-of-vallaki.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/03-004.village-of-vallaki.png)

#### Castle Ravenloft {#rthw:barovia:CastleRavenloft}

Castle Ravenloft is Strahd von Zarovich’s accursed sanctuary. Tormented spirits and Strahd’s minions haunt the vast castle, each serving the count’s schemes, reflecting some aspect of his depraved past, or protecting his coffin in the castle catacombs. Mementos of lost times and fallen heroes lie throughout the count’s home, some of which might hold the key to his undoing. The adventure [Curse of Strahd](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/cos) details Castle Ravenloft.

#### Von Zarovich Sanctuaries {#rthw:barovia:VonZarovichSanctuaries}

Hidden across Barovia lie secret sanctuaries known only to Strahd and his servants. These crypt-like boltholes are hidden from the sun and exist primarily to shelter the count should he require. Over the centuries, Strahd has granted trusted servants access to some of these sanctuaries and used others in plots or experiments that he keeps distant from Castle Ravenloft. Still others Strahd has forgotten, allowing other evils to fester there. An example of one of these sites is depicted on [map 2.2](#rthw:barovia:map0202bloodofthevinetavern "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/barovia#map0202bloodofthevinetavern") and has the following features:

**Count’s Coffin.** Hidden in each sanctuary lies a coffin bearing the von Zarovich crest. This might be obvious or in a space only accessible to vampires.

**The Lord’s Presence.** Behind a vault-like iron door, an entry chamber holds a high-backed throne. Strahd forbids servants from using these symbols of his authority.

**Servants’ Space.** Alcoves carved in the walls provide space for the coffins or bunks of Strahd’s living or dead servants. Sometimes, the Darklord uses these spaces for arcane experiments or as makeshift prisons.

## Adventures in Barovia {#rthw:barovia:AdventuresinBarovia}

Adventures set in Barovia involve oppressive, gothic menace; suspicion; and the legendary threat of Strahd von Zarovich. Use this section to develop horror adventures in this domain.

[![Castle Ravenloft, the accursed home of Count Strahd von Zarovich, casts its shadows across the village of Barovia and far beyond (Artist: Bastien Grivet)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/03-005.castel-ravenloft.png.jpg)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/03-005.castel-ravenloft.png.jpg)

### Horror in Barovia {#rthw:barovia:HorrorinBarovia}

Adventures in Barovia often include the following elements.

#### The Ancient, The Land {#rthw:barovia:TheAncientTheLand}

Strahd remains bound to Barovia and it to him in a way few rulers or Darklords understand. He knows when any creature enters or dies violently within Barovia, and he takes offense when someone slays his servants or the domain’s wolves. Strahd can manifest a variety of dramatic effects, such as casting his voice on the wind, making his visage appear in the clouds, or changing the weather. These effects don’t aid him in combat, but they contribute to making him feel like an oppressive and ever-present threat.

#### Incarnations of the Past {#rthw:barovia:IncarnationsofthePast}

The subject of Strahd’s obsession, Tatyana, perpetually reincarnates among the people of Barovia. No matter what form she takes, the Darklord unceasingly seeks her, determined to possess her and make her part of an idealized fantasy of his past. Tatyana’s incarnation might be anyone, including a player character. If her incarnation is an NPC, roll on the Tatyana’s Reincarnation and Connection to Strahd tables to inspire a new chapter in the count’s tale of obsession.

**Tatyana’s Reincarnation**

| 1d10 | Tatyana’s Reincarnation Is…                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ---- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1    | Anna, the keeper of what another Darklord desires—such as [Ankhtepot’s ka](#rthw:harakir:pharaohssoul "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/harakir#pharaohssoul") or [Mordenheim’s Unbreakable Heart](#rthw:lamordia:unbreakableheart "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/lamordia#unbreakableheart") (both detailed later in this book). |
| 2    | [**Ez d’Avenir**](#ref:monster:6491354-ez-davenir "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491354-ez-davenir") (see [chapter 5](#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:ezdavenir "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/denizens-of-the-mists#ezdavenir")), a monster hunter.                                                               |
| 3    | Ireena Kolyana, adopted daughter of Burgomaster Indirovich of the village of Barovia.                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| 4    | Lyssa von Zarovich, a distant relative of Strahd’s, who has become a vampire.                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| 5    | Nasseri and Yasmine, identical twins who serve the god Ezra.                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| 6    | Petra Rilenovich, an artist who paints images of what she calls “dream lives.”                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| 7    | Quentin L’Argent, the dragonborn son of herders living near Argynvostholt.                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| 8    | Renoir Laurent, the son of Chantal Laurent, a woman Strahd abducted years ago.                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| 9    | Vanasia, a member of a far-ranging Vistani band or other group of mist wanderers.                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| 10   | Vasilka, a [**Flesh Golem**](#ref:monster:5194997-flesh-golem "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5194997-flesh-golem") or reborn (see [chapter 1](#rthw:character-options:reborn "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/character-options#reborn")) who lives in the abbey of Krezk.                                 |

**Connection to Strahd**

| 1d10 | Tatyana’s Reincarnation…                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ---- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1    | Has weaponized their blood with poison that will put Strahd to sleep for a generation.                                                                                                              |
| 2    | Is hidden from Strahd by another Darklord or some more mysterious evil.                                                                                                                             |
| 3    | Becomes trapped by a deceitful servant of Strahd, either bodily or by an effect such as a [**Magic Jar**](#ref:spell:2619021-magic-jar "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619021-magic-jar") spell. |
| 4    | Knows of their reincarnations and seeks to end them by freeing Barovia from the Mists.                                                                                                              |
| 5    | Lives a charmed life, unknowingly protected and cultivated by the count.                                                                                                                            |
| 6    | Misguidedly plans to redeem Strahd through their exceptional kindness or faith.                                                                                                                     |
| 7    | Uses magic to hide from Strahd by appearing elderly, childlike, or as a mysterious animal.                                                                                                          |
| 8    | Searches for a relic that can weaken Strahd.                                                                                                                                                        |
| 9    | Seeks to join a group of adventurers and organize a siege of Castle Ravenloft.                                                                                                                      |
| 10   | Wants to resurrect past incarnations of Tatyana to battle Strahd.                                                                                                                                   |

#### Roots of Evil {#rthw:barovia:RootsofEvil}

As the first Domain of Dread, Barovia might serve an important role in the metaphysical underpinnings of the setting. Some Darklords might have emerged from the Mists first in Barovia, encountered Strahd, and found their ways to their own domains later. Others might have a particular interest in Barovia and in undoing Strahd’s connection to his land. Consider these possibilities when developing plots involving conflicts between Darklords or escaping the Mists, as outlined in [chapter 3](#rthw:ravenloft-adventures "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/ravenloft-adventures").

#### Signs of the Count {#rthw:barovia:SignsoftheCount}

Servants of Strahd are everywhere in Barovia. While in the domain, characters experience regular reminders that the Darklord watches them—and that they are unwelcome. Roll on the Strahd’s Presence table to inspire such encounters.

**Strahd’s Presence**

| 1d8 | Strahd’s Presence Is Suggested…                                                           |
| --- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1   | As clouds momentarily resemble clawed hands, gaping skulls, or Castle Ravenloft.          |
| 2   | As wolves or ravens soundlessly follow the characters and mirror their actions.           |
| 3   | By faded carvings or tapestries bearing the von Zarovich crest.                           |
| 4   | During a tarokka reading, when the Darklord card changes to resemble Strahd.              |
| 5   | In a dream where a character becomes charmed or threatened by Strahd.                     |
| 6   | In a rustic shrine littered with vials of dried blood, snapped splinters, and wolf fangs. |
| 7   | When characters awake to find swarms of roosting bats or bloodless animal corpses.        |
| 8   | When spying villagers try to eavesdrop on or steal small things from the characters.      |

### Barovia Campaign Arc {#rthw:barovia:BaroviaCampaignArc}

Campaigns set in Barovia involve communities oppressed by fear of Strahd and his cycles of obsession. A campaign here might follow this outline:

**Levels 1–5.** The characters emerge from the Mists and seek shelter from danger in the village of Barovia, Krezk, or Vallaki. There they learn the people fear Count von Zarovich, and the characters might meet a [reincarnation of Tatyana](#rthw:barovia:tatyanasreincarnationtable "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/barovia#tatyanasreincarnationtable"). They help strike back against agents of the count, such as deadly [**Wolves**](#ref:monster:4775850-wolf "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/4775850-wolf") or [**Zombies**](#ref:monster:4775851-zombie "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/4775851-zombie").

**Levels 6–8.** The characters learn more of the count’s history and about magical relics that might help oppose him. They seek these in haunted corners of the domain, facing servants of Strahd and remnants of his past, including [**Ghosts**](#ref:monster:5195008-ghost "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195008-ghost"), [**Werewolves**](#ref:monster:5195267-werewolf "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195267-werewolf"), and deadly [**Druids**](#ref:monster:5194976-druid "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5194976-druid").

**Levels 9–10.** Armed with knowledge and magical weapons, the characters lay siege to [Castle Ravenloft](#rthw:barovia:castleravenloft "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/barovia#castleravenloft"), facing [**Strahd’s**](#ref:monster:6491390-strahd-von-zarovich "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491390-strahd-von-zarovich") most terrifying servants and the count himself.

### Blood o’ the Vine {#rthw:barovia:BloodotheVine}

Adventure for Level 6 Characters

**Situation.** A discovery beneath the Blood of the Vine tavern in the village of Barovia has unleashed sinister magic, transforming the owners.

**Hook.** Disguised as a human, Urwin Martikov (Medium [**Wereraven**](#ref:monster:6491402-wereraven "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491402-wereraven"); see [chapter 5](#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:wereraven "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/denizens-of-the-mists#wereraven")) of the Blue Water Inn in Vallaki hires the characters to investigate why the Blood of the Vine tavern in the village of Barovia has closed, claiming he was in negotiations with the owners to buy it. Urwin offers to pay each character 500 GP.

[![The Blood of the Vine tavern is one of the few places in the village of Barovia that welcomes strangers (Artist: Titus Lunter)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/03-006.blood-of-the-vine-tavern.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/03-006.blood-of-the-vine-tavern.png)

#### Encounters {#rthw:barovia:Encounters}

This adventure uses [map 2.2: Blood of the Vine Tavern](#rthw:barovia:map0202bloodofthevinetavern "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/barovia#map0202bloodofthevinetavern") and consists of these encounters.

**_Corrupted Owners._** The three human sisters who owned the Blood of the Vine tavern—Alenka, Mirabel, and Sorvina—have been transformed into the following ravenous embodiments of primal hunger:

**Alenka** ([**Relentless Slasher**](#ref:monster:6491385-relentless-slasher "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491385-relentless-slasher"); see [chapter 5](#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:relentlessslasher "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/denizens-of-the-mists#relentlessslasher")) wields kitchenware and prowls the first floor.

**Mirabel** (Medium [**Ghast Gravecaller**](#ref:monster:5195006-ghast-gravecaller "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195006-ghast-gravecaller")) stalks the second floor with her two [**Ghoul**](#ref:monster:5195009-ghoul "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195009-ghoul") servants.

**Sorvina** ([**Unspeakable Horror**](#ref:monster:6491396-unspeakable-horror "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491396-unspeakable-horror"); see [chapter 5](#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:unspeakablehorror "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/denizens-of-the-mists#unspeakablehorror")) conducts strange rituals in the basement.

**_Taproom._** Dust covers the taproom. Here, the animate corpse of Arik the barkeep mindlessly cleans pieces of shattered glassware at the bar. If attacked or otherwise interrupted, Arik falls to pieces.

**_Office._** The office in the northeast corner of the first floor is cluttered with junk and unfinished notes to the count describing the activities of the tavern’s patrons. This suggests the owners spied on the locals. If the characters have visited the tavern before, their activities are detailed. A trapdoor descends to an area beneath the tavern.

**_Private Dining Room._** The dining room in the southeast corner of the second floor is strewn with broken dishes, rotten food, and pages from a destroyed book. The pages are from the journal of Mirabel, one of the inn’s owners. Surviving entries note the following information:

**First Entry.** Mirabel’s sister Sorvina discovered a hollow hidden under the tavern. Strange ruins lie amid the dirt walls. Sorvina wants to excavate them, hoping to find a tomb filed with treasures.

**Second Entry.** Sorvina’s digging revealed strange standing stones. Mirabel worries about her sister, who’s started whispering to herself as she obsesses over learning more about the stones.

**Third Entry.** Sorvina discovered the bones of some monster at the center of the standing stones. All three sisters are having nightmares from which they wake up ravenous. Sorvina claims the hunger is a blessing. Food has lost its taste, but the inn’s patrons suddenly smell delicious.

**_Temple of Ravenkind._** A circle of ancient menhirs carved with stylized ravens and sunbursts is partially unearthed beneath the tavern. The creature that was once Sorvina is here, chanting over a monstrous skeleton of black bones with stag horns and tusks. When she notices intruders, Sorvina howls, causing the bones to rise as a [**Minotaur Skeleton**](#ref:monster:5195127-minotaur-skeleton "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195127-minotaur-skeleton"). Both it and Sorvina fight the characters to the death. When the skeleton is defeated, its bones remain intact.

**_Cursed Remains._** The skeleton exudes evil magic. Casting [**Remove Curse**](#ref:spell:2618943-remove-curse "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618943-remove-curse") on the monster destroys the skeleton. However, if a character touches the skeleton (while it’s animate or otherwise), its spirit whispers to the character, bidding them to end its ancient curse. Doing so destroys the skeleton and grants the character the Second Skin Dark Gift (see [chapter 1](#rthw:character-options:secondskin "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/character-options#secondskin")). A character who already has a Dark Gift can’t accept the curse.

**_Returning to Urwin._** If the characters defeat the monsters in the tavern and return to Urwin, he pays them and shares that a benevolent relic, the [**Holy Symbol of Ravenkind**](#ref:magic_item:5529-holy-symbol-of-ravenkind "https://www.dndbeyond.com/magic-items/5529-holy-symbol-of-ravenkind"), was created at a site like the one hidden under the tavern. The circle was used later to imprison a vicious spirit of the Svalich Woods. If the characters destroyed the skeleton, Urwin rewards them with two random [**Quaal’s Feather Tokens**](#ref:magic_item:9228948-quaals-feather-token "https://www.dndbeyond.com/magic-items/9228948-quaals-feather-token"). Each character also receives a bonus 1,400 XP.

[![Map 2.2: Blood of the Vine Tavern View Player Version (Artist: Mike Schley)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/map-03-02.blood-of-the-vine-tavern.jpg)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/map-03-02.blood-of-the-vine-tavern.jpg)

[![Map 2.2: Beneath the Tavern View Player Version (Artist: Mike Schley)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/map-03-03.beneath-the-tavern.jpg)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/map-03-03.beneath-the-tavern.jpg)

[![Map 2.2: Outside the Village View Player Version (Artist: Mike Schley)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/map-03-05.outside-the-village.jpg)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/map-03-05.outside-the-village.jpg)

### Treacherous Blood {#rthw:barovia:TreacherousBlood}

Adventure for Level 9 Characters

**Situation.** Lyssa von Zarovich (Medium, Chaotic Evil [**Vampire Nightbringer**](#ref:monster:5195248-vampire-nightbringer "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195248-vampire-nightbringer")), a distant relative of Strahd, plots to undermine the count by unleashing her monstrous servants on Barovia.

**Hook.** A human resident of Vallaki named Ernst Larnak (Medium, Lawful Evil [**Spy**](#ref:monster:5195217-spy "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195217-spy")) tells the characters that locals have seen figures excavating the churchyard in the ruins of Berez. He offers to pay 2,500 GP if they investigate. He doesn’t share that his information comes from the count’s servants.

#### Encounters {#rthw:barovia:Encounters}

This adventure uses [map 2.2: Von Zarovich Sanctuary](#rthw:barovia:map0202vonzarovichsanctuary "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/barovia#map0202vonzarovichsanctuary") and consists of these encounters.

**_Berez Churchyard._** A stone slab covering a grave in the churchyard has been shattered, revealing stairs leading down to a von Zarovich sanctuary. There, two [**Vampire Spawn**](#ref:monster:5195249-vampire-spawn "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195249-vampire-spawn") guardians fight trespassers.

**_Lyssa’s Plot._** Lyssa greets the characters in the sanctuary’s central room. Observing that they don’t look like servants of the count, she shares the following information:

- She is a distant relative of Count Strahd von Zarovich. She, too, is a vampire.
- She seeks to depose Strahd and raise Barovia to its deserved glory.
- With the aid of allies beyond the Mists, she has created servants immune to many of Strahd’s powers. Now she needs to test them.

Regardless of whether the characters agree to aid Lyssa, she opens a door to the adjacent chamber and unleashes a pair of [**Vampire Mind Flayers**](#ref:monster:6491397-vampire-mind-flayer "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491397-vampire-mind-flayer") (see [chapter 5](#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:vampiremindflayer "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/denizens-of-the-mists#vampiremindflayer")). The monsters obey Lyssa’s commands and fight the characters. Lyssa fights as well but flees if she takes damage, swearing her revenge.

**_Crypt._** The chamber to the north holds the bloodless corpse of a mind flayer and a journal filled with accounts of strange dreams. The journal is a Mist talisman linked to the domain of [Bluetspur](#rthw:other-domains-of-dread:Bluetspur "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/other-domains-of-dread#Bluetspur") (see “[Other Domains of Dread](#rthw:other-domains-of-dread "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/other-domains-of-dread")” later in this book).

**_Hidden Chamber._** A character who investigates the large room as a [**Study**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#studyaction) action and succeeds on a DC 16 Intelligence ([**Investigation**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#skills)) check finds evidence of a bricked-over hidden chamber in the east wall. Characters can physically remove the wall in 1 hour (half that time if they have Mason’s Tools).

**_Elder Evil._** Strahd buried a foe in a coffin behind the main chamber’s east wall. Opening the coffin releases a [**Vampire Nosferatu**](#ref:monster:6491398-vampire-nosferatu "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491398-vampire-nosferatu") and a [**Swarm of Infesting Insects**](#ref:monster:6491393-swarm-of-infesting-insects "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491393-swarm-of-infesting-insects") (both detailed in [chapter 5](#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/denizens-of-the-mists")) that fight to the death. Also in the coffin is a [**Gem of Brightness**](#ref:magic_item:9228652-gem-of-brightness "https://www.dndbeyond.com/magic-items/9228652-gem-of-brightness").

**_Conclusion._** If the characters defeat or drive off Lyssa, each character gains a bonus 2,600 XP.

[![Map 2.2: Von Zarovich Sanctuary View Player Version (Artist: Mike Schley)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/map-03-04.von-zarovich-sanctuary.jpg)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/map-03-04.von-zarovich-sanctuary.jpg)

</CHAPTER>

<CHAPTER id="rthw:borca" title="Borca">

# Borca {#rthw:borca:Borca}

Domain of Desire and Deceit

> #### **Darklords:** [Ivana Boritsi](#rthw:borca:IvanaBoritsi "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/borca#IvanaBoritsi") and [Ivan Dilisnya](#rthw:borca:IvanDilisnya "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/borca#IvanDilisnya") {#rthw:borca:ivanaboritsi)}
>
> **Genres:** [Gothic horror](#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:gothichorror "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/creating-domains-of-dread#gothichorror") and [psychological horror](#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:psychologicalhorror "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/creating-domains-of-dread#psychologicalhorror")
>
> **Hallmarks:** Political intrigue, poison, revenge
>
> **Mist Talismans:** Dram of sweet-smelling poison, flame-singed love letter, tarnished signet ring
>
> **Aligned Tarokka Card:** Beggar
>
> **Opposed Tarokka Card:** Tempter

[![(Artist: Pam Wishbow)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/04-001.beggar-tarokka.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/04-001.beggar-tarokka.png) [![](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/04-002.tempter-tarokka.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/04-002.tempter-tarokka.png)

The noble families of Borca engage in an endless war of conspiracies and lethal betrayals as they pursue influence, thrills, and age-old rivalries. People here value guile and callousness, and none embody those traits better than the domain’s two Darklords: the genius poisoner [**Ivana Boritsi**](#ref:monster:6491366-ivana-boritsi "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491366-ivana-boritsi") and the childishly cruel stalker [**Ivan Dilisnya**](#ref:monster:6491365-ivan-dilisnya "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491365-ivan-dilisnya").

Beyond the fashionable holdings of Borca’s elite, commoners struggle against crime, poverty, and starvation. In scattered villages and tenement-filled cities, locals view nobles as celebrities, and the commoners’ idealized vision of noble life leads them to mimic the aristocrats’ callousness and appetite for empty fads. Desperate commoners are tempted into debt and depravity in pursuit of nobles’ favor and passing fancies. Those who don’t bend to the whims of Borca’s elite face humiliation before they’re crushed.

## Domain Features {#rthw:borca:DomainFeatures}

Borca is known for the following features:

**Two Darklords.** [Ivana Boritsi](#rthw:borca:IvanaBoritsi "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/borca#IvanaBoritsi") and [Ivan Dilisnya](#rthw:borca:IvanDilisnya "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/borca#IvanDilisnya") are both Darklords of Borca. They control the domain equally—one of countless facts that contributes to their mutual loathing.

**Cruel Intentions.** Borca’s most influential families are vicious rivals bound by blood, politics, and business. Their rivalries unfold in an endless shadow war of lies, shifting alliances, and assassinations. The nobles value appearances above all else; they favor stylish poisons, clever clockwork devices, and public embarrassment in their plots.

**Desperate Sycophants.** Commoners own little, renting homes in crowded cities or rural villages that serve noble interests. Many commoners desperately court the favor of the elite.

**Noble Intrigue.** Nobles control all aspects of Borcan society. They squabble over artistic, political, and religious influence to feed their gluttonous egos and fill their idle lives. The Boritsi family holds the greatest influence.

## Locations in Borca {#rthw:borca:LocationsinBorca}

The impoverished lands of Borca languish in the shadow of opulent noble estates and garish monuments to greed. The exploited land bears the scars of age-old rivalries and the hiding places of noble secrets.

The capital of Levkarest is described below, and other notable locations are summarized on the [Borca Locations table](#rthw:borca:borcalocations "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/borca#borcalocations").

### Levkarest {#rthw:borca:Levkarest}

Borca’s capital of Levkarest stands at the pinnacle of culture and ostentatious power. Here, lesser nobles pursue fickle dramas and vogue trends while the populace labors amid workhouses and cultlike fashion houses. Commoners glimpse this world of toxic glamor only from afar or when nobles exploit street-level fads.

At the city’s heart rises the People’s Parliament, the land’s ineffective seat of government. Here, unpopular members of noble families squabble over meaningless legislation. The nation’s true rulers conduct business on noble estates, in avant-garde clubs, and in the offices of faceless mercantile ventures.

Near the People’s Parliament stands the Great Cathedral. Within, pious commoners and ostentatious aristocrats attend ceremonies sacred to the deity Ezra. Locals say the cathedral was created by nobles who believed they’d earned the ire of some great evil. Centuries later, these families still support the church, transactionally investing in dubious supernatural insurance.

[![Map 2.3: Borca View Player Version (Artist: Damien Mammoliti)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/map-04-01.borca.jpg)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/map-04-01.borca.jpg)

**Borca Locations**

| Location        | Description                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| --------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Alichino’s Hall | No one knows who built the cursed mansion of Alichino’s Hall, but tales claim that devils gather here nightly to gamble. Allegedly anyone who bests the cheating devils is granted a wish.      |
| House of Lament | The abandoned House of Lament abuts the tower of a ruined castle. Numerous spirits haunt this accursed place, which has been known to appear in the Mists and in other domains.                 |
| Lechberg        | The residents of Lechburg pretend not to notice that many of their neighbors are clockwork creations of Ivan Dilisnya, fearing their unpredictable lord’s reprisal if they don’t play along.    |
| Leoni           | Owned by the Ocrotire family, Leoni has a baseless reputation for harboring bandits. Zealous circuit judges from Sturben often visit and arrest those they deem suspicious.                     |
| New Ilvin       | After Ilvin burned, the residents rebuilt their homes to the east. The people of New Ilvin never speak of the tragedy that befell them and constructed a new road to avoid Old Ilvin.           |
| Noble estates   | The homes of Borca’s most influential families are detailed in “[Nobles of Borca](#rthw:borca:noblesofborca "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/borca#noblesofborca").”                                                                                             |
| Old Ilvin       | Only ruins remain of the town of Ilvin. Hidden within sealed cellars lie the charred remains of many who now appear to reside in the town of New Ilvin.                                         |
| Poison Orchard  | Poisonous fungi and plants grow in the Poison Orchard—the deadliest grow at the forest’s heart. Several noble-backed companies use these plants as secret ingredients in their products.        |
| Scholomance     | Scions of Borca’s noble families viciously compete to attend the elite Scholomance school of magic. The school is home to the Rainmaker Society, which is said to control Borcan politics.      |
| Sturben         | Sturben is home to the Faceless Court, in which groups of five masked judges execute severe justice across social classes. Their iron-masked circuit judges travel widely.                      |
| Vor Ziyden      | A hound-like horror appears nightly to terrorize the village of Vor Ziyden. Only one local knows the monster seeks the corpse of its brother, who died near a druidic site in the nearby woods. |

## Ivana Boritsi {#rthw:borca:IvanaBoritsi}

Darklord of Poisonous Ambition

[![(Artist: WeirdUndead (Karina Refrynn))](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/04-003.ivana-boritsi.jpg)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/04-003.ivana-boritsi.jpg)

> “Your kind can’t possibly fathom how much this sort of interruption costs the House of Boritsi. Don’t make it worse by being tedious.”
>
> —Ivana Boritsi

Ivana Boritsi tires of playing games no one realizes she’s already won. The head of Borca’s most influential family, Ivana effortlessly manipulates all aspects of society. Her servants, employees, and fractious cousins prove endlessly unreliable, forcing her to attend personally to tedious duties and social functions to maintain her power.

Ivana looks eternally youthful, causing some to doubt her competence and attribute her success to her elder cousin, [**Ivan Dilisnya**](#ref:monster:6491365-ivan-dilisnya "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491365-ivan-dilisnya"). Perpetually bored with and disappointed by predictable people, she takes refuge in her alchemical studies and her gardens of poisonous plants. Her vast knowledge of toxins makes her a peerless poisoner. She uses her creations to make people more pliable and to assassinate those she deems too boorish to live. Secretly, Ivana seeks someone who can match her intellect and relieve her boredom, but she quickly grows weary of even the most charming and clever souls.

### Ivana’s Tale {#rthw:borca:IvanasTale}

The firstborn of a fantastically wealthy family, Ivana Boritsi was clever, poised, and—in the eyes of her father, Klaus—utterly unfit to lead the family. Driven to prove her father wrong and encouraged by her mother, Camille, Ivana learned every aspect of her family’s vast perfume and medicine business.

Her focus on her goals faltered when she met Pieter, a skilled chemist in her family’s service. Camille recognized her daughter’s budding romance and saw the lowborn Pieter as a threat to the girl’s prospects. Camille seduced Pieter and arranged for her daughter to discover them, intent on convincing her to forsake this and all future romances.

Ivana took a different lesson from the experience. Realizing the depths of her family’s depravity, she poisoned her mother and her callous younger siblings with toxins of her own design. None suspected Ivana, but soon after, Klaus summoned her. Having lost his sons, Klaus named her cousin, Ivan Dilisnya, his heir. Ivana was the last to be informed, her father having already announced his decision to the estate and sent a messenger to inform the Dilisnyas.

Having expected this, Ivana had poisoned the perfumery on the estate’s grounds, turning its far-ranging smells deadly. Ivana laughed as toxic mist poured across the estate. As she sipped the antidote, she watched Klaus and the manor’s staff die choking amid a violet fog. When the poison cleared, the Mists had surrounded the land of Borca (for details on Ivana’s [domain](#rthw:borca:ivanaandivansdomain "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/borca#ivanaandivansdomain") and [lair](#rthw:borca:ivanaslair "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/borca#ivanaslair"), see “[Ivan Dilisnya](#rthw:borca:IvanDilisnya "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/borca#IvanDilisnya")”).

### [Ivana Boritsi](#ref:monster:6491366-ivana-boritsi "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491366-ivana-boritsi") {#rthw:borca:IvanaBoritsirefmonster6491366ivanaboritsihttpswwwdndbeyondcommonsters6491366ivanaboritsi}

Medium Humanoid (Human), Neutral Evil

**AC** 17**Initiative** +9 (19)

**HP** 104 (16d8 + 32)

**Speed** 30 ft.

**STR** 10 (+0) | **DEX** 17 (+3) | **CON** 14 (+2) | **INT** 18 (+4) | **WIS** 15 (+2) | **CHA** 14 (+2)

**Skills** [**Deception**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#skills) +8, [**Nature**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#skills) +7, [**Perception**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#skills) +5

**Immunities** Poison; [**Poisoned**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#poisonedcondition)

**Senses** Passive Perception 15

**Languages** Common

**CR** 5 (XP 1,800, or 2,300 in domain; PB +3)

#### Traits {#rthw:borca:Traits}

**_Darklord Restoration._** If Ivana dies, she revives with all her Hit Points in 1d10 weeks somewhere in Borca.

**_Legendary Resistance (2/Day, or 3/Day in Domain)._** If Ivana fails a saving throw, she can choose to succeed instead.

#### Actions {#rthw:borca:Actions}

**_Multiattack._** Ivana makes two Toxic Touch attacks.

**_Toxic Touch._** _Melee Attack Roll:_ +7, reach 5 ft. _Hit:_ 8 (1d8 + 4) Poison damage. A Humanoid reduced to 0 Hit Points by this damage rises 24 hours later as a [**Vine Blight**](#ref:monster:5195252-vine-blight "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195252-vine-blight") under Ivana’s control unless the Humanoid is restored to life or its body is destroyed.

**_Stifling Perfume (Recharge 5–6)._** _Constitution Saving Throw:_ DC 15, each creature in a 30-foot [**Emanation**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#emanationareaofeffect) originating from Ivana. _Failure:_ 13 (3d8) Poison damage, and the target has the [**Prone**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#pronecondition) condition. _Success:_ Half damage only.

#### Bonus Action {#rthw:borca:BonusAction}

**_Charm (Recharge 5–6)._** Ivana casts [**Charm Person**](#ref:spell:2618964-charm-person "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618964-charm-person"), requiring no spell components and using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 15), and the duration is 24 hours.

**_Tree Stride._** If within 5 feet of a Large or bigger inanimate plant, Ivana teleports to an unoccupied space within 5 feet of a second Large or bigger inanimate plant that is within 60 feet of the previous plant.

#### Legendary Actions {#rthw:borca:LegendaryActions}

Legendary Action Uses: 2 (3 in Domain). Immediately after another creature’s turn, Ivana can expend a use to take one of the following actions. Ivana regains all expended uses at the start of each of her turns.

**_Retaliate._** Ivana makes one Toxic Touch attack.

**_Toxin Wave._** _Dexterity Saving Throw:_ DC 15, each creature in a 15-foot [**Cone**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#coneareaofeffect). _Failure:_ The target has the [**Poisoned**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#poisonedcondition) condition until the end of its next turn. While Poisoned, the target subtracts 1d6 from its damage rolls. _Failure or Success:_ Ivana can’t take this action again until the start of her next turn.
