## Ivan Dilisnya {#rthw:borca:IvanDilisnya}

Darklord of Childish Cruelty

[![(Artist: WeirdUndead (Karina Refrynn))](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/04-004.ivan-dilisnya.jpg)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/04-004.ivan-dilisnya.jpg)

> “Oh ho oh! What succulent insipidity I see in those lumpish eyes! What divine folly! I swoon, I croon, I know! You’ll be a new favorite!”
>
> —Ivan Dilisnya

Ivan Dilisnya—a spoiled, selfish attention seeker—has the tastes of a child but a withered wreck of a body. Borcan society widely regards this recluse as an innovator and a genius. In truth, he is neither. Ivan is a wicked and off-putting manipulator who, despite his appearance and intellect, affects childlike behaviors and speech patterns for attention. He is alone—despite having been born with everything—and the solitude terrifies him.

By staying out of sight or using deceptive correspondence, Ivan makes his targets doubt reality and overestimate his control. He manipulates people into performing pointless errands for him or spying on his cousin, [**Ivana Boritsi**](#ref:monster:6491366-ivana-boritsi "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491366-ivana-boritsi"), whom he believes mocks him and has caused his aged, squalid state.

Ivan surrounds himself with dangerous clockwork toys and fawning, mechanical servants. While he goes through the motions of crafting such devices, the Dark Powers provide him with any creation he desires, no matter how bizarre.

### Ivan’s Tale {#rthw:borca:IvansTale}

Treachery is tradition for the Dilisnya family. The land of Borca originates from the same world as Barovia’s conquerors, the von Zaroviches. Dilisnyas were at Castle Ravenloft the night of Strahd von Zarovich’s transformation.

Ages later, the siblings Boris and Camille Dilisnya plotted to steal the prestige of their cousins, the Boritsis. Camille manipulated her way into the Boritsi family, while Boris prepared his son, Ivan, to act as head of a united Boritsi–Dilisnya house.

Despite abundant opportunities, Ivan resented his family’s plans for him and grew to embody puerile vice and impulses. His family’s wealth and doting servants exacerbated this problem, even as Ivan fixated on childish toys and behaviors. Frequent “accidents” transpired around him, forcing his family to cover up the maimings and deaths of numerous pets and servants. Only his beloved sister, Kristina, remained immune to his wicked tricks. Although Ivan’s family grew unsettled by Ivan, they sheltered the future head of their house, reshaping their estate and investing in whimsical diversions for him.

On the same night Ivana Boritsi poisoned her family, Ivan learned his parents intended to send Kristina to a prestigious boarding school. Screams, cruel cackling, and clockwork screeching filled the estate that night. When it ended, Ivan Dilisnya was the last living member of his family, and the Mists had closed around Borca.

### [Ivan Dilisnya](#ref:monster:6491365-ivan-dilisnya "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491365-ivan-dilisnya") {#rthw:borca:IvanDilisnyarefmonster6491365ivandilisnyahttpswwwdndbeyondcommonsters6491365ivandilisnya}

Medium Humanoid (Human), Lawful Evil

**AC** 12**Initiative** +8 (18)

**HP** 90 (12d8 + 36)

**Speed** 40 ft., Climb 40 ft.

**STR** 18 (+4) | **DEX** 14 (+2) | **CON** 16 (+3) | **INT** 19 (+4) | **WIS** 12 (+1) | **CHA** 15 (+2)

**Skills** [**History**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#skills) +7, [**Investigation**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#skills) +7, [**Perception**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#skills) +7

**Senses** Passive Perception 17

**Languages** Common

**CR** 5 (XP 1,800, or 2,300 in domain; PB +3)

#### Traits {#rthw:borca:Traits}

**_Darklord Restoration._** If Ivan dies, he revives with all his Hit Points in 1d10 weeks somewhere in Borca.

**_Legendary Resistance (2/Day, or 3/Day in Domain)._** If Ivan fails a saving throw, he can choose to succeed instead.

#### Actions {#rthw:borca:Actions}

**_Multiattack._** Ivan makes two Foreleg attacks. He can replace one attack with a use of Deadly Contraption.

**_Foreleg._** _Melee Attack Roll:_ +7, reach 10 ft. _Hit:_ 11 (2d6 + 4) Piercing damage.

**_Deadly Contraption._** _Dexterity Saving Throw:_ DC 15, one creature Ivan can see within 30 feet. _Failure:_ 13 (3d8) Slashing damage. _Failure or Success:_ A flailing clockwork contraption attaches to the target until the start of Ivan’s next turn. If the target willingly moves 5 feet or more before then, the target takes 4 (1d8) Slashing damage.

At the start of Ivan’s next turn, the device crumbles to dust and vanishes.

#### Legendary Actions {#rthw:borca:LegendaryActions}

Legendary Action Uses: 2 (3 in Domain). Immediately after another creature’s turn, Ivan can expend a use to take one of the following actions. Ivan regains all expended uses at the start of each of his turns.

**_Retaliate._** Ivan makes one Foreleg attack.

**_Trapped Ground._** Ivan spreads special caltrops to cover a 20-foot-square area within 5 feet of himself. The caltrops dissolve at the end of Ivan’s next turn. Ivan can’t take this action again until the start of his next turn.

When the caltrops appear, each creature in the area is subjected to the following effect; a creature that enters the caltrops for the first time on a turn or ends its turn there is also subjected to this effect. _Dexterity Saving Throw:_ DC 15 (a creature makes this save only once per turn). _Failure:_ 9 (2d8) Piercing damage, and its Speed is reduced to 0 until the start of its next turn.

### Ivana and Ivan’s Domain {#rthw:borca:IvanaandIvansDomain}

Borca is altered by Ivana’s and Ivan’s presences, creating the following effects:

**Closing the Borders.** While in their domain, Ivana or Ivan can close or open the borders to Borca at will. While the borders are closed, the Mists surrounding Borca are filled with briar vines (Ivana) or barbed wire (Ivan). The Mists become [**Difficult Terrain**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#difficultterrain), and whenever a creature moves into or within the Mists, it takes 2d4 Piercing damage for every 5 feet it travels. Once Ivana or Ivan closes or opens the borders, neither Darklord can do so again until the next dawn.

**Ivana’s Whispers (Ivana Only).** Ivana can encode a message of 25 words or fewer into flowers in Borca at dawn. Until the next dawn, the first time a creature smells a flower, it hears the message in its mind, understanding the meaning of the message.

**Mystery Letters (Ivan Only).** Whenever Ivan writes a letter and addresses it to a creature in Borca whose name he knows and that he’s seen before, the letter appears near that creature at the next dawn. The letter appears in an unobserved but obvious space, such as a bedside table or among gear.

**Spies.** While in Borca, Ivana and Ivan can cast [**Clairvoyance**](#ref:spell:2618972-clairvoyance "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618972-clairvoyance"), requiring no Material components and using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability. To cast the spell, there must be a Large or bigger plant (Ivana) or a Tiny doll or similar toy (Ivan) within range from which the sensor appears.

If a Darklord of Borca dies, that Darklord’s effects end immediately. Those effects resume if that Darklord gains a new body (see [Ivana’s](#rthw:borca:ivanaboritsistatblock "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/borca#ivanaboritsistatblock") and [Ivan’s](#rthw:borca:ivandilisnyastatblock "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/borca#ivandilisnyastatblock") Darklord Restoration traits).

### Ivana’s Lair {#rthw:borca:IvanasLair}

The vast Boritsi estate, Misericordia, hosts fields, greenhouses, and alchemy labs used to create Boritsi-branded perfumes and tinctures. Within the manor, the Darklord cultivates rare and unique plants in greenhouse-like conservatory wings only she can enter.

#### Misericordia Conservatories {#rthw:borca:MisericordiaConservatories}

The conservatories of Misericordia, the Boritsi estate, hold strange plants, many of which Ivana cultivated. One such site is depicted on map 2.4 and has the following features:

**Gardens.** Plants of exceptional beauty and toxicity flourish under Ivana’s care in Misericordia’s gardens and greenhouses. Many require unusual fertilizers to flourish—particularly the carnivorous plants.

**Laboratory.** In her lab, the Darklord brews deadly alchemical concoctions and wondrous perfumes. A sizable perfume organ here is filled with rare scents and lethal poisons.

**Nursery.** Hidden behind a rotating wall is Ivana’s private nursery and study. Here she cultivates new plant species, many of which have supernatural properties or monstrous life.

[![Map 2.4: Misericordia Greenhouse View Player Version (Artist: Mike Schley)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/map-04-02.misericordia-greenhouse.jpg)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/map-04-02.misericordia-greenhouse.jpg)

### Ivan’s Lair {#rthw:borca:IvansLair}

The Dilisnya estate, Degravo, is a confusing tangle of topiary gardens, hedge mazes, and neglected petting zoos that abut sheer cliffs. At the heart of the grounds sits a largely abandoned compound that includes the Laughing House, Ivan’s home.

#### The Laughing House {#rthw:borca:TheLaughingHouse}

The only occupied structure in Degravo, the Laughing House has been renovated and redecorated to suit a child’s whimsical tastes. The site is depicted on map 2.4 and has the following features:

**Ivan’s Playroom.** On the second floor of the manor, a gallery of childish art leads to doors minded by a clockwork attendant that Ivan can taunt intruders through. At the hall’s end is a fake bedroom decorated for a neglected youngster. A hidden door there leads to Ivan’s true personal chambers. This playroom is a wonderland of ingenious toys, all of which are secretly deadly. Beyond the Darklord’s personal chamber lie secret rooms where he creates new playthings and discards toys he’s grown tired of.

**Playhouse.** Beyond a lobby attended by clockwork staff, a theater hosts brutal stage productions for Ivan’s amusement. Performers might be life-size toys or desperate prisoners.

[![Map 2.4: Degravo Laughing House View Player Version (Artist: Mike Schley)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/map-04-03.degravo-laughing-house.jpg)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/map-04-03.degravo-laughing-house.jpg)

## Adventures in Borca {#rthw:borca:AdventuresinBorca}

Adventures set in Borca involve intrigue between petty nobles, family secrets, manipulation, and deception. Use this section to develop horror adventures in this domain.

[![At Misericordia, the Boritsi family estate, Ivana Boritsi indulges her research into rare and deadly plants (Artist: Maihope)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/04-005.boritsi-family-estate.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/04-005.boritsi-family-estate.png)

### Horror in Borca {#rthw:borca:HorrorinBorca}

Adventures in Borca often include the following elements.

#### Nobles of Borca {#rthw:borca:NoblesofBorca}

Twelve depraved families rule over every aspect of life in Borca. Each is a core family of fifteen or fewer irredeemable individuals united around the head of the house, who tyrannically controls the clan’s myriad ventures. Servants and business representatives across the domain support these core families, as do members of branch families—lackeys with different surnames who are distantly related to the core family or indentured to them.

The Noble Families of Borca table details the domain’s most powerful families.

**Noble Families of Borca**

| Name      | Estate Name  | Concern                            |
| --------- | ------------ | ---------------------------------- |
| Boritsi   | Misericordia | Beauty and medical tonics, perfume |
| Dilisnya  | Degravo      | Agriculture                        |
| Eris      | Coairdeiador | Art, theater                       |
| Ivliskova | Abreptoro    | Education, orphanages              |
| Nobriskov | Cubratdis    | Religion                           |
| Nuikin    | Esecklae     | Academia, athletics                |
| Ocrotire  | Sanctesalat  | Fishing, woodwork                  |
| Olzanik   | Kinisaradia  | Metalwork                          |
| Piechota  | Alieselti    | Ranching                           |
| Pretorius | Mundorhova   | Gambling                           |
| Ritter    | Vetistiqua   | Fashion                            |
| Tatenna   | Fulchighora  | Banking                            |

#### Supernatural Intrigue {#rthw:borca:SupernaturalIntrigue}

Magic and the supernatural heighten the gilded depravities of Borca. When planning adventures in Borca, consider including the following elements.

**_Curses and Poison._** [Chapter 3](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/dmg-2024/dms-toolbox) of the [Dungeon Master’s Guide](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/dmg-2024) describes curses, magical contagions, and poison. Villains in Borca might use these or adjusted versions of your own design—perhaps with signature cosmetic effects.

**_Monsters._** Monsters can serve as threats but also agents of noble houses. [**Shape-shifting**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#shapeshifting) creatures such as [**Imps**](#ref:monster:4775825-imp "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/4775825-imp") and [**Wererats**](#ref:monster:5195265-wererat "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195265-wererat") excel at infiltration, while [**Doppelgangers**](#ref:monster:5174955-doppelganger "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5174955-doppelganger") and [**Succubi**](#ref:monster:4904865-succubus "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/4904865-succubus") might pose as nobles, innocents, or trusted allies. Creatures like [**Ghosts**](#ref:monster:5195008-ghost "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195008-ghost") and [**Intellect Devourers**](#ref:monster:5195088-intellect-devourer "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195088-intellect-devourer") might control individuals, making them behave in unusual ways. Choose a single monster, and consider how you might make it central to a devious noble’s plot.

**_Spells and Magic Items._** Don’t try to account for or incorporate all magic into adventures involving supernatural intrigue. Choose a single spell—such as [**Clairvoyance**](#ref:spell:2618972-clairvoyance "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618972-clairvoyance"), [**Geas**](#ref:spell:2618940-geas "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618940-geas"), or [**Speak with Dead**](#ref:spell:2619068-speak-with-dead "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619068-speak-with-dead")—and consider how to make it central to a plot involving secrets and mysterious revelations. Consider doing the same with a magic item such as a [**Cloak of the Bat**](#ref:magic_item:4608-cloak-of-the-bat "https://www.dndbeyond.com/magic-items/4608-cloak-of-the-bat"), a [**Hag Eye**](#ref:magic_item:9228705-hag-eye "https://www.dndbeyond.com/magic-items/9228705-hag-eye"), or [**Sending Stones**](#ref:magic_item:9180147-sending-stones "https://www.dndbeyond.com/magic-items/9180147-sending-stones"). Characters should earn rewards for using their own magic in clever ways.

### Borca Campaign Arc {#rthw:borca:BorcaCampaignArc}

Campaigns set in Borca typically involve the domain’s noble families. A campaign here might follow this outline:

**Levels 1–3.** A scheming noble targets the characters, presenting them with an opportunity or exorbitant compensation for a simple task. In the aftermath, the characters discover they have given up something of great value or realize they look like criminals.

**Levels 4–6.** The scheming noble or a rival offers the characters a way out of their predicament, but this involves a dangerous confrontation or daring infiltration. Supernatural forces—such as jilted doppelgangers, cursed family members, or dead nobility—might aid the characters. Against expectations, the characters complete their mission and turn the tables on their foe.

**Levels 7–8.** The characters’ activities attract the attention of [**Ivana Boritsi**](#ref:monster:6491366-ivana-boritsi "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491366-ivana-boritsi") or [**Ivan Dilisnya**](#ref:monster:6491365-ivan-dilisnya "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491365-ivan-dilisnya"). The Darklord invites the characters to their estate or corresponds with them from afar, using them as agents in their rivalry. For example, either Darklord might task the characters with seeking out the missing will of Ivana’s father, Klaus.

### Lethal Lavender {#rthw:borca:LethalLavender}

Adventure for Level 5 Characters

**Situation.** The human siblings Eroso and Siobhan Manduchi (Medium, Neutral Evil [**Nobles**](#ref:monster:5195145-noble "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195145-noble")) are scions of a minor noble family who stole a rare plant, not realizing it belonged to the Boritsis. After discovering the owner, they feign their deaths to avoid reprisal.

**Hook.** Eroso and Siobhan seek out the characters to use as patsies in their staged murder.

#### Encounters {#rthw:borca:Encounters}

The adventure consists of these encounters.

**_Dig Your Vibe._** Eroso and Siobhan Manduchi approach the characters and invite them to go carousing if the adventurers agree to share tales of their exploits. The two are [**Friendly**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#friendlyattitude) and flattering.

**_Exquisite Corpse._** Soon after the characters leave the siblings, they hear a scream. If they investigate, they find Eroso’s stabbed corpse surrounded by guards. Siobhan accuses the characters of killing her brother. A group of four [**Guards**](#ref:monster:5195065-guard "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195065-guard") and one [**Guard Captain**](#ref:monster:5195064-guard-captain "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195064-guard-captain") (in the Manduchis’ employ) moves to kill the characters, while Siobhan vanishes into the night.

**_Wanted._** More guards hunt for the characters but are easy to avoid. Before the characters flee the community, Nostalia Romaine (Medium, Lawful Evil [**Assassin**](#ref:monster:5194904-assassin "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5194904-assassin")), who appears to be human, discovers them. She explains that she works for the Boritsi family, shares the details in “Situation” above, and insists the characters help her find the Manduchis.

**_Dead Walking._** Any character who spends a day searching for the Manduchis and succeeds on a DC 14 Wisdom ([**Insight**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#skills)) or Charisma ([**Persuasion**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#skills)) check learns Eroso’s or Siobhan’s whereabouts. If they investigate, they find a public site—like a theater or bar—where the noble is behaving recklessly. These aren’t the actual Manduchis, but [**Waxworks**](#ref:monster:6491401-waxwork "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491401-waxwork") (see [chapter 5](#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:waxwork "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/denizens-of-the-mists#waxwork")) striving to destroy themselves in public. The characters encounter at least two of these creatures, perhaps more at your discretion.

**_Flawed Perfection._** After the characters encounter at least two self-destructive Manduchi waxworks, they find a **Waxwork** convinced that it is the new, improved Eroso Manduchi, and it doesn’t want to die. If the characters promise to let it go, the Construct leads them to Lethal Lavender, the secret club where the Manduchis are hiding.

**_Lethal Lavender._** The interior of the Lethal Lavender club is overgrown with bruise-colored fungus. A pair of fungus-covered [**Zombie Plague Spreaders**](#ref:monster:6491406-zombie-plague-spreader "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491406-zombie-plague-spreader") (see [chapter 5](#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:zombieplaguespreader "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/denizens-of-the-mists#zombieplaguespreader")) haunts the bar. In the VIP lounge, the plant the Manduchis stole has bloomed into a [**Violet Fungus Necrohulk**](#ref:monster:5195253-violet-fungus-necrohulk "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195253-violet-fungus-necrohulk") composed of the real Manduchis and their remaining wax duplicates.

**_Ivana’s Favor._** After the monster’s defeat, Nostalia finds the characters. She rewards them with a vial of Boritsi perfume worth 2,000 GP and a letter from Ivana Boritsi inviting them to a private social event at Misericordia in a week’s time. Each character also earns a bonus 1,100 XP.

</CHAPTER>

<CHAPTER id="rthw:darkon" title="Darkon">

# Darkon {#rthw:darkon:Darkon}

Domain on the Brink of Destruction

> #### **Darklord:** None {#rthw:darkon:DarklordNone}
>
> **Genres:** [Dark fantasy](#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:darkfantasy "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/creating-domains-of-dread#darkfantasy") and [disaster horror](#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:disasterhorror "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/creating-domains-of-dread#disasterhorror")
>
> **Hallmarks:** Fractured realm, magical ruins, ongoing supernatural catastrophe
>
> **Mist Talismans:** Ashes of a corpse, coin stamped with Azalin Rex’s face, tainted spring water
>
> **Aligned Tarokka Card:** Necromancer
>
> **Opposed Tarokka Card:** Donjon

[![(Artist: Pam Wishbow)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/05-001.necromancer-tarokka.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/05-001.necromancer-tarokka.png) [![](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/05-002.donjon-tarokka.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/05-002.donjon-tarokka.png)

Darkon is a sprawling realm of somber gothic cities, vast wildernesses, hidden secrets, and the dead. The ruins of forgotten magical empires scar the land. Undead creatures haunt the domain’s lonely reaches, and the living acknowledge that the land’s morbid magic might one day reanimate their corpses.

Yet, for all its mysteries, the domain of Darkon has failed. Across the realm, the Mists close in, inexorably overwhelming the land. These Mists turned ravenous are known as the Shroud, and what they consume doesn’t reemerge.

Darkon’s dissolution ties to the disappearance of its Darklord, [**Azalin Rex**](#ref:monster:6491340-azalin-rex "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491340-azalin-rex"). During a disastrous event known as the Hour of Ascension, Azalin’s citadel, Castle Avernus, was destroyed, and a mysterious golden star called the King’s Tear appeared in the heavens. Since then, no one has seen Azalin, and the Shroud has eroded the domain.

Despite the encroaching annihilation, life in Darkon hasn’t changed. The residents of towns and cities far from the domain’s borders dismiss reports of vanishing frontiers as fearmongering. As Darkon splits into crumbling islands, ambitious individuals vie for Azalin’s power, each touting that they alone can save the land by becoming its tyrant.

## Domain Features {#rthw:darkon:DomainFeatures}

Darkon is known for the following features:

**Divided Domain.** The Mists consuming Darkon have divided the land into four separate regions.

**Hour of Ascension.** [Azalin Rex](#rthw:darkon:AzalinRex "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/darkon#AzalinRex") vanished during an event his servants call the Hour of Ascension.

**Inevitable Undeath.** The night after any Humanoid dies, its corpse reanimates and shambles into the night. Locals swiftly burn bodies to prevent this.

**King’s Tear.** Since the Hour of Ascension, a golden star called the King’s Tear hangs in the sky. The sun and moon pass behind this star in their orbits.

**Secret Police.** The Kargat, the domain’s secret police, remains active in Darkon’s largest cities: Il Aluk and Martira Bay.

## Locations in Darkon {#rthw:darkon:LocationsinDarkon}

Darkon is a place of dark wonders and apathy. The ruins of impossible structures litter the landscape, but the domain’s jaded people ignore these marvels to focus on daily concerns.

The regions of Darkon are described below, and other notable locations are summarized on the [Darkon Locations table](#rthw:darkon:darkonlocations "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/darkon#darkonlocations").

### Regions of Darkon {#rthw:darkon:RegionsofDarkon}

The Shroud has divided Darkon into four parts (see “[Fractures of Darkon](#rthw:darkon:FracturesofDarkon "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/darkon#FracturesofDarkon")” for details):

**Jagged Coast.** Dense forests and shattered cliffs compose the [Jagged Coast](#rthw:darkon:jaggedcoast "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/darkon#jaggedcoast"), skirting the Sea of Souls. Undead within the forests prey on isolated communities here.

**Lychgate.** [Lychgate](#rthw:darkon:lychgate "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/darkon#lychgate") is ruled by the dead. Aimless undead creatures wander the forest, milling around amid the time-locked ruins of Castle Avernus and many of Azalin’s powerful servants.

**Mistlands.** Scattered communities dot the [Mistlands](#rthw:darkon:mistlands "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/darkon#mistlands"), which were once Darkon’s wild eastern reaches. Strange monsters emerge from the forests and mountains to prey on the isolated lands.

**Rexcrown.** The heart of Darkon, [Rexcrown](#rthw:darkon:rexcrown "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/darkon#rexcrown") has become a sagging bog. From it rise the spires and grim wonders of Il Aluk, Darkon’s capital, and the homes of the domain’s indifferent elite.

## Azalin Rex {#rthw:darkon:AzalinRex}

Darklord Who Won’t Be Caged

[![(Artist: Guilherme Motta)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/05-003.azalin-rex.jpg)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/05-003.azalin-rex.jpg)

> #### “It is customary to kneel before your dread lord.” {#rthw:darkon:azalinrex:Itiscustomarytokneelbeforeyourdreadlord}
>
> —Azalin Rex

In Darkon, Azalin was a tyrannical wizard-king obeyed by the living and the dead. When he first appeared before his people, he adopted an illusion of the form he possessed in life: that of a middle-aged human man with dark hair and a superior demeanor. However, his true form was that of a moldering lich, eyes ablaze with blasphemous energy.

Since arriving in the Domains of Dread, Azalin has been unable to learn new magic. For a wizard who forsook his mortality to pursue arcane studies, this was the ultimate frustration. Despite the limits on his studies, Azalin numbered among the few Darklords who understood the mysterious nature of the Domains of Dread. For generations, Azalin struggled to escape Darkon. His magical atrocities reshaped Darkon and the Domains of Dread time and again. However, these struggles gave Azalin only a glimpse of freedom, and his metaphysical violations inevitably reverted to the Dark Powers’ original designs. Nevertheless, Azalin refused to stay a prisoner. His most recent plot culminated in the Hour of Ascension and the destruction of [Castle Avernus](#rthw:darkon:castleavernus "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/darkon#castleavernus"). Since then, no one in Darkon has seen the Darklord, and his realm has begun deteriorating.

The stat block in this section presents the Darklord as he was prior to his disappearance and how he would be should he return. Azalin’s current spirit jar is a golden amulet he carries. If this amulet is destroyed, Azalin’s original spirit jar—an immovable dragon skull in the ruins of Castle Avernus—reactivates, and the lich’s spirit returns to Darkon if his body is destroyed.

#### Traits {#rthw:darkon:Traits}

**_Darklord Restoration._** If Azalin dies and his spirit jar remains intact, he revives with all his Hit Points in 2d10 days in the unoccupied space nearest his spirit jar. If Azalin’s spirit jar is destroyed, he instead revives in 4d10 days in Castle Avernus in Darkon.

**_Legendary Resistance (4/Day, or 5/Day in Domain)._** If Azalin fails a saving throw, he can choose to succeed instead.

#### Actions {#rthw:darkon:Actions}

**_Multiattack._** Azalin makes three attacks, using Eldritch Burst or Paralyzing Touch in any combination.

**_Eldritch Burst._** _Melee or Ranged Attack Roll:_ +12, reach 5 ft. or range 120 ft. _Hit:_ 31 (4d12 + 5) Force damage.

**_Paralyzing Touch._** _Melee Attack Roll:_ +12, reach 5 ft. _Hit:_ 15 (3d6 + 5) Cold damage, and the target has the [**Paralyzed**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#paralyzedcondition) condition until the start of Azalin’s next turn.

**_Spellcasting._** Azalin casts one of the following spells, requiring no spell components and using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 20):

**At Will:** [**Detect Magic**](#ref:spell:2619097-detect-magic "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619097-detect-magic") , [**Detect Thoughts**](#ref:spell:2619099-detect-thoughts "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619099-detect-thoughts"), [**Dispel Magic**](#ref:spell:2619103-dispel-magic "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619103-dispel-magic"), [**Invisibility**](#ref:spell:2619116-invisibility "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619116-invisibility"), [**Lightning Bolt**](#ref:spell:2618999-lightning-bolt "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618999-lightning-bolt") (level 5 version), [**Mage Hand**](#ref:spell:2619008-mage-hand "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619008-mage-hand"), [**Prestidigitation**](#ref:spell:2618893-prestidigitation "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618893-prestidigitation")

**2/Day Each:** [**Animate Dead**](#ref:spell:2618853-animate-dead "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618853-animate-dead"), [**Dimension Door**](#ref:spell:2619100-dimension-door "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619100-dimension-door"), [**Modify Memory**](#ref:spell:2619109-modify-memory "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619109-modify-memory"), [**Plane Shift**](#ref:spell:2618867-plane-shift "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618867-plane-shift"), [**Scrying**](#ref:spell:2619007-scrying "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619007-scrying")

**1/Day Each:** [**Chain Lightning**](#ref:spell:2618960-chain-lightning "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618960-chain-lightning"), [**Finger of Death**](#ref:spell:2618885-finger-of-death "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618885-finger-of-death"), [**Power Word Kill**](#ref:spell:2618886-power-word-kill "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618886-power-word-kill")

#### Reactions {#rthw:darkon:Reactions}

**_Siphon Spell._** Azalin casts [**Counterspell**](#ref:spell:2619072-counterspell "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619072-counterspell") in response to the spell’s trigger, using the same spellcasting ability as Spellcasting. If the target creature fails its saving throw against this _Counterspell_, Azalin steals knowledge of the triggering spell. For 1 hour or until Azalin takes this Reaction again, Azalin can cast that spell once, using the same spellcasting ability as Spellcasting.

#### Legendary Actions {#rthw:darkon:LegendaryActions}

Legendary Action Uses: 3 (4 in Domain). Immediately after another creature’s turn, Azalin can expend a use to take one of the following actions. Azalin regains all expended uses at the start of each of his turns.

**_Eldritch Teleport._** Azalin teleports up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space he can see and makes one Eldritch Burst or Paralyzing Touch attack.

**_Forbidden Knowledge._** _Intelligence Saving Throw:_ DC 20, up to three creatures Azalin can see within 60 feet. _Failure:_ 28 (8d6) Psychic damage, and the target has the [**Stunned**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#stunnedcondition) condition until the end of Azalin’s next turn. _Success:_ Half damage only. _Failure or Success:_ Azalin can’t take this action again until the start of his next turn.

### Azalin’s Tale {#rthw:darkon:AzalinsTale}

Firan Zal’honan was a noble and heir to the city-state of Knurl on the world of Oerth. A student of magic, Firan adopted the title “Azal’Lan,” meaning “wizard-king,” when he came to power. Firan’s rule was marked by harsh laws and violent expansion, but his people flourished, as their lives were filled with magical wonders.

As Firan aged, he looked toward his succession. His son, Irik, was generous and charming but, in Firan’s eyes, soft and unfit to rule. No matter how Firan tried to teach his son of the world’s harsh realities, Irik’s kind spirit wouldn’t bend to his father’s cynical outlook. This difference came to a head when Firan caught Irik freeing political prisoners. Firan could have ignored the crime or pardoned his son. Instead, Firan personally wielded the axe during Irik’s execution.

In the years that followed, Firan was tormented by his son’s death, but he also became convinced that only he was fit to rule. Researching the mysteries of death, he discovered the secret to becoming a lich. After embracing the transition into undeath, Firan ruled for decades more, increasing Knurl’s power and earning himself many foes. Eventually, tales of magic that might restore Irik lured Firan from his home. During his search, a band of mercenaries ambushed the ruler. Firan fled into the mist to avoid the assassins. When the mist cleared, Firan found himself in [Barovia](#rthw:barovia "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/barovia").

In Barovia, peasants Firan encountered mistook his title and called him Azalin. Soon, Azalin encountered Barovia’s ruler, [**Strahd von Zarovich**](#ref:monster:6491390-strahd-von-zarovich "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491390-strahd-von-zarovich"). The two came to respect each other, and Azalin taught Strahd much of the way of magic. Together, the pair learned a great deal about the nature of the Domains of Dread and made attempts to escape. Their plots failed, though, and resulted in other realms—such as the domain of [Mordent](#rthw:mordent "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/mordent")—being drawn into Barovia’s orbit. Eventually, the two tyrants’ respect soured into loathing. Before Azalin and Strahd could destroy each other, Azalin entered the Mists, and the domain of Darkon spread before him.

### Azalin’s Domain {#rthw:darkon:AzalinsDomain}

Darkon is altered by Azalin’s presence, creating the following effects:

**Closing the Borders.** While in his domain, Azalin can close or open the borders to Darkon at will. While the borders are closed, undead terrors fill the Mists surrounding Darkon. Whenever a creature enters the Mists, one [**Hostile**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#hostileattitude) [**Zombie Clot**](#ref:monster:6491405-zombie-clot "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491405-zombie-clot") (see [chapter 5](#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:zombieclot "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/denizens-of-the-mists#zombieclot")) appears in a random unoccupied space within 30 feet of that creature.

**Lord of the Dead.** While in his domain, Azalin can cast [**Clairvoyance**](#ref:spell:2618972-clairvoyance "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618972-clairvoyance"), requiring no spell components and using the same spellcasting ability as his Spellcasting action. When Azalin casts this spell in this way, he can place the sensor in any Undead in Darkon with an Intelligence of 6 or less, even if it is beyond 1 mile of Azalin. In addition, Azalin can speak through the Undead he placed the sensor in.

**No Secrets.** Whenever a creature in Darkon casts a spell using a level 5+ spell slot, Azalin becomes aware of that creature’s name and location. A [**Nondetection**](#ref:spell:2619122-nondetection "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619122-nondetection") spell blocks this effect.

If Azalin dies, these effects end immediately.

### Azalin’s Lair {#rthw:darkon:AzalinsLair}

During the Hour of Ascension, Castle Avernus—Azalin’s seat of rule and magical laboratory—erupted in a magical conflagration. Now, Castle Avernus stands frozen in time at the instant of its destruction, blasted to magically floating chunks of rubble. Its towers pitch wildly and crumble to pieces amid arcane flames, yet they don’t fall. Although time has halted in the ruins, Azalin’s servants who avoided the disaster have returned, unaffected by the castle’s frozen time. Meanwhile, the fortress’s magic attempts to heal the wreckage, slowly creating new halls and winding stairs between the fractured floors.

#### Castle Avernus {#rthw:darkon:CastleAvernus}

Amid its magical destruction, Castle Avernus is a vast structure filled with Azalin’s arcane creations and summoned servants. Prominent locations from this ruin are depicted on [map 2.7](#rthw:darkon:map207castleavernus "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/darkon#map207castleavernus") and detailed here:

**Outer Bailey and Gallery.** The castle’s entry, called the Maw by Azalin’s servants, remains partially intact. Undead from the surrounding wilds lurk here, waiting for their lord’s commands.

**Hall of Records.** A column of stationary but still deadly magical fire blasts through Avernus’s library. Scattered on ruined islands of rubble are the remains of a collection said to hold the biographies of all who have died in Darkon.

**Tomb of Irik Zal’honan.** Here stands the tomb of Azalin’s son, Irik. The [**Ghost**](#ref:monster:5195008-ghost "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195008-ghost") of Irik appears to those with benevolent intentions. Despite his tragic fate, he forgives his father—but he doesn’t want Azalin to harm anyone else. He can’t leave the crypt and knows little of Azalin’s plots.

**Lair of Ebbasheyth.** The [**Shadow Dragon**](#ref:monster:5195201-shadow-dragon-huge "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195201-shadow-dragon-huge") Ebbasheyth served as Azalin’s adviser and steed. While she has moved much of her hoard to Mount Nyid, she still watches over the treasures here.

**Hall of Life.** The Hall of Life has largely crumbled and is accessible only via gaps in the ceiling of the floor below. Within survives a circle of glass and emerald cylinders. These hold the remains of Azalin’s magical cloning experiments. A gigantic dragon skull made of gold has fallen into the midst of these failed experiments. This is Azalin’s original spirit jar, but the skull’s eyes, which once glowed with unholy flames, now look empty.

**Heart of Avernus.** Amid the tower’s wreckage glows the magical anomaly called the Heart of Avernus. This is the epicenter of the disaster that destroyed the castle during the Hour of Ascension. This mysterious force draws droves of the undead to feed on the ongoing magical reaction.

## Fractures of Darkon {#rthw:darkon:FracturesofDarkon}

The domain of Darkon has fractured into four regions: the Jagged Coast, [Lychgate](#rthw:darkon:lychgate "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/darkon#lychgate"), the [Mistlands](#rthw:darkon:mistlands "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/darkon#mistlands"), and [Rexcrown](#rthw:darkon:rexcrown "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/darkon#rexcrown"). In Azalin’s absence, ambitious villains unleash terrors as they strive to dominate their piece of the domain. This section explores the horrors unfolding in each region of Darkon.

### Jagged Coast {#rthw:darkon:JaggedCoast}

Stark vistas of sheer cliffs, mysterious islands, and knotted forests bleed from one to the next along the Jagged Coast. The shadow of Castle Avernus once loomed over the southern part of the region, enforcing grim peace on the small communities there. In the north, the thriving city of Martira Bay prides itself on its inhabitants’ wealth and reason.

Since Azalin’s disappearance, the Darklord’s secret police have maintained order here—obeying not the commands of the missing king, but rather the will of their regional leader, Alcio Metus.

[![The Treacherous Harbor of Martira Bay (Artist: Titus Lunter)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/05-004.martira-bay.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/05-004.martira-bay.png)

#### Kargat {#rthw:darkon:Kargat}

Azalin’s secret police, the Kargat, has long enforced the Darklord’s edicts and smothered any ember of rebellion in Darkon. Those “disappeared” by the Kargat are never seen again.

While all Darkon fears these dark-cloaked spies, few realize the Kargat is largely composed of vampires and other shape-shifting creatures. Members operate in cells assigned to particular tasks or locations, with each reporting to a regional leader. The highest-ranking members reported to Azalin. Serving the Kargat are the Kargatane, a cultlike rank of living informants and initiates who spy on their neighbors in hopes of earning supernatural power and induction into the larger organization.

The Hour of Ascension threw the Kargat into disorder. Taking advantage of this opportunity, Alcio Metus (Medium, Neutral Evil [**Vampire**](#ref:monster:5195251-vampire "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195251-vampire")), a Kargat leader and criminal kingpin in Martira Bay, slew her peers and took over the western branch of the group. From the Black Tower in Martira Bay, Alcio spreads her Kargat spies across region and beyond.

#### Martira Bay {#rthw:darkon:MartiraBay}

A foggy port on the Sea of Souls, Martira Bay is a cosmopolitan hub of trade and ideas. The populace prides itself on its worldliness and believes that the best of Darkon and lands beyond passes through the city. Martira Bay’s people appreciate reason and tangibility, and many have never left the city. This makes many residents incredulous of magic and the supernatural, even as séances and spiritualist practices flourish in posh salons.

Martira Bay is infamous for sensationalist murders. Newspapers such as _The Bullseye_ update their devoted readership on the grisly details of sprees committed by killers such as the Midnight Slasher, the Spider, and the Weeping Woman. The overwhelmed Martira Bay constabulary works to counter these killers, as do professional detective agencies including the Ray Detectives (founded by Alanik Ray; see [chapter 3](#rthw:ravenloft-adventures:alanikray "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/ravenloft-adventures#alanikray")) and the Dusklight Detectives.

[![Map 2.6: Martira Bay View Player Version (Artist: Jared Blando)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/map-05-02.martira-bay.jpg)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/map-05-02.martira-bay.jpg)

### Lychgate {#rthw:darkon:Lychgate}

Lychgate hides the magically shattered remains of Castle Avernus. Whatever ongoing magical disaster befell the castle during the Hour of Ascension has locked its ruins in time, freezing it in a semiexploded state. While Castle Avernus remains the lair of some of Azalin’s most dangerous servants, the surrounding wilderness has become overrun by shuffling corpses and mournful spirits drawn to the castle’s strange magic. The region is ruled by Ebbasheyth, Azalin’s [**Shadow Dragon**](#ref:monster:5195201-shadow-dragon-huge "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195201-shadow-dragon-huge") ally who maintains a lair in Castle Avernus.

Adventures in Lychgate likely relate to the mystery of Azalin’s disappearance. Roll on or choose a result from the Doom in Lychgate table to inspire adventures in this ruined realm.

**Doom in Lychgate**

| 1d6 | In Lychgate, Adventurers Might Seek …                                          |
| --- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| 1   | Azalin’s spirit jar or other magical treasure.                                 |
| 2   | The corpse of an ally whose body rose as a zombie and wandered into the Mists. |
| 3   | A Darklord’s treasure held in Avernus.                                         |
| 4   | Details of Azalin’s fate.                                                      |
| 5   | Duplicates of Azalin, an ally, or themselves.                                  |
| 6   | A passage to the King’s Tear.                                                  |

### Mistlands {#rthw:darkon:Mistlands}

Even before the Hour of Ascension, western Darkon was a land of magical mysteries and strange creatures. No longer fearing the Darklord’s magic, ancient evils have crept from the shadows to terrorize and control the scattered communities.

In the town of Nevuchar Springs, an elf mystic and leader of the Eternal Order, Cardinna Artazas, works to turn back the Shroud. To do this, she sought to resurrect a being bonded to the land and capable of bending the Mists to its will. This resulted in the corruption of her order’s sacred pools and unleashed Darcalus Rex, a [**Necrichor**](#ref:monster:6491378-necrichor "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491378-necrichor") (see [chapter 5](#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:necrichor "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/denizens-of-the-mists#necrichor")) that claims to be the first king of Darkon. Uncertain of what it has unleashed but desperate for salvation, the Eternal Order serves the whims of Darcalus Rex as the strange being grows in power.

#### Rexcrown {#rthw:darkon:Rexcrown}

Residents of Rexcrown consider themselves the only true Darkonians due to their proximity to the capital, Il Aluk. Despite that prestige, Rexcrown is covered in deadly swamps, depleted mountains, and fields that produce disturbingly malformed crops.

The city of Il Aluk is built in a bend in the Vuchar River and rises in countless gothic spires. These mark the homes of the city’s elite, severe governmental buildings, and temples dedicated to dozens of grim deities. Serving the city are the vassal villages of Decimus, Desolatus, and Despondia, where peasants struggle to feed the city’s people and the decadent lifestyles of local nobles.

As the Shroud spreads fear among traders, Il Aluk suffers from shortages in food and other supplies. The city’s residents have grown desperate and resentful of the exploitative upper class. This has resulted in violence and the ransacking of wealthy homes. The city’s elite have rallied behind one of their eldest members, Lady Talisveri Eris.

Eris is a vain human who uses elaborate fashions and makeup to disguise the fact that her body is permanently imperceptible. Once each moon, she incites her fearful peers to go out at night and commit violence while using her high-priced [**Potions of Greater Invisibility**](#ref:magic_item:9228934-potion-of-greater-invisibility "https://www.dndbeyond.com/magic-items/9228934-potion-of-greater-invisibility"). These magical attacks and Eris’s pompous, detached rhetoric exacerbate tensions in the city while enriching her nearly bankrupt family.

## Adventures in Darkon {#rthw:darkon:AdventuresinDarkon}

Adventures set in Darkon’s disconnected regions often involve the mystery of Azalin’s disappearance, the domain’s dissolution, or the metaphysical nature of the Domains of Dread. Use this section to develop horror adventures in this domain.

### Horror in Darkon {#rthw:darkon:HorrorinDarkon}

Beyond the adventures you might develop in Darkon’s disconnected regions, the following elements persist across the domain.

#### Azalin’s Fate {#rthw:darkon:AzalinsFate}

The events of the Hour of Ascension and the fate of Azalin loom over adventures in Darkon. The details of these mysteries are yours to decide. You can take inspiration from the following possibilities when determining Azalin’s fate.

**_Severed Darklord._** During the Hour of Ascension, Azalin’s body was destroyed as he tore open portals to the Negative and Positive Energy Planes. The former portal lies at the heart of Castle Avernus, while the latter is known as the King’s Tear. The opposed planar energies are disrupting Darkon. Once the domain is destroyed, Azalin theorizes, his spirit jar will be released into the Shadowfell.

**_Shattered Darklord._** The Hour of Ascension was Azalin’s failed attempt to become one of the Dark Powers. His essence is now trapped within his spirit jar, scattered pieces of his iron crown, and the floating amber sarcophagus known as the King’s Tear. Whoever frees Azalin’s essence will become the new Darklord.

**_Unmoored Darklord._** During the Hour of Ascension, Azalin split his soul, leaving a piece in Darkon while the greater part escaped through a metaphysical rent between domains—the King’s Tear. Now, disguised as the scholar Firan Zal’honan, Azalin searches for secrets of the Dark Powers in other domains. He avoids entering the Mists without Mist-wandering guides, fearing the Dark Powers will find him otherwise.

#### The Dead Serve {#rthw:darkon:TheDeadServe}

In Darkon, Humanoid corpses reanimate as [**Zombies**](#ref:monster:4775851-zombie "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/4775851-zombie") 24 hours after death. These corpses obey Azalin. While he remains missing, they roam in a winding path toward Castle Avernus. These zombies avoid other creatures, but they fight anything that blocks their path.

#### The Shroud {#rthw:darkon:TheShroud}

During the day, one can traverse the Mists surrounding Darkon as normal, allowing travel between domains or regions of Darkon. At night, the Mists surrounding the domain turn deadly and encroach on the land—sometimes by infinitesimal degrees, other times in unstoppable floods. A creature that touches the Shroud takes 7 (2d6) Necrotic damage and is [**Frightened**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#frightenedcondition) until the end of its next turn. If a creature is slain by the Shroud or enters it entirely, the creature vanishes. What becomes of it is a mystery.

### Darkon Campaign Arc {#rthw:darkon:DarkonCampaignArc}

Campaigns set in Darkon likely involve the mystery of the Hour of Ascension. A campaign here might follow this outline:

**Levels 1–3.** The characters arrive in Darkon near Il Aluk, Martira Bay, or Nevuchar Springs. They soon make an ally among those who oppose the villains rising to replace Azalin: Alcio Metus, Darcalus Rex, or Talisveri Eris. The characters help defend their allies and learn of these villains’ methods.

**Levels 4–15.** The characters confront the region’s villain. Rather than fighting the characters, the villain entreats the group to help them establish control over the domain, which they believe will reunite Darkon’s regions and end the threat of the Shroud. To do so, they must defeat the domain’s other villains or recover the scattered remnants of Azalin’s power. The characters work to save Darkon while undermining their wicked patron.

**Levels 16–18.** The characters’ adventures take them to Castle Avernus, where they must either claim a remnant of Azalin’s might or learn his fate. In doing so, they can restore Azalin and bring his wrath down on those who would claim his throne.

### Secrets of Avernus {#rthw:darkon:SecretsofAvernus}

Adventure for Level 16 Characters

**Situation.** The characters must learn the secret of Azalin’s disappearance.

**Hook.** The threat of the Shroud and those who would claim Azalin’s throne has grown too great to ignore. An ally directs the characters to the only place they can find answers regarding Azalin’s disappearance: Castle Avernus.

[![Map 2.7: Castle Avernus View Player Version (Artist: Mike Schley)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/map-05-03.castle-avernus-prominent-ruins.jpg)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/map-05-03.castle-avernus-prominent-ruins.jpg)

#### Encounters {#rthw:darkon:Encounters}

This adventure uses map 2.7: Castle Avernus. Before starting, consult the “[Azalin’s Fate](#rthw:darkon:azalinsfate "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/darkon#azalinsfate")” section and develop the details behind the Darklord’s disappearance. The floors of Castle Avernus are disconnected, allowing characters to access them in any order.

**_Lychgate Encounters._** While traveling through Lychgate or between floors of Castle Avernus, roll on the following table to determine what the characters encounter.

| 1d4 | Encounter                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| --- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1   | Two scavenging [**Arcanaloths**](#ref:monster:5194899-arcanaloth "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5194899-arcanaloth")                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| 2   | Two [**Dullahans**](#ref:monster:6491351-dullahan "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491351-dullahan") (see [chapter 5](#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:dullahan "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/denizens-of-the-mists#dullahan")) and two [**Nightmares**](#ref:monster:5195143-nightmare "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195143-nightmare") |
| 3   | Two [**Haunting Revenants**](#ref:monster:5195070-haunting-revenant "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195070-haunting-revenant") disguised as rubble                                                                                                                                                               |
| 4   | Two [**Relentless Juggernauts**](#ref:monster:6491383-relentless-juggernaut "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491383-relentless-juggernaut") (see [chapter 5](#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:relentlessjuggernaut "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/denizens-of-the-mists#relentlessjuggernaut"))                                                              |

**_Into the Maw._** Droves of animate corpses fill the outer bailey. A [**Spirit Naga**](#ref:monster:5195215-spirit-naga "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195215-spirit-naga") named Lossa lurks amid the rubble. If she spots the characters, she impersonates Azalin and commands the corpses to fight. They rise as three [**Zombie Clots**](#ref:monster:6491405-zombie-clot "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491405-zombie-clot") (see [chapter 5](#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:zombieclot "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/denizens-of-the-mists#zombieclot")).

**_The Archive._** Elzarath, an [**Indifferent**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#indifferentattitude) [**Ghost**](#ref:monster:5195008-ghost "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195008-ghost") with a floating severed head, laments the state of the archives. Elzarath shares that they once held the biographies of all who died in Darkon, but now the books are scattered. If asked about Azalin’s biography, the ghost searches and finds nothing. Elzarath doesn’t know Azalin’s actual name, but if specifically asked about the biography of Firan Zal’honan, the ghost finds the book. This biography relates the information in the “[Azalin’s Tale](#rthw:darkon:azalinstale "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/darkon#azalinstale")” section and key details of the Hour of Ascension.

**_Crypt of Irik Zal’honan._** The [**Ghost**](#ref:monster:5195008-ghost "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195008-ghost") Irik Zal’honan appears to any Good-aligned creature or those who call out to him. Irik can’t leave this area, but he aids those who seek to restore his father. He knows Azalin’s true name is Firan Zal’honan and shares that with anyone who destroys the corrupted experiment in the Hall of Life in the ruins above. Irik reveals that he is Azalin’s son only if asked directly.

**_Hall of Life._** This room holds a dragon skull made of gold and a circle of glass and emerald cylinders. The dragon skull remains magically anchored so only Azalin can move it. The cylinders are cracked and filled with bubbling decay. If someone smashes all the cylinders, the cylinders fuse into a Hostile abomination with the same stat block as a [**Lesser Star Spawn Emissary**](#ref:monster:6491369-lesser-star-spawn-emissary "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491369-lesser-star-spawn-emissary") (see [chapter 5](#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:lesserstarspawnemissary "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/denizens-of-the-mists#lesserstarspawnemissary")).

**_Ebbasheyth’s Lair._** Ebbasheyth the [**Shadow Dragon**](#ref:monster:5195201-shadow-dragon-huge "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195201-shadow-dragon-huge") is in her lair, attended by a Kargat messenger (Medium [**Vampire Nightbringer**](#ref:monster:5195248-vampire-nightbringer "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195248-vampire-nightbringer")). The monsters are [**Hostile**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#hostileattitude), but any character who takes an [**Influence**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#influenceaction) action and succeeds on a DC 16 Charisma ([**Persuasion**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#skills)) check can make them [**Indifferent**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#indifferentattitude). Characters who mention their desire to restore Azalin have [**Advantage**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#advantage) on this check. If made Indifferent, Ebbasheyth tells the characters the archives might hold details of Azalin’s schemes. If asked what name to search for, she doesn’t know but relates that the spirit in the room below might.

**_Conclusion._** The biography of Firan Zal’honan in the archive reveals the secret of Azalin’s disappearance. From this, the characters should know how to find or restore Azalin or how to recover his power. Each character also earns a bonus 9,800 XP.

</CHAPTER>

# Dementlieu {#rthw:dementlieu:Dementlieu}

Domain of Decadent Delusion

> #### **Darklord:** [Saidra d’Honaire](#rthw:dementlieu:SaidradHonaire "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/dementlieu#SaidradHonaire") {#rthw:dementlieu:SaidradHonaire}
>
> **Genres:** [Dark fantasy](#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:darkfantasy "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/creating-domains-of-dread#darkfantasy") and [psychological horror](#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:psychologicalhorror "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/creating-domains-of-dread#psychologicalhorror")
>
> **Hallmarks:** Masquerades, decadent aristocracy, social decay, illusions, impostor syndrome
>
> **Mist Talismans:** Jeweled or feathered mask, article of well-worn fine clothing, shoe made of glass or gold
>
> **Aligned Tarokka Card:** Charlatan
>
> **Opposed Tarokka Card:** Seer

[![(Artist: Pam Wishbow)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/06-001.charlatan-tarokka.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/06-001.charlatan-tarokka.png) [![](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/06-002.seer-tarokka.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/06-002.seer-tarokka.png)

Composed of the city of Port-a-Lucine and its shining, fog-shrouded outskirts, Dementlieu is a realm where the truth is smothered by collective delusion. Everything in Port-a-Lucine appears to be more than it is, and people behave as if the few examples of grandeur and prosperity were the norm. Beneath its facade, the city is rotten.

Despite pervasive claims of happiness and success, the people of Dementlieu fight to survive and maintain social appearances. Every individual struggles to hide their struggles. Lying is central to life in the domain, creating a breeding ground for con artists and smiling villains.

Behind the domain’s denial of reality is its Darklord, the phantomlike [**Duchess Saidra d’Honaire**](#ref:monster:6491387-saidra-dhonaire "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491387-saidra-dhonaire"). The cynosure of high society, this masked duchess ensnares the city’s upper class in her exaggerated ideas of luxury and civility. During her weekly masquerade balls, Saidra’s guests must perform to her expectations. Those who fail to charm her are decried as impostors and reduced to ash by her magic. Saidra’s terror also grips the city’s desperate. Her murderous, unmasked form—the Red Death—stalks the benighted streets, preying on any who tarnish her preposterous vision of a perfect society.

## Domain Features {#rthw:dementlieu:DomainFeatures}

Dementlieu is known for the following features:

**City of Lies.** Nothing in Port-a-Lucine is as it appears. Everyone pretends to be more successful than they are. Lies great and small fill everyday communication. All residents know these truths, but none dares speak of them.

**Grand Masquerade.** Every week [Duchess d’Honaire](#rthw:dementlieu:SaidradHonaire "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/dementlieu#SaidradHonaire") holds a Grand Masquerade. Invitations are coveted, and invitees who don’t attend rarely survive for long.

**Lord Governor.** Administration of Port-a-Lucine rests in the hands of Lord Governor Marcel Guignol. He is counseled by aristocratic advisers, including the duchess.

**Masks.** Decorative masks are common accessories, worn at social events and in daily life.

## Locations in Dementlieu {#rthw:dementlieu:LocationsinDementlieu}

Port-a-Lucine’s grand structures and garish promenades dazzle viewers, distracting most from the grimy streets and cramped homes beyond. The countryside of Chateaufaux is described below, and other notable locations are summarized on the [Dementlieu Locations table](#rthw:dementlieu:dementlieulocations "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/dementlieu#dementlieulocations").

### Chateaufaux {#rthw:dementlieu:Chateaufaux}

The people of Port-a-Lucine speak of the countryside, Chateaufaux, where nobles summer at their estates and where idyllic villages send goods for sale into the city. But no one travels far beyond the city walls, no goods arrive from beyond, and Chateaufaux doesn’t actually exist. The Mists creep close to Port-a-Lucine, occasionally exposing patches of forests and meadows but nothing more. Nevertheless, Chateaufaux remains a convenient explanation for whatever mysteriously appears or disappears.

[![Map 2.8: Dementlieu View Player Version (Artist: Francesca Baerald)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/map-06-01.dementlieu.jpg)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/map-06-01.dementlieu.jpg)

**Dementlieu Locations**

| Location                     | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Bonniville Museum of the Sea | Green windows tint this museum’s collection of aquatic oddities and preserved sea creatures in drowned light. A display of the wolfish masthead of the _S.S. Bonniville_ is said to be cursed.                                                                                        |
| D’Honaire Estate             | The home of [**Saidra d’Honaire**](#ref:monster:6491387-saidra-dhonaire "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491387-saidra-dhonaire") and the site of her Grand Masquerades is accessible only by the nobles’ stylish gondolas or larger ships (see “[Saidra’s Lair](#rthw:dementlieu:saidraslair "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/dementlieu#saidraslair")”). |

A few rare tomes hide among the unremarkable copies.                                                                                                          |

In the basements, those who’ve been replaced by lifelike wax constructs remain imprisoned.                                                                                                            |

The staff maintains only a portion of the estate, as the rest is said to be haunted by the city’s former rulers.                                                                                                 |

The hags fulfill their guests’ dreams, but their contracts always have a hidden catch.                   |

Some true scholars conduct actual research hidden from their clout-chasing peers.                                                                                                 |

Dr. Doloros Zuvich recognizes that some of her patients’ accounts describe encounters with supernatural beings.                                                                                                           |
