## Saidra d’Honaire {#rthw:dementlieu:SaidradHonaire}

Darklord Who Rules Illusions

[![(Artist: Lenka Šimečková)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/06-003.saidra-dhonaire.jpg)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/06-003.saidra-dhonaire.jpg)

> “Welcome, treasured guests—you bright jewels in my city’s sterling crown. Bask in all you’ve earned and deserve. Oh… that’s not a loose button, is it?”
>
> —Saidra d’Honaire

Duchess Saidra d’Honaire knows her life isn’t her own—she knows she isn’t alive at all—yet she ignores that for the sparkle of empty celebrations and a parody of her ideal life. The duchess terrorizes Dementlieu, forcing the realm to conform to her desires. Those who expose the flaws in her fantasy and remind her of the desperation she once endured, she slays using her life-sapping power.

All can plainly see Duchess d’Honaire isn’t one of the living. Nevertheless, servants and sycophants flatter her poise, beauty, and array of lavish masquerade costumes. When not hosting decadent social events, Saidra removes her mask and slips into the night. Through the streets and alleys of Port-a-Lucine, the Darklord prowls as the Red Death: a murderous spirit that preys on liars, the struggling, and all who remind her of her humble origins.

Saidra is overbearing and elitist, despite being unworldly. She fears being exposed as a fraud and projects this fear onto others, violently accusing them of being liars on the barest evidence or sign of vulgarity. Yet, in mysterious letters and rumors, Saidra receives evidence that her own simple, spiteful family dwells somewhere beyond her city. Their confessions could bring all her deceptions to light.

### [Saidra d’Honaire](#ref:monster:6491387-saidra-dhonaire "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491387-saidra-dhonaire") {#rthw:dementlieu:SaidradHonairerefmonster6491387saidradhonairehttpswwwdndbeyondcommonsters6491387saidradhonaire}

Medium Undead, Neutral Evil

**AC** 13 **Initiative** +11 (21)

**HP** 90 (12d8 + 36)

**Speed** 5 ft., Fly 60 ft. (hover)

|     |     | Mod | Save |
| --- | --- | --- | ---- |
| STR | 6   | \-2 | \-2  |
| DEX | 17  | +3  | +7   |
| CON | 16  | +3  | +3   |

|     |     | Mod | Save |
| --- | --- | --- | ---- |
| INT | 12  | +1  | +1   |
| WIS | 14  | +2  | +6   |
| CHA | 17  | +3  | +3   |

**Skills** [**Insight**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#skills) +10, [**Perception**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#skills) +6, [**Performance**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#skills) +7, [**Stealth**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#skills) +7

**Resistances** Acid, Bludgeoning, Cold, Fire, Piercing, Slashing

**Immunities** Necrotic, Poison; [**Charmed**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#charmedcondition), [**Exhaustion**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#exhaustioncondition), [**Grappled**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#grappledcondition), [**Paralyzed**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#paralyzedcondition), [**Petrified**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#petrifiedcondition), [**Poisoned**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#poisonedcondition), [**Prone**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#pronecondition), [**Restrained**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#restrainedcondition), [**Unconscious**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#unconsciouscondition)

**Senses** [**Darkvision**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#darkvision) 60 ft.; Passive Perception 16

**Languages** Common

**Challenge** 9 (XP 5,000, or 5,900 in domain; PB +4)

#### Traits {#rthw:dementlieu:Traits}

**_Darklord Restoration._** If Saidra dies, she revives with all her Hit Points in 1d10 weeks somewhere in Dementlieu.

**_Incorporeal Movement._** Saidra can move through other creatures and objects as if they were [**Difficult Terrain**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#difficultterrain). She takes 5 (1d10) Force damage if she ends her turn inside an object.

**_Lie Detector._** Saidra knows whether she hears a lie.

**_Legendary Resistance (3/Day, or 4/Day in Domain)._** If Saidra fails a saving throw, she can choose to succeed instead.

**_Sunlight Sensitivity._** While in sunlight, Saidra has [**Disadvantage**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#disadvantage) on ability checks and attack rolls.

#### Actions {#rthw:dementlieu:Actions}

**_Multiattack._** Saidra makes three Necrotic Burst attacks. She can replace one of these attacks with a use of Spellcasting.

**_Necrotic Burst._** _Melee Attack Roll:_ +7, reach 5 ft. or range 30 ft. _Hit:_ 14 (2d10 + 3) Necrotic damage.

**_Life Drain._** _Constitution Saving Throw:_ DC 15, one creature Saidra can see within 30 feet. _Failure:_ 28 (8d6) Necrotic damage, and its Hit Point maximum decreases by an amount equal to the damage taken. _Success:_ Half damage only.

**_Truth or Die (1/Day)._** Saidra asks a creature she can see within 60 feet to identify itself and casts [**Disintegrate**](#ref:spell:2619094-disintegrate "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619094-disintegrate") targeting the creature, requiring no Material components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (DC 15, with [**Disadvantage**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#disadvantage) if the target lies).

**_Spellcasting._** Saidra casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 15):

**At Will:** [**Charm Person**](#ref:spell:2618964-charm-person "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618964-charm-person") (duchess form only), [**Fear**](#ref:spell:2618872-fear "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618872-fear") (Red Death form only).

#### Bonus Actions {#rthw:dementlieu:BonusActions}

**_Shape-Shift._** Saidra [**shape-shifts**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#shapeshifting) into the Red Death, or she returns to her true form as the duchess. Her game statistics are the same in each form. Any equipment she is wearing or carrying isn’t transformed.

#### Legendary Actions {#rthw:dementlieu:LegendaryActions}

Legendary Action Uses: 3 (4 in Domain). Immediately after another creature’s turn, Saidra can expend a use to take one of the following actions. Saidra regains all expended uses at the start of each of her turns.

**_Lash Out._** Saidra makes one Necrotic Burst attack.

**_Shadow Veil._** Saidra gives herself the [**Invisible**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#invisiblecondition) condition until the start of her next turn and can fly up to half her Fly Speed. The condition ends early immediately after Saidra deals damage. Saidra can’t take this action again until the start of her next turn.

### Saidra’s Tale {#rthw:dementlieu:SaidrasTale}

Despite being raised in poverty, Saidra d’Honaire was an arrogant bully whose father led her to believe she was secretly royalty. When her father remarried, Saidra suffered slights and mockery at the hands of her callous stepmother and stepsisters.

The night her father revealed that Saidra was only distantly related to nobility, she fled into the night. At her mother’s grave, Saidra’s curses were overheard by a mysterious stranger. This grandmotherly figure offered to grant Saidra any wish. When the stranger heard Saidra’s desire, she cackled and dressed the girl in rubies and a crimson gown. Resplendent, Saidra set off to the masquerade ball celebrating the coronation of the land’s new duke.

At the masquerade, Saidra charmed the duke and his court. Yet, as bells tolled midnight, the gems on her dress evaporated, releasing a magical poison. The evil magic killed everyone at the masquerade, a massacre that would have fulfilled Saidra’s murderous wish and left her within reach of the throne. As Saidra toured a palace full of the dying, clouds of spreading poison rose in a mysterious mist.

When the mist cleared, Saidra found herself in a grand estate in Port-a-Lucine. The estate’s servants acknowledged her as their duchess, but the lethal poison had dissolved Saidra’s body into a deathly vapor. As none seemed to notice, Saidra embraced the fantasy that she had achieved her vain desires.

### Saidra’s Domain {#rthw:dementlieu:SaidrasDomain}

Dementlieu is altered by Saidra’s presence, creating the following effects:

**Closing the Borders.** While in her domain, Saidra can close or open the borders to Dementlieu at will. While the borders are closed, the countryside called Chateaufaux appears in the Mists surrounding Dementlieu. Creatures in the Mists get lost amid mazelike hedgerows and fogbanks, only to reappear on the outskirts of Port-a-Lucine 2d6 hours later.

**Empowered Actors.** Humanoids add 1d8 to Charisma ([**Deception**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#skills) or [**Performance**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#skills)) checks made while wearing a mask.

**Invitation.** At dawn, Saidra can choose a creature whose name she knows or that she’s seen before. A simple mask and an invitation to the next Grand Masquerade appear to that creature. The letter and mask appear in an unobserved but obvious space, such as a bedside table or among gear.

If [Saidra](#rthw:dementlieu:saidradhonairestatblock "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/dementlieu#saidradhonairestatblock") dies, these effects end immediately. The effects resume if Saidra gains a new body (see her Darklord Restoration trait).

### Saidra’s Lair {#rthw:dementlieu:SaidrasLair}

The duchess dwells at the d’Honaire Estate. This lavish manor and its manicured grounds cover the largest island in Lucine Bay.

#### D’Honaire Estate {#rthw:dementlieu:DHonaireEstate}

The d’Honaire Estate is well lit and filled with expensive decor and artwork—some of it quite good, but most is of middling quality. The estate is depicted on [map 2.9](#rthw:dementlieu:map209dhonaireestate "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/dementlieu#map209dhonaireestate") and has the following features:

**Grand Entry.** A grand staircase sweeps from the estate’s entry to airy balconies above. This broad space also serves as a ballroom and is the focus of the duchess’s social events.

**Salons.** Elegant rooms with distinct themes fill the estate. Popular spaces include the Skobeloff Salon (themed like a sunken ship), the Sulfur Salon (with dizzying wallpaper), and the Taupe Salon (filled with underwhelming taxidermies).

**Sea Caves and Docks.** Those who travel to the island estate by gondola dock in this sculpted sea cave. Stairs rise from the docks to the main estate.

**Second Floor.** The halls remain locked and guarded. Within are the duchess’s quarters, a joyless, hollow space that the Darklord haunts between stalkings and social events.

## Adventures in Dementlieu {#rthw:dementlieu:AdventuresinDementlieu}

Adventures set in Dementlieu feature mystery and deception, often involving illusions and fairy-tale grandeur masking depravity and murder. Use this section to develop horror adventures in this domain.

[![The desperate elite of Port-a-Lucine gather at Duchess d’Honaire’s island estate for the Grand Masquerade (Artist: Sylvain Sarrailh)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/06-004.port-a-lucine.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/06-004.port-a-lucine.png)

### Horror in Dementlieu {#rthw:dementlieu:HorrorinDementlieu}

Adventures in Dementlieu often include the following elements.

#### Lies and Liars {#rthw:dementlieu:LiesandLiars}

In Dementlieu, one can take little at face value. Terrible food might be called gourmet, while horrendous art might be dubbed avant garde. Those who resist such claims might find themselves mocked for not understanding a thing’s appeal. This can lead to challenges that range from the comical to the surreal. Roll on or choose a result from the Dementlieu Deceptions table to inspire overlooked events that might lead to broader consequences.

**Dementlieu Deceptions**

| 1d6 | A Dementlieuse Liar …                                                                        |
| --- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1   | Claims to personally know Duchess d’Honaire and so deserve special treatment.                |
| 2   | Insists they’re investing all their resources in solving a problem they’re clearly ignoring. |
| 3   | Is publicly trapped or wounded but claims to passersby that they’re fine.                    |
| 4   | Passes off their rat-meat pies and gutter-water wine as food fads.                           |
| 5   | Poses as an expert, but their advice is ludicrous or dangerous nonsense.                     |
| 6   | Says their stolen wares come from Chateaufaux.                                               |

#### Scourge of the Red Death {#rthw:dementlieu:ScourgeoftheRedDeath}

Between masquerades, Saidra d’Honaire fixates on her past and her fear that people suspect her ignoble origins. At these times, her glamorous facade fades, reducing her to a crimson spirit. In this guise, she slips into the night and scours Port-a-Lucine, targeting the sick, poor, or uncouth; those who disparage nobles; and those she suspects of investigating her past. The resulting life-drained bodies are attributed to a notorious figure locals call the Red Death.

**_Using the Red Death._** While Port-a-Lucine’s residents ignore the Red Death’s victims—potentially chiding corpses for their laziness or public drunkenness—the characters are unlikely to overlook bodies so clearly drained of life. Use such corpses to remind the group that the lies of Dementlieu’s people are dangerous denials of reality.

### Dementlieu Campaign Arc {#rthw:dementlieu:DementlieuCampaignArc}

Campaigns set in Dementlieu often involve the discovery and unraveling of a conspiracy. A campaign here might follow this outline:

**Levels 1–3.** Someone asks the characters in Port-a-Lucine for help finding a missing friend, opera performer, or noble. Following the clues, the characters learn this is but one of a rash of disappearances involving dangerous creatures hiding in plain sight—such as [**Gargoyles**](#ref:monster:5195003-gargoyle "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195003-gargoyle"), [**Wererats**](#ref:monster:5195265-wererat "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195265-wererat"), or [**Waxworks**](#ref:monster:6491401-waxwork "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491401-waxwork") (see [chapter 5](#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:waxwork "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/denizens-of-the-mists#waxwork")).

**Level 4–5.** The mystery points toward an elite member of society. The characters can’t gain access to this individual, but they know the noble attends the Grand Masquerade of Duchess d’Honaire. The characters must prepare for and infiltrate the event (detailed below) to learn more.

**Levels 6–8.** Learning that the suspicious noble supports or benefits from the disappearances, the characters investigate the noble’s home or business (such as the opera house or House of Wax). There, they discover and disrupt the creatures behind the disappearances, likely finding that the vanished people have been turned into monsters. If the noble escapes, an unrefusable invitation to the Grand Masquerade might draw them out, resulting in a showdown during that event—and potentially attracting the ire of [**Duchess d’Honaire**](#ref:monster:6491387-saidra-dhonaire "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491387-saidra-dhonaire").

### The Grand Masquerade {#rthw:dementlieu:TheGrandMasquerade}

Adventure for Level 4 Characters

**Situation.** The Grand Masquerade is an opportunity for characters to meet Dementlieuse nobles and gain information they can’t otherwise access.

**Hook.** The date of the next masquerade is public knowledge. To attend, the characters need to create their own costumes and invitations.

[![Map 2.9: D’Honaire Estate View Player Version (Artist: Mike Schley)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/map-06-02.dhonaire-estate.jpg)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/map-06-02.dhonaire-estate.jpg)

#### Encounters {#rthw:dementlieu:Encounters}

The adventure uses map 2.9 and consists of these encounters.

**_Dressed to Kill._** Attendees at the Grand Masquerade are expected to sport lavish costumes featuring fanciful masks. Any character not wearing an appropriate [**Costume**](#ref:equipment:536-costume "https://www.dndbeyond.com/equipment/536-costume"), a mask, and at least 100 GP worth of jewelry (or appropriate magical alternatives) has [**Disadvantage**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#disadvantage) on Charisma checks made during this adventure. Armor can’t be worn with a nonmagical costume. If a character becomes [**Bloodied**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#bloodied) while wearing a nonmagical costume, their costume is destroyed.

**_Arrival._** At the entrance to the estate, servants check the characters’ invitations. A character with a forged invitation must succeed on a DC 10 Charisma ([**Deception**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#skills)) check to be admitted. Those who fail are asked to leave. If they refuse, four [**Ghouls**](#ref:monster:5195009-ghoul "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195009-ghoul") wearing formal wear and masks fight them.

**_Masquerade._** The Grand Masquerade unfolds in three tableaux. During each, the characters can decide to dance, gossip, flirt, or do something else. Each character can earn renown for their group with the ball’s attendees and host by making positive impressions on other guests (see [chapter 3](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/dmg-2024/dms-toolbox#renown) of the [Dungeon Master’s Guide](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/dmg-2024) for details on renown). Each positive interaction can increase the group’s Renown Score by 1 per character per tableau.

Duchess d’Honaire has yet to appear, but hundreds of other costumed nobles mingle during the masquerade. These masked guests might share their names, but a character must succeed on a DC 10 Wisdom ([**Perception**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#skills)) check to identify even someone they’re familiar with. The following guests pay particular attention to the characters:

**Alexandre du Cire** (Medium [**Waxwork**](#ref:monster:6491401-waxwork "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491401-waxwork"); see [chapter 5](#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:waxwork "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/denizens-of-the-mists#waxwork")) poses as a human and runs the House of Wax. He urges the characters to visit his establishment. His costume is a suit on one side and a ball gown on the other. He is [**Friendly**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#friendlyattitude).

**Angel Pajaro** (Medium [**Werewolf**](#ref:monster:5195267-werewolf "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195267-werewolf")) is a famed diva of the Port-a-Lucine opera and is [**Hostile**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#hostileattitude). She likes to humiliate her fans but loves flattery from other performers. She’s dressed as an arctic fox.

**Julienne d’Honaire** (Medium, Neutral Good [**Bandit**](#ref:monster:5194915-bandit "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5194915-bandit")) is a Friendly human. She’s bubbly and behaves in an unrefined manner. She claims to be related to the duchess but confides that she wasn’t invited. Julienne wears a secondhand ballerina costume.

**Lord Governor Marcel Guignol** (Medium [**Noble**](#ref:monster:5195145-noble "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195145-noble")) is [**Indifferent**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#indifferentattitude) and didn’t want to attend the event. The elderly human is jittery and hates loud noises, and he seeks an excuse to leave. He’s dressed as a smiling jester.

**Raoul Rameau** (Medium [**Guard Captain**](#ref:monster:5195064-guard-captain "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195064-guard-captain")) is a member of the city watch. He tries to guess who people are and why they’ve been invited—his hunches are poor. He’s dressed as a toy monkey with cymbals.

**_Uncouth Exchange._** After the second tableau, two revelers wearing the same costumes as two nearby characters spot their lookalikes. Outraged by this faux pas, these [**Berserkers**](#ref:monster:4904621-berserker "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/4904621-berserker") fight them, wielding sharpened candelabras (these function as [**Greataxes**](#ref:equipment:21-greataxe "https://www.dndbeyond.com/equipment/21-greataxe")). If the characters defeat their attackers, their Renown Score increases by 2.

**_The Duchess Appears._** After three tableaux, [**Saidra d’Honaire**](#ref:monster:6491387-saidra-dhonaire "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491387-saidra-dhonaire") (see earlier in [this chapter](#rthw:dementlieu:SaidradHonaire "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/dementlieu#SaidradHonaire")) appears. She is fabulous and terrible as she drifts over the flattering crowd. Nearing the characters, she halts, gasps in revulsion, and points. “You! Never have I seen such an audaciously incompetent impostor! Who do you think you are to violate these hallowed halls?!” Near a character, Julienne d’Honaire begins to reply, and the duchess instantly disintegrates her. A ghoulish servant soon appears with a dustpan to clean the spot where Julienne stood. If party members spent two or more tableaux with Julienne, the group’s Renown Score decreases by 1.

**_Conclusion._** If the group’s Renown Score is 5 or less, the duchess shrieks, outraged to find more unworthies. Right away, four [**Ghoul**](#ref:monster:5195009-ghoul "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195009-ghoul") servants appear and fight the characters; two **Ghouls** arrive every round until the party flees the estate. The duchess doesn’t fight.

If the characters’ Renown Score is at least 6, the duchess compliments one of their costumes as she drifts by in time with the music. If the characters came to the masquerade to meet or influence someone, that individual appears soon after, impressed by the duchess’s compliment. Other members of the city’s nobility or individuals the characters met earlier in the night also might approach them with invitations or offers of employment. Each character earns a bonus 600 XP.

</CHAPTER>

# Falkovnia {#rthw:falkovnia:Falkovnia}

Domain Besieged by the Dead

> #### **Darklord:** [Vladeska Drakov](#rthw:falkovnia:VladeskaDrakov "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/falkovnia#VladeskaDrakov") {#rthw:falkovnia:VladeskaDrakov}
>
> **Genre:** [Disaster horror](#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:disasterhorror "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/creating-domains-of-dread#disasterhorror")
>
> **Hallmarks:** Dwindling resources, impending disaster, suspicion, totalitarianism, zombies
>
> **Mist Talismans:** Correspondence from the capital, Lekar; gear marked with the Blood Falcon; zombie flesh
>
> **Aligned Tarokka Card:** Dictator
>
> **Opposed Tarokka Card:** Executioner

[![(Artist: Pam Wishbow)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/07-001.dictator-tarokka.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/07-001.dictator-tarokka.png) [![](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/07-002.executioner-tarokka.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/07-002.executioner-tarokka.png)

Falkovnia is a land besieged. Empty countryside surrounds ruined or crumbling cities. Only a few desperate pockets of civilization survive, carrying on not out of hope, but out of fear of the land’s merciless soldiers. Led by [**General Vladeska Drakov**](#ref:monster:6491400-vladeska-drakov "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491400-vladeska-drakov"), Falkovnia’s military organizes a desperate and occasionally effective defense against an implacable foe: the ever-growing armies of the dead.

Every moon, a new zombie legion emerges from the Mists. Never appearing from the same place twice, the horde sweeps across the land, drawn to the densest populations of the living. That always includes the Falkovnian capital of Lekar, where unfit and underfed conscripts defend crumbling walls alongside General Drakov and her crimson-armored elite soldiers, the Talons. Causalities mount during the zombie sieges, but miracles and moments of desperate valor haven’t abandoned Falkovnia. The people’s numbers dwindle, but they soldier on.

In the aftermath of a zombie attack, the Falkovnians burn their dead, repair what they can, and whisper that now might be the time to flee the city. Invariably, someone speaks too loudly, and soldiers drag off the so-called traitor to be impaled as an example. The people might want to abandon their homes, but Vladeska Drakov refuses to accept defeat.

## Domain Features {#rthw:falkovnia:DomainFeatures}

Falkovnia is known for the following features:

**Army of the Dead.** Every night of the new moon, thousands of ravenous zombies emerge from the Mists to feed on the living.

**Capital Punishment.** There is only one punishment for any crime in Falkovnia: impalement.

**Rotten Remnants.** Ruins cover Falkovnia—towns and villages crushed by zombie hordes and haunted by undead stragglers.

**Talon Soldiers.** Falkovnian soldiers known as Talons patrol the land, hunting for deserters and strangers to press into service. Talon officers bear prominent tattoos of the Blood Falcon, the symbol of [Vladeska Drakov](#rthw:falkovnia:VladeskaDrakov "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/falkovnia#VladeskaDrakov").

## Locations in Falkovnia {#rthw:falkovnia:LocationsinFalkovnia}

Falkovnia is an unnervingly still domain, where people and animals hide to avoid attracting the attention of zombies and Drakov’s brutal Talons. The city of Lekar is described below, and other notable locations are summarized on the [Falkovnia Locations table](#rthw:falkovnia:falkovnialocations "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/falkovnia#falkovnialocations").

### Lekar {#rthw:falkovnia:Lekar}

The only city of the living left in Falkovnia, Lekar bears the brunt of the zombie invasion. The city has outgrown its walls multiple times since its founding, leaving its districts divided by fortifications. During the first zombie siege, General Drakov sacrificed the northern River Ward, leaving hundreds of souls to be slaughtered but allowing the remaining defenders to turn back the zombie horde.

Now the city’s survivors face harsh conditions. Talon soldiers keep the peace in the cramped slums. Troops lead civilians outside the walls to scavenge from ruins and work the fields of abandoned farms, but their harvests are never enough for the city’s survivors. Though bitter and desperate, soldiers live better than civilians, assured of rations and housing in the Bastion Ward—the Talons-only district around General Drakov’s command center at Custodian’s Hall. From there, Drakov orders daily public executions as conscripts dispense supplies to the suffering masses.

[![Map 2.10: Falkovnia View Player Version (Artist: Jared Blando)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/map-07-01.falkovnia.jpg)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/map-07-01.falkovnia.jpg)

**Falkovnia Locations**

| Location             | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Aerie                | Swarms of zombified birds of prey attack any living creatures near the village of Aerie, especially those who use the cable ferries crossing the Archer River.                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Delmunster           | Zombies avoid the idyllic village of Delmunster. People say that it is protected by a fallen star; Few suspect the [**Bodytaker Plant**](#ref:monster:6491341-bodytaker-plant "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491341-bodytaker-plant") (see [chapter 5](#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:bodytakerplant "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/denizens-of-the-mists#bodytakerplant")) that has claimed the community. |
| Fort Watten          | A force of Talons under the command of Major Olana Crepeau was ordered to guard Falkovnia’s southern border at Fort Watten. No one in Lekar has heard from them for moons.                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Hatzimvas Hospital   | The doctors of the secluded Hatzimvas Hospital seek a medical or supernatural cure to zombification. Mysteriously, Drakov allows the hospital to work unimpeded.                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Morfenzi             | The ruins of Morfenzi hide a Talon outpost. Here the amoral scientist Vjorn Horstman conducts monstrous experiments, creating living weapons using “primal serum.”                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Silbervas            | Fractious bands of survivors sworn to silence scavenge the ruined city of Silbervas. They avoid the ominously lit Dekovan Palace, which overlooks the ruins.                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Stangengrad          | The silent, scarred spirits of commoners and Talons haunt the ruined fortress-city of Stangengrad. Vladeska forbids entry to the city so no one can learn of the atrocity that took place there.                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Stonespine Mountains | The knight Gondegal leads rebels opposed to the Talons. Her stronghold is said to be hidden in the Stonespine Mountains, but none who join Gondegal are ever seen again.                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Three Traitors       | Between the three lakes known as the Three Traitors is a muddy patch where Vistani often camp. These travelers have a knack for avoiding Talon patrols.                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Vigila Forest        | In the dense Vigila Forest stand towering black trees called Sentries of Death. Tales say the wood is haunted and these trees’ roots reach into the realm of the dead.                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Willow Watch         | The hastily constructed Willow Watch tower was built on the ruins of a church of Ezra. The Talons here report strange lights in the nearby forest and sounds from the catacombs below.                                                                                                                                                                                         |

## Vladeska Drakov {#rthw:falkovnia:VladeskaDrakov}

Darklord Who Wars Against the Dead

[![(Artist: Marianne Khalil)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/07-003.vladeska-drakov.jpg)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/07-003.vladeska-drakov.jpg)

> “If you’re reinforcements, I expect you to prove you’re worth the gear you’re wearing. I need soldiers, not more bait for the undead.”
>
> —Vladeska Drakov

General of a demoralized occupying army, Vladeska Drakov rules what little of Falkovnia hasn’t been overrun by the dead. A cunning authoritarian, she believes any tactics—no matter how immoral—are permissible in the pursuit of victory. The Mists torment her by keeping her ever on the edge of defeat, exhausting her and forcing her to watch her precision fail in the face of an endless string of emergencies and an undefeatable enemy horde. Drakov is ever being pushed to the edge. Hunger, sleep deprivation, and the endless demands of terrified troops and civilians drive her toward outbursts of paranoia and violence.

### [Vladeska Drakov](#ref:monster:6491400-vladeska-drakov "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491400-vladeska-drakov") {#rthw:falkovnia:VladeskaDrakovrefmonster6491400vladeskadrakovhttpswwwdndbeyondcommonsters6491400vladeskadrakov}

Medium Humanoid (Human), Lawful Evil

**AC** 18 **Initiative** +5 (15)

**HP** 170 (20d8 + 80)

**Speed** 30 ft.

|     |     | Mod | Save |
| --- | --- | --- | ---- |
| STR | 19  | +4  | +4   |
| DEX | 15  | +2  | +2   |
| CON | 18  | +4  | +8   |

|     |     | Mod | Save |
| --- | --- | --- | ---- |
| INT | 14  | +2  | +2   |
| WIS | 13  | +1  | +1   |
| CHA | 16  | +3  | +7   |

**Skills** [**Athletics**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#skills) +8, [**Perception**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#skills) +5

**Immunities** [**Frightened**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#frightenedcondition)

**Gear** [**Pike**](#ref:equipment:27-pike "https://www.dndbeyond.com/equipment/27-pike"), [**Spears**](#ref:equipment:14-spear "https://www.dndbeyond.com/equipment/14-spear") (6), [**Studded Leather Armor**](#ref:equipment:3-studded-leather "https://www.dndbeyond.com/equipment/3-studded-leather")

**Senses** Passive Perception 15

**Languages** Common, Giant, Orc

**Challenge** 12 (XP 8,400, or 10,000 in domain; PB +4)

#### Traits {#rthw:falkovnia:Traits}

**_Darklord Restoration._** If Vladeska dies, she revives with all her Hit Points in 1d10 weeks somewhere in Falkovnia.

**_Legendary Resistance (3/Day, or 4/Day in Domain)._** If Vladeska fails a saving throw, she can choose to succeed instead.

#### Actions {#rthw:falkovnia:Actions}

**_Multiattack._** Vladeska makes two Pike attacks. She can replace one attack with an Impaling Spear attack.

**_Impaling Spear._** _Melee or Ranged Attack Roll:_ +8, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft. _Hit:_ 13 (2d8 + 4) Piercing damage, and the target is impaled on Vladeska’s spear. While impaled, the creature has the [**Restrained**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#restrainedcondition) condition and takes 3 (1d6) Piercing damage at the start of each of its turns. The target or a creature within 5 feet of it can take an action to remove it from the spear.

**_Pike._** _Melee Attack Roll:_ +8, reach 10 ft. _Hit:_ 15 (2d10 + 4) Piercing damage.

**_Artillery Fire (1/Day)._** _Dexterity Saving Throw:_ DC 15, each creature in a 20-foot-radius, 60-foot-high [**Cylinder**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#cylinderareaofeffect) centered on a point Vladeska can see within 300 feet. _Failure:_ 13 (3d8) Bludgeoning damage plus 13 (3d8) Fire damage, and the target has the [**Prone**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#pronecondition) condition. _Success:_ Half damage only.

#### Reactions {#rthw:falkovnia:Reactions}

**_Redirect Attack._** _Trigger:_ A creature Vladeska can see makes an attack roll against her. _Response:_ Vladeska chooses a Small or Medium ally within 5 feet of herself. She and that ally swap places, and the ally becomes the target of the attack instead.

#### Legendary Actions {#rthw:falkovnia:LegendaryActions}

Legendary Action Uses: 3 (4 in Domain). Immediately after another creature’s turn, Vladeska can expend a use to take one of the following actions. Vladeska regains all expended uses at the start of each of her turns.

**_Advance._** Vladeska moves up to half her Speed and makes one Pike attack.

**_Dreadful Impaling._** Vladeska makes an Impaling Spear attack. If the attack hits and the target is a creature, each ally of the target within 30 feet is subjected to the following effect. _Wisdom Saving Throw:_ DC 15. _Failure:_ The target has the [**Frightened**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#frightenedcondition) condition until the end of its next turn. _Failure or Success:_ Vladeska can’t take this action again until the start of her next turn.

**_Order Ballista._** _Dexterity Saving Throw:_ DC 15, one creature Vladeska can see within 120 feet. _Failure:_ 14 (4d6 + 3) Piercing damage, and the target’s Speed is halved until the end of its next turn.

### Drakov’s Tale {#rthw:falkovnia:DrakovsTale}

In the world of her birth, Vladeska Drakov was known as the Crimson Falcon, leader of a peerless mercenary army called the Falcon’s Talons. In a land of bitterly feuding royal families, she and her troops executed a thousand ancient grudges and petty atrocities. Drakov amassed a fortune and planned to retire young and buy a title and a realm to rule.

The sacking of Yeivere changed her plans. During that city’s razing, Drakov’s mercenaries went too far. The Falcon’s Talons killed a unique soul during the slaughter. None can say who the soul was—a royal, a saint, a witch, an angel—but with its death, the world turned against them.

The ruling families united to hunt the Talons. Thanks to her tactical genius, Drakov repelled her pursuers and went on the offensive. One by one she attacked her former benefactors, burning villages, pressing citizens into service, and impaling anyone with a drop of noble blood. Over years of work, Drakov forged a bloody empire. But while sacking the burning city of her last remaining foe, Drakov and her troops were engulfed by smoke. When it cleared, everything they knew was gone.

Transported to an unfamiliar land, Drakov and her troops wasted little time subjugating it. This unprepared realm fell quickly, almost willingly. On taking the city of Lekar, Drakov named herself ruler of her new empire: Falkovnia.

However, under a moonless sky, the dead rose against Drakov, claws scraping against Lekar’s walls before alarms could be raised. Drakov’s brilliant and desperate strategies eventually turned back the zombies during the days-long First Siege of Lekar, but victory came at the cost of most of her veteran troops.

Since then, Drakov has nearly lost her nation. Every moon, a new desperate battle unfolds. She prepares ceaselessly for each one, certain of her ultimate victory but doubtful of her troops’ mettle. With threats and public impalings, she keeps her people more terrified of her than of the undead. And with every new moon, she faces an unconquerable foe, never revealing a secret only she knows: that each zombie bears the face of an innocent her soldiers once put to the sword.

[![Custodian’s Hall rises over the few remaining wards of Lekar that haven’t fallen to the zombie hordes (Artist: Miro Petrov)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/07-004.custodians-hall.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/07-004.custodians-hall.png)

### Drakov’s Domain {#rthw:falkovnia:DrakovsDomain}

Falkovnia is altered by Drakov’s presence, creating the following effects:

**Authoritarian Regime.** Drakov’s allies have [**Advantage**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#advantage) on Wisdom saving throws.

**Closing the Borders.** Drakov can’t close or open the borders of her domain. Falkovnia’s borders are usually closed, but they open one week every month starting on the night of the new moon.

**Endless War.** Whenever a creature other than Drakov or her allies finishes a Long Rest in the domain, roll 1d20. On a 1, the creature doesn’t remove any [**Exhaustion**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#exhaustioncondition) levels as a result of finishing that rest, and the creature gains 1 Exhaustion level.

If Drakov dies, these effects end immediately.

### Drakov’s Lair {#rthw:falkovnia:DrakovsLair}

When she conquered the city, Vladeska Drakov claimed Lekar’s seat of governance, Custodian’s Hall, as her army’s headquarters. Since the First Siege of Lekar, one emergency after another has forced Drakov and her Talon troops to repurpose the building’s chambers for military purposes.

[![Map 2.11: Custodian’s Hall View Player Version (Artist: Mike Schley)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/map-07-02.custodians-hall.jpg)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/map-07-02.custodians-hall.jpg)

#### Custodian’s Hall {#rthw:falkovnia:CustodiansHall}

The polished marble and hopeful mosaics of Custodian’s Hall now bear the dirt and scars of invaders’ boots and tools of war. The site is depicted on [map 2.11](#rthw:falkovnia:map211custodianshall "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/falkovnia#map211custodianshall") and has the following features:

**Chamber of Peers.** The chamber of Lekar’s dissolved senate now serves as a command center for Drakov’s officers.

**Drakov’s Chambers.** Drakov has repurposed offices at the heights of Custodian’s Hall as her personal chambers. Her bedroom is cold and simple and features little more than a hard cot. Nearby, she maintains a war room full of maps and reports where she obsesses over desperate battle scenarios. Across the hall is a well-used chamber full of torture devices, many of her own design.

**Plaza Stairs.** Daily, Talons disseminate meager rations to Lekar’s citizens while other soldiers execute supposed traitors by impaling them on pikes.

## Adventures in Falkovnia {#rthw:falkovnia:AdventuresinFalkovnia}

Adventures set in Falkovnia involve zombie hordes, cruel soldiers, and Drakov herself. Use this section to develop horror adventures in this domain.

### Horror in Falkovnia {#rthw:falkovnia:HorrorinFalkovnia}

Adventures in Falkovnia often include the following elements.

#### Zombie March {#rthw:falkovnia:ZombieMarch}

Zombies emerge from the Mists on the night of the new moon. This surge brings a recurring threat to besiege the walls of Lekar, but it also makes encountering droves of zombies more likely throughout the domain. Use the zombies from [chapter 5](#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:zombies "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/denizens-of-the-mists#zombies"), the [Monster Manual](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/mm-2024) or other sources to create surprising and terrifying encounters.

#### The Falcon’s Talons {#rthw:falkovnia:TheFalconsTalons}

Drakov’s military forces are both completely overwhelming and entirely outnumbered. Though relatively few in number, the Talons are organized enough to oppress Falkovnia’s survivors and enforce Drakov’s totalitarian laws. In the face of zombie hordes, though, the Talons are fighting a losing battle. Talon soldiers are [**Warrior Infantry**](#ref:monster:5195259-warrior-infantry "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195259-warrior-infantry"), while officers are [**Warrior Veterans**](#ref:monster:5195260-warrior-veteran "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195260-warrior-veteran").

#### Martial Law {#rthw:falkovnia:MartialLaw}

Lekar is a martial dictatorship. Drakov’s troops carry out example-setting impalings as punishment for even the slightest crimes. These executions impose order through terror and make it clear that zombies aren’t the realm’s only monsters.

#### Only Bad Choices {#rthw:falkovnia:OnlyBadChoices}

There is one simple truth in Falkovnia: The dead are going to kill everyone. This sets the stage for countless bad decisions, from leaders making terrible sacrifices or permitting immoral acts to individuals making fatalistic choices. Locals behave as if it’s their last day alive—because it probably is.

#### Trapped with the Dead {#rthw:falkovnia:TrappedwiththeDead}

Falkovnia’s borders are usually closed, and Vladeska Drakov has no control over when they open. Anyone who enters the Mists surrounding Falkovnia encounters endless numbers of zombies. Travelers who somehow avoid these shambling corpses emerge from the Mists back in Falkovnia, pursued by the undead. For one week following the night of the new moon, the Mists are empty of zombies and the borders open. During this time, Drakov sends patrols of Talons to sweep the edges of the Mists for deserters. These patrols are difficult to avoid, and battles with them often attract zombies.

#### Falkovnia Campaign Arc {#rthw:falkovnia:FalkovniaCampaignArc}

Falkovnia is one of the few domains where the characters and the Darklord might be on the same side, united against unrelenting hordes of zombies. The characters might try to defend Falkovnia’s people alongside Drakov, but as the Darklord’s obsession with victory becomes clear, they must balance keeping her trust and upholding their principles. A campaign here might follow this outline:

**Levels 1–4.** The characters save a group of commoners and outmatched Talons from [**Zombies**](#ref:monster:4775851-zombie "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/4775851-zombie"). The thankful band takes the characters to Lekar, where people hail them as heroic “Trueborn of Falkovnia.” [**Vladeska Drakov**](#ref:monster:6491400-vladeska-drakov "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491400-vladeska-drakov") recruits them to bring scattered pockets of common folk to safety in Lekar.

**Levels 5–8.** The characters witness the suffering in Lekar and see some of those they’ve saved impaled for disloyalty. Rebels entreat them to help smuggle people out of Lekar to hidden encampments in the mountains.

**Levels 9–12.** The characters are captured by Talons, but Drakov offers them freedom if they defend the city’s southern gate, the Gate of Torches, from the impending zombie siege. Unknown to the characters, Drakov plans to sacrifice the gate as detailed in the “Siege of Lekar” adventure.

### Siege of Lekar {#rthw:falkovnia:SiegeofLekar}

Adventure for Level 9 Characters

**Situation.** Zombie hordes attack Lekar. Vladeska Drakov seeks to defeat them by sacrificing the characters and a district of Lekar.

**Hook.** The characters are ordered by Drakov or entreated by citizens to defend the Gate of Torches.

[![Map 2.12: Lekar Gate View Player Version (Artist: Stacey Allan & William Doyle)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/map-07-03.lekar-gate.jpg)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/map-07-03.lekar-gate.jpg)

#### Lekar Gates {#rthw:falkovnia:LekarGates}

This adventure takes place at a gate in Lekar’s southern wall, the Gate of Torches, and a second gate to Lekar’s central district, Loyalist’s Gate. The Gate of Torches shows the scars of countless zombie claws, but otherwise the gates are identical. Both have the following features:

**Fortifications.** The walls of Lekar are 30 feet tall, with the gatehouse’s towers rising 40 feet. Crenelations atop both provide defenders with [**Three-Quarters Cover**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#cover) from beyond the wall.

**Gates.** The gatehouse’s battle-scarred gates are Huge objects with AC 19, 72 HP, and Immunity to Poison and Psychic damage. Any character adjacent to the mechanism over the gate can open or close the gate in 1 round.

#### Encounters {#rthw:falkovnia:Encounters}

These encounters begin at the Gate of Torches, which uses [map 2.12](#rthw:falkovnia:map212lekargate "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/falkovnia#map212lekargate"). Characters can position themselves where they please. Describe inexperienced soldiers guarding other posts or zombies beyond the map, but don’t track their actions in battle. When you’re ready to begin the siege, the Siege Events by Round table outlines what occurs each round. The following sections further detail these events.

**Siege Events by Round**

| Round | Siege Event                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| 1     | Eight [**Zombies**](#ref:monster:4775851-zombie "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/4775851-zombie") and six [**Ogre Zombies**](#ref:monster:5174956-ogre-zombie "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5174956-ogre-zombie") appear.                                       |
| 3     | Four [**Ogre Zombies**](#ref:monster:5174956-ogre-zombie "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5174956-ogre-zombie") and a [**Beholder Zombie**](#ref:monster:5194922-beholder-zombie "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5194922-beholder-zombie") appear.                |
| 5     | Two [**Zombie Clots**](#ref:monster:6491405-zombie-clot "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491405-zombie-clot") (see [chapter 5](#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:zombieclot "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/denizens-of-the-mists#zombieclot")) appear. Talons roll a wagon to the gate from the north. |
| 6     | Talons light fuses on the wagon.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| 7     | Four [**Ogre Zombies**](#ref:monster:5174956-ogre-zombie "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5174956-ogre-zombie") appear. Talons flee.                                                                                                                                  |
| 8     | Wagon explodes (if not prevented).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| 9     | Explosion (see “Siege Climax”).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |

**_Zombie Attack._** Zombies shamble from the south and attack the gatehouse’s gates. Rather than having foes make individual attacks on the gates, assume the gates take 4d6 damage every time a round ends with a zombie adjacent to them. When reduced to 0 Hit Points, the gate is destroyed. If this occurs, troops flee as detailed in “Siege Climax.”

**_Drakov’s Talons._** Starting on round 5, any character on or behind the walls who succeeds on a DC 12 Wisdom ([**Perception**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#skills)) check notices Talons (four [**Warrior Veterans**](#ref:monster:5195260-warrior-veteran "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195260-warrior-veteran")) behind the gate. The Talons are supposedly allied troops, so this shouldn’t cause concern. The Talons behave as detailed on the Siege Events by Round table. They flee if fought.

**_Talon Wagon._** This wagon contains kegs of gunpowder. A character adjacent to the wagon who spends a round investigating discovers these explosives. On round 6, any character who has noticed the Talons and is within sight of them sees them setting fuses. If no one prevents the soldiers from lighting the fuses or extinguishes the lit fuses, the wagon explodes at the end of round 8. Creatures within 30 feet of it when it explodes make a DC 12 Dexterity saving throw, taking 42 (12d6) Fire damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. The explosion destroys the gatehouse’s gate, regardless of its remaining Hit Points.

**_Siege Climax._** The siege continues until either the gatehouse’s gate is destroyed or the end of round 9. At the end of round 9, an explosion hundreds of feet to the west destroys part of the city wall, and [**Zombies**](#ref:monster:4775851-zombie "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/4775851-zombie") pour into Lekar. Surviving soldiers abandon their posts—it’s clear the Gate of Torches will be overrun. These survivors race through the slums to Loyalist’s Gate.

**_Loyalist’s Gate._** Loyalist’s Gate is identical to the Gate of Torches and uses [map 2.12: Lekar Gate](#rthw:falkovnia:map212lekargate "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/falkovnia#map212lekargate"). When the characters arrive from the south, the gate is closed. Hundreds of surviving soldiers and slum residents scream for the guards to let them through. Talon soldiers (eight [**Warrior Infantry**](#ref:monster:5195259-warrior-infantry "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195259-warrior-infantry")) and [**Vladeska Drakov**](#ref:monster:6491400-vladeska-drakov "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491400-vladeska-drakov") (see earlier in [this chapter](#rthw:falkovnia:VladeskaDrakov "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/falkovnia#VladeskaDrakov")) guard the gate. Drakov thanks the panicking assemblage for their sacrifice and reveals her plan to set the slums ablaze once the zombies flood in. The characters can open the gate to admit the crowd using the mechanism in the gatehouse, but Drakov and her troops fight to prevent this.

The characters have 4 rounds before groups of 1d6 [**Zombies**](#ref:monster:4775851-zombie "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/4775851-zombie") begin appearing from the south at the end of each round. Narrate these zombies attacking the crowd, but don’t track the crowd’s Hit Points. If the characters open the gate before the zombies appear, each of them earns 5,900 bonus XP.

**_Drakov’s Defeat._** If Drakov is defeated, Falkovnia’s borders open, and no zombies appear from the Mists for several moons. Some people rebuild, others flee into the Mists. After this time, though, Drakov reappears and slowly retakes control of Falkovnia. The borders close, and zombies return soon afterward.

</CHAPTER>

<CHAPTER id="rthw:harakir" title="Harakir">

# Har’Akir {#rthw:harakir:HarAkir}

Domain of the Ancient Dead

> #### **Darklord:** [Ankhtepot](#rthw:harakir:Ankhtepot "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/harakir#Ankhtepot") {#rthw:harakir:Ankhtepot}
>
> **Genre:** [Dark fantasy](#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:darkfantasy "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/creating-domains-of-dread#darkfantasy")
>
> **Hallmarks:** Ancient tombs, desert perils, lost gods, mummies
>
> **Mist Talismans:** Canopic jar, lapis lazuli scarab, scroll of hieroglyphics
>
> **Aligned Tarokka Card:** Monk
>
> **Opposed Tarokka Card:** Raven

[![(Artist: Pam Wishbow)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/08-001.monk-tarokka.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/08-001.monk-tarokka.png) [![](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/08-002.raven-tarokka.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/08-002.raven-tarokka.png)

Untold generations of tombs and monuments choke on the obsidian sands of the desert domain of Har’Akir. Here, past splendors lie forgotten, and the living bow in service to the mummified god-king, [**Ankhtepot**](#ref:monster:6491339-ankhtepot "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491339-ankhtepot").

From a golden pyramid in the City of the Dead, Ankhtepot reigns as speaker for the gods and immortal pharaoh. The deathless ruler cares nothing for his domain or mortal concerns. Rather, he relentlessly sends servants in search of his one desire: his ka, the missing piece of his fractured soul.

As the pharaoh obsesses over his lost soul, his servants plague the domain in his name. In hidden tomb-courts, mummies known as the Children of Ankhtepot dominate cults as emissaries of mysterious gods. And in the mud-brick city of Muhar, Ankhtepot’s priests oversee all aspects of life, apportioning food to the worthy and punishing blasphemers. But all the pharaoh’s servants also pursue the Darklord’s quest for his mysterious ka, though only his Children know the truth of this “treasure” he seeks. Each of them is desperate for some clue to placate Ankhtepot and spare them from his wrath.

## Domain Features {#rthw:harakir:DomainFeatures}

Har’Akir is known for the following features:

**Distant Pharaoh.** The people of Har’Akir know their ruler is an immortal who resides in the golden mountain called Pharaoh’s Rest. Only priests can enter this massive pyramid.

**Extreme Environs.** [Intense heat](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/dmg-2024/dms-toolbox#extremeheat) and [winds](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/dmg-2024/dms-toolbox#strongwind) are common in Har’Akir (see the [Dungeon Master’s Guide](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/dmg-2024)), and water is scarce.

**Forgotten Ruins.** The deserts of Har’Akir are littered with the remnants of a strange and glorious empire. The origins of these ruins remain a mystery.

**Mysterious Gods.** Har’Akir’s people worship a pantheon of false or silent gods. Manipulative or deluded priests oversee all aspects of society in these gods’ and the pharaoh’s names.

**Preserved Dead.** Akirrans mummify their dead so the pharaoh might call them to service. It is a crime to burn the dead.

## Locations in Har’Akir {#rthw:harakir:LocationsinHarAkir}

Har’Akir is dominated by treacherous, surreal deserts that obey Ankhtepot’s will. The Labyrinth and city of Muhar are described below, and other notable locations are summarized on the [Har’Akir Locations table](#rthw:harakir:harakirlocations "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/harakir#harakirlocations").

### Labyrinth {#rthw:harakir:Labyrinth}

Har’Akir’s countless trap-laden ruins interconnect beneath the desert in a hidden maze called the Labyrinth. Monstrous [**Mummies**](#ref:monster:5195135-mummy "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195135-mummy") and stranger creatures stalk these sprawling tunnels. Nevertheless, some priests use the few mapped sections to move about the domain unseen.

### Muhar {#rthw:harakir:Muhar}

The city of Muhar is the only permanent settlement in Har’Akir. Here, pious people thank the gods for the water and food of the Muhar Oasis. From the city’s largest structure, the Temple of Ese, High Priest Isu Rehkotep speaks for Pharaoh Ankhtepot in all matters; her word is considered both royal decree and divine edict. Ankhtepot doesn’t care how Isu runs Muhar so long as she maintains order and uses her influence to continue his unending search. Those who displease Isu or oppose her priest-guards are thrown into the Mouth of Oru, a pit that connects to the Labyrinth.

[![Map 2.13: Har’Akir View Player Version (Artist: Marco Bernardini)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/map-08-01.harakir.jpg)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/map-08-01.harakir.jpg)

**Har’Akir Locations**

| Location              | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| --------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Bent Pyramid          | This bent, black granite pyramid has no interior or obvious purpose. Some Akirrans claim it holds the magic of a forgotten god that one can manipulate using ancient music.                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| City of the Dead      | Massive statues and the ornate tombs of heroes and priests compose the City of the Dead. These crypts climb toward Ankhtepot’s mountain-size golden pyramid, Pharaoh’s Rest.                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Kharafek’s Excavation | The historian Kharafek has discovered numerous tombs at this excavation. Each unleashes a curse once opened, so Kharafek regularly hires new laborers to bear the brunt of these curses.                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Muhar Oasis           | Muhar Oasis supplies the city of Muhar and attracts predators such as [**Chimeras**](#ref:monster:5194943-chimera "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5194943-chimera") and [**Giant Scorpions**](#ref:monster:5195026-giant-scorpion "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195026-giant-scorpion"). During droughts, the water recedes, revealing a lapis lazuli tomb along the banks. |
| Ousa’s Pyramid        | Ousa’s Pyramid holds a gate to the afterlife, but only Thute—a jackal-headed Child of Ankhtepot—knows how to enter. Thute’s jackal-masked followers seek to sacrifice all strangers.                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Path of the Asp       | Deadly serpents inhabit the canyon known as the Path of the Asp. The spirits of those slain by these snakes can appear to anyone they know and speak ten words before vanishing.                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Red Oasis             | Akirrans say that the gods gave the Red Oasis to animals and that its waters are poison to people. Supernaturally cunning lions hunt in the area and offer sacrifices to a nearby monument.                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Sands of Sute         | Within the desert rage two vast sandstorms: the Breath of the Forgotten and the Breath of the False. The storms impose tests that punish those whose lives lack consequence or faith.                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Sek’s Tears           | People say the waters of Sek’s Tears can heal any affliction, but grim [**Sphinxes**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/br-2024/creature-stat-blocks#sphinxes) guard the oasis. The answers to the sphinxes’ riddles are usually found in other domains.                                                                                                                           |
| Senmet’s Tomb         | The Child of Ankhtepot named Senmet seeks to steal the pharaoh’s throne. From his tomb, Senmet navigates the Labyrinth and stokes rebellion among the living and the dead.                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| White Oasis           | The White Oasis is considered holy. A nearby abandoned quarry called River’s Shelter houses numerous cursed and dying hermits who seek to cleanse themselves in the oasis.                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
