## Ankhtepot {#rthw:harakir:Ankhtepot}

Darklord Who Pursues Death

[![(Artist: Anna Podedworna)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/08-003.ankhtepot.jpg)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/08-003.ankhtepot.jpg)

> #### “Bow before the pharaoh—whether as a servant or as dust.” {#rthw:harakir:ankhtepot:Bowbeforethepharaohwhetherasaservantorasdust}
>
> —Ankhtepot

Ankhtepot has known treachery and conquest. He has known divinity and rule. But now he knows simply boredom and despair. He desires only to recover his lost ka, which he knows lies hidden in Har’Akir. With it, he hopes to become mortal again, die, and face his gods’ judgment. Whether this means peace or oblivion matters not to him. Ankhtepot seeks only an end, and he and his followers will be a plague on Har’Akir until he finds it.

### [Ankhtepot](#ref:monster:6491339-ankhtepot "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491339-ankhtepot") {#rthw:harakir:Ankhtepotrefmonster6491339ankhtepothttpswwwdndbeyondcommonsters6491339ankhtepot}

Medium Undead, Lawful Evil

**AC** 17 **Initiative** +6 (16)

**HP** 202 (27d8 + 81)

**Speed** 30 ft., Fly 30 ft. (hover)

|     |     | Mod | Save |
| --- | --- | --- | ---- |
| STR | 18  | +4  | +4   |
| DEX | 10  | +0  | +0   |
| CON | 17  | +3  | +3   |

|     |     | Mod | Save |
| --- | --- | --- | ---- |
| INT | 15  | +2  | +8   |
| WIS | 20  | +5  | +11  |
| CHA | 16  | +3  | +3   |

**Skills** [**History**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#skills) +8, [**Perception**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#skills) +11, [**Religion**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#skills) +8

**Vulnerabilities** Fire

**Immunities** Necrotic, Poison; [**Charmed**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#charmedcondition), [**Exhaustion**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#exhaustioncondition), [**Frightened**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#frightenedcondition), [**Paralyzed**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#paralyzedcondition), [**Poisoned**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#poisonedcondition)

**Senses** [**Truesight**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#truesight) 60 ft.; Passive Perception 21

**Languages** Celestial, Common, Draconic

**Challenge** 17 (XP 18,000, or 20,000 in domain; PB +6)

#### Traits {#rthw:harakir:Traits}

**_Darklord Restoration._** If Ankhtepot dies, he revives with all his Hit Points in 1d10 weeks somewhere in Har’Akir.

**_Legendary Resistance (3/Day, or 4/Day in Domain)._** If Ankhtepot fails a saving throw, he can choose to succeed instead.

**_Magic Resistance._** Ankhtepot has [**Advantage**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#advantage) on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

#### Actions {#rthw:harakir:Actions}

**_Multiattack._** Ankhtepot makes four Negative Energy Burst attacks. He can replace one attack with a use of Spellcasting to cast [**Power Word Stun**](#ref:spell:2618889-power-word-stun "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618889-power-word-stun").

**_Negative Energy Burst._** _Melee or Ranged Attack Roll:_ +11, reach 5 ft. or range 60 ft. _Hit:_ 26 (6d6 + 5) Necrotic damage.

**_Spellcasting._** Ankhtepot casts one of the following spells, requiring no spell components and using Wisdom as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 19):

**At Will:** [**Dispel Magic**](#ref:spell:2619103-dispel-magic "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619103-dispel-magic"), [**Divination**](#ref:spell:2619140-divination "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619140-divination"), [**Mage Hand**](#ref:spell:2619008-mage-hand "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619008-mage-hand") (hand is [**Invisible**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#invisiblecondition)), [**Power Word Stun**](#ref:spell:2618889-power-word-stun "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618889-power-word-stun")

**1/Day Each:** [**Animate Dead**](#ref:spell:2618853-animate-dead "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618853-animate-dead"), [**Sunburst**](#ref:spell:2619123-sunburst "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619123-sunburst")

**_Touch of Death (Recharge 6)._** Ankhtepot touches one creature within 5 feet. If the creature has 80 Hit Points or fewer, it dies. Otherwise, it takes 52 (8d12) Necrotic damage.

#### Legendary Actions {#rthw:harakir:LegendaryActions}

Legendary Action Uses: 3 (4 in Domain). Immediately after another creature’s turn, Ankhtepot can expend a use to take one of the following actions. Ankhtepot regains all expended uses at the start of each of his turns.

**_Death Strike._** Ankhtepot makes one Negative Energy Burst attack.

**_Hand of Fate._** _Strength Saving Throw:_ DC 19, one Large or smaller creature Ankhtepot can see within 60 feet. _Failure:_ 14 (2d8 + 5) Force damage, and the target is pushed or pulled up to 20 feet straight away or toward Ankhtepot. _Success:_ Half damage only. _Failure or Success:_ Ankhtepot can’t take this action again until the start of his next turn.

**_Sands of Time._** Ankhtepot teleports up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space he can see. _Charisma Saving Throw:_ DC 19, each creature in a 10-foot [**Emanation**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#emanationareaofeffect) originating from Ankhtepot at his destination space. _Failure:_ 11 (2d10) Necrotic damage, and the target magically ages 10 years. _Success:_ Half damage only. _Failure or Success:_ Ankhtepot can’t take this action again until the start of his next turn.

### Ankhtepot’s Tale {#rthw:harakir:AnkhtepotsTale}

In a nation called the Land of Reeds and Lotuses, Ankhtepot served the royal family as high priest. As old pharaohs died and new ones rose, the influential priest came to believe that the gods wanted a wiser leader to rule. On the day of a new pharaoh’s ascension, Ankhtepot rallied his priests and murdered their liege. But he had misjudged the people’s will, and an outraged mob rose up and executed the traitorous priests.

Moreover, Ankhtepot had misjudged the will of the gods. As he stood before them in death, the immortals forsook him, cursing him and denying him entry to the afterlife. They returned him to the world but stripped away a piece of his soul, his ka—the vital essence that inspires all living beings.

Ankhtepot awoke, trapped within his corpse, as he was mummified along with his treacherous followers. Untold centuries passed, but on the day the last memory of Ankhtepot faded from the Land of Reeds and Lotuses, the high priest’s bindings rotted away, and Ankhtepot crawled forth from his sarcophagus. He emerged from his tomb in an unfamiliar land: Har’Akir.

In this new land, Ankhtepot found a pious people devoted to the same gods he once served. Over generations, he wiped out that religion, replacing it with false divinities of his own imagining for whom he alone could speak. Ankhtepot also resurrected the priests buried alongside him as [**mummy lords**](#ref:monster:5195134-mummy-lord "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195134-mummy-lord"), replacing their heads with those of beasts and monsters holy to his new faith. These Children of Ankhtepot served him as they did in life, and together the dead conquered the souls of Har’Akir.

In the ages since, Ankhtepot hasn’t forged the land of his ambitions. His servants scheme against him, his people don’t flourish, and his monuments crumble to dust in mere centuries. Ankhtepot’s ambitions have withered. Now he seeks only to reclaim his soul and use it to put an end to his accursed immortality.

### Ankhtepot’s Domain {#rthw:harakir:AnkhtepotsDomain}

Har’Akir is altered by Ankhtepot’s presence, creating the following effects:

**Blistering Sun.** Any outdoor area of [**Bright Light**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#brightlight) in Har’Akir is an area of [extreme heat](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/dmg-2024/dms-toolbox#extremeheat) (see the [Dungeon Master’s Guide](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/dmg-2024)).

**Closing the Borders.** While in his domain, Ankhtepot can close or open the borders to Har’Akir at will. While the borders are closed, whirling sands fill the Mists surrounding Har’Akir. A creature that enters the Mists for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there takes 2d6 Slashing damage.

**Control Undead.** Undead of CR 5 or lower in Har’Akir have the [**Charmed**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#charmedcondition) condition and obey Ankhtepot’s orders.

If Ankhtepot dies, these effects end immediately.

### Ankhtepot’s Lair {#rthw:harakir:AnkhtepotsLair}

A mountain-size black pyramid, Ankhtepot’s tomb—called Pharaoh’s Rest—looms over the City of the Dead. It can be seen from all across Har’Akir.

#### Pharaoh’s Rest Features {#rthw:harakir:PharaohsRestFeatures}

Ancient and ornate, Pharaoh’s Rest holds countless carvings of mysterious deities and Ankhtepot as an idealized pharaoh. A labyrinth of trapped tombs, embalming rooms, and treasure chambers fills the majority of this massive pyramid. Broad paths used by Ankhtepot’s servants lead past deadly side passages to the heights of the monument. Prominent locations are depicted on [map 2.14](#rthw:harakir:map214pharaohsrest "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/harakir#map214pharaohsrest") and have the following features:

**Ankhtepot’s Tomb.** The burial treasures and reliefs lining Ankhtepot’s tomb’s walls are shattered, having suffered ages of Ankhtepot’s frustration. Hidden behind a bejeweled throne is a thoroughly defaced sarcophagus. Within, Ankhtepot awaits word of his ka’s discovery, rising only when disturbed by trespassers or at the call of servants from the funeral barge chamber below.

**Funeral Barge.** Ankhtepot envisions his trip to the afterlife taking place on a river. In an ornate ritual site, he has prepared a funeral barge and other ceremonial trappings necessary for his journey after his ka’s recovery.

**Lesser Tombs.** Throughout the pyramid are shrines, mummification chambers, and the crypts of Ankhtepot’s servants. These include the burial chambers of several Children of Ankhtepot and the Darklord’s son, Thutepot.

**Shrine of Ankhtepot.** A vast, open shrine holds ominous statues of Har’Akir’s gods and columns etched with exaggerated and fictitious events from Ankhtepot’s rule. On the night of the full moon, a hidden magical elevator activates, granting access to the tombs above.

## Adventures in Har’Akir {#rthw:harakir:AdventuresinHarAkir}

Adventures set in Har’Akir involve ancient secrets, manipulative cultists, the ancient dead, and the search for Ankhtepot’s missing ka. Use this section to develop horror adventures in this domain.

[![From the Temple of Ese, the priests of Pharaoh Ankhtepot control the people of Muhar (Artist: Maihope)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/08-004.temple-of-ese.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/08-004.temple-of-ese.png)

### Horror in Har’Akir {#rthw:harakir:HorrorinHarAkir}

Adventures in Har’Akir often include the following elements.

#### Children of Ankhtepot {#rthw:harakir:ChildrenofAnkhtepot}

Ankhtepot resurrected the priests who died alongside him as [**Mummy Lords**](#ref:monster:5195134-mummy-lord "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195134-mummy-lord"), granting each the head of an animal or monster corresponding to the fictitious gods he imposed on Har’Akir. The Children of Ankhtepot style themselves as harbingers of these gods while they manipulate cults or the domain’s priesthood. Some have grown tired of Ankhtepot’s detachment and seek to depose the pharaoh—particularly the treacherous mummy lord Senmet.

#### Gods of Har’Akir {#rthw:harakir:GodsofHarAkir}

Ankhtepot has destroyed all evidence of the deities the people of Har’Akir worshipped in ages past, replacing that pantheon with gods of his own creation, as summarized on the Gods of Har’Akir table.

**Gods of Har’Akir**

| God  | Animal         | Concern                    |
| ---- | -------------- | -------------------------- |
| Anu  | Jackal         | Judging the dead           |
| Ese  | Oryx           | Life and the living        |
| Neb  | Rust monster   | Passage from life to death |
| Oru  | Hydra          | Cosmic order               |
| Ousa | Raven          | Death and the dead         |
| Sek  | Dragonfly      | Healing and life           |
| Sute | Three-eyed cat | Despair and discord        |

#### Pharaoh’s Priests {#rthw:harakir:PharaohsPriests}

The priests of Har’Akir work Ankhtepot’s will, not realizing their deities are false. They keep alert for strangers and omens related to the treasure their pharaoh covets without knowing its true nature. Promising strangers are brought to High Priest Isu Rehkotep at the Temple of Ese in Muhar. The decadent high priest wants to possess what her pharaoh seeks, planning to use it to manipulate Ankhtepot.

#### Pharaoh’s Soul {#rthw:harakir:PharaohsSoul}

Ankhtepot seeks his ka, the missing piece of his soul. It’s up to you what form this takes. Roll on or choose a result from The Darklord’s Soul table to determine the form of Ankhtepot’s ka.

**The Darklord’s Soul**

| 1d8 | Ankhtepot’s Ka Is …                                                                                                                                          |
| --- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| 1   | An ankh holy to the old gods of Har’Akir.                                                                                                                    |
| 2   | A blessing granted to those who survive trials within the domain’s endless sandstorms.                                                                       |
| 3   | A canopic jar containing the pharaoh’s heart hidden within a forgotten tomb.                                                                                 |
| 4   | A hawk or giant eagle that circles the sun.                                                                                                                  |
| 5   | Manifested in a joyous song sung by Muhar’s people.                                                                                                          |
| 6   | Pieces of a jewel hidden within each of the Children of Ankhtepot.                                                                                           |
| 7   | The soul of a character, perhaps one with the Echoing Soul feat (see [chapter 1](#rthw:character-options:echoingsoul "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/character-options#echoingsoul")). |
| 8   | The spirit of an innocent healer who resembles the pharaoh as he was in life.                                                                                |

Once the Darklord recovers his ka, Ankhtepot can restore his soul by completing an elaborate 1-hour ritual involving the sacrifice of a living person. Only then might he journey to the afterlife—whether he succeeds is up to the Dark Powers.

[![Frightful monuments such as Ousa’s Pyramid rise from the haunted, black-sand deserts of Har’Akir (Artist: Bastien Grivet)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/08-005.ousas-pyramid.jpg)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/08-005.ousas-pyramid.jpg)

### Har’Akir Campaign Arc {#rthw:harakir:HarAkirCampaignArc}

Campaigns set in Har’Akir often involve the domain’s treacherous priests, its ancient tombs, and the hunt for Ankhtepot’s ka. A campaign here might follow this outline:

**Levels 1–4.** The characters help a priest named Basras search a trap-laden, buried palace complex for a mysterious treasure. Within, they discover a set of oversize canopic jars. They take them to Isu Rehkotep in Muhar, but the high priest deems them worthless. Basras is thrown into the Mouth of Oru.

**Levels 5–10.** Isu Rehkotep hires the characters to search for the pharaoh’s missing treasure. She sends them to Senmet’s Tomb to recover an ark full of ancient scrolls, claiming these are what the pharaoh desires. (She doesn’t actually know the object of the pharaoh’s search.)

**Levels 11–15.** After the characters return the scrolls to Isu, Basras (now an Undead), reveals that the high priest seeks to use them to control a [**Mummy Lord**](#ref:monster:5195134-mummy-lord "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195134-mummy-lord") and oppose Ankhtepot, as detailed in the “Scrolls of the Dead” adventure.

### Scrolls of the Dead {#rthw:harakir:ScrollsoftheDead}

Adventure for Level 12 Characters

**Situation.** High Priest Isu Rehkotep claims to have found the treasure Ankhtepot has been searching for and prepares to offer it to him during a ritual at the pyramid of Pharaoh’s Rest. In truth, she plans to use a scroll that controls the Child of Ankhtepot called Senmet to destroy the pharaoh and claim his throne.

**Hook.** The priest De’rah fears the pharaoh will vent his wrath on the people of Muhar when the high priest is discovered. She offers the characters 5,000 GP and a random magic item from the [Relics—Rare table](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/dmg-2024/random-magic-items#relicsrare) in the [Dungeon Master’s Guide](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/dmg-2024) if they stop Isu.

[![Map 2.14: Pharaoh’s Rest View Player Version (Artist: Mike Schley)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/map-08-02.pharohs-rest.jpg)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/map-08-02.pharohs-rest.jpg)

#### Encounters {#rthw:harakir:Encounters}

This adventure uses map 2.14 and consists of these encounters.

**_Exploring the Pyramid._** Rehkotep’s ritual takes place during the full moon, when the entrance to Pharaoh’s Rest stands open. Pharaoh’s Rest is a vast structure, but the path Rehkotep and her followers followed through the thick dust and sand of the lower reaches is obvious. Details of the pyramid’s lower levels are beyond the scope of this adventure.

**_Pyramid Heights._** When the characters reach the Shrine of Ankhtepot in the upper levels of Pharaoh’s Rest, and when they enter the Lesser Tombs, roll on the following table to determine what lurks within.

| 1d6 | Encounter                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| --- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1   | A [**Dao**](#ref:monster:5194958-dao "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5194958-dao") compelled to defend the pyramid                                                                                                             |
| 2   | Three [**Invisible Stalkers**](#ref:monster:5195089-invisible-stalker "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195089-invisible-stalker") that chant curses                                                                            |
| 3   | Four [**Mummies**](#ref:monster:5195135-mummy "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195135-mummy") and two [**Death Dogs**](#ref:monster:5194961-death-dog "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5194961-death-dog")                  |
| 4   | Two [**Mummies**](#ref:monster:5195135-mummy "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195135-mummy") and two [**Shield Guardians**](#ref:monster:5195204-shield-guardian "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195204-shield-guardian") |
| 5   | Two [**Stone Golems**](#ref:monster:4904850-stone-golem "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/4904850-stone-golem") dressed as pharaohs                                                                                              |
| 6   | Four [**Wraiths**](#ref:monster:5174960-wraith "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5174960-wraith") made of black sand                                                                                                             |

**_Ritual Site._** On the funeral barge level of the pyramid, Isu Rehkotep (Medium, Lawful Evil [**Archpriest**](#ref:monster:5194903-archpriest "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5194903-archpriest")) readies to call forth Ankhtepot from his tomb using a ritual involving a gong on the ceremonial ship. Meanwhile, two [**Priests**](#ref:monster:5195170-priest "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195170-priest") and two [**Death Cultists**](#ref:monster:5194960-death-cultist "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5194960-death-cultist") defend her. Isu avoids battle, but if any of her allies fall, she produces an ancient papyrus scroll and reads it, summoning Senmet.

**_The Mummy._** If Isu reads her scroll, 1 round after her allies are defeated, the [**Mummy Lord**](#ref:monster:5195134-mummy-lord "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195134-mummy-lord") Senmet appears. Isu orders him to destroy the characters, and he obeys. Senmet fights until he or the scroll the high priest holds is destroyed. Isu doesn’t join the battle and attempts to escape if Senmet is destroyed.

**_The Scroll._** A character adjacent to Isu can steal the scroll from her by succeeding on a DC 16 Dexterity ([**Sleight of Hand**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#skills)) check or by taking an action if she has the [**Incapacitated**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#incapacitatedcondition) or [**Restrained**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#restrainedcondition) condition. Any character can take an action to destroy the scroll but can’t use it to command Senmet. If it is destroyed, Senmet turns [**Hostile**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#hostileattitude) toward Isu.

**_The Pharaoh._** Once Isu and Senmet are dealt with, [**Ankhtepot**](#ref:monster:6491339-ankhtepot "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491339-ankhtepot") (see earlier in [this chapter](#rthw:harakir:Ankhtepot "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/harakir#Ankhtepot")) appears at the path leading up to his tomb. He demands the characters depart immediately but return with his missing ka. If they do so, fabulous riches will be theirs. If they don’t, they will know his wrath. Characters who escape the tomb after the encounter with Ankhtepot earn a bonus 4,700 XP.

<CHAPTER id="rthw:hazlan" title="Hazlan">

# Hazlan {#rthw:hazlan:Hazlan}

Domain Doomed by Magic

> #### **Darklord:** [Hazlik](#rthw:hazlan:Hazlik "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/hazlan#Hazlik") {#rthw:hazlan:Hazlik}
>
> **Genres:** [Dark fantasy](#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:darkfantasy "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/creating-domains-of-dread#darkfantasy") and [disaster horror](#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:disasterhorror "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/creating-domains-of-dread#disasterhorror")
>
> **Hallmarks:** Amoral spellcasters, magical experiments, magic-ravaged environment, wild magic
>
> **Mist Talismans:** Eye of Hazlik amulet, gremishka foot, scrap from a red robe
>
> **Aligned Tarokka Card:** Diviner
>
> **Opposed Tarokka Card:** Ghost

[![(Artist: Pam Wishbow)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/09-001.diviner-tarokka.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/09-001.diviner-tarokka.png) [![](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/09-002.ghost-tarokka.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/09-002.ghost-tarokka.png)

Hazlan is a domain drained of vitality, frayed by magical disasters, and overrun with abominations. Here the amoral, spellcasting elite have so exploited magic that it’s turned erratic and dangerous to use.

Encouraging these magical abuses is [**Hazlik**](#ref:monster:6491361-hazlik "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491361-hazlik"), the domain’s zulkir, a title meaning wizard-overlord. The Darklord postures as the domain’s most powerful wizard and views all others as either apprentices or test subjects. All the while, Hazlik hides the fact that he’s lost the ability to learn new magic. Paranoid and controlling, Hazlik constantly spies on those in his domain through the Eyes of Hazlik. These pervasive, eye-shaped symbols appear on structures, decorations, clothing, and individuals across the domain—and through these eyes, the Darklord watches. Hazlik surveils his domain endlessly, reveling in the fear of his people, encouraging rivalries between his apprentices, and searching for magical innovations he can claim as his own.

## Domain Features {#rthw:hazlan:DomainFeatures}

Hazlan is known for the following features:

**Eye of Hazlik.** Inhabitants claim the eyelike design called the Eye of Hazlik bears Hazlik’s blessing and wards off dangerous magic. In truth, the symbol is a sensor for Hazlik’s magical surveillance.

**Magocracy.** The wizard [Hazlik](#rthw:hazlan:Hazlik "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/hazlan#Hazlik") rules Hazlan. His apprentices have free rein to exploit the land and its people to further their magical experiments.

**Shattered by Magic.** The effects of magical disasters disfigure the domain, poisoning rivers with alchemical runoff, scarring the land with magical blasts, and unleashing unpredictable hazards.

**Wild Magic.** Magic is unreliable in Hazlan, resulting in dangerous side effects (see “[Hazlan Wild Magic](#rthw:hazlan:hazlanwildmagic "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/hazlan#hazlanwildmagic")”).

## Locations in Hazlan {#rthw:hazlan:LocationsinHazlan}

Magical disasters and supernatural environments make Hazlan’s arid landscape even deadlier and its natural rock monuments even stranger. The settlements of Sly-Var and Toyalis are described below, and other notable locations are summarized on the [Hazlan Locations table](#rthw:hazlan:hazlanlocations "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/hazlan#hazlanlocations").

### Sly-Var {#rthw:hazlan:SlyVar}

In Sly-Var, mages obsessed with earning the Darklord’s favor raise architecturally discordant towers that defy physical laws. The residents magically create whatever they need, resulting in little need for trade. This leaves the labyrinthine streets and knotted bridges between intertwined compounds eerily empty. The few common folk who traverse these surreal streets often disappear—the victims of magical guardians or of wizards who see the magically deficient as stock for their experiments.

### Toyalis {#rthw:hazlan:Toyalis}

The largest town in Hazlan, Toyalis boasts a population of poor, hardworking commoners united by terror of the domain’s magic-using elite. Colorful depictions of magical creatures, arcane symbols, and the Eye of Hazlik cover the town’s rough wooden and adobe structures. Every few weeks, one of Hazlik’s apprentices leads a procession of attendants and magical wonders to Toyalis in search of replacement servants, new apprentices, or stock for magical experiments. A carnival atmosphere ensues, with the apprentice displaying their magical accomplishments and setting up competitions to assess the locals’ capabilities—magical or otherwise. When a mage’s procession leaves, it takes townsfolk deemed valuable with it.

[![Map 2.15: Hazlan View Player Version (Artist: Marco Bernardini)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/map-09-01.hazlan.jpg)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/map-09-01.hazlan.jpg)

**Hazlan Locations**

| Location          | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Balsam Wood       | A plant at the center of the dense Balsam Wood can cure any illness. Unnervingly, the forest is alive, aware, and prone to agony, screaming if someone disturbs so much as a leaf.                                                                                 |
| The Brew          | Alchemical pollution from the village of Ramulai has poisoned the toxic marsh now known as the Brew. Creeks and bogs often erupt with violent fungal creatures and magical eﬀects.                                                                                 |
| Fallen Sisters    | The Fallen Sisters are three mountains that have collapsed into triangular, bottomless pits. Vistani often camp here.                                                                                                                                              |
| Fleshless Forest  | Plants and creatures in the Fleshless Forest were turned to stone. The condition is infectious.                                                                                                                                                                    |
| The Lacuna        | The Lacuna is a region of knee-high mists that reach toward places of powerful magic, such as Hazlik’s palace, Veneficus. Anyone who steps into these mists vanishes, and few reemerge.                                                                            |
| The Marks         | The sigils of Hazlik’s mightiest apprentices mark the land in giant, magic-enhancing geoglyphs. The Lacuna grows toward these Marks—and a fourth, mysterious glyph.                                                                                                |
| Moonstone Valley  | Meteors and otherworldly creatures crash into this wasteland during every new moon.                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Mound of the Worm | Earth from deep underground rose to form the Mound of the Worm mesa, unleashing dozens of [**Purple Worms**](#ref:monster:5195174-purple-worm "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195174-purple-worm"). The aged, albino worm Gravedrinker dominates this region. |
| Orbitoclasts      | The Orbitoclasts are floating rock formations that resemble lobotomy tools. Their pointed ends align toward the nearest magic-user.                                                                                                                                |
| Philosopher’s Egg | A cult of magic-warped beings worships an eight-story, citrine egg. The cult searches for a prophet who’s never been touched by magic to release the antimagic entity within.                                                                                      |
| The Playas        | Former lakes, the Playas are now quicksand-riddled [**Purple Worm**](#ref:monster:5195174-purple-worm "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195174-purple-worm") feeding grounds.                                                                                   |
| Ramulai           | Mines near the village of Ramulai yield rare magical elements. Refineries process these volatile resources, but in so doing, they magically sicken the people and the land.                                                                                        |
| Seething          | The lifeless Seething region crumbles away into the Mists. A heavy footfall can break its surface.                                                                                                                                                                 |

## Hazlik {#rthw:hazlan:Hazlik}

Darklord of Desperation and Magical Disaster

[![(Artist: Marianne Khalil)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/09-003.hazlik.jpg)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/09-003.hazlik.jpg)

> “You’re new, I can tell. Impress me, and maybe I’ll let you be my newest apprentice.”
>
> —Hazlik

The paranoid, egomaniacal archmage Hazlik clings to his power despite his magical ambitions being supernaturally smothered. Since Hazlik entered Hazlan, his magic has become unstable. Spells he casts behave erratically and fade swiftly—most lasting no more than an hour—while his magical creations fall apart in about a day. The idea of others learning this terrifies the Darklord, which leads him to claim others’ works as his own, spy on potential rivals, and order reckless research into the nature of magic and his domain.

Hazlik suffers vivid nightmares wherein past rivals taunt and torment him. The Darklord avoids sleeping, employing magical tinctures to stay awake, but this causes him to vacillate between bouts of exhaustion, jitters, and paranoia.

Hazlik knows that his domain is being ripped apart by magical disasters—many of his own creation. He openly denies the realm’s devastation, though, his fear of cascading ruin clashing with his inability to admit he’s wrong.

### [Hazlik](#ref:monster:6491361-hazlik "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491361-hazlik") {#rthw:hazlan:Hazlikrefmonster6491361hazlikhttpswwwdndbeyondcommonsters6491361hazlik}

Medium Humanoid (Human, Wizard), Chaotic Evil

**AC** 16 **Initiative** +13 (23)

**HP** 154 (28d8 + 28)

**Speed** 30 ft.

**Immunities** Psychic; [**Charmed**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#charmedcondition) (with [**Mind Blank**](#ref:spell:2619036-mind-blank "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619036-mind-blank"))

#### Traits {#rthw:hazlan:Traits}

**_Darklord Restoration._** If Hazlik dies, he revives with all his Hit Points in 1d10 weeks somewhere in Hazlan.

**_Legendary Resistance (3/Day, or 4/Day in Domain)._** If Hazlik fails a saving throw, he can choose to succeed instead.

**_Magic Resistance._** Hazlik has [**Advantage**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#advantage) on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

#### Actions {#rthw:hazlan:Actions}

**_Multiattack._** Hazlik makes three Arcane Burst attacks.

**_Arcane Burst._** _Melee or Ranged Attack Roll:_ +10, reach 5 ft. or range 150 ft. _Hit:_ 21 (3d10 + 5) Force damage.

**_Spellcasting._** Hazlik casts one of the following spells, using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 18):

**At Will:** [**Detect Magic**](#ref:spell:2619097-detect-magic "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619097-detect-magic"), [**Detect Thoughts**](#ref:spell:2619099-detect-thoughts "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619099-detect-thoughts"), [**Disguise Self**](#ref:spell:2619102-disguise-self "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619102-disguise-self"), [**Invisibility**](#ref:spell:2619116-invisibility "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619116-invisibility"), [**Light**](#ref:spell:2618996-light "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618996-light"), [**Mage Armor**](#ref:spell:2619006-mage-armor "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619006-mage-armor") (included in AC), [**Mage Hand**](#ref:spell:2619008-mage-hand "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619008-mage-hand"), [**Prestidigitation**](#ref:spell:2618893-prestidigitation "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618893-prestidigitation")

**2/Day Each:** [**Fly**](#ref:spell:2618909-fly "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618909-fly"), [**Lightning Bolt**](#ref:spell:2618999-lightning-bolt "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618999-lightning-bolt") (level 5 version)

**1/Day Each:** [**Cone of Cold**](#ref:spell:2619042-cone-of-cold "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619042-cone-of-cold"), [**Mind Blank**](#ref:spell:2619036-mind-blank "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619036-mind-blank") (cast before combat), [**Scrying**](#ref:spell:2619007-scrying "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619007-scrying"), [**Teleport**](#ref:spell:2619163-teleport "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619163-teleport")

#### Bonus Actions {#rthw:hazlan:BonusActions}

**_Wild Magic Surge._** Hazlik manifests one of the following magic surges, targeting a creature he can see within 120 feet. While [**Bloodied**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#bloodied), Hazlik manifests two surges (roll 1d4; reroll if Hazlik has already used that surge during this turn):

**1: Misty Movement.** Hazlik can teleport the target up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space he can see on a surface or liquid large enough to support the target.

**2: Eye Blight.** _Constitution Saving Throw:_ DC 18. _Failure:_ The target has the [**Blinded**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#blindedcondition) condition until the end of its next turn.

**3: Mind Flare.** _Intelligence Saving Throw:_ DC 18. _Failure:_ 13 (2d12) Psychic damage, and the target can’t take the [**Magic**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#magicaction) action until the end of its next turn.

**4: Implode.** _Dexterity Saving Throw:_ DC 18. _Failure:_ The target takes 10 (3d6) Force damage. _Failure or Success:_ Each creature within 5 feet of the target takes 10 (3d6) Force damage.

#### Reactions {#rthw:hazlan:Reactions}

**_Protective Magic (3/Day)._** Hazlik casts [**Counterspell**](#ref:spell:2619072-counterspell "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619072-counterspell") or [**Shield**](#ref:spell:2619019-shield "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619019-shield") in response to the spell’s trigger, using the same spellcasting ability as Spellcasting.

#### Legendary Actions {#rthw:hazlan:LegendaryActions}

Legendary Action Uses: 3 (4 in Domain). Immediately after another creature’s turn, Hazlik can expend a use to take one of the following actions. Hazlik regains all expended uses at the start of each of his turns.

**_Arcane Strike._** Hazlik makes one Arcane Burst attack.

**_Arcane Teleport._** Hazlik teleports up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space he can see, and each creature within 10 feet of the space he left takes 11 (2d10) Force damage. Hazlik can’t take this action again until the start of his next turn.

### Hazlik’s Tale {#rthw:hazlan:HazliksTale}

On the world of Toril, Hazlik rose among the ranks of the merciless Red Wizards of Thay. Arrogant and convinced mortality was a weakness, he sought hidden truths of magic, ways to visit realms within the psyche, and command of reality.

As Hazlik’s power increased, he developed rivalries with other Red Wizards, many of which ended with his foes magically scarred. But one rival Hazlik couldn’t defeat: the wizard Indreficus. Hazlik gradually came to obsess over Indreficus, viewing him as his only worthy opponent. Indreficus shared Hazlik’s genius and arrogance, and they spent seasons as vicious adversaries and passionate lovers. They drove one another to feats of magical brilliance both revolutionary and unspeakable. This culminated when Hazlik discovered that Indreficus planned to betray Hazlik to garner the favor of Thay’s ruling zulkirs. Heartbroken and enraged, Hazlik captured Indreficus and subjected him to nightmarish magical manipulations that permanently transformed him into a pain-wracked, living magical portal. Hazlik presented his creation to the zulkirs, hoping to gain their patronage

The zulkirs revealed that Indreficus hadn’t betrayed Hazlik. Rather, the ruling mages had watched the pair’s ascent and, wary of their ambitions, undermined them before they became threats. Moreover, they deemed Hazlik’s transformation of Indreficus an abomination. As punishment, the zulkirs decreed that every mage Hazlik had scarred could do the same in return to him, marking him with their personal symbols. As the first brand-wielding member of the mob of Hazlik’s rivals closed on the wizard, Hazlik fled through the groaning portal that was Indreficus.

Hazlik emerged amid the pain-wracked dreamscapes of Indreficus. Unwittingly, Hazlik had entered the Domain of Dread known as the [Nightmare Lands](#rthw:other-domains-of-dread:NightmareLands "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/other-domains-of-dread#NightmareLands"), where Indreficus’s shrieking and condemnation hounded him. After months of torment, Hazlik escaped into the Mists and eventually emerged into a realm that knew nothing of magic. His Thayan tattoos had turned gold and warped into symbols meaning “traitor.” Undaunted, Hazlik used his magic to dominate the people of this new realm, claiming the title of zulkir and dubbing his realm Hazlan.

### Hazlik’s Domain {#rthw:hazlan:HazliksDomain}

Hazlan is altered by Hazlik’s presence, creating the following effects:

**Closing the Borders.** While in his domain, Hazlik can close or open the borders to Hazlan at will. While the borders are closed, the Mists surrounding Hazlan are filled with monstrous magical experiments. A creature that enters the Mists for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there must succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw or take 5 (1d10) Force damage and have the [**Restrained**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#restrainedcondition) condition until the start of its next turn. A creature makes this save only once per turn.

**Frayed Magic.** Whenever a creature (excluding Hazlik and his allies) casts a spell using a level 5+ spell slot, it rolls on the [Wild Magic Surge table](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/character-classes-continued#wildmagicsurge) in the [Player’s Handbook](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024) to create a magical effect.

**Magic Nightmares.** While in his lair, Veneficus, Hazlik can cast [**Clairvoyance**](#ref:spell:2618972-clairvoyance "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618972-clairvoyance"), requiring no spell components and using the same spellcasting ability as his Spellcasting action. When the spell is cast this way, its range is all of Hazlan, Hazlik can see but can’t hear through the sensor, and the sensor can appear only on an Eye of Hazlik.

If [Hazlik](#rthw:hazlan:hazlikstatblock "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/hazlan#hazlikstatblock") dies, these effects end immediately. The effects resume if Hazlik gains a new body (see his Darklord Restoration trait).

### Hazlik’s Lair {#rthw:hazlan:HazliksLair}

Hazlik’s crimson-towered palace, Veneficus, stands atop the jagged mesa called the Red Rise. The Darklord is attended by a staff of magical creations and his most accomplished apprentices.

#### Veneficus Features {#rthw:hazlan:VeneficusFeatures}

Veneficus is littered with frivolous magic effects and magic items that no longer keep Hazlik’s attention. The site is depicted on [map 2.16](#rthw:hazlan:map216veneficus "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/hazlan#map216veneficus") and has the following features:

**Halls of Triumph.** Multiple audience chambers, display galleries, and pleasure gardens rival one another in decadence, each exhibiting grotesque artwork and trophies of Hazlik’s achievements.

**House of Solitude.** The secluded House of Solitude is magically locked, and Hazlik forbids anyone from entering. At night, muffled screams and flickering lights emanate from within.

**Red Tower.** Hazlik’s personal chambers fill the Red Tower. Magical portals connect the untold numbers of demiplanar chambers that make up the tower. Somewhere within lies Hazlik’s orrery, a multistory magical device that allows the Darklord to see through any Eye of Hazlik in the domain.

## Adventures in Hazlan {#rthw:hazlan:AdventuresinHazlan}

Tales in Hazlan involve radical magical experiments, supernatural environments, rivalries between mages, and magical surveillance. Use this section to develop horror adventures in this domain.

[![The Eye of Hazlik watches the city of Sly-Var and the approaching retinue of one of the Darklord’s apprentices (Artist: Sam Keiser)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/09-004.eye-of-hazlik.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/09-004.eye-of-hazlik.png)

### Horror in Hazlan {#rthw:hazlan:HorrorinHazlan}

Adventures set in Hazlan often include the following elements.

#### Eyes of Hazlik {#rthw:hazlan:EyesofHazlik}

Hazlik spies on his domain’s inhabitants using the Eye of Hazlik. This eyelike sigil adorns buildings, clothing, talismans, and creatures across the domain. Locals claim the symbol protects them from dangerous magic and creatures. Hazlik uses the eyes to spy on useful or threatening mages and to reinforce his reputation as an ever-present overlord.

Hazlik often sends loyal apprentices or magical creatures to capture those whose behavior witnessed through the eyes offended him. He turns such individuals into fodder for experimentation in Sly-Var or Veneficus.

#### Hazlan Wild Magic {#rthw:hazlan:HazlanWildMagic}

As a result of unchecked arcane experimentation, magic functions erratically in Hazlan. Whenever a creature in Hazlan expends a spell slot to cast a spell or activates a magic item, it rolls 1d10. On a 1, it unleashes a random magical effect. Roll on the [Wild Magic Surge table](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/character-classes-continued#wildmagicsurge) in chapter 3 of the [Player’s Handbook](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024) to determine the effect. Consider describing these results in unsettling ways that don’t change their effects, as in these examples:

- Summoned creatures use the proscribed stat blocks but are cosmetically warped to resemble undead or aberrant creatures.
- Effects that teleport the caster relocate the caster into a misty expanse full of threatening shapes.
- Effects on creatures cause unsettling sensations, such as the feeling of earwigs wriggling beneath one’s skin or one’s teeth struggling free.

Anyone who openly wears an Eye of Hazlik can choose not to roll on the Wild Magic Surge table in this way once per day.

#### Hazlik’s Apprentices {#rthw:hazlan:HazliksApprentices}

Dozens of mages serve as Hazlik’s apprentices. Between infrequent, demeaning group lessons with the Darklord, these apprentices pit themselves against one another to impress Hazlik by pushing the boundaries of magical innovation. Those who gain Hazlik’s favor are promised arcane secrets known only to the Darklord—secrets that might not exist. This creates a cadre of Hazlani mages who recklessly seek to impress Hazlik by the following means, among others:

- Changing the nature of reality to suit their whims
- Creating monuments in Hazlik’s honor
- Devising new magic items, spells, or supernatural materials
- Forging unique magical servants for Hazlik
- Stealing rare magic items
- Unleashing dramatic displays of magical might

Hazlik’s current favorite apprentices include the masked wizard Yhal the Skygazer, the shadow-cloaked Ruzelo, and the daring genius Eleni.

### Hazlan Campaign Arc {#rthw:hazlan:HazlanCampaignArc}

Campaigns set in Hazlan often involve mages abusing their power to garner Hazlik’s fickle favor. A campaign here might follow this outline:

**Levels 1–3.** The characters arrive in Toyalis, where servants of the mage Khrinitov abduct locals with supposed psychic potential. Eleni, an apprentice of Hazlik, believes Khrinitov’s experiments are pointless. She hires the characters to rescue the villagers from Khrinitov’s tower amid the Orbitoclasts. In doing so, the characters reveal Khrinitov to be an [**Intellect Devourer**](#ref:monster:5195088-intellect-devourer "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195088-intellect-devourer"), a [**Brain in a Jar**](#ref:monster:6491344-brain-in-a-jar "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491344-brain-in-a-jar") (see [chapter 5](#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:braininajar "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/denizens-of-the-mists#braininajar")), or another aberrant being.

**Levels 4–8.** Eleni reveals that she’s trying to undermine Hazlik and protect the people of Hazlan. She tells the characters of a magic mineral in the Mound of the Worm that [**Purple Worms**](#ref:monster:5195174-purple-worm "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195174-purple-worm") pursue. She encourages the party to collect the mineral and use the purple worms to destroy locations like the Marks. As the characters do so, they face magical guardians and hazards. During their travel, they’re exposed to strange magic and might gain Dark Gift feats (see [chapter 1](#rthw:character-options:darkgifts "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/character-options#darkgifts")).

**Levels 9–12.** Eleni asks the characters to come to Sly-Var to plan a raid on Hazlik’s palace. There, she reveals that she’s been exposing them to dangerous magic from across the domain. She entraps them with a portal that leads to arena-like laboratories connected to Veneficus, where [**Hazlik**](#ref:monster:6491361-hazlik "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491361-hazlik") pits them against terrors his other apprentices have created. The characters must escape, potentially facing Eleni and Hazlik along the way.

### Eyes of the Darklord {#rthw:hazlan:EyesoftheDarklord}

Adventure for Level 10 Characters

**Situation.** Subjects of magical experimentation seek to escape Hazlan, but every time they try, they’re spotted through the Eyes of Hazlik, and the Darklord’s apprentices hunt them down.

**Hook.** Allies hire the characters to help them escape Hazlan by destroying Hazlik’s orrery in Veneficus. They offer to pay the party 4,000 GP once they’re guided to another domain.

[![Map 2.16: Veneficus View Player Version (Artist: Mike Schley)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/map-09-02.veneficus.jpg)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/map-09-02.veneficus.jpg)

#### Encounters {#rthw:hazlan:Encounters}

The adventure uses map 2.16 and consists of these encounters:

**_Greeting at Veneficus._** The rooms within Veneficus (see map 2.16) and the walls outside all bear at least one Eye of Hazlik. If the characters are spotted, one of Hazlik’s former apprentices (Medium, Chaotic Evil [**Archmage**](#ref:monster:5194902-archmage "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5194902-archmage")) appears. This apprentice has been transformed to look and behave like the Darklord. The duplicate belittles the characters and fights to the death.

**_Galleries of Suffering._** As the characters explore Veneficus, roll on the following table to determine what they find within.

| 1d6 | Encounter                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| --- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1   | Another [**Archmage**](#ref:monster:5194902-archmage "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5194902-archmage") that behaves like Hazlik (see above), or a similarly disguised [**Incubus**](#ref:monster:4904793-incubus "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/4904793-incubus") |
| 2   | Artwork that releases a [**Bone Devil**](#ref:monster:5194930-bone-devil "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5194930-bone-devil") if touched                                                                                                                                |
| 3   | Three [**Mages**](#ref:monster:4831023-mage "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/4831023-mage") arguing about who’s greatest                                                                                                                                                 |
| 4   | Three [**Waxworks**](#ref:monster:6491401-waxwork "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491401-waxwork") (see [chapter 5](#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:waxwork "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/denizens-of-the-mists#waxwork")) disguised as mages arguing about who’s Hazlik’s favorite                |
| 5   | One [**Stone Golem**](#ref:monster:4904850-stone-golem "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/4904850-stone-golem") sculpted to look like Hazlik                                                                                                                               |
| 6   | Flawed Magic (see below)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |

**_Flawed Magic._** Among mundane decorations, this room contains a random magic item. Roll on the [Arcana—Common table](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/dmg-2024/random-magic-items#arcanacommon) in chapter 7 of the [Dungeon Master’s Guide](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/dmg-2024). The item functions once, causes a wild magic surge (see “[Hazlan Wild Magic](#rthw:hazlan:hazlanwildmagic "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/hazlan#hazlanwildmagic")”), and then crumbles to dust.

**_Red Tower._** Shifting portals connect the passages in the Red Tower. Every time the characters pass through a portal in the tower, roll 1d8. If the number rolled is lower than the number of portals passed through, the characters arrive in the orrery chamber. On an 8, the characters appear at the entrance to Veneficus.

**_Orrery Chamber._** This room is dominated by a magical orrery only Hazlik can use. It is defended by a [**Relentless Juggernaut**](#ref:monster:6491383-relentless-juggernaut "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491383-relentless-juggernaut") (see [chapter 5](#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:relentlessjuggernaut "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/denizens-of-the-mists#relentlessjuggernaut")). The orrery has AC 19, HP 25, and Immunity to Psychic damage. Every time the orrery takes damage, roll on the [Wild Magic Surge table](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/character-classes-continued#wildmagicsurge) in chapter 3 of the [Player’s Handbook](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024). Negative effects affect the character who damaged the orrery, while beneficial effects affect the juggernaut.

**_Hazlik._** After the orrery is destroyed, [**Hazlik**](#ref:monster:6491361-hazlik "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491361-hazlik") (see earlier in [this chapter](#rthw:hazlan:Hazlik "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/hazlan#Hazlik")) appears and offers a magic-using character power and influence as his apprentice. If the character accepts, he commands that character to murder the others. If the character declines, Hazlik mocks the party. The Darklord uses magic to flee if he takes any damage, swearing revenge. Characters who destroy the orrery and escape Veneficus earn a bonus 3,100 XP.

</CHAPTER>

<CHAPTER id="rthw:innsmouth" title="Innsmouth">

# Innsmouth {#rthw:innsmouth:Innsmouth}

Domain of the Imprisoned Apocalyptic

> #### **Darklord:** [Cthulhu](#rthw:innsmouth:Cthulhu "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/innsmouth#Cthulhu") {#rthw:innsmouth:Cthulhu}
>
> **Genre:** [Cosmic horror](#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:cosmichorror "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/creating-domains-of-dread#cosmichorror")
>
> **Hallmarks:** Cosmic horror creatures, invasive alien dreams, surreal locations, warring cults
>
> **Mist Talismans:** Effigy of Great Cthulhu, starmetal rod or amulet with eldritch runes, sahuagin-tooth fishing lure
>
> **Aligned Tarokka Card:** Bishop
>
> **Opposed Tarokka Card:** Donjon

[![(Artist: Pam Wishbow)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/10-001.bishop-tarokka.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/10-001.bishop-tarokka.png) [![](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/10-002.donjon-tarokka.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/10-002.donjon-tarokka.png)

Hidden amid the Domains of Dread lies a hideous realm defiant of reason and smothered by the Mists. From a violent, murky sea rises a crescent of shattered peaks, mangled spires broken like the jaws of some slain thalassic titan. From noxious fumaroles, miasmic pillars lurch from this accursed isle into a sky inconsistently lit by a distant, drowned light.

Strange ruins dot this island’s rocky coasts, some suggestive of forgotten peoples, others alien in form and purpose. Massive statues of crimson-flecked bloodstone loom over sheer cliffs, each a towering effigy of some profane monstrosity or alien god. One shore bears the wreckage of a few dozen collapsing wooden structures. Little evidence remains of this settlement’s residents, but at its edge lies a toppled sign bearing a word in Common that gives the island its name: Innsmouth.

Despite its forsaken appearance, the isle of Innsmouth isn’t abandoned. Cults vie for control of the island, among them the servants of Great Cthulhu, a harbinger of world-rending aberrance. At the island’s hidden heart, [**Cthulhu**](#ref:monster:6491348-cthulhu "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491348-cthulhu") lies dreaming, its alien mind reaching across the Domains of Dread and beyond, drawing to it those who might rouse its full might and unleash it from its prison in the Mists.

## Domain Features {#rthw:innsmouth:DomainFeatures}

Innsmouth is known for the following features:

**Cosmic Horror Visions.** Cthulhu’s dreams draw aberrant beings and shape Innsmouth as an amalgamation of cosmic horrors, from disparate ruins on the surface to stranger realms in the depths.

**Cult Haven.** Evil cults devoted to the entities Cthulhu, Dagon, Olhydra, and Zhudun struggle to control the domain. These cults view strangers as useful allies (see “[Cults of Innsmouth](#rthw:innsmouth:CultsofInnsmouth "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/innsmouth#CultsofInnsmouth")” for details).

**Dreams of Cthulhu.** [Cthulhu](#rthw:innsmouth:Cthulhu "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/innsmouth#Cthulhu") seeks freedom. It manipulates the dreams of those on the island, sharing visions of their escape from the domain resulting from the same rituals that would free it.

## Locations in Innsmouth {#rthw:innsmouth:LocationsinInnsmouth}

Innsmouth is an inhospitable expanse of alien mountains and ruin-littered coasts. The village of Innsmouth and the mazelike Vaults are described below, and other notable locations are summarized on the [Innsmouth Locations table](#rthw:innsmouth:innsmouthlocations "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/innsmouth#innsmouthlocations").

The ruined coastal village of Innsmouth is the most obvious shelter from the storms, alien creatures, and strange events on the island. The Cult of the Chthonic Night knows this and realizes its imprisoned master, Great Cthulhu, calls to strangers to aid the cultists in releasing it. This makes the ruined village a shadowy war zone, where cultists and their servants hunt for fresh acolytes and sacrifices.

### The Vaults {#rthw:innsmouth:TheVaults}

Beneath the mountains of Innsmouth winds a labyrinth of improbable passages. Dramatic caverns narrow into the corridors of buried palaces that transform into the wooden halls of forgotten farmhouses. Regularly, these underground paths open into vast cavities, many with their own strange environments, weather, and celestial bodies. What lies among the Vaults? Cultists speak of the realms of alien beings, ghoul empires, countrysides ravaged by sapient energies, the dwellings of reclusive witches, and a thin place in the walls of the prison where Great Cthulhu lies trapped.

## Cthulhu {#rthw:innsmouth:Cthulhu}

Darklord What Eternal Lies

[![(Artist: Brian Valenzuela)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/10-003.cthulhu.jpg)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/10-003.cthulhu.jpg)

> #### “Ph’nglui mglw’nafh Cthulhu R’lyeh wgah’nagl fhtagn.” {#rthw:innsmouth:cthulhu:PhngluimglwnafhCthulhuRlyehwgahnaglfhtagn}
>
> —Cult of the Chthonic Night chant

Cthulhu was—and inevitably will be once more—a threat to the entire multiverse. For untold ages, the Dark Powers have bound this harbinger of doom. Unlike the other prisoners of the Domains of Dread, Cthulhu isn’t plagued by ironic torments or thwarted ambitions. Rather, this ageless terror remains physically bound and can exert only a fraction of its terrible might. Nevertheless, Cthulhu’s dreams slip beyond its prison, manipulating minds and orchestrating events to ensure its release and a new epoch of multiversal doom.

### [Cthulhu](#ref:monster:6491348-cthulhu "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491348-cthulhu") {#rthw:innsmouth:Cthulhurefmonster6491348cthulhuhttpswwwdndbeyondcommonsters6491348cthulhu}

Gargantuan Aberration, Chaotic Evil

**AC** 19 **Initiative** +9 (19)

**HP** 385 (22d20 + 154)

**Speed** 30 ft., Climb 30 ft., Swim 60 ft.
