#### Traits {#rthw:innsmouth:Traits}

**_Amphibious._** Cthulhu can breathe air and water.

**_Darklord Restoration._** If Cthulhu dies, it revives with all its Hit Points in 1d10 weeks inside the Vault of Cthulhu.

**_Impossible Geometry._** Ground, air, and water in a 10-foot [**Emanation**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#emanationareaofeffect) originating from Cthulhu is [**Difficult Terrain**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#difficultterrain). A creature that starts its turn in the Emanation takes 7 (2d6) Bludgeoning damage.

**_Legendary Resistance (4/Day, or 5/Day in Domain)._** If Cthulhu fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

**_Magic Resistance._** Cthulhu has [**Advantage**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#advantage) on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

#### Actions {#rthw:innsmouth:Actions}

**_Multiattack._** Cthulhu makes three Eldritch Claw attacks and uses Spellcasting to cast [**Befuddlement**](#ref:spell:2618832-befuddlement "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618832-befuddlement") if available or [**Mind Spike**](#ref:spell:2619038-mind-spike "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619038-mind-spike") (level 4 version). It can replace one Eldritch Claw attack with a use of Tentacle.

**_Eldritch Claw._** _Melee Attack Roll:_ +17, reach 10 ft. _Hit:_ 18 (2d8 + 9) Slashing damage plus 9 (2d8) Acid damage. If the target is a Large or smaller creature, it has the [**Grappled**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#grappledcondition) condition (escape DC 19) from one of two limbs.

**_Spellcasting._** Cthulhu casts one of the following spells, requiring no spell components and using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 25):

**At Will:** [**Mind Spike**](#ref:spell:2619038-mind-spike "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619038-mind-spike") (level 4 version)

**3/Day Each:** [**Dream**](#ref:spell:2619156-dream "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619156-dream"), [**Geas**](#ref:spell:2618940-geas "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618940-geas") (can target creatures through dreams)

**1/Day Each:** [**Befuddlement**](#ref:spell:2618832-befuddlement "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618832-befuddlement"), [**Plane Shift**](#ref:spell:2618867-plane-shift "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618867-plane-shift") (self only)

**_Tentacle._** _Constitution Saving Throw:_ DC 25, one creature [**Grappled**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#grappledcondition) by Cthulhu. _Failure:_ 21 (6d6) Acid damage plus 13 (3d8) Psychic damage. _Success:_ Half damage. _Failure or Success:_ The target’s Hit Point maximum decreases by an amount equal to the Psychic damage taken, and Cthulhu regains Hit Points equal to that amount.

#### Bonus Actions {#rthw:innsmouth:BonusActions}

**_Warp._** Cthulhu teleports to an unoccupied space it can see within 120 feet, taking creatures it is [**grappling**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#grappledcondition) with it. Then each creature within 10 feet of the space it left is subjected to the following effect. _Strength Saving Throw:_ DC 25. _Failure:_ 7 (2d6) Bludgeoning damage plus 7 (2d6) Thunder damage, and if the target is a Large or smaller creature, it has the [**Prone**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#pronecondition) condition. _Success:_ Half damage only.

#### Legendary Actions {#rthw:innsmouth:LegendaryActions}

Legendary Action Uses: 3 (4 in Domain). Immediately after another creature’s turn, Cthulhu can expend a use to take one of the following actions. Cthulhu regains all expended uses at the start of each of its turns.

**_Clamp._** Cthulhu makes an Eldritch Claw attack.

**_Fold Space._** _Charisma Saving Throw:_ DC 25, each creature and object that isn’t being worn or carried in a 10-foot-radius [**Sphere**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#sphereareaofeffect) centered on a point Cthulhu can see within 60 feet. _Failure:_ 36 (8d8) Force damage, and the target is teleported to an unoccupied space within 60 feet of Cthulhu that is horizontal to it. _Success:_ Half damage only. _Failure or Success:_ Cthulhu can’t take this action again until the start of its next turn.

### Cthulhu’s Tale {#rthw:innsmouth:CthulhusTale}

Spawned beyond the borders of the multiverse in realities where time and life have little worth, Cthulhu is a servant of elder evils and a harbinger of their inevitable ruin. For untold eons, Cthulhu’s will influenced receptive minds across the multiverse, reaching out in dreams and using them to open gateways to the Far Realm. Through such portals, Cthulhu visited the Material Plane, corrupted and laid waste to civilizations, and erected city-size monuments to its mighty predecessors.

Such distortion and defilement didn’t go unnoticed by the Dark Powers. Multiple times the Mists closed around dread Cthulhu, and multiple times the terror evaded them. It was drawn into the Shadowfell when an extinct cabal of mages summoned it onto a sepulchral world of the Material Plane during a once-in-an-era alignment of eclipses. With the magic of the Shadowfell enhanced, the Mists rose and drew in Cthulhu. Raging and grasping, Cthulhu dragged with it remnants of past conquests and violent minds linked to its own. These disparate nightmares became the foundation of its prison: a surreal island hidden amid the Domains of Dread.

### Cthulhu’s Domain {#rthw:innsmouth:CthulhusDomain}

Innsmouth is altered by Cthulhu’s presence, creating the following effects:

**Choking Depths.** A creature can [**hold its breath**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#suffocationhazard) for only 30 seconds while in the domain.

**Closing the Borders.** While in its domain, Cthulhu can close or open the borders of Innsmouth at will. While the borders are closed, those who enter the Mists surrounding Innsmouth become lost at sea amid inky fog for 3d4 days before arriving once more at Innsmouth.

**Something in the Air.** Creatures other than Cthulhu and its allies have [**Disadvantage**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#disadvantage) on saving throws to avoid or end the [**Frightened**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#frightenedcondition) condition.

If Cthulhu dies, these effects end immediately.

### Cthulhu’s Lair {#rthw:innsmouth:CthulhusLair}

Amid surreal expanses within Innmouth’s depths lies the entrance to Cthulhu’s Vault, a prison within the Mists where Cthulhu lies trapped. The entrance to Cthulhu’s Vault is a ritual site etched with symbols of power from across time and hundreds of worlds. Those who perform the proper rituals, guided by visions from Cthulhu itself, might free themselves from the domain of Innsmouth, and, in so doing, unleash Cthulhu on the multiverse.

#### Cthulhu’s Vault Features {#rthw:innsmouth:CthulhusVaultFeatures}

Cthulhu’s Vault is a hidden realm, but the entrance to it lies amid the Vaults beneath the island. The vault is depicted on [map 2.18](#rthw:innsmouth:map218cthulhusvault "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/innsmouth#map218cthulhusvault") and has the following features:

**Noisome Brine.** A dark, frothy waterway winds through the Vaults, ultimately emerging from either the Cleft of Dreams or the mouth of the Drowned Colossus.

**Ritual Site.** A partially toppled monument bearing a tentacled visage marks a weak point in Cthulhu’s prison. Before it stands an altar etched with bizarre runes. These symbols are of otherworldly design, but each cult of Innsmouth knows the meaning of a few. Only cultists imbued with the might of all four cults can perform the ritual these runes describe and force open Cthulhu’s prison.

**The Perceptive.** A small ship called the _Perceptive_ lies beached here, a remnant of a group of cultists’ past attempt to access Cthulhu’s Vault. The bowsprit is broken, ending in a jagged point.

**The Providence.** The shattered remains of a ship called the _Providence_ serves as the shelter of a mysterious seer. It’s said this former cultist knows more of Cthulhu’s Vault than any other creature.

## Cults of Innsmouth {#rthw:innsmouth:CultsofInnsmouth}

Four cults operate in Innsmouth, each with its own vile ends. While these groups are ruinously evil, characters might temporarily ally with one or more to oppose another foe or to escape the domain.

### Cults and Cultists {#rthw:innsmouth:CultsandCultists}

The following groups vie for power on and under Innsmouth. Following each cult’s name are the ritual words cult members use in their blasphemous practices, along with other details.

#### Cult of the Chthonic Night {#rthw:innsmouth:CultoftheChthonicNight}

Hail, Hail, Cthulhu Awaits

**Worships:** Cthulhu  
**Leader:** King-Priest Eeyog-Yah  
**Goal:** Free Cthulhu from imprisonment  
**Lair:** The village of Innsmouth and the Vaults

Initiates of the Cult of the Chthonic Night open their minds to the whispers of Great Cthulhu and seek to free the imprisoned terror from the Domains of Dread. Predominantly composed of [**Aberrant Cultists**](#ref:monster:5194866-aberrant-cultist "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5194866-aberrant-cultist") and [**Kuo-toa**](#ref:monster:5195101-kuo-toa "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195101-kuo-toa") that dwell amid waterlogged ruins deep below the Graven Peak, the cult interprets visions from Cthulhu as omens, calls for sacrifice, and signs of their god’s coming.

King-Priest Eeyog-Yah, an ageless and desiccated [**Kuo-toa Archpriest**](#ref:monster:5195098-kuo-toa-archpriest "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195098-kuo-toa-archpriest"), leads the cult. Eeyog-Yah occupies a state of perpetual somnambulism and narrates its visions. The priest’s attendants decipher their leader’s rambling as directives from their god.

Those who join the cult and participate in its induction rituals hear the voice of Cthulhu more clearly than others do (see “[Cult Dark Gifts](#rthw:innsmouth:cultdarkgifts "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/innsmouth#cultdarkgifts")”).

[![Symbol of the Cult of the Chthonic Night Symbol of the Cult of the Drowning Wave Symbol of the Cult of the Heavenly Doom Symbol of the Cult of the Scaly Abyss (Artist: CoupleOfKooks)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/10-004.cult-symbols.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/10-004.cult-symbols.png)

#### Cult of the Drowning Wave {#rthw:innsmouth:CultoftheDrowningWave}

Make Clean for the Aeon Wave

**Worships:** Olhydra  
**Leader:** Draa Shoom  
**Goal:** Sink Innsmouth below the waves  
**Lair:** Eyes of Olhydra

Those who await the Drowning Wave seek to make Innsmouth and all its inhabitants part of Olhydra’s realm on the Elemental Plane of Water. Olhydra, the Prince of Evil Water, then could use the might of Cthulhu and the mass sacrifice of the island to dominate the Elemental Planes and flood the Material Plane.

Draa Shoom, the cult’s [**Aboleth**](#ref:monster:5194867-aboleth "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5194867-aboleth") leader, believes Olhydra will return the cult to a place of dominance over countless worlds in return for its sacrifice. To effect this, Draa Shoom coaxes [**Elemental Cultists**](#ref:monster:5194983-elemental-cultist "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5194983-elemental-cultist") and shipwrecked individuals to the Eyes of Olhydra. There, amid boggy ruins and the lairs of murky elemental creatures, rises the Fathomless Gate. This ancient stone arch, thought to connect to the Elemental Plane of Water, is covered by bars of starmetal, which prevent passage by solid creatures. The cult seeks the proper rituals to open the gate, allowing Olhydra’s scouring waters to flood the domain.

Those who participate in the cult’s induction rituals are infused with a draught of Olhydra’s sapient form (see “[Cult Dark Gifts](#rthw:innsmouth:cultdarkgifts "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/innsmouth#cultdarkgifts")”).

#### Cult of the Heavenly Doom {#rthw:innsmouth:CultoftheHeavenlyDoom}

Empty Yourself to Gorge on the Stars

**Worships:** Zhudun  
**Leader:** Celesta Grayl  
**Goal:** Open gateways to join Zhudun  
**Lair:** Blind Observatory and the Map of the Eclipse

Among the broken heights of the domain, the obsessed astronomers of the Cult of the Heavenly Doom seek signs in the heavens and omens from Zhudun, the Corpse Star, an Elder Evil that wanders space and knows the secrets of extinction. These cultists hope to climb into the heavens and join Zhudun.

The cult’s leader, Celesta Grayl, has sought Zhudun for centuries. While documenting her observations, Grayl discovered a path to immortality and became a [**Vampire Umbral Lord**](#ref:monster:5195250-vampire-umbral-lord "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195250-vampire-umbral-lord"). [**Death Cultists**](#ref:monster:5194960-death-cultist "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5194960-death-cultist"), along with desperate and deluded souls, have flocked to the ancient stargazer, forming the cult around Grayl and her discoveries despite their leader’s protestations and predations. The vampire suffers the cultists only so long as they help her decipher secrets from ruins around the island and retrieve knowledge from the grip of other cults. She believes their discoveries will help her reveal when the stars are right to join Zhudun in the dark places between the stars.

Those who join the cult and participate in its induction rituals release a portion of their life to the stars (see “[Cult Dark Gifts](#rthw:innsmouth:cultdarkgifts "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/innsmouth#cultdarkgifts")”).

#### Cult of the Scaly Abyss {#rthw:innsmouth:CultoftheScalyAbyss}

The Prince Awaits—Become the Way

**Worships:** Dagon  
**Leader:** Xr’gh  
**Goal:** Summon Dagon  
**Lair:** Dagon’s Claws

The followers of Dagon, Demon Prince of the Darkened Depths, lurk among and beneath the waves of Innsmouth. Ancient even among inhabitants of the Abyss, Dagon seeks to drag demon lords and their Abyssal realms into its demesne of Shadowsea. Once sated on the flesh of its foes, Dagon aspires to unleash its might across the multiverse in a sanity-shattering wave.

Xr’gh, a [**Sahuagin Baron**](#ref:monster:5195188-sahuagin-baron "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195188-sahuagin-baron") fanatically devoted to Dagon, seeks to turn all who dwell beneath the waves to the demon lord’s worship. Xr’gh seeks enough sacrifices to turn the sea red with blood, an offering great enough to attract Dagon’s notice and draw the demon lord to Innsmouth. The cult leader expects Dagon then to feed on Cthulhu and begin its conquest of the Abyss. Ravenous [**Sahuagin**](#ref:monster:5195190-sahuagin-warrior "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195190-sahuagin-warrior") follow Xr’gh, as do [**Fiend Cultists**](#ref:monster:5194993-fiend-cultist "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5194993-fiend-cultist") and murderers desirous of the eerie gold treasures the sahuagin offer from their submerged vaults. The Cult of the Scaly Abyss hunts the domain’s ruined villages, abducting anyone who seeks shelter amid the wreckage. Those they find, they drag through secret paths beneath the waves to their ritual site under the island called Dagon’s Claw.

Those who join the cult and participate in its induction rituals develop shark-like organs (see “[Cult Dark Gifts](#rthw:innsmouth:cultdarkgifts "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/innsmouth#cultdarkgifts")”).

### Cult Rites {#rthw:innsmouth:CultRites}

The cults of Innsmouth seek initiates to aid in their unfathomable works. Those who prove themselves reliable devotees gain access to the transformative power of strange gods.

#### Cult Renown {#rthw:innsmouth:CultRenown}

The cults of Innsmouth reward those who honor their obscene patrons. Use the [guidance](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/dmg-2024/dms-toolbox#renown) in the [Dungeon Master’s Guide](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/dmg-2024) to track characters’ individual standing within Innsmouth’s cults. Characters can gain renown with a cult by performing deeds such as those in the Innsmouth Cults Renown table.

**Innsmouth Cults Renown**

| Deed                                                     | Renown Gained |
| -------------------------------------------------------- | ------------- |
| Slaying an enemy cultist\*                               | +1            |
| Despoiling an enemy ritual site\*                        | +1            |
| Participating in a cult ritual\*                         | +1            |
| Ritual sacrifice of an enemy or magic item               | +2            |
| Retrieving alien devices                                 | +2            |
| Disrupting an enemy ritual                               | +3            |
| Slaying the leader of an enemy cult                      | +5            |
| \*Renown for this deed can be gained only once per week. |

#### Cult Dark Gifts {#rthw:innsmouth:CultDarkGifts}

Characters who have a Renown Score of 10+ with an Innsmouth cult are honored as the chosen of the cult’s patron. They are urged to take part in a ritual that inducts them into the cult and bestows on them a supernatural boon. A character who participates in such a ritual gains the Dark Gift (see [chapter 1](#rthw:character-options:darkgifts "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/character-options#darkgifts")) noted on the Innsmouth Cults Dark Gifts table.

**Innsmouth Cults Dark Gifts**

| Cult                                                | Dark Gift                                                                                          |
| --------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [Cult of Chthonic Night](#rthw:innsmouth:cultofthechthonicnight "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/innsmouth#cultofthechthonicnight")   | [Gathered Whispers](#rthw:character-options:gatheredwhispers "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/character-options#gatheredwhispers") |
| [Cult of the Drowning Wave](#rthw:innsmouth:cultofthedrowningwave "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/innsmouth#cultofthedrowningwave") | [Symbiotic Being](#rthw:character-options:symbioticbeing "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/character-options#symbioticbeing")     |
| [Cult of the Heavenly Doom](#rthw:innsmouth:cultoftheheavenlydoom "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/innsmouth#cultoftheheavenlydoom") | [Touch of Death](#rthw:character-options:touchofdeath "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/character-options#touchofdeath")        |
| [Cult of the Scaly Abyss](#rthw:innsmouth:cultofthescalyabyss "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/innsmouth#cultofthescalyabyss")     | [Aberrant Anatomy](#rthw:character-options:aberrantanatomy "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/character-options#aberrantanatomy")   |

These Dark Gifts include magical transformations associated with the cult’s patron and its members. This magic can make it easier to navigate parts of the domain and bypass seals made by cult magic. This includes the binding sigils that mark Cthulhu’s Vault. A character with one of these Dark Gifts can’t gain another. A character with one of these gifts who leaves Innsmouth can choose to lose the Dark Gift or keep it.

## Adventures in Innsmouth {#rthw:innsmouth:AdventuresinInnsmouth}

Adventures in Innsmouth involve cults, degenerate rituals, nightmarish visions, and aberrant transformations. Use this section to develop horror adventures in this domain.

[![Nightmarish monuments and reality-defying ruins cover the island called Innsmouth (Artist: David Frasheski)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/10-005.nightmarsh-monuments.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/10-005.nightmarsh-monuments.png)

### Corruptive Horror {#rthw:innsmouth:CorruptiveHorror}

The cults of Innsmouth are monstrous and dangerous, but not unwelcoming. Each seeks to bring a different terrifying cataclysm to Innsmouth. As characters interact with these cults and learn more of the island’s secrets, bizarre dreams encourage the characters to accept the Dark Gifts the cults offer and balance rivalries to gain the might of each. Groups that engage with each cult might have strange adventures across Innsmouth and undergo bizarre transformations. Those that do will find themselves with the power to free Cthulhu from the island—and maybe themselves as well.

### Dreams of Innsmouth {#rthw:innsmouth:DreamsofInnsmouth}

Cthulhu sends dreams to those in Innsmouth—and in realms beyond—that might help it escape its prison. These dreams include strange images spurring the dreamers to seek the cults of Innsmouth, gain their powers, and then dispel the sigils in Cthulhu’s Vault. Dreams sent by Cthulhu might focus on the following topics and imagery:

**Cult of the Chthonic Night:** The village of Innsmouth, the Graven Peak, desiccated fish, tentacles

**Cult of the Drowning Wave:** The Eyes of Olhydra, shipwrecks, tidal waves, three eyes underwater

**Cult of the Heavenly Doom:** The peaks of Innsmouth, corpses in space, monoliths, whirling stars

**Cult of the Scaly Abyss:** Dagon’s Claws, deep-sea predators, sharks eating sharks, undersea ruins

**Cthulhu’s Vault:** The Cleft of Dreams, the Drowned Colossus, dark passages, strange sigils

Any of these dreams might end with a vision of the Mists parting and the characters’ home or a similarly tantalizing location appearing beyond.

### Old One’s Bargain {#rthw:innsmouth:OldOnesBargain}

Cthulhu’s dream-messages tempt characters to release the entity to win their own escape from its domain. Whether Cthulhu can or will fulfill this offer is up to you, but the characters might not wish to jeopardize reality to escape. In the course of exploring Innsmouth, they can find the writings of obsessed wizards and cult heresies that suggest the following secrets:

**Cthulhu’s Disruption.** Cthulhu’s power is such that, should someone release it, the Mists around Innsmouth would open and those in the domain could escape.

**Cthulhu’s Might.** Cthulhu wouldn’t emerge from its prison at full strength. For approximately one hour after its release, heroes might force Cthulhu back into its prison, should they subject the terror to potent magic such as [**Imprisonment**](#ref:spell:2619175-imprisonment "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619175-imprisonment") or [**Wish**](#ref:spell:2619213-wish "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619213-wish"), or a blow powerful enough to disrupt its physical form, like a powerful lightning strike, a massive explosion, or a strike from a large sailing ship.

Elaborate on these possibilities as characters explore Innsmouth, and encourage them to believe they might be able to outwit a Great Old One.

### Otherworldly Relics {#rthw:innsmouth:OtherworldlyRelics}

The monsters noted in the “[Cosmic Horror](#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:cosmichorror "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/creating-domains-of-dread#cosmichorror")” section of [chapter 4](#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/creating-domains-of-dread") make appropriate inhabitants of the ruins and vaults of Innsmouth. These beings often possess evidence of alien technologies and cultures. Innsmouth’s cults covet such relics. Roll on or choose a result from the Alien Relics table to inspire what otherworldly beings might possess.

**Alien Relics**

| 1d6 | The Alien Being Possesses …                   |
| --- | --------------------------------------------- |
| 1   | A crystalline wand with a monstrous face.     |
| 2   | A faintly glowing trapezohedron.              |
| 3   | An jade amulet shaped like a sphinx.          |
| 4   | A metallic cluster of globes and half globes. |
| 5   | An oversize, pattern-etched silver key.       |
| 6   | A preserved brain in a glass cylinder.        |

### Innsmouth Campaign Arc {#rthw:innsmouth:InnsmouthCampaignArc}

Campaigns set in Innsmouth involve warring cults, unfathomable beings, and bizarre transformations. A campaign here might follow this outline:

**Levels 1–2.** The characters wash up on Innsmouth island and shelter in the village. They experience strange dreams. Soon after, they encounter cultists who seek to initiate them and others who seek to sacrifice them. The characters gain allies among one of the island’s cults.

**Levels 3–5.** The allied cult sends the characters to disrupt other cults and retrieve relics from the ruins. In return, the cult offers insights into the characters’ dreams and suggests ways to escape the island. After proving their worth, a character receives the cult’s Dark Gift (see “[Cult Rites](#rthw:innsmouth:cultrites "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/innsmouth#cultrites")”).

**Levels 6–16.** Led by their dreams and duplicitous cult members, the characters move from cult to cult, gaining influence by delving into ruins and strange vaults. In doing so, they collect Dark Gifts, as well as hints about Cthulhu’s Vault and ways to undermine the Great Old One (see “[Old One’s Bargain](#rthw:innsmouth:oldonesbargain "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/innsmouth#oldonesbargain")”).

**Levels 17–20.** After collecting a Dark Gift from each cult, the characters follow a treacherous path through the Vaults to Cthulhu’s Vault. There, they can risk releasing [**Cthulhu**](#ref:monster:6491348-cthulhu "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491348-cthulhu") to escape the island.

### Vault of the Elder {#rthw:innsmouth:VaultoftheElder}

Adventure for Level 11 Characters

**Situation.** Cult lore tells of a vault that is home to a wise elder who knows the secrets of escaping the island.

**Hook.** A cult leader shares directions to the vault but wants one of the strange relics the elder is said to hoard.

[![Map 2.18: Cthulhu’s Vault View Player Version (Artist: Mike Schley)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/map-10-02.cthulhus-vault.jpg)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/map-10-02.cthulhus-vault.jpg)

[![Map 2.18: Cthulhu’s Vault Surroundings View Player Version (Artist: Mike Schley)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/map-10-04.cthulhus-vault-surroundings.jpg)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/map-10-04.cthulhus-vault-surroundings.jpg)

[![Map 2.18: Wreck of the Providence (Artist: Mike Schley)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/map-10-03.wreck-of-the-providence.jpg)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/map-10-03.wreck-of-the-providence.jpg)

#### Encounters {#rthw:innsmouth:Encounters}

The adventure uses map 2.18 and consists of these encounters:

**_Vault Ambush._** On the way to the vault, two [**Cult Fanatics**](#ref:monster:16836-cult-fanatic "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/16836-cult-fanatic") and a [**Fiend Cultist**](#ref:monster:5194993-fiend-cultist "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5194993-fiend-cultist") (or another enemy cultist selected from those mentioned in “[Cults of Innsmouth](#rthw:innsmouth:CultsofInnsmouth "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/innsmouth#CultsofInnsmouth")”) ambush the characters.

**_Frigid Spires._** The Vault of the Elder lies in a realm of icy mountains gripped by extreme cold (see “[Environmental Effects](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/dmg-2024/dms-toolbox#environmentaleffects)” in the [Dungeon Master’s Guide](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/dmg-2024)). The towers of a gravity-defying stone city protrude from one mountain.

**_Hollow City._** The characters find the city filled with narrow ramps and abandoned, tubelike structures etched with eerie hieroglyphs. Of particular note is an out-of-place collection of tents and a templelike building.

**_Encampment._** Brown mold covers the tents (see [chapter 3](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/dmg-2024/dms-toolbox#brownmold) of the _Dungeon Master’s Guide_). If the characters remove the mold, they find five cultists frozen inside the tents, wrapped in blankets. One wears a [**Ring of Mind Shielding**](#ref:magic_item:9228967-ring-of-mind-shielding "https://www.dndbeyond.com/magic-items/9228967-ring-of-mind-shielding").

**_Elder Temple._** The templelike building bears carvings depicting five-winged beings fighting giant, fungus-like insects. Through the temple lies a path leading deeper into the mountain—and defended by a [**Shoggoth**](#ref:monster:6491388-shoggoth "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491388-shoggoth") (see [chapter 5](#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:shoggoth "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/denizens-of-the-mists#shoggoth")).

**_Frozen Warning._** Ice encrusts the walls of the deeper temple, covering more strange carvings. Etched into the ice over a depiction of another five-winged creature is a warning in Common: “Beware the Elder.”

**_Elder’s Reliquary._** The passage ends in a chamber with four pillars of ice. Perched on one is a [**Hostile**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#hostileattitude) [**Elder Thing**](#ref:monster:6491353-elder-thing "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491353-elder-thing") (see [chapter 5](#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:elderthing "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/denizens-of-the-mists#elderthing")).

**_Ice Tombs._** The pillars of ice each hold a shadowy shape. These pillars have AC 14, HP 20, Immunity to Poison and Psychic damage, and Vulnerability to Fire damage. The pillars contain the following:

**Alien Relic.** The first pillar contains a strange relic. Roll on the “[Alien Relics](#rthw:innsmouth:alienrelics "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/innsmouth#alienrelics")” table earlier in this chapter to determine what it is.

**Mi-Go.** Two pillars contain [**Mi-Go**](#ref:monster:6491373-mi-go "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491373-mi-go") (see [chapter 5](#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:migo "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/denizens-of-the-mists#migo")), which awake 1 round after being freed.

**Vault Map.** A hieroglyph-etched slab in the final pillar charts a route from Innsmouth’s surface to Cthulhu’s Vault. It also provides information from the “[Old One’s Bargain](#rthw:innsmouth:oldonesbargain "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/innsmouth#oldonesbargain")” section. However, only someone with the [Dark Gift](#rthw:innsmouth:innsmouthcultsdarkgiftstable "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/innsmouth#innsmouthcultsdarkgiftstable") of the [Cult of Heavenly Doom](#rthw:innsmouth:cultoftheheavenlydoom "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/innsmouth#cultoftheheavenlydoom") can decipher its alien language.

</CHAPTER>

<CHAPTER id="rthw:kalakeri" title="Kalakeri">

# Kalakeri {#rthw:kalakeri:Kalakeri}

Domain of Betrayal and Revenge

> #### **Darklord:** [Ramya Vasavadan](#rthw:kalakeri:RamyaVasavadan "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/kalakeri#RamyaVasavadan") {#rthw:kalakeri:RamyaVasavadan}
>
> **Adventure Genres:** [Gothic horror](#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:gothichorror "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/creating-domains-of-dread#gothichorror") and [dark fantasy](#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:darkfantasy "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/creating-domains-of-dread#darkfantasy")
>
> **Hallmarks:** Monstrous leaders, family intrigue, war-torn nation
>
> **Mist Talismans:** Rusted tulwar, shield with a wyvern-and-lotus emblem, a polished skull
>
> **Aligned Tarokka Card:** Avenger
>
> **Opposed Tarokka Card:** Artifact

[![(Artist: Pam Wishbow)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/11-001.avenger-tarokka.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/11-001.avenger-tarokka.png) [![](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/11-002.artifact-tarokka.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/11-002.artifact-tarokka.png)

Deceptively beautiful, Kalakeri is a land of verdant rainforests and a web of rivers and lakes known as the Backwaters. At the height of its prosperity, Kalakeri was a robust center of art, commerce, and religion, with merchants spreading wild tales of the land, using fanciful names such as Sri Raji and the Steaming Lands. Now Kalakeri is a conflict-torn shadow of its past glory. The remnants of the Vasavadan dynasty—three heirs transformed into monsters by their depravity and hatred—trap the land in an endless cycle of war.

The people of Kalakeri live in fear of [**Maharani Ramya Vasavadan**](#ref:monster:6491382-ramya-vasavadan "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491382-ramya-vasavadan"), the domain’s Darklord, as well as her treacherous siblings, Arijani and Reeva. The Darklord’s curse manifests both in her deathless desire to rule Kalakeri and in her siblings’ endless rebellions. Both sides escalate their atrocities against one another, drawing the powerful and the innocent alike into their squabbles. As the maharani’s siblings court allies, the Darklord’s forces hunt and execute renegades, adding skulls to the grim Tower of Traitors.

## Domain Features {#rthw:kalakeri:DomainFeatures}

Kalakeri is known for the following features:

**Factions in Conflict.** Two factions claim Kalakeri’s Sapphire Throne: the soldiers and loyalists of [Maharani Ramya Vasavadan](#rthw:kalakeri:RamyaVasavadan "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/kalakeri#RamyaVasavadan"), and the nobles and merchants who support the younger royal siblings, [Arijani and Reeva Vasavadan](#rthw:kalakeri:arijaniandreeva "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/kalakeri#arijaniandreeva").

**Jadurai, a City at War.** The vast city of Jadurai is Kalakeri’s capital, the site of the royal palace, and a battlefield where factions struggle to claim or hold it as a symbol of rule.

**The Backwaters.** Rare creatures and extraordinary magical plants flourish in the Backwaters, the collective name for the wilderness away from Kalakeri’s cities. Scattered refugee groups hide in the wilds and organize dangerous, desperate attacks on the Vasavadan factions.

## Locations in Kalakeri {#rthw:kalakeri:LocationsinKalakeri}

Tropical rainforests isolate Kalakeri’s communities. While the domain’s residents are adept at navigating these wildernesses, strangers often fall prey to the domain’s myriad hazards and predators.

The capital of Jadurai is detailed below, and other notable locations are summarized on the [Kalakeri Locations table](#rthw:kalakeri:kalakerilocations "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/kalakeri#kalakerilocations").

### Jadurai {#rthw:kalakeri:Jadurai}

Ancient structures adorned with the artistry of past dynasties stand alongside modern buildings in Kalakeri’s capital, Jadurai. The city retains its splendor, but the conflict between the Vasavadan siblings takes an enormous toll as they struggle over the Cerulean Citadel, the nation’s capitol, as well as the Sapphire Throne within. Sections of the city lie in ruins.

On the outskirts of Jadurai rises the Tower of Traitors. Rows of skulls taken from the Darklord’s enemies fill depressions in this stone tower. Two skulls hold places of special prominence: the original human skulls of Arijani and Reeva Vasavadan. The Darklord’s skeletal soldiers build the tower as part of her plan to rid Kalakeri of evil and receive the gods’ blessings.

[![Map 2.19: Kalakeri View Player Version (Artist: Marco Bernardini)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/map-11-01.kalakeri.jpg)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/map-11-01.kalakeri.jpg)

**Kalakeri Locations**

| Location              | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Ashwagangha Mountains | The forbidden ruins of the accursed city of Bahru lie hidden somewhere in the Ashwagangha Mountains. A powerful evil force lies imprisoned there, attended by monstrous cultists.                                                                                                                 |
| Bay of Lost Lights    | The villages of Kattachira and Grantha flank the Bay of Lost Lights, which is named for the [**will-o’-wisps**](#ref:monster:5195270-will-o-wisp "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195270-will-o-wisp") that bob in and above it.                                                              |
| Drowned Altar         | The sea boils around an ancient, submerged ruin called the Drowned Altar. With Kalakeri’s upheaval, no one has performed the rites to placate what dwells in the deep.                                                                                                                            |
| Forest of the Still   | Statues of helpless animals and terrified refugees alike decorate the quiet, [**basilisk**](#ref:monster:5194919-basilisk "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5194919-basilisk")\-infested Forest of the Still. Some of the statues are said to be the remains of heroes from past ages.          |
| Gharial Rivers        | The villages of Banyan and Veena are renowned for their remarkable herbalists, but their secrets rely on plants guarded by the titanic crocodiles of the Gharial Rivers.                                                                                                                          |
| Island of the Naga    | The eternal [**guardian nagas**](#ref:monster:5195066-guardian-naga "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195066-guardian-naga") of the Isle of the Naga have a perfect memory of Kalakeri’s lost secrets. Suspicious of strangers, the nagas test the worthiness of any who seek their knowledge. |
| Jalendu’s Sanctuary   | The [**stone giant**](#ref:monster:5195220-stone-giant "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195220-stone-giant") guru Jalendu lives in his sanctuary and claims to know a path to religious enlightenment. Those who fail to prove their devotion to his teachings turn up petrified.             |
| Meenakara             | The shadows of people of Meenakara are disappearing, and the shadow-bereft soon sicken and die. Meenakara’s people believe the cure lies in the Ashram of Niranjan.                                                                                                                               |
| Neelakurinji          | Bandits overtook the village of Neelakurinji, claiming Arijani Vasavadan as their leader. In truth, they serve no one, opportunistically robbing those who fear disobeying the Vasavadan factions.                                                                                                |
| Silent Sitars         | The giants who occupy the islands known as the Silent Sitars were cursed for oﬀending the gods. Sound is magically suppressed on these isles, stifling the truths within the giants’ music.                                                                                                       |
| The Vochalams         | Temples crown the Vochalam mountains. In one, a deity placed a treasure that grants wishes. In the other is a treasure that turns people into wyverns loyal to Kalakeri’s ruler.                                                                                                                  |

## Ramya Vasavadan {#rthw:kalakeri:RamyaVasavadan}

Darklord Perpetually Denied Control

[![(Artist: Camille Alquier)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/11-003.ramya-vasvadan.jpg)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/11-003.ramya-vasvadan.jpg)

> “Are you loyal to your maharani? Or are you yet more rebel skulls to add to the Tower of Traitors?”
>
> —Ramya Vasavadan

Ramya Vasavadan desperately fights to claim and hold power over Kalakeri in a brutal cycle of victory and loss with her equally uncompromising siblings. Unlike most Darklords, Ramya struggles to control her domain, leading her to seek allies in opposing her siblings and their treacherous allies.

In her true form, Ramya is an undead horror, but illusions mask her monstrous appearance. Her true nature is revealed by her chilled skin and her reflection, which always appears withered and terrifying.

Although Ramya’s siblings, Arijani and Reeva, aren’t Darklords of Kalakeri, they motivate the rebellions in Kalakeri and Ramya’s torments. This monstrous pair is detailed in “[Arijani and Reeva](#rthw:kalakeri:arijaniandreeva "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/kalakeri#arijaniandreeva").”

### [Ramya Vasavadan](#ref:monster:6491382-ramya-vasavadan "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491382-ramya-vasavadan") {#rthw:kalakeri:RamyaVasavadanrefmonster6491382ramyavasavadanhttpswwwdndbeyondcommonsters6491382ramyavasavadan}

Medium Undead, Chaotic Evil

**AC** 18 **Initiative** +15 (25)

**HP** 190 (20d8 + 100)

**Speed** 30 ft.

**Skills** [**Perception**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#skills) +8, [**Persuasion**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#skills) +9

**Immunities** Necrotic, Poison; [**Exhaustion**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#exhaustioncondition), [**Frightened**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#frightenedcondition), [**Poisoned**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#poisonedcondition)

#### Traits {#rthw:kalakeri:Traits}

**_Darklord Restoration._** If Ramya dies, her body dissolves into mist, and she gains a new body in 1d10 weeks, reviving with all her Hit Points somewhere in Kalakeri.

**_Legendary Resistance (3/Day, or 4/Day in Domain)._** If Ramya fails a saving throw, she can choose to succeed instead.

**_Magic Resistance._** Ramya has [**Advantage**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#advantage) on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

**_Marshal Undead._** Undead creatures of Ramya’s choice (excluding herself) in a 60-foot [**Emanation**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#emanationareaofeffect) originating from her have [**Advantage**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#advantage) on attack rolls and saving throws. She can’t use this trait if she has the [**Incapacitated**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#incapacitatedcondition) condition.

#### Actions {#rthw:kalakeri:Actions}

**_Multiattack._** Ramya makes three Dread Blade attacks.

**_Dread Blade._** _Melee Attack Roll:_ +10, reach 5 ft. _Hit:_ 12 (2d6 + 5) Slashing damage plus 9 (2d8) Necrotic damage.

**_Vengeful Fire (Recharge 5–6)._** _Dexterity Saving Throw:_ DC 17, each creature in a 20-foot-radius [**Sphere**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#sphereareaofeffect) centered on a point Ramya can see within 120 feet. _Failure:_ 28 (8d6) Fire damage plus 28 (8d6) Necrotic damage. _Success:_ Half damage.

**_Spellcasting._** Ramya casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 17):

**At Will:** [**Phantom Steed**](#ref:spell:2618859-phantom-steed "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618859-phantom-steed")

**1/Day:** [**Create Undead**](#ref:spell:2619076-create-undead "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619076-create-undead")

#### Bonus Actions {#rthw:kalakeri:BonusActions}

**_Illusory Disguise._** Ramya casts [**Disguise Self**](#ref:spell:2619102-disguise-self "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619102-disguise-self") using the same spellcasting ability as Spellcasting. The spell lasts until Ramya drops to 80 Hit Points or fewer or uses her Vengeful Fire action. Intelligence ([**Investigation**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#skills)) checks to discern her true appearance are made with [**Disadvantage**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#disadvantage).

When the disguise ends, each creature in a 30-foot [**Emanation**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#emanationareaofeffect) originating from Ramya is subjected to the following effect. _Wisdom Saving Throw:_ DC 17 (the target succeeds automatically if it is a Construct or an Undead). _Failure:_ The target has the [**Frightened**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#frightenedcondition) condition for 1 minute. While Frightened, the target has Disadvantage on saving throws.

#### Reactions {#rthw:kalakeri:Reactions}

**_Parry._** _Trigger:_ Ramya is hit by a melee attack roll while holding a weapon. _Response:_ Ramya adds 5 to her AC against that attack, possibly causing it to miss.

#### Legendary Actions {#rthw:kalakeri:LegendaryActions}

Legendary Action Uses: 3 (4 in Domain). Immediately after another creature’s turn, Ramya can expend a use to take one of the following actions. Ramya regains all expended uses at the start of each of her turns.

**_Dread Authority._** Ramya casts [**Command**](#ref:spell:2618985-command "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618985-command"), using the same spellcasting ability as Spellcasting. Ramya can’t take this action again until the start of her next turn.

**_Lunge._** Ramya moves up to half her Speed and makes one Dread Blade attack.

**_Words of Silence._** _Constitution Saving Throw:_ DC 17, one creature Ramya can see within 120 feet. _Failure:_ 21 (6d6) Psychic damage, and the target is cursed until the end of its next turn. Until the curse ends, the target can’t speak or cast spells with a Verbal component. _Success:_ Half damage only.

### Ramya’s Tale {#rthw:kalakeri:RamyasTale}

The Vasavadan dynasty has ruled Kalakeri since ancient times. Ramya Vasavadan was handpicked by her father to succeed him, but on the bleak day of his death, Ramya’s brother, Arijani, declared himself the new maharaja.

Ramya refused to yield to her brother, and with her allies, she captured and prepared to execute him. But Ramya’s sister, Reeva, counseled mercy. Instead, Ramya imprisoned Arijani and ascended as Kalakeri’s maharani, Queen of Kings.

In the years that followed, Ramya ruled justly. But in the shadows, Reeva plotted with rebels, who eventually freed Arijani and spurred nobles across the nation to revolt.

Regretting her mercy, Ramya sent her army to crush the rebels and mercilessly execute the treacherous. Reeva and Arijani combated Ramya’s superior forces with ambushes and deceptions. Once again exploiting Ramya’s sympathies, the pair tricked Ramya, invaded the Cerulean Citadel, and executed their sister by strangling. With her final gasps, Ramya cursed her brother and sister, calling them bloodthirsty beasts. Soon after, a terrible monsoon struck Kalakeri, bringing with it the Mists.

The storm lashed Kalakeri for weeks. At its height, Ramya returned from the dead and called on those who had fallen in her service. Loyal in death, a corpse legion joined the revitalized maharani, besieged the Cerulean Citadel, and slaughtered Arijani and Reeva. Ramya then stole their skulls and built them into the foundations of what would become the Tower of Traitors.

Arijani and Reeva’s plots didn’t end with their lives. They too were reborn, transformed into monstrous reflections of their ravenous desires.

Now in the Land of the Mists, the conflict gripping Kalakeri continues, trapping the nation in an endless war and forcing its people to swear loyalty to monsters.

### Ramya’s Domain {#rthw:kalakeri:RamyasDomain}

While Ramya is in control of the Sapphire Throne, Kalakeri is altered by Ramya’s presence, creating the following effects:

**Closing the Borders.** While in her domain, Ramya can close or open the borders to Kalakeri at will. While the borders are closed, the Mists surrounding Kalakeri sap the life of those within them. A creature that enters the Mists for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there and isn’t a Construct or an Undead must succeed on a DC 20 Constitution saving throw or gain 1 [**Exhaustion**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#exhaustioncondition) level. A creature makes this save only once per turn.

**Everlasting Army.** A Medium or Small Humanoid slain in combat rises 24 hours later as a [**Wight**](#ref:monster:5195269-wight "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195269-wight") under Ramya’s control, unless the Humanoid is restored to life or its body is destroyed.

If Ramya dies or if her siblings control the Sapphire Throne, these effects end immediately.

### Ramya’s Lair {#rthw:kalakeri:RamyasLair}

The Cerulean Citadel is Kalakeri’s royal palace. It derives its name from the blue sandstone used in its construction. Control of the citadel and the Sapphire Throne within regularly passes between Ramya and her siblings.

#### Cerulean Citadel {#rthw:kalakeri:CeruleanCitadel}

Bas-reliefs adorn the palace, depicting the history, heroes, and legends of the kingdom. The site is depicted on [map 2.20](#rthw:kalakeri:map220ceruleancitadel "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/kalakeri#map220ceruleancitadel") and has the following features:

**Domed Court.** The central domed court houses the Sapphire Throne. It hosts guardians and treasures gathered by the paranoid Vasavadans. Towers guard the surrounding walls, which are accessible via bridges from the court’s upper floors.

**War-Torn Courtyards.** Within the palace walls lie marble pavilions arranged among baths, ponds, and gardens. Some are intact, but sieges and repeated conflicts have ravaged others.

## Adventures in Kalakeri {#rthw:kalakeri:AdventuresinKalakeri}

Adventures set in Kalakeri involve suspicion and power struggles. Use this section to develop horror adventures in this domain.

[![Evidence of the endless conflict between the Vasavadan siblings lies rotting before the Cerulean Citadel (Artist: Miro Petrov)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/11-004.cerulean-citadel.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/11-004.cerulean-citadel.png)

### Horror in Kalakeri {#rthw:kalakeri:HorrorinKalakeri}

Adventures in Kalakeri often include the following elements.

#### Arijani and Reeva {#rthw:kalakeri:ArijaniandReeva}

Ramya’s rule is jeopardized by her siblings’ pursuit of power. Arijani and Reeva Vasavadan promise their followers wealth and freedom, but in truth, their agendas serve only them. Ramya still loves her siblings, making her vulnerable to their promises and lies. So long as Ramya exists, the Dark Powers resurrect Arijani and Reeva as if they had [Ramya’s](#rthw:kalakeri:ramyavasavadanstatblock "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/kalakeri#ramyavasavadanstatblock") Darklord Restoration trait.

**_Arijani._** Arijani is the charming face of resistance for all who oppose Ramya. Now a [**Rakshasa**](#ref:monster:5195178-rakshasa "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195178-rakshasa"), gregarious Arijani has decadent tastes. When in control of the Cerulean Citadel, he hosts parties for Kalakeri’s elite that conceal private feasts featuring obscene delicacies and mortal flesh.

**_Reeva._** Reeva’s adoration of Ramya gave way to jealousy when Ramya eclipsed her in their family’s esteem. Now an [**Arcanaloth**](#ref:monster:5194899-arcanaloth "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5194899-arcanaloth"), Reeve uses insidious magic from beneath the Cerulean Citadel to summon fiends and manipulate foes from afar. Behind her back, many mockingly call Reeva “Inajira,” her charismatic Arijani’s opposite.

### Renown in Kalakeri {#rthw:kalakeri:RenowninKalakeri}

You can track the characters’ influence with Ramya’s loyalist faction and her siblings’ rebel faction, using the [renown rules](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/dmg-2024/dms-toolbox#renown) from the [Dungeon Master’s Guide](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/dmg-2024) to track the characters’ standing with these groups. Characters might gain renown with either faction by performing missions such as these:

- Capturing or killing a rival agent
- Planting evidence that a rival committed a crime
- Conscripting a powerful ally for the faction
- Revealing the location of a rival’s hold
- Revealing traitors within the faction

Anytime the characters complete a mission for either group, their Renown Score with that group increases by 1, but their Renown Score with the other group decreases by 1 (to a minimum of 0). After the first time characters gain renown with either faction, any faction the characters have a Renown Score of 0 with treat the characters as follows:

**Loyalist Faction.** Members of this faction are [**Hostile**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#hostileattitude) toward the characters. The faction sends troops of [**Wights**](#ref:monster:5195269-wight "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195269-wight") or other Undead to capture the characters weekly.

**Rebel Faction.** Members of this faction are Hostile toward the characters. The faction sends [**Assassins**](#ref:monster:5194904-assassin "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5194904-assassin") or [**Wraiths**](#ref:monster:5174960-wraith "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5174960-wraith") under Reeva’s command to kill the characters weekly.

Characters can gain renown with a faction they have a Renown Score of 0 with by presenting proof of an action that undermines the other group. Even if betrayed, the factions seek the party’s aid, as they view the characters as useful pawns.

If the characters have a Renown Score of 5+ with either group, their deeds might benefit the faction enough for it to take control of Jadurai and claim the Sapphire Throne. The longer either faction controls the capital, the more extreme its reign becomes, its atrocities escalating week after week. The characters must balance aiding and opposing both factions to maintain equilibrium.

### Kalakeri Campaign Arc {#rthw:kalakeri:KalakeriCampaignArc}

Campaigns set in Kalakeri typically involve balancing the horrors committed by the Vasavadan factions. A campaign here might follow this outline:

**Levels 1–4.** Agents from the rebel faction contact the characters, presenting Arijani and Reeva Vasavadan as misunderstood heroes seeking to overthrow a tyrant. They entreat the characters to save the heir of an allied noble family from a compound controlled by Ramya’s [**Wight**](#ref:monster:5195269-wight "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195269-wight") soldiers and return him to a hidden safe house.

**Levels 5–8.** The characters meet Arijani and Reeva in their disguises as charming human royals. They thank the characters for their aid and ask them to reclaim the shield of an ancient hero petrified in the Forest of the Still, hoping the shield will be a symbol of their right to rule. As the characters travel to the forest, a messenger delivers a request from [**Ramya**](#ref:monster:6491382-ramya-vasavadan "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491382-ramya-vasavadan") to do the same. The characters must face [**Basilisks**](#ref:monster:5194919-basilisk "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5194919-basilisk") and the [**Wraiths**](#ref:monster:5174960-wraith "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5174960-wraith") of the petrified dead to recover the shield and then decide who to return it to.

**Levels 9–12.** Arijani and Reeva plot to attack Jadurai to claim the Sapphire Throne and request the characters’ help. Ramya’s spies have informed her of this plot, and she also seeks the characters’ aid. In the ensuing conflict, the characters might strike at any of the Vasavadan siblings.

### Tower of Traitors {#rthw:kalakeri:TowerofTraitors}

Adventure for Level 11 Characters

**Situation.** Arijani and Reeva Vasavadan seek to recover the skulls of their mortal bodies from the Tower of Traitors. They believe the skulls will grant them greater power.

**Hook.** Arijani or Reeva order the characters to recover two skulls from the Tower of Traitors but don’t say who the skulls belong to. They offer to pay the party with 10,000 GP in gemstones and a [**Candle of Invocation**](#ref:magic_item:9228374-candle-of-invocation "https://www.dndbeyond.com/magic-items/9228374-candle-of-invocation").

[![Map 2.20: Cerulean Citadel View Player Version](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/map-11-02.cerulean-citadel.jpg)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/map-11-02.cerulean-citadel.jpg)

[![Map 2.20: Tower of Traitors](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/map-11-03.tower-of-traitors.jpg)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/map-11-03.tower-of-traitors.jpg)

#### Encounters {#rthw:kalakeri:Encounters}

This adventure assumes you are tracking the characters’ renown with Kalakeri’s loyalist and rebel factions (see “[Renown in Kalakeri](#rthw:kalakeri:renowninkalakeri "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/kalakeri#renowninkalakeri")” earlier in this section). It includes these encounters.

**_Stolen Skulls._** The skulls Arijani and Reeva seek are from their own corpses, which were defiled by Ramya. The skulls are among hundreds in the Tower of Traitors. The pair don’t reveal who the skulls belong to but insist they’re vital to the rebel faction’s allies. To aid in the search, the siblings give the characters two [**Spell Scrolls**](#ref:magic_item:9229076-spell-scroll-level-2 "https://www.dndbeyond.com/magic-items/9229076-spell-scroll-level-2") of [**Locate Object**](#ref:spell:2619002-locate-object "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619002-locate-object"). However, they don’t provide the characters with enough details for the spell to pinpoint the skulls.

**_Learning About the Skulls._** The characters must learn three details about the skulls for them to be familiar enough to the characters that a spell like _Locate Object_ can locate them. Characters can learn details in three ways:

**Research.** Characters who spend a day searching for rumors or investigating records in one of Kalakeri’s settlements learn a detail by succeeding on a DC 16 Charisma ([**Persuasion**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#skills)) check or Intelligence ([**Investigation**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#skills)) check respectively.

**Renown.** A character can spend a day questioning non-[**Hostile**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#hostileattitude) members of a faction. After doing so, the characters learn a detail, but their Renown Score with that faction is reduced by 1. The group can do this only once.

**Magic.** The [**Legend Lore**](#ref:spell:2619010-legend-lore "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619010-legend-lore") spell reveals one detail; each character can use this spell once.

Each time the party learns a detail about the skulls, reveal a portion of the story from the “[Ramya’s Tale](#rthw:kalakeri:ramyastale "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/kalakeri#ramyastale")” section, obscuring the names of the maharani and the traitors until the end.

**_Tower of Traitors._** The Tower of Traitors is depicted on [map 2.20](#rthw:kalakeri:map220toweroftraitors "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/kalakeri#map220toweroftraitors") and is guarded by patrols of two [**Revenants**](#ref:monster:5195182-revenant "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195182-revenant") and four [**Wights**](#ref:monster:5195269-wight "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195269-wight"). If the characters have a Renown Score of 3+ with the loyalist faction, the undead are [**Indifferent**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#indifferentattitude) and tell the party to move along—they fight only if characters linger for more than 5 minutes or remove a skull from the tower. If the characters have less renown with the loyalists, the undead are Hostile. A new patrol appears 2d6 rounds after a patrol is defeated.

**_Searching the Tower._** The tower is composed of thousands of skulls, and the ones the rebels want can be found via magic such as the [**Locate Object**](#ref:spell:2619002-locate-object "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619002-locate-object") spell. Once discovered, a skull can be removed in 1 minute using a sharp implement. When both skulls are freed, the hatred lurking in the skulls manifests as two Hostile [**Gallows Speakers**](#ref:monster:6491355-gallows-speaker "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491355-gallows-speaker") (see [chapter 5](#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:gallowsspeaker "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/denizens-of-the-mists#gallowsspeaker")).

**_Loyalty or Treachery._** The next time the characters rest, Arijani ([**Rakshasa**](#ref:monster:5195178-rakshasa "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195178-rakshasa")) appears and demands the skulls. If the characters give him the skulls, he compensates them and the characters’ Renown Score with the rebel faction increases by 4. If the characters refuse to give him the skulls, Arijani fights them. The party’s Renown Score with the rebels decreases by 4 if Arijani is slain. Soon after, Ramya invites the characters to discuss future plans.

Regardless of how the adventure concludes, each character earns a bonus 4,100 XP.

# Kartakass {#rthw:kartakass:Kartakass}

Domain of Tarnished Dreams

> #### **Darklord:** [Harkon Lukas](#rthw:kartakass:HarkonLukas "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/kartakass#HarkonLukas") {#rthw:kartakass:HarkonLukas}
>
> **Adventure Genres:** [Dark fantasy](#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:darkfantasy "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/creating-domains-of-dread#darkfantasy") and [gothic horror](#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:gothichorror "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/creating-domains-of-dread#gothichorror")
>
> **Hallmarks:** Hidden identities, dangerous performances, exploitative ambitions, werewolves
>
> **Mist Talismans:** Handbill advertising remarkable performances, rustic woodcut of hunting wolves, wolf’s tooth necklace
>
> **Aligned Tarokka Card:** Swashbuckler
>
> **Opposed Tarokka Card:** Beast

[![(Artist: Pam Wishbow)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/12-001.swashbuckler-tarokka.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/12-001.swashbuckler-tarokka.png) [![](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/12-002.beast-tarokka.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/12-002.beast-tarokka.png)

Life in Kartakass feels staged and surreal, as every plant, beast, and person strives to prove their greatness. Trees and flowers erupt into bloom; songbirds sing themselves hoarse; and every local knows that dreams, fame, and immortal adulation are theirs should they prove worthy. And where talent and expertise fail, obsession and duplicity reign, leading to cycles of triumph, betrayal, and despair. Predators flourish in this land of unrealistic hopes, consuming passions, and vicious secrets.

With each full moon, the truth of Kartakass is exposed, as the domain’s many werewolves and other lycanthropes indulge their hunger for dominance and blood. After the full moon passes, the idyllic facade returns. Locals don’t speak of why most bar their doors and shutter their windows on the nights of the full moon, but they acknowledge that the path to greatness is messy.

## Domain Features {#rthw:kartakass:DomainFeatures}

Kartakass is known for the following features:

**False Idylls.** Kartakass is supernaturally picturesque and outwardly serene. Every season is strikingly beautiful, communities appear idyllic, and many animals are affected as if by the [**Awaken**](#ref:spell:2618897-awaken "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618897-awaken") spell. This makes deceptions and violence all the more stark.

**Meistersingers.** Kartakass has no unified government. Each settlement is governed by a meistersinger, the acknowledged mayor and embodiment of local art. Meistersingers maintain creative rivalries with one another largely for show.

**Theatricality.** Settlements pride themselves on performative traditions, such as distinctive dress, traditional dances, or song stylings.

**Wolves and Werewolves.** Wolves roam the land freely, and [**Werewolves**](#ref:monster:5195267-werewolf "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195267-werewolf") lurk in the domain’s settlements. Residents seldom venture outside during the full moon, fearing the lycanthropes’ hunger.

## Locations in Kartakass {#rthw:kartakass:LocationsinKartakass}

Kartakass is a land of rolling hills, light forests, clear lakes, and pastoral farmlands. Communities are welcoming and host frequent festivals. The settlements of Harmonia and Skald are detailed below, and other notable locations are summarized on the [Kartakass Locations table](#rthw:kartakass:kartakasslocations "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/kartakass#kartakasslocations").

### Harmonia {#rthw:kartakass:Harmonia}

Artists vie to perform at the town of Harmonia’s popular Crystal Club, a members-only venue inside a cave that features a stage constructed from a massive geode. The club features dramatic decor and discerning clientele. Rumors say that performers who fail to impress are exiled. The bloodier truth is that the club restricts membership to lycanthropes. Talented artists gain the curse and join their ranks, while the mediocre get devoured.

### Skald {#rthw:kartakass:Skald}

The largest community in Kartakass, Skald is a bustling hub of commerce and creativity. The lure of overnight celebrity and fawning crowds attracts the ambitious. Yet behind the facade of creativity and freethinking, business owners and celebrities prey on creativity, while performers struggle viciously over paltry opportunities. Vice, criminality, dark bargains, and supernatural predators flourish amid Skald’s many stages and frequent festivals. Among Skald’s most popular venues is the Old Kartakan Inn and Taverna, owned by the performer and Darklord Harkon Lukas.

[![Map 2.21: Kartakass View Player Version (Artist: Marco Bernardini)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/map-12-01.kartakass.jpg)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/map-12-01.kartakass.jpg)

**Kartakass Locations**

| Location                  | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Argent Falls Conservatory | Performers flock to a bardic college atop the Argent Falls. Caverns behind the falls bear rich silver deposits but are haunted by [**Banshees**](#ref:monster:5194916-banshee "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5194916-banshee")—the souls of failed performers. |
| The Catacombs             | Violent goblins lurk amid mazelike canyons called the Catacombs. Here, the goblin gladiator Nym Pymplee hosts fighting tournaments, with victors winning treasures from distant domains.                                                                            |
| Cavea Plains              | The Cavea Plains’ acoustics carry voices over great distances. Any speech above a whisper might attract the attention of [**wolves**](#ref:monster:4775850-wolf "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/4775850-wolf").                                                 |
| Cesca’s Vantage           | On the night of a full moon, a tarokka-reading wolf appears atop Cesca’s Vantage. She produces crimson cards from any corpse she is offered, and her readings are never wrong.                                                                                      |
| Cortton                   | A plague has taken root in Cortton. The town’s residents cake heavy makeup and garish blush on their faces, desperate to convince themselves and others that they’re uninfected.                                                                                    |
| Emherst                   | Every “resident” of Emherst is an in-character improvisational actor. They live in the Understage, an underground network of backstages, and they never interrupt performances.                                                                                     |
| Goblyn Graves             | Undead goblinoids often emerge from the Goblyn Graves, the former lair of Radaga, an undead witch said to possess powerful magic treasures.                                                                                                                         |
| House of Illusions        | This fun house of visual illusions is run by Jack Bequick: a vampire cursed with eternal invisibility and a twisted sense of humor.                                                                                                                                 |
| Medria                    | Several dramatic-effects artists call the fishing village of Medria home. Colorful explosions and wandering puppets are commonplace.                                                                                                                                |
| Point Hallucination       | The Mists often surge over Lake Variatio to deposit newcomers at the rickety quay known as Point Hallucination, where traveling merchants and performers eagerly greet them.                                                                                        |
| Wildersung Wood           | At twilight, a sourceless chorus drifts through these woods. Those who don’t sing along risk losing their lives, while those who discover the last verse discover a hidden sanctuary.                                                                               |

## Harkon Lukas {#rthw:kartakass:HarkonLukas}

Darklord Who Preys on Talent

[![(Artist: Igor Krstic)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/12-003.harkon-lukas.jpg)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/12-003.harkon-lukas.jpg)

> “I must say, your skill is unlike any I’ve ever seen. The name’s Harkon. I’m sure you’ve heard of me.”
>
> —Harkon Lukas

The charming werewolf Harkon Lukas manipulates those around him to satisfy his narcissistic needs for adulation and control. Endlessly seeking fame, Harkon travels widely, earning applause and accolades. Yet, whenever he returns to a town he’s performed in, he finds he’s been forgotten. Lukas believes he needs just the right song or inspiration to make himself unforgettable. To that end, he searches for talented protégés, cultivating their skills, then stealing their work. He ensures their loyalty by gifting them copies of his cursed wolf-tooth necklace, [**Harkon’s Bite**](#ref:magic_item:11610584-harkons-bite "https://www.dndbeyond.com/magic-items/11610584-harkons-bite"), or by transforming them into werewolves. He then manipulates these victims into believing only he will accept them.

Harkon wears a signature wide-brimmed hat and wolf-tooth necklace, and he carries a violin he calls Bleeding Heart. He uses flattery to charm those he takes an interest in. A skilled artist who declines the offer to become his protégé often earns his obsession. The Darklord might go to any extreme to claim such performers’ talents as his own.

### [Harkon Lukas](#ref:monster:6491360-harkon-lukas "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491360-harkon-lukas") {#rthw:kartakass:HarkonLukasrefmonster6491360harkonlukashttpswwwdndbeyondcommonsters6491360harkonlukas}

Medium Monstrosity (Lycanthrope), Chaotic Evil

**AC** 15 **Initiative** +14 (24)

**HP** 187 (22d8 + 88)

**Speed** 30 ft. 40 ft. (hybrid form only), 50 ft. (dire wolf form only)

|     |     | Mod | Save |
| --- | --- | --- | ---- |
| STR | 21  | +5  | +5   |
| DEX | 18  | +4  | +4   |
| CON | 19  | +4  | +9   |

|     |     | Mod | Save |

| INT | 14  | +2  | +2   |

| CHA | 19  | +4  | +4   |

**Skills** [**Perception**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#skills) +8, [**Performance**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#skills) +9, [**Stealth**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#skills) +9

**Immunities** [**Charmed**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#charmedcondition), [**Frightened**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#frightenedcondition)
