#### Traits {#rthw:kartakass:Traits}

**_Blood Frenzy._** Harkon has [**Advantage**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#advantage) on attack rolls against any creature that doesn’t have all its Hit Points.

**_Darklord Restoration._** If Harkon dies, he revives with all his Hit Points in 1d10 weeks somewhere in Kartakass.

**_Legendary Resistance (3/Day, or 4/Day in Domain)._** If Harkon fails a saving throw, he can choose to succeed instead.

**_Regeneration._** Harkon gains 10 Hit Points at the start of each of its turns if he has at least 1 Hit Point. If Harkon takes Radiant damage, this trait doesn’t function at the start of its next turn.

#### Actions {#rthw:kartakass:Actions}

**_Multiattack._** Harkon makes two Swipe attacks. He can replace one attack with (A) Bite or (B) Enthralling Performance.

**_Bite (Dire Wolf or Hybrid Form Only)._** _Melee Attack Roll:_ +10, reach 5 ft. _Hit:_ 14 (2d8 + 5) Piercing damage plus 14 (4d6) Necrotic damage. If the target is a Humanoid, it is subjected to the following effect: _Constitution Saving Throw:_ DC 17. _Failure:_ The target is cursed. If the cursed target drops to 0 Hit Points, it instead becomes a [**Werewolf**](#ref:monster:5195267-werewolf "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195267-werewolf") under the DM’s control and has 50 Hit Points. The curse can’t be removed until Harkon dies. _Success:_ The target is immune to Harkon’s curse for 24 hours.

**_Swipe (Dire Wolf or Hybrid Form Only)._** _Melee Attack Roll:_ +10, reach 5 ft. _Hit:_ 16 (2d10 + 5) Slashing damage. If the target is a Medium or smaller creature, it has the [**Prone**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#pronecondition) condition.

**_Enthralling Performance (Humanoid Form Only)._** _Wisdom Saving Throw:_ DC 17, each creature in a 30-foot [**Emanation**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#emanationareaofeffect) originating from Harkon. _Failure:_ The target has the [**Charmed**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#charmedcondition) condition for 1 hour or until it takes damage.

#### Bonus Actions {#rthw:kartakass:BonusActions}

**_Shape-Shift._** Harkon [**shape-shifts**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#shapeshifting) into a Large dire wolf–humanoid hybrid or a Large dire wolf, or he returns to his true humanoid form. His game statistics, other than his size, are the same in each form. Any equipment he is wearing or carrying isn’t transformed.

#### Legendary Actions {#rthw:kartakass:LegendaryActions}

Legendary Action Uses: 3 (4 in Domain). Immediately after another creature’s turn, Harkon can expend a use to take one of the following actions. Harkon regains all expended uses at the start of each of his turns.

**_Crushing Insult._** Harkon uses Shape-Shift to return to his humanoid form, then uses the following effect. _Wisdom Saving Throw:_ DC 17, each creature of Harkon’s choice that he can see within 30 feet of himself (creatures [**Charmed**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#charmedcondition) by Harkon automatically fail this save). _Failure:_ 16 (3d10) Psychic damage. _Failure or Success:_ Harkon can’t take this action again until the start of his next turn.

**_Pounce._** Harkon moves up to half his Speed and makes one Swipe attack.

**_Surprise Bite._** Harkon uses Shape-Shift to turn into his hybrid or dire wolf form and then makes one Bite attack. Harkon can’t take this action again until the start of his next turn.

### Harkon’s Tale {#rthw:kartakass:HarkonsTale}

Harkon Lukas weaves numerous self-aggrandizing tales of his origins. Among them, Harkon tells of being spurned for his ambitions by the werewolves that raised him. Through talent and sacrifice, he became a legendary performer, and people flocked to bask in his remarkable presence.

Eventually, the rulers of Harkon’s homeland realized the threat posed by Harkon’s growing fame. Officials tried to imprison him for invented crimes, but Harkon’s fans defended him. When royal agents came for him, Harkon feigned his death, and his followers revolted. When outraged masses bearing Harkon’s coffin besieged the royal palace, Harkon ended his ploy. He burst from his crimson coffin in wolf form and devoured the land’s monarch. Drenched in blood, the “resurrected” Harkon returned to his human form and donned the monarch’s crown amid the cheers of his deluded followers. Yet before Harkon’s reign could begin, the Mists rose around him. When they cleared, Harkon found himself in an unfamiliar land called Kartakass.

### Harkon’s Domain {#rthw:kartakass:HarkonsDomain}

Kartakass is altered by Harkon’s presence, creating the following effects:

**Beast Spies.** From dawn until dusk, Tiny Beasts in the domain magically gain the ability to understand Common and can communicate telepathically with other Beasts and Monstrosities.

**Children of the Night.** Harkon exerts influence over the animals of his domain. From dusk until dawn, Medium or smaller Beasts within 1 miles of Harkon have the [**Charmed**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#charmedcondition) condition. If Harkon pleases, these animals become [**Hostile**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#hostileattitude) to creatures other than Harkon and his allies.

**Closing the Borders.** While in his domain, Harkon can close or open the borders to Kartakass at will. While the borders are closed, a strange melody fills the Mists surrounding Kartakass. A creature that enters the Mists for the first time on a turn or starts its turn in them must succeed on a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw, or it has the [**Unconscious**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#unconsciouscondition) condition for 1d6 hours, then awakes within sight of the town of Harmonia in Kartakass. A creature makes this save only once per turn.

If Harkon dies, these effects end immediately.

### Harkon’s Lair {#rthw:kartakass:HarkonsLair}

The Darklord owns a tavern in Skald called the Old Kartakan Inn and Taverna. The inn occupies a small island on the Sing Song River. Nightly, Harkon Lukas or artists under his tutelage perform there.

#### Old Kartakan Inn and Taverna {#rthw:kartakass:OldKartakanInnandTaverna}

Welcoming and rustic, the Old Kartakan features subtle wolf-themed decor. The site is depicted on [map 2.22](#rthw:kartakass:map222oldkartakaninnandtaverna "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/kartakass#map222oldkartakaninnandtaverna") and has the following features:

**Bedrooms.** The inn’s rooms are insulated to block the sounds of performances and maulings alike.

**Harkon Lukas’s Room.** Several secret doors and a trapdoor lead to Harkon’s tower bedroom, where he hides evidence of his own uninspired music and trophies from past victims.

**Secret Doors and Chambers.** The inn is riddled with secret spaces to spy into other chambers, hide bodies, or indulge in bestial meals.

**Taproom.** Among the drinks the taverna offers is Meekulbrau, a blood-red berry wine that soothes the throat and improves vocal performances.

## Adventures in Kartakass {#rthw:kartakass:AdventuresinKartakass}

Adventures set in Kartakass involve art, werewolves, and sinister ambitions. Use this section to develop horror adventures in this domain.

[![Locals celebrate during a festival in Skald, unaware of the predators lurking among them (Artist: Maihope)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/12-004.festival-in-skald.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/12-004.festival-in-skald.png)

### Horror in Kartakass {#rthw:kartakass:HorrorinKartakass}

Kartakan adventures often include the following elements.

#### Harkon’s Curse {#rthw:kartakass:HarkonsCurse}

Harkon Lukas can create a copy of his signature necklace once per month on the night of the full moon. This cursed copy is called _Harkon’s Bite._

---

##### [Harkon’s Bite](#ref:magic_item:11610584-harkons-bite "https://www.dndbeyond.com/magic-items/11610584-harkons-bite") {#rthw:kartakass:HarkonsBiterefmagicitem11610584harkonsbitehttpswwwdndbeyondcommagicitems11610584harkonsbite}

Wondrous Item, Uncommon (Requires Attunement by a Humanoid)

A dire wolf’s tooth dangles from this simple cord necklace. You gain a +1 bonus to ability checks and saving throws while you wear this necklace.

**_Curse._** This necklace is cursed. Attuning to the necklace curses you; this curse can’t be removed until [**Harkon Lukas**](#ref:monster:6491360-harkon-lukas "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491360-harkon-lukas") dies. As long as you remain cursed, you become a [**Werewolf**](#ref:monster:5195267-werewolf "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195267-werewolf") serving Harkon Lukas under the DM’s control during the night of a full moon.

---

#### Harkon’s Manipulations {#rthw:kartakass:HarkonsManipulations}

Harkon Lukas seeks to win the attention and trust of artistic and charismatic individuals. This might include characters—especially bards—or their allies. Harkon might do this to further a grand plot, but he also does so to assuage his perpetually bruised ego and satisfy his need for control. Harkon also seeks supernatural forces he can exploit, including magic items or beings with performative powers—such as an [**Instrument of the Bards**](#ref:magic_item:9228788-instrument-of-the-bards "https://www.dndbeyond.com/magic-items/9228788-instrument-of-the-bards"), [**harpies**](#ref:monster:5195069-harpy "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195069-harpy"), or [**satyrs**](#ref:monster:5195195-satyr "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195195-satyr").

Harkon presents himself as a charming admirer or mentor seeking to aid others. He tries to manipulate those he pursues and earn their trust by encouraging them to do the following:

- Collaborate in creating a new song or show
- Compete in performances against the domain’s meistersingers
- Join him for tutoring or training exercises
- Protect him from a jealous former student
- Find a performer who stole one of his songs
- Travel with him on a tour of other towns

Harkon’s requests eventually turn criminal or violent. He might then blackmail those who aided him or threaten their reputations, or he might isolate them by gifting them [**Harkon’s Bite**](#ref:magic_item:11610584-harkons-bite "https://www.dndbeyond.com/magic-items/11610584-harkons-bite"). Harkon continues such manipulations until it bores him, at which point he consumes his prey.

#### The Lukas Pack {#rthw:kartakass:TheLukasPack}

An ever-changing entourage of followers and victims surrounds Harkon Lukas, but three individuals are constants in the Darklord’s life:

**Akriel Lukas.** Harkon’s eldest daughter, Akriel (Medium, Chaotic Evil [**Performer Legend**](#ref:monster:5195154-performer-legend "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195154-performer-legend")), idolizes Harkon and pursues her own performing career. The Dark Powers don’t torment Akriel as they do her father, and her reputation steadily grows—much to her father’s resentment. Akriel is a human and isn’t a lycanthrope.

**Casimir Lukas.** Harkon’s eldest son, Casimir (Medium, Chaotic Neutral [**Spy Master**](#ref:monster:5195216-spy-master "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195216-spy-master")), is seeking his place in the world. He wants nothing to do with Harkon, preferring to travel, even to other domains. Whether at the whims of his father or the Mists, Casimir always finds his way back to Skald. Casimir is a human and isn’t a lycanthrope.

**Haldrake Moonbaun.** Harkon’s oldest ally, Haldrake (Medium [**Werewolf**](#ref:monster:5195267-werewolf "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195267-werewolf")) appears as a heavily tattooed human. He serves as the Old Kartakan Inn and Taverna mixologist and head bouncer. When Harkon isn’t in Skald, he ensures things at the taverna run smoothly. Haldrake aids Harkon in his plots and knows many of the Darklord’s secrets, so Harkon compensates him well.

#### Traces of Terror {#rthw:kartakass:TracesofTerror}

Kartakass’s charm masks its horrors. Roll on or choose a result from the Kartakass Sights table to inspire unsettling scenes in the domain.

**Kartakass Sights**

| 1d6 | Characters Witness …                           |
| --- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| 1   | Awakened sheep plotting against a shepherd.    |
| 2   | A cheery home that shows signs of slaughter.   |
| 3   | Folk carvings of youths dragged off by wolves. |
| 4   | A fountain depicting dancing wolves.           |
| 5   | Lupine paw prints in a tavern or theater.      |
| 6   | A songbird singing until its heart stops.      |

### Kartakass Campaign Arc {#rthw:kartakass:KartakassCampaignArc}

A campaign in Kartakass might follow this outline:

**Levels 1–2.** The characters meet Maria, a human woman whose idealistic son, Frantosh, ran away to Harmonia to become a performer. She gives the characters an Uncommon [**Instrument of the Bards**](#ref:magic_item:9228788-instrument-of-the-bards "https://www.dndbeyond.com/magic-items/9228788-instrument-of-the-bards") and will allow them to keep it if they return Frantosh home safely. Along the way to Harmonia, the characters are plagued by [**Wolves**](#ref:monster:4775850-wolf "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/4775850-wolf") and people-eating [**Goblins**](#ref:monster:16907-goblin "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/16907-goblin").

**Levels 3–6.** In Harmonia, the characters find Frantosh has begun performing with a skilled bard named [**Harkon Lukas**](#ref:monster:6491360-harkon-lukas "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491360-harkon-lukas"). Harkon encourages the characters to help Frantosh follow his dreams. To help Frantosh, Harkon asks the characters to fetch voice-enchanting waters from a mystical silver spring near Argent Falls Conservatory. The spring is guarded by dead performers risen as [**Banshees**](#ref:monster:5194916-banshee "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5194916-banshee") and a covetous [**Young Copper Dragon**](#ref:monster:5195281-young-copper-dragon "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195281-young-copper-dragon").

**Levels 7–8.** On returning to Harmonia, the characters find Frantosh went to Skald with Harkon. There, Frantosh is performing nightly with Harkon at the Old Kartakan Inn and Taverna. Frantosh—now wearing a wolf-tooth necklace Harkon gave him—refuses to leave with the characters until after his first solo performance. The “Hungry for More” adventure below details this performance. After this Harkon might resent the characters or start obsessing over one of them.

### Hungry for More {#rthw:kartakass:HungryforMore}

Adventure for Level 7 Characters

**Situation.** The singer Frantosh has fallen under the sway of Harkon Lukas. He refuses to return to his family until after he performs at the Old Kartakan Inn and Taverna on the night of the full moon.

**Hook.** Frantosh’s mother, Maria, offers the party an Uncommon [**Instrument of the Bards**](#ref:magic_item:9228788-instrument-of-the-bards "https://www.dndbeyond.com/magic-items/9228788-instrument-of-the-bards") if they return her son.

[![Map 2.22: Old Kartakan Inn and Taverna View Player Version (Artist: Mike Schley)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/map-12-02.old-kartakan-inn-and-taverna.jpg)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/map-12-02.old-kartakan-inn-and-taverna.jpg)

#### Encounters {#rthw:kartakass:Encounters}

This adventure uses map 2.22 and includes these encounters.

**_Frantosh’s Debut._** Frantosh (Medium [**Performer**](#ref:monster:5195156-performer "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195156-performer")) is performing on his own for the first time tonight. If the characters seek him out and mention his mother, he agrees to leave with them after his performance—it ends around midnight. If the characters try to abduct Frantosh, three [**Tough Bosses**](#ref:monster:4904883-tough-boss "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/4904883-tough-boss") (or more) in Harkon Lukas’s service intervene.

**_Full-Moon._** Mention that the performance is on first night of the full moon only if a character asks.

**_The Old Kartakan._** The taverna is a popular spot in Skald. Crowds of [**Commoners**](#ref:monster:5194951-commoner "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5194951-commoner") fill the first floor of the Old Kartakan. [**Harkon Lukas**](#ref:monster:6491360-harkon-lukas "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491360-harkon-lukas") (detailed earlier in [this section](#rthw:kartakass:HarkonLukas "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/kartakass#HarkonLukas")) is here, but he avoids combat unless otherwise mentioned.

**_The Show._** During his 1-hour performance, Frantosh makes a DC 15 Charisma ([**Performance**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#skills)) check every 15 minutes. Characters can aid him with the [**Help**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#helpaction) action or in other ways. Track how many of these checks Frantosh succeeds on. During the performance, these events occur:

**Heckler.** A drunk **Commoner** heckles Frantosh. If he’s not silenced within 3 rounds, Frantosh has [**Disadvantage**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#disadvantage) on his next ability check.

**Brawl.** A fight breaks out between three [**Bandits**](#ref:monster:5194915-bandit "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5194915-bandit"). After the first round of combat, a **Bandit** with bad aim targets Frantosh with its Light Crossbow action each round. If Frantosh is struck, he automatically fails his next ability check.

**Howl.** A wolf howls outside, distracting the audience. The characters have 1 round to direct attention back to Frantosh, perhaps with flashy magic or by making a DC 18 Charisma ([**Performance**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#skills)) check. If they don’t, Frantosh has [**Disadvantage**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#disadvantage) on his next ability check.

**_After the Show._** After the show, the characters see Frantosh vanish through a secret door. The next events take place in the inn’s hidden areas.

If Frantosh succeeded on three or more checks during the show, Harkon Lukas seeks to keep Frantosh. He won’t fight the characters, but he uses the necklace Frantosh wears to transform the singer into a [**Werewolf**](#ref:monster:5195267-werewolf "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195267-werewolf"). Frantosh and four more **Werewolf** servants of Harkon assault the characters.

If Frantosh didn’t succeed on three or more checks during the show, Harkon has grown bored with Frantosh. The characters find Frantosh [**Bloodied**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#bloodied) and being attacked by four **Werewolves**.

**_Conclusion._** If the characters escape the Old Kartakan with Frantosh (potentially now a **Werewolf**), each earns a bonus 1,700 XP. Even if forced into battle, Harkon Lukas won’t kill the characters—they’ve intrigued the Darklord, and he might appear to toy with them later.

</CHAPTER>

# Lamordia {#rthw:lamordia:Lamordia}

Domain of Snow and Stitched Flesh

> #### **Darklord:** [Viktra Mordenheim](#rthw:lamordia:ViktraMordenheim "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/lamordia#ViktraMordenheim") {#rthw:lamordia:ViktraMordenheim}
>
> **Adventure Genres:** [Body horror](#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:bodyhorror "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/creating-domains-of-dread#bodyhorror") and [gothic horror](#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:gothichorror "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/creating-domains-of-dread#gothichorror")
>
> **Hallmarks:** Amoral science, bizarre constructs, frigid wilderness, mutagenic radiation
>
> **Mist Talismans:** Animated digits, glowing minerals, preserved humanoid limb
>
> **Aligned Tarokka Card:** Transmuter
>
> **Opposed Tarokka Card:** Marionette

[![(Artist: Pam Wishbow)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/13-001.transmuter-tarokka.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/13-001.transmuter-tarokka.png) [![](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/13-002.marionette-tarokka.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/13-002.marionette-tarokka.png)

A domain of amoral science, Lamordia shudders amid the icy environment and terror of its residents’ creations. Revolutions of steam and steel spur Lamordia’s people into frenzies of amoral invention. From industrialized communities and the iron walls of Ludendorf, the domain’s largest city, flow streams of scrap and chemical poisons that taint the land and transform creatures into horrors. Yet, the domain’s reckless scientists don’t pursue just mechanized inventions—the greatest goal is reinvention of life itself, transmuting people into ideals and unlocking generations of potential. In the name of such ambitions, the depraved reshape life and unleash abominations. And no aspirations have unleashed greater evils than those of the domain’s Darklord, [**Dr. Viktra Mordenheim**](#ref:monster:6491399-viktra-mordenheim "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491399-viktra-mordenheim").

## Domain Features {#rthw:lamordia:DomainFeatures}

Lamordia is known for the following features:

**Frigid Environs.** Lamordia is a frigid land of bleak mountains, frozen swaps, and icy seas. Few voluntarily trek into its wilderness, fearing freak blizzards and starving beasts.

**Mutated Creatures.** Creatures warped by alchemy roam Lamordia. The most infamous are the monstrous “whales” of the Sea of Secrets—violent, unnatural leviathans, no two of which are alike.

**Rational Culture.** The people of Lamordia are direct and skeptical of superstition. They revere scientific innovation—as it’s all that stands between them and a life of frigid starvation. Magic is acknowledged but widely considered backward.

**Steam Technology.** Steam power driven by boiling sewers fuels clockwork inventions and massive cranes in the city of Ludendorf.

## Locations in Lamordia {#rthw:lamordia:LocationsinLamordia}

Lamordia is a frigid land. In the north, the Sea of Secrets is choked with ice, while the mountains known as the Sleeping Beast are never without snow. The cities of Ludendorf and Neufurchtenburg are detailed below, and other notable locations are summarized on the [Lamordia Locations table](#rthw:lamordia:lamordialocations "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/lamordia#lamordialocations").

### Ludendorf {#rthw:lamordia:Ludendorf}

The city of Ludendorf is a morass of steam-powered factories operating at the behest of morally bankrupt barons. Boiling sewers and steam tunnels thread the city’s foundations, heating cramped tenements and powering cranes serving the city’s fleet of ironclad ships. These ice-breaking, whaling vessels dare the Sea of Secrets to bring back massive beasts that provide vital food and fuel for the city.

At the city’s heart, the unscrupulous Ludendorf University conducts risky investigations into such fields as alchemical combustion, automated ingenuity, chemical sentience, and speculative anatomy. The university continually needs new subjects for experiments and hires volunteers or pays individuals for “flesh rights”—ownership of their cadavers once they die. A secret society within Ludendorf University idolizes Viktra and follows the reckless paths laid by her work.

### Neufurchtenburg {#rthw:lamordia:Neufurchtenburg}

The smoking refineries of Neufurchtenburg process minerals harvested from the Sleeping Beast. These rare, little-understood elements are then shipped to Ludendorf’s factories. Radiation-warped monsters from the nearby bogs frequently attack, disrupting operations, but the town’s people use hulking clockwork machines, cutting-edge firearms, and destructive alchemy to fend off incursions.

## Viktra Mordenheim {#rthw:lamordia:ViktraMordenheim}

Darklord Who Pursues Perfection

[![(Artist: Lenka Šimečková)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/13-003.viktra-mordenheim.jpg)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/13-003.viktra-mordenheim.jpg)

> “Ah. You’re conscious. Good. Test your limbs, and get accustomed to your new body.”
>
> —Viktra Mordenheim

From her laboratory at Schloss Mordenheim, Dr. Viktra Mordenheim uses her scientific genius to create horrors and wonders. All manner of undead and constructs march from her laboratory, but such flawed creations don’t satisfy Mordenheim. Rather, she seeks to re-create or reclaim her greatest creation, the Unbreakable Heart, a miraculous device that grants life to Mordenheim’s elusive reanimated victim, Elise.

Medium Humanoid (Human), Lawful Evil

**AC** 15 **Initiative** +3 (13)

**HP** 123 (19d8 + 38)

**Speed** 30 ft.

**Gear** [**Studded Leather Armor**](#ref:equipment:3-studded-leather "https://www.dndbeyond.com/equipment/3-studded-leather")

#### Traits {#rthw:lamordia:Traits}

**_Bolster Inventions._** At the end of each of Viktra’s turns, each of her Construct allies in a 5-foot [**Emanation**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#emanationareaofeffect) originating from Viktra gains 5 [**Temporary Hit Points**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#temporaryhitpoints). This trait doesn’t function if Viktra has the [**Incapacitated**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#incapacitatedcondition) condition.

**_Darklord Restoration._** If Viktra dies, she revives with all her Hit Points in 1d10 weeks somewhere in Lamordia.

**_Legendary Resistance (3/Day, or 4/Day in Domain)._** If Viktra fails a saving throw, she can choose to succeed instead.

#### Actions {#rthw:lamordia:Actions}

**_Multiattack._** Viktra makes two Lightning Rod attacks. She can replace one attack with a use of Syringe.

**_Lightning Rod._** _Melee or Ranged Attack Roll:_ +6, reach 5 ft. or range 90 ft. _Hit:_ 12 (2d8 + 3) Lightning damage, and the target can’t take Reactions until the start of its next turn.

**_Syringe._** _Constitution Saving Throw:_ DC 16, one creature Viktra can see within 5 feet. _Failure:_ The target has the [**Poisoned**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#poisonedcondition) condition for 1 minute. While Poisoned in this way, the target suffers one of the following effects (Viktra’s choice). The target repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. The target succeeds automatically after 1 minute:

**Corrosive Serum.** The target takes 10 (4d4) Acid damage at the start of each of its turns, and its Speed decreases by 10 feet.

**Deadly Serum.** The target takes 11 (2d10) Necrotic damage at the start of each of its turns, and it can’t regain Hit Points.

**Mind-Altering Serum.** The target takes 10 (3d6) Psychic damage at the start of each of its turns, and it has [**Disadvantage**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#disadvantage) on saving throws to maintain [**Concentration**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#concentration).

#### Bonus Actions {#rthw:lamordia:BonusActions}

**_Activate Constructs (1/Day)._** Viktra casts [**Animate Objects**](#ref:spell:2618855-animate-objects "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618855-animate-objects"), using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability.

#### Reactions {#rthw:lamordia:Reactions}

**_Redirect Attack._** _Trigger:_ A creature Viktra can see makes an attack roll against her. _Response:_ Viktra chooses a Small or Medium ally within 5 feet of herself. Viktra and that ally swap places, and the ally becomes the target of the attack instead.

#### Legendary Actions {#rthw:lamordia:LegendaryActions}

Legendary Action Uses: 3 (4 in Domain). Immediately after another creature’s turn, Viktra can expend a use to take one of the following actions. Viktra regains all expended uses at the start of each of her turns.

**_Shocking Prod._** Viktra moves up to half her Speed and makes one Lightning Rod attack. Viktra can’t take this action again until the start of her next turn.

**_Static Explosion._** _Dexterity Saving Throw:_ DC 16, each creature in a 10-foot-radius [**Sphere**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#sphereareaofeffect) centered on a point Viktra can see within 90 feet. _Failure:_ 5 (2d4) Lightning damage. _Success:_ Half damage.

### Viktra’s Tale {#rthw:lamordia:ViktrasTale}

From an early age, Viktra Mordenheim sought to understand the complexities of anatomy. She pursued medicine not to aid patients but to reveal the secrets of life. Eventually, her research bent toward reanimating dead flesh and improving humanoid bodies. When Viktra began employing thieves to procure specimens for her tests, she met Elise, a beautiful resurrectionist whose spontaneity entranced the methodical surgeon. Viktra was smitten, and with Elise she discovered there might be more to life than chemical reactions.

When Elise started exhibiting signs of an incurable disease, Viktra hastened her experiments. On the doctor’s operating table, victims were killed, returned to life, and died again as Viktra sought a breakthrough. When finally Elise passed away, Viktra refused to accept failure. The doctor worked feverishly crafting her masterpiece, an artificial organ she called the Unbreakable Heart. But as she fitted the device into Elise’s corpse, constables burst into the lab and accused the doctor of numerous murders. As Viktra struggled against arrest, smoking chemicals, arcing electricity, and a strange mist filled the laboratory.

When the chaos cleared, Viktra awoke in Lamordia, an unfamiliar land where her genius was celebrated. Elise and the Unbreakable Heart were nowhere to be found, but the doctor soon heard rumors of a wondrous and terrifying figure who wandered the icy realm and whose chest glowed as though her heart were the sun. Ever since, Viktra has continued her experiments, striving to re-create her successes but failing every time. Between disappointments she searches for whatever Elise has become—and with her, the miracle of the Unbreakable Heart.

### Viktra’s Domain {#rthw:lamordia:ViktrasDomain}

Lamordia is altered by Viktra’s presence, creating the following effects:

**Air of Obsession.** When a creature fails a Constitution saving throw to maintain [**Concentration**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#concentration), that creature takes 3 (1d6) Psychic damage.

**Closing the Borders.** While in her domain, Viktra can close or open the borders to Lamordia. While the borders are closed, lightning storms roll through the Mists surrounding Lamordia. A creature that enters the Mists for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there makes a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw, taking 4d6 Lightning damage on a failed save and half as much on a successful one. A creature makes this save only once per turn.

If Viktra dies, these effects end immediately.

### Viktra’s Lair {#rthw:lamordia:ViktrasLair}

Schloss Mordenheim is a castle that stands amid dramatic cliffs overlooking the sea. Travelers from Ludendorf reach Schloss Mordenheim by crossing the ice and following a treacherous road.

#### Schloss Mordenheim {#rthw:lamordia:SchlossMordenheim}

Schloss Mordenheim holds dozens of rooms, but most are empty or have furnishings pushed aside to make room for scientific supplies. Prominent locations from this site are depicted on map 2.24 and have the following features:

**Auxiliary Workshops.** Viktra’s assistants toil in workshops where they craft tools and devices to the doctor’s exacting specifications.

**Disused Chambers.** Rooms originally constructed for relaxation serve as storage rooms, act as extra laboratories, or sit eerily empty. A dining hall half filled with crates is set for a single diner, but it’s rarely used.

**Gate and Entry.** A stone bridge crosses a chasm leading to the castle’s keep. Stairs flanked by grim statuary lead to the keep’s entrance.

**Laboratory Tower.** A heavily renovated turret holds Viktra’s laboratory. Mechanisms allow the tower’s roof to part and its operating table to rise 30 feet, exposing subjects to lightning during the island’s frequent storms.

## Adventures in Lamordia {#rthw:lamordia:AdventuresinLamordia}

Lamordia provides a stage for adventures featuring amoral science and altered or resurrected beings. Use this section to develop horror adventures in this domain.

[![Schloss Mordenheim hosts the laboratories and obscene experiments of Viktra Mordenheim (Artist: Sean Vo)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/13-004.schloss-mordenheim.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/13-004.schloss-mordenheim.png)

### Horror in Lamordia {#rthw:lamordia:HorrorinLamordia}

Adventures in Lamordia often include the following elements.

#### Elise von Brandthofen {#rthw:lamordia:ElisevonBrandthofen}

Elise knows she died yet finds herself alive again. She is now a [**Mordenheim’s Monster**](#ref:monster:6491376-mordenheims-monster "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491376-mordenheims-monster") (see [chapter 5](#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:mordenheimsmonster "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/denizens-of-the-mists#mordenheimsmonster")), and her life is sustained by the Unbreakable Heart (see the following section). Elise is learning to accept her new life but avoids Lamordia’s people, who label her as an outcast and a monster. She also knows that Viktra Mordenheim seeks to recover the Unbreakable Heart. The doctor’s actions—as well as the mercenaries she sends to abduct Elise—have shattered the pair’s bond. Now Elise hides at a secret sanctuary in the [Isles of Agony](#rthw:lamordia:islesofagony "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/lamordia#islesofagony") called Hope’s Heart. Here, she shelters other victims and creations of Viktra, showing them the esteem their creator denies them. Those in Elise’s care have taken to calling themselves the Children (detailed below).

#### Mordenheim’s Masterpiece {#rthw:lamordia:MordenheimsMasterpiece}

The Unbreakable Heart is a nonmagical scientific wonder. Despite being the creator of the Unbreakable Heart, Viktra can’t re-create it and is obsessed with reclaiming it and rediscovering its secrets.

---

##### Unbreakable Heart {#rthw:lamordia:UnbreakableHeart}

This heart-shaped, clockwork device installs itself, fastening into place if positioned where a creature’s heart used to be. A creature that contains the device is affected as if by the [**Raise Dead**](#ref:spell:2618922-raise-dead "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618922-raise-dead") spell. After this, the creature is immune to disease, ceases to age, and doesn’t die of old age. The Unbreakable Heart glows, shedding [**Bright Light**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#brightlight) in a 10-foot radius and [**Dim Light**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#dimlight) for an additional 10 feet. While inside a creature, the device causes the creature to shed Dim Light in a 10-foot radius.

---

#### The Children {#rthw:lamordia:TheChildren}

The Children are discarded creations of Dr. Viktra Mordenheim who have found shelter with Elise. Composed a few dozen Constructs and chemically animated Undead, the Children follow Elise’s lead and seek to live peacefully away from those who would misunderstand and harm them.

The exception to this is Adam, a [**Mordenheim’s Monster**](#ref:monster:6491376-mordenheims-monster "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491376-mordenheims-monster") who recently joined the Children. Adam was created by Viktra to capture Elise, but Elise convinced him to join her instead. Unlike Elise, Adam was created from disparate parts and knows no previous life. Although Elise seeks to teach Adam humanity, he shows little respect for the lives of more fragile beings. Moreover, Adam is fascinated by Mordenheim’s work and quietly seeks ways to create life that will serve him.

[![A desperate crew of Ludendorf whalers runs afoul of Rahab, a fleshless leviathan that hunts the Sea of Secrets (Artist: Bastien Grivet)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/13-005.sea-of-secrets.jpg)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/13-005.sea-of-secrets.jpg)

### Lamordia Campaign Arc {#rthw:lamordia:LamordiaCampaignArc}

Campaigns set in Lamordia often make the characters subjects or accomplices to Viktra’s schemes. A campaign here might follow this outline:

**Levels 1–2.** A dean of Ludendorf University hires the characters to escort the coach of students traveling to an assistantship at Schloss Mordenheim. Along the way, they are plagued by mismatched [**Homunculi**](#ref:monster:5195080-homunculus "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195080-homunculus") that sabotage their travels. These are members of the Children, seeking to stymie folk they take for Mordenheim’s allies.

**Levels 3–6.** At Schloss Mordenheim, Viktra Mordenheim hires the character to recover her invention, the Unbreakable Heart. She explains it was stolen by a monster that dwells on the Isles of Agony. Viktra wishes the characters to bring back the heart and the monster. The characters face dangers in the wilds, but the quest culminates in the “Isles of Agony” adventure (see below).

The conclusion of the campaign depends on whether the characters aid Viktra or Elise. When they return to Schloss Mordenheim, events might play out in the following ways:

**Levels 7–9 (Aiding Viktra).** If the characters aid Dr. Mordenheim, the doctor seeks to remove the Unbreakable Heart from Elise or test it by reanimating a new being. This results in a dramatic operation where an enraged [**Mordenheim’s Monster**](#ref:monster:6491376-mordenheims-monster "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491376-mordenheims-monster") (see [chapter 5](#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:mordenheimsmonster "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/denizens-of-the-mists#mordenheimsmonster")) breaks free and rampages through the castle.

**Levels 7–9 (Aiding Elise).** If the characters aid Elise, the characters must free innocent victims of the doctor from the castle and prevent Dr. Mordenheim from animating new terrors by destroying her laboratory. Ultimately the characters must face [**Viktra Mordenheim**](#ref:monster:6491399-viktra-mordenheim "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491399-viktra-mordenheim") (detailed earlier in [this section](#rthw:lamordia:ViktraMordenheim "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/lamordia#ViktraMordenheim")) and two [**Flesh Golems**](#ref:monster:5194997-flesh-golem "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5194997-flesh-golem") made from the assistants the characters brought to the castle.

The campaign might continue with the characters continuing to aid or being targeted by the Children.

### Isles of Agony {#rthw:lamordia:IslesofAgony}

Adventure for Level 5 Characters

**Situation.** The characters must recover the Unbreakable Heart (detailed earlier in [this section](#rthw:lamordia:unbreakableheart "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/lamordia#unbreakableheart")). They don’t know it’s inside the outcast Elise.

**Hook.** Viktra hires the characters to recover the Unbreakable Heart, which was stolen by a monster. They are offered 2,500 GP, plus a 1,000 GP bonus if they capture the monster.

#### Encounters {#rthw:lamordia:Encounters}

The adventure begins when the characters reach the Isles of Agony and consists of these encounters.

**_Shipwreck._** Soon after reaching the icy isles, the characters find six human survivors of a wrecked whaling ship. These sailors ([**Pirates**](#ref:monster:4904830-pirate "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/4904830-pirate")) are led by Mate Herzogin, and their captain was carried off by a half-human, half-machine monster. The survivors seek help returning home but want to recover their captain’s corpse (and their pay, which he carried).

**_The Monster._** The monster the survivors fear is one of the Children, a [**Flesh Golem**](#ref:monster:5194997-flesh-golem "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5194997-flesh-golem") named Kartad. He’s peaceful, but the survivors’ captain, Hans Giesbrecht (Medium [**Pirate Captain**](#ref:monster:4904838-pirate-captain "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/4904838-pirate-captain")), attacked him on sight. Kartad knocked out Hans, panicked, picked him up, and fled to Hope’s Heart.

**_Track of the Monster._** Characters who succeed on a DC 12 Wisdom ([**Survival**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#skills)) check find and can follow Kartad’s tracks to Hope’s Heart. If the characters fail, a survivor points out the path. Roll on or choose results from the following table for three encounters that happen on the way (rerolling duplicates).

| 1d4 | Encounter                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| --- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1   | Six [**Dire Wolves**](#ref:monster:4775812-dire-wolf "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/4775812-dire-wolf") pursue a [**Homunculus**](#ref:monster:5195080-homunculus "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195080-homunculus"). The homunculus flees as soon as possible.                                                  |
| 2   | 1d8 [**Zombies**](#ref:monster:4775851-zombie "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/4775851-zombie") animated by mechanical apparatuses stare into the sky. They are Constructs and don’t react, even if harmed.                                                                                                              |
| 3   | A [**Primeval Owlbear**](#ref:monster:5195171-primeval-owlbear "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195171-primeval-owlbear") made of mismatched parts forages for food; it is a Construct. It is [**Indifferent**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#indifferentattitude) to the characters. |
| 4   | A [**Troll**](#ref:monster:5195241-troll "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195241-troll") hunts alongside a [**Winter Wolf**](#ref:monster:5195272-winter-wolf "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195272-winter-wolf").                                                                                                |

**_Hope’s Heart._** Hope’s Heart is a hidden canyon home to numerous harmless Constructs that is accessed via a passage in an abandoned cabin. When the characters approach, Elise appears on the cliffs 20 feet above and demands to know their business. Elise is a [**Mordenheim’s Monster**](#ref:monster:6491376-mordenheims-monster "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491376-mordenheims-monster") (see [chapter 5](#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:mordenheimsmonster "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/denizens-of-the-mists#mordenheimsmonster")). The Unbreakable Heart glows from her chest.

**_Fighting Elise._** Elise attacks to prevent entry to the cabin and to defend herself. She avoids killing and won’t pursue those who flee. If the characters attack, they’ll likely have to make multiple attempts to wear down Elise or use trickery to defeat her.

**_Negotiating with Elise._** Elise is [**Indifferent**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#indifferentattitude) to the characters or [**Hostile**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#hostileattitude) if they harmed any Constructs on the isle. She’s wary of those who working for Viktra and can share the details described in “[Viktra’s Tale](#rthw:lamordia:viktrastale "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/lamordia#viktrastale").” If a character explains they’re seeking the missing captain, she brings forth Hans and Kartad. Kartad has nursed Hans back to health; he apologizes and releases the bewildered captain.

**_The Crew._** The six survivors arrive to see the characters speaking with Kartad. They overreact on seeing the “monster” and initiate combat. Kartad panics and defends himself. Hans has 10 Hit Points but is too weak to command his crew or fight.

**_Aftermath._** If the characters fight alongside the crew, Kartad and Elise defend themselves but flee after 3 rounds or if anyone is killed. Elise leads her followers to hide elsewhere on the island. The sailors thank the characters and offer to help them rally aid in Ludendorf to return and hunt the monsters.

If the characters deescalate the conflict or defend Kartad, Elise’s attitude toward them improves. She won’t give them the Unbreakable Heart or return to Schloss Mordenheim. Rather, she tries to convince the characters to see Viktra for the villain she is. She entreats them to return to the castle, save captive members of the Children, and thwart the doctor, as detailed in “[Lamordia Campaign Arc](#rthw:lamordia:lamordiacampaignarc "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/lamordia#lamordiacampaignarc").” In return, Elise offers a trove of 4,000 GP and an [**Immovable Rod**](#ref:magic_item:9228785-immovable-rod "https://www.dndbeyond.com/magic-items/9228785-immovable-rod").

Characters who defeat or choose to aid Elise earn a bonus 1,100 XP.

</CHAPTER>

<CHAPTER id="rthw:mordent" title="Mordent">

# Mordent {#rthw:mordent:Mordent}

Domain of the Haunted

> #### **Darklord:** [Wilfred Godefroy](#rthw:mordent:WilfredGodefroy "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/mordent#WilfredGodefroy") {#rthw:mordent:WilfredGodefroy}
>
> **Adventure Genre:** [Ghost stories](#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:ghoststories "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/creating-domains-of-dread#ghoststories")
>
> **Hallmarks:** Ancestral curses, haunted mansions, mist-shrouded moors, vengeful spirits
>
> **Mist Talismans:** Broken jewelry, death mask, faded love letter, family portrait
>
> **Aligned Tarokka Card:** Miser
>
> **Opposed Tarokka Card:** Horseman

[![(Artist: Pam Wishbow)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/14-001.miser-tarokka.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/14-001.miser-tarokka.png) [![](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/14-002.horseman-tarokka.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/14-002.horseman-tarokka.png)

In Mordent, the dead don’t rest. Here, farmers and fishers toil in scattered villages, cleaving to stoic, hardworking traditions. In the manors of landed, aristocratic families, the bearers of noble names view themselves as conservators of the land and of stifling reputations. Tradition, memory, and expectation haunt the lives of Mordent’s people, and when they die, nothing changes.

Little known to the living, the dead in Mordent rise as spirits, and for most—knowing no other ways—their work continues. Abandoned estates hide spectral generations of frustrated nobles and their downtrodden servants. While some spirits drift idly or deteriorate to mere impressions of their past selves, others greedily cling to their former possessions and ambitions. Some pernicious spirits become infamous hauntings, while others—such as the domain’s Darklord, the ghostly [**Lord Wilfred Godefroy**](#ref:monster:6491403-wilfred-godefroy "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491403-wilfred-godefroy")—seek to dominate the living and dead.

## Domain Features {#rthw:mordent:DomainFeatures}

Mordent is known for the following features:

**Lingering Spirits.** All manner of spectral undead and other hauntings lurk in Mordent. Ghost stories and rumors of haunted sites are common.

**Local Nobility.** Mordent is governed by town mayors and local lords. Few nobles remain, and some have only decrepit manors left to their names.

**Old Faiths.** People casually worship vague deities in Mordent, but evidence of forgotten druidic traditions lies scattered around the wilds.

**Spiritualism.** Attempting to communicate with the dead is a popular pursuit for investigators, bored nobles, and charlatans.

**Tradition and Shame.** The people of Mordent follow traditions that prioritize hard work, self-sufficiency, and avoiding public embarrassment. Locals overlook blatant strangeness so not to shame their neighbors, and every family has secrets.

## Locations in Mordent {#rthw:mordent:LocationsinMordent}

Mordent is a foggy land of forests, fields, and moors that endures frequent rainstorms. The land is dotted with tiny farming hamlets and the rotting homes of forgotten nobles.

The town of Mordentshire is detailed below, and other notable locations are summarized on the [Mordent Locations table](#rthw:mordent:mordentlocations "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/mordent#mordentlocations").

### Mordentshire {#rthw:mordent:Mordentshire}

Mordentshire is the largest community in Mordent. Sturdy fisherfolk work the town docks and, after dusk, fill crowded tavern common rooms. Cold winds frequently blow in from Arden Bay. When they stop, they’re replaced by a shroud of fog the locals call “the breath of the dead.”

To the chagrin of the town’s no-nonsense populace, Mordentshire is home to a small community of scholars and adventurers. Saulbridge Sanitarium provides a refuge for the ill while also welcoming researchers from other domains. Across town, an unassuming herbalist shop is run by [**Rudolph van Richten**](#ref:monster:6491386-rudolph-van-richten "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491386-rudolph-van-richten") (see [chapter 5](#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:rudolphvanrichten "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/denizens-of-the-mists#rudolphvanrichten")), an investigator of all things monstrous and mysterious.

The lands around Mordentshire host two prominent estates. Heather House is the home of the Weathermay family, regional lords who count numerous heroes among their number. To the east stands Gryphon Manor, the notorious House on Gryphon Hill. The mansion has a history of violence, tragedy, and hauntings and is the home of the domain’s Darklord, Lord Wilfred Godefroy.

[![Map 2.25: Mordent View Player Version (Artist: Francesca Baerald)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/map-14-01.mordent.jpg)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/map-14-01.mordent.jpg)

**Mordent Locations**

| Location              | Description                                                                                                                                                                                |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Abbey Point           | A group of silent Ezra worshippers maintain a sanctuary at Abbey Point. Maps there claim that only the sea lies north of the abbey, making the nearby wooded coast a mystery.              |
| Blairsbay             | Little more than a dock, market, and tavern, Blairsbay serves a line of coastal noble estates. Many of these great homes are abandoned, including Lumley House and Preston Hill.           |
| Candle Cross          | The hamlet of Candle Cross spills from the remains of a ruined castle, the drawbridge of which extends over the Arden River. The bridge rises of its own accord to bar evil from entering. |
| Crawford              | Near the village of Crawford, countless of ravens roost at Crawford Manor. A carving in the manor reads: “The Death of Ravens Shalt Thou Abhor, Lest the Crawford Line Be Nevermore.”      |
| Glaston               | The residents of the village of Glaston cleave to druidic traditions. Rumors say ancient druids forged magical passages between the nearby Sigil Lakes and similar sites in realms beyond. |
| Glenwich              | Years ago, the sand cliff that bore half the village of Glenwich—including its ancient church—collapsed into the bay. Locals avoid the tide pools mingling amid dilapidation and the dead. |
| Haworth Hall          | Haworth Hall numbers among the domain’s dozens of lonely, decaying manors. Something inhabits the estate, but whatever it is terrifies Mordent’s ghost and they avoid it at all costs.     |
| Idlethorp             | Miniature constructs made of stitched-together body parts run amok in this abandoned hamlet’s Punchinel Manor, once home to an eccentric inventor.                                         |
| Locustbranch Hospital | Locustbranch was once a renowned hospital, but it was abandoned after a series of mysterious deaths. Now, ghostly patients pack its wards, crying out for cures to eternal ills.           |
| Waterford             | The hamlet of Waterford stands at a confluence of rivers and roads. Here, the Globe inn quietly keeps a back entrance and rooms to accommodate silent, ghostly travelers.                  |
| Whelk Spring House    | The last of the noble Esker family recently died, bequeathing Whelk Spring House to distant relatives. At low tide, the waters of Bent Key Causeway reveal a muddy path to the estate.     |

## Wilfred Godefroy {#rthw:mordent:WilfredGodefroy}

Darklord Tormented by Ghostly Undeath

[![(Artist: Winona Nelson)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/14-003.wilfred-godefory.jpg)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/14-003.wilfred-godefory.jpg)

> “Speak your piece, then hold your tongue. No fools are more insufferable than the living.”
>
> —Wilfred Godefroy

Lord Wilfred Godefroy rules the afterlife of all who die in Mordent. Arrogant, impatient, and vengeful, the Darklord seeks any opportunity to exert his control and reinforce his undying noble standing.

Lord Godefroy haunts the House on Gryphon Hill, along with countless other spirits. Wilfred can send mobs of obedient spirits to do his will anywhere in the domain. He uses his control over the dead to influence the living, threatening to harm his victims’ dead loved ones if they don’t obey his fickle commands.

A generation ago, the creators of the mist-piercing device called the [Apparatus](#rthw:mordent:theapparatus "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/mordent#theapparatus") vanished from Mordent. Lord Godefroy has discovered the hidden machine, but, to his frustration, lacks a way to use it.

### [Wilfred Godefroy](#ref:monster:6491403-wilfred-godefroy "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491403-wilfred-godefroy") {#rthw:mordent:WilfredGodefroyrefmonster6491403wilfredgodefroyhttpswwwdndbeyondcommonsters6491403wilfredgodefroy}

Medium Undead, Neutral Evil

**AC** 12 **Initiative** +2 (12)

**HP** 72 (16d8)

**Speed** 30 ft., Fly 30 ft.

|     |     | Mod | Save |
| --- | --- | --- | ---- |
| STR | 8   | \-1 | \-1  |
| DEX | 14  | +2  | +2   |
| CON | 10  | +0  | +0   |

|     |     | Mod | Save |
| --- | --- | --- | ---- |
| INT | 13  | +1  | +1   |
| WIS | 14  | +2  | +2   |
| CHA | 17  | +3  | +3   |

**Skills** [**Intimidation**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#skills) +6, [**Perception**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#skills) +5

**Resistances** Acid, Bludgeoning, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Piercing, Slashing, Thunder

**Immunities** Necrotic, Poison; [**Charmed**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#charmedcondition), [**Exhaustion**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#exhaustioncondition), [**Grappled**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#grappledcondition), [**Paralyzed**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#paralyzedcondition), [**Petrified**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#petrifiedcondition), [**Poisoned**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#poisonedcondition), [**Prone**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#pronecondition), [**Restrained**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#restrainedcondition), [**Unconscious**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#unconsciouscondition)

**Senses** [**Darkvision**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#darkvision) 120 ft.; Passive Perception 15

**Languages** Common

**Challenge** 6 (XP 2,300, or 2,900 in domain; PB +3)

#### Traits {#rthw:mordent:Traits}

**_Darklord Restoration._** If Wilfred dies, he revives with all his Hit Points in 1d10 weeks somewhere in Mordent.

**_Incorporeal Movement._** Wilfred can move through other creatures and objects as if they were [**Difficult Terrain**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#difficultterrain). He takes 5 (1d10) Force damage if he ends his turn inside an object.

**_Legendary Resistance (3/Day, or 4/Day in Domain)._** If Wilfred fails a saving throw, he can choose to succeed instead.

**_Possessive Aura._** Grasping, ghostly servants surround Wilfred in a 5-foot [**Emanation**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#emanationareaofeffect) originating from him. A creature that ends its turn in this area is subjected to the following effect. _Charisma Saving Throw:_ DC 14. _Failure:_ The target has the [**Charmed**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#charmedcondition) condition. While the creature is Charmed in this way, its Speed is reduced to 0. The target repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. After 1 minute, it succeeds automatically.

#### Actions {#rthw:mordent:Actions}

**_Multiattack._** Wilfred makes two attacks, using Object Slam or Hunting Rifle in any combination.

**_Object Slam._** _Melee Attack Roll:_ +6, reach 5 ft. _Hit:_ 10 (2d6 + 3) Force damage.

**_Hunting Rifle._** _Ranged Attack Roll:_ +6, range 40/120 ft. _Hit:_ 9 (1d12 + 3) Necrotic damage.

#### Reactions {#rthw:mordent:Reactions}

**_Redirect Attack._** _Trigger:_ A creature Wilfred can see makes an attack roll against him. _Response:_ Wilfred chooses a Small or Medium creature within 5 feet of himself that has the [**Charmed**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#charmedcondition) condition. Wilfred and that creature swap places, and the creature becomes the target of the attack instead.

#### Legendary Actions {#rthw:mordent:LegendaryActions}

Legendary Action Uses: 3 (4 in Domain). Immediately after another creature’s turn, Wilfred can expend a use to take one of the following actions. Wilfred regains all expended uses at the start of each of his turns.

**_Bone-Chilling Step._** Wilfred teleports up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space he can see, and each creature within 10 feet of the space he left takes 4 (1d8) Necrotic damage. Wilfred can’t take this action again until the start of his next turn.

**_Fated Bullet._** _Dexterity Saving Throw:_ DC 14, one creature Wilfred can see within 120 feet. _Failure:_ 16 (2d12 + 3) Necrotic damage, and the target can’t regain Hit Points until the start of its next turn. _Failure or Success:_ Wilfred can’t take this action again until the start of his next turn.

**_Slam._** Wilfred makes one Object Slam attack.

### Wilfred’s Tale {#rthw:mordent:WilfredsTale}

In life, Lord Wilfred Godefroy was an unremarkable minor aristocrat. He inherited the estate of Gryphon Hill near Mordentshire centuries ago by murdering his father and framing it as an accident. During a bloody night years later, the entire Godefroy family—Wilfred; his wife, Estelle; and their daughter, Penelope—died violently. But instead of passing on to the afterlife, the Godefroys’ souls lingered at Gryphon Hill. In death, Wilfred is haunted by the ghosts of his family, recent and the past generations, who blame him for their deaths and the family’s disgrace.

A generation ago, a mysterious alchemist created a device in Mordent called the [Apparatus](#rthw:mordent:theapparatus "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/mordent#theapparatus"). This magical machine had many fantastic powers, including the ability to open passages between the planes and separate a creature’s good and evil natures into separate beings. The Apparatus drew multiple powerful beings to Mordent and eventually attracted the Mists themselves when the device malfunctioned, causing a deadly disaster. The Mists collected Mordent into the Domains of Dread, and the mysterious alchemist vanished. With the departure of mightier beings, Lord Godefroy remained as the land’s most fearful villain. He inherited the mantle of Darklord of the new domain of Mordent.

Since then, Wilfred has claimed lordship of all who die in Mordent. He knows the location of the Apparatus and seeks to master its powers, but how to do so and the location of a vital piece of the machine—the Rod of Rastinon—both elude him. He seeks to blackmail anyone who might be able to reveal the device’s secrets or find the missing rod. Wilfred forces Alice Weathermay, mayor of Mordentshire, to keep him appraised of useful visitors to the domain, by holding her dead husband, Daniel Foxgrove, hostage.

### Wilfred’s Domain {#rthw:mordent:WilfredsDomain}

Mordent is altered by Lord Godefroy’s presence, creating the following effects:

**Closing the Borders.** While in his domain, Lord Godefroy can close or open the borders to Mordent. While the borders are closed, the groans and whispers of the dead fill the Mists surrounding Mordent. Creatures in the Mists have the [**Deafened**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#deafenedcondition) condition.

**Ears Everywhere.** While in his domain, Lord Godefroy can cast [**Sending**](#ref:spell:2619015-sending "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619015-sending"), requiring no Material components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability. When casting the spell in this way, Lord Godefroy can target any Undead creature in Mordent, in addition to the usual targets.

**Spectral Serfs.** A Humanoid that dies in Mordent rises 7 days later as a [**Specter**](#ref:monster:5195210-specter "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195210-specter") under Lord Godefroy’s control, unless the Humanoid is restored to life.

If Wilfred dies, these effects end immediately.

### Wilfred’s Lair {#rthw:mordent:WilfredsLair}

The House on Gryphon Hill lies just outside Mordentshire and is home to Lord Wilfred Godefroy. Hundreds of spirits remain bound to the house and the surrounding grounds, and all serve the lord of the house and struggle to stay in his good graces. Spirits that rebel are punished—either forced to face Wilfred’s kennel of spectral hounds or dragged into the deepest recesses of the house, which even the eldest spirits fear.

#### House on Gryphon Hill {#rthw:mordent:HouseonGryphonHill}

Cobwebs and dust coat the House on Gryphon Hill. Lurking spirits remain out of sight until trespassers pose a threat or Lord Godefroy orders them to attack. The house has the following features:

**Basement.** Lord Godefroy orders ghostly teams to endlessly dig deeper and wider basements beneath the house. As if creating his own underworld, Wilfred imprisons spirits who displease him in the expanding haunted dungeons beneath the house. Somewhere amid these dungeons, a passage connects to the site where the [Apparatus](#rthw:mordent:theapparatus "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/mordent#theapparatus") is hidden.

**Haunted Rooms.** Estelle and Penelope Godefroy haunt the house’s attic, avoiding Wilfred and doing all they can to frustrate the Darklord and stymie his ambitions. The house’s other spirits obey Estelle and Penelope unless their commands contradict an order from Wilfred.

**Withered Estate.** Wilfred’s ghostly hounds patrol the house’s grounds, while spectral groundskeepers tend to dead topiaries and hedges as if they still thrived.

## Adventures in Mordent {#rthw:mordent:AdventuresinMordent}

Mordent is a realm of ghost stories (see [chapter 4](#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:ghoststories "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/creating-domains-of-dread#ghoststories")). Moldering manors, lonely moors, neglected graveyards, and similar gothic sites provide natural settings for encounters with spirits and the tragic dead. Use this section to develop horror adventures in this domain.

[![Fog locally known as the breath of the dead obscures mysterious shapes on the streets of Mordentshire (Artist: Richard Wright)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/14-004.breath-of-death.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/14-004.breath-of-death.png)

### Horror in Mordent {#rthw:mordent:HorrorinMordent}

Adventures in Mordent often include the following elements.

#### The Apparatus {#rthw:mordent:TheApparatus}

Wilfred is obsessed with control over the dead and the living. He knows where the magical device known as the Apparatus is hidden but has limited understanding of how to use it. Nevertheless, he knows it is powerful and can produce devastating effects. He cares nothing for the machine’s remarkable abilities and seeks to use it as a weapon to force all in Mordent to obey him.

To fulfill his goals, Wilfred seeks individuals with magical and alchemical insights, as well as rumors of the Apparatus’s missing piece, the Rod of Rastinon. He might threaten or blackmail the living into aiding him. Should he suspect the Rod of Rastinon or other vital information lies beyond Mordent, he might send his agents to other domains.

The Apparatus can exchange souls, open passages through the Mists, and create more dangerous effects, but the magical device might have any properties an adventure demands.

#### Bastion of Heroes {#rthw:mordent:BastionofHeroes}

Despite the horrors lurking in Mordent, the domain hosts several quiet, relatively peaceful communities. Characters from Mordent might have had relatively peaceful, mundane lives before mysteries or tragedies led them to adventure. The abandoned estates of Mordent also make fine places to use the rules for Haunted Bastions, detailed in [chapter 3](#rthw:ravenloft-adventures:HauntedBastions "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/ravenloft-adventures#HauntedBastions").

#### Ghosts of Mordent {#rthw:mordent:GhostsofMordent}

Ghost stories often involve spirits that linger as the result of some tragedy or unfinished work. In Mordent, spirits linger and might request help from the living. Roll on or choose a result from the Mordent Hauntings table to inspire adventures featuring the lingering dead.

**Mordent Hauntings**

| 1d8 | The Spirit Seeks Aid In …                                                              |
| --- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1   | Freeing a living loved one from possession by another ghost.                           |
| 2   | Hiding a secret that could embarrass or undermine a living loved one.                  |
| 3   | Liberating another spirit from the dungeons beneath the House on Gryphon Hill.         |
| 4   | Locating a spirit that wanders a broad region or who appears only during the new moon. |
| 5   | Restoring the memory of an ancient spirit that has almost lost its sense of self.      |
| 6   | Searching a distant haunted site for a spirit it has been separated from.              |
| 7   | Sealing the site of an ancient evil or the lair of a creature that torments spirits.   |
| 8   | Smuggling a living relative out of Mordent, away from Wilfred’s clutches.              |

Even though spirits are trapped in Mordent, many find secluded places where they reflect on nature, their lives, and eternity. Over generations, such spirits often become little more than vague shapes or disembodied voices or emotions before fading away entirely.

#### Van Richten’s Herbalist Shop {#rthw:mordent:VanRichtensHerbalistShop}

[**Rudolph van Richten**](#ref:monster:6491386-rudolph-van-richten "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491386-rudolph-van-richten") (see [chapter 5](#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:rudolphvanrichten "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/denizens-of-the-mists#rudolphvanrichten")) is the foremost scholar of monsters and strange occurrences in the Domains of Dread. He lives and works from the Mordentshire herbalist shop (see [map 2.27](#rthw:mordent:map227vanrichtensherbalistshop "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/mordent#map227vanrichtensherbalistshop")). Beyond the storefront, Rudolph’s studies and prepares methods of combating evils plaguing the Land of the Mists. Adventurers might find lore and tools to combat all manner of monsters here.

When absent from his shop, Rudolph leaves it in the care of his protégés, [**Gennifer**](#ref:monster:6491356-gennifer-weathermay-foxgrove "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491356-gennifer-weathermay-foxgrove") and [**Laurie Weathermay-Foxgrove**](#ref:monster:6491368-laurie-weathermay-foxgrove "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491368-laurie-weathermay-foxgrove") (detailed in [chapter 5](#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:weathermayfoxgrovetwins "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/denizens-of-the-mists#weathermayfoxgrovetwins")) and Beatrice Polk, an elderly local gardener and accomplished detective.

### Mordent Campaign Arc {#rthw:mordent:MordentCampaignArc}

Mordent campaigns often involve ghostly mysteries. A campaign here might follow this outline:

**Levels 1–2.** Caarey Gelthik, a local ne’er-do-well in Mordent, has become a [**Ghast**](#ref:monster:5195007-ghast "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195007-ghast") and lurks beneath the town docks. By night, he robs graves to consume the bodies within. The characters take note when silent spirits—perhaps of allies—begin wandering town, each missing limbs, tongues, and other soft features. Only finding and defeating Gelthik causes the dismember spirits to depart.

**Levels 3–4.** Beatrice Polk, caretaker at the Mordentshire herbalist shop, hires the characters to end a haunting afflicting the shop. See the adventure “[The Ghost Hunter’s Haunting](#rthw:mordent:theghosthuntershaunting "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/mordent#theghosthuntershaunting").”

**Levels 5–10.** Alice Weathermay, mayor of Mordentshire, hires the characters to find a lost piece of local history: the Rod of Rastinon. She shares leads involving various strange sites, but the rod doesn’t appear. Eventually, [**Lord Godefroy**](#ref:monster:6491403-wilfred-godefroy "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491403-wilfred-godefroy")—who has been working through Alice Weathermay—grows impatient. He threatens the party’s dead loved ones, insisting the characters find the rod swiftly and help him use the Apparatus (see [chapter 3](#rthw:ravenloft-adventures "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/ravenloft-adventures")).

[![Map 2.26: Mordentshire View Player Version (Artist: Francesca Baerald)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/map-14-02.mordentshire.jpg)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/map-14-02.mordentshire.jpg)

### The Ghost Hunter’s Haunting {#rthw:mordent:TheGhostHuntersHaunting}

Adventure for Level 3 Characters

**Situation.** An accident at [Rudolph van Richten’s](#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:rudolphvanrichten "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/denizens-of-the-mists#rudolphvanrichten") herbalist shop broke a strange relic and unleashed a deadly feline spirit from another domain.

**Hook.** Beatrice Polk, the shop’s caretaker, offers the characters 400 GP if they end the haunting.

[![Map 2.27: Van Richten’s Herbalist Shop View Player Version (Artist: Sean Macdonald)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/map-14-03.van-richtens-herbalist-shop.jpg)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/map-14-03.van-richtens-herbalist-shop.jpg)

#### Encounters {#rthw:mordent:Encounters}

This adventure uses map 2.27 and consists of these encounters.

**_Beatrice Polk’s Aid._** Beyond her folksy politeness and dislike of curse words, Beatrice Polk takes her stewardship of the herbalist shop seriously but doesn’t enter the shop during the haunting. She can provide the characters with a number of [**Potions of Healing**](#ref:magic_item:8960641-potion-of-healing "https://www.dndbeyond.com/magic-items/8960641-potion-of-healing") equal to the party’s members. She scuttles plans that involve harming or stealing Rudolph’s possessions.

**_Ghost Cat._** A [**Wraith**](#ref:monster:5174960-wraith "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5174960-wraith") that appears as a black cat the size of a panther haunts the shop. Whenever the characters enter a room without monsters present, roll a die. If the number is odd, the cat is in the room. If the cat has more than half its Hit Points, it fights for a round, then flees to another room or floor; otherwise, it flees without attacking. If destroyed, the wraith reappears 24 hours later with full Hit Points. Its threat ends only if the ritual in the cellar is completed.

**_Laboratory._** Two [**Poltergeists**](#ref:monster:5195168-poltergeist "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195168-poltergeist") haunt this room.

**_Stairs._** An unnatural wind blows against anyone who tries to ascend either stairway to the second floor. A character must succeed on a DC 16 Strength ([**Athletics**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#skills)) check to climb the stairs.

**_Dumbwaiter._** A dumbwaiter connects the kitchen and the upstairs hall. It can hold one Medium or smaller creature. A creature outside the dumbwaiter can use an action to raise or lower the dumbwaiter and its contents.

**_Upstairs Hall._** Broken on the floor is a strange relic: a mummied cat. Shelves nearby hold accounts of Rudolph’s travels in a land called [Har’Akir](#rthw:harakir "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/harakir").

**_Library._** Rudolph’s library is filled with occult texts. Any character who spends a minute investigating the library finds a copy of _Van Richten’s Guide to Ghosts._ Those who spend at least 10 minutes reading this book and have seen both the relic in the upstairs hall and the ritual room in the cellar understand how to use the cellar room to exorcise the ghostly cat. Additionally, a character who succeeds on a DC 12 Intelligence ([**Investigation**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#skills)) check finds a [**Spell Scroll**](#ref:magic_item:8960643-spell-scroll-level-1 "https://www.dndbeyond.com/magic-items/8960643-spell-scroll-level-1") of [**Protection from Evil and Good**](#ref:spell:2618912-protection-from-evil-and-good "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618912-protection-from-evil-and-good").

**_Guest Room._** Standing facing a corner of this room is [**Gennifer Weathermay-Foxgrove**](#ref:monster:6491356-gennifer-weathermay-foxgrove "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491356-gennifer-weathermay-foxgrove") (see [chapter 5](#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:genniferweathermayfoxgrove "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/denizens-of-the-mists#genniferweathermayfoxgrove")). She is possessed by a [**Ghost**](#ref:monster:5195008-ghost "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195008-ghost"), which holds her in a catatonic state. Gennifer is freed of her possession if she’s affected by a spell like _Protection from Evil and Good_ or if she’s removed from the shop. The feline-featured wraith attacks the party if its possession ends or if Gennifer is moved from the room. If freed from the ghost’s control, Gennifer is aware of the ghostly cat, as she accidentally broke the relic in the hall. She knows how to exorcise the spirit using the wards in the cellar.

**_Cellar._** A room in the cellar is prepared for magic rituals. A character who succeeds on a DC 12 Intelligence ([**Arcana**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#skills)) check realizes this space is warded to contain or dispel spirits. If the characters place the relic from the upstairs hall within the space, the ghostly cat appears 1 minute later and fights until destroyed. If the cat is defeated here, the relic repairs itself and the haunting ends. Each character gains a bonus 400 XP for ending the haunting.

</CHAPTER>
