<CHAPTER id="rthw:shadowlands" title="Shadowlands">

# Shadowlands {#rthw:shadowlands:Shadowlands}

Domain of Faded Glory and False Virtue

> #### **Darklord:** [_Ebonbane_](#rthw:shadowlands:Ebonbane "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/shadowlands#Ebonbane") {#rthw:shadowlands:Ebonbane}
>
> **Genre:** [Gothic horror](#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:gothichorror "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/creating-domains-of-dread#gothichorror")
>
> **Hallmarks:** Cursed magic items, doomed quests, falls from grace, knightly lineages, obsessive zeal
>
> **Mist Talismans:** Broken holy symbol, religious relic, symbol of the Circle
>
> **Aligned Tarokka Card:** Torturer
>
> **Opposed Tarokka Card:** Broken One

[![(Artist: Pam Wishbow)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/15-001.torturer-tarokka.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/15-001.torturer-tarokka.png) [![](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/15-002.broken-one-tarokka.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/15-002.broken-one-tarokka.png)

For the knights of the Shadowlands, the struggle with evil isn’t a philosophical trial—it is an active war. East of the rugged Theospine Mountains spreads the peaceful realm of Nidala, where the virtuous knights of the Circle guard their lands against wickedness beyond and within. To the mountains’ west lies the ruined land of Avonleigh, the birthplace of the knightly Circle; this realm fell to evil long ago and has become overgrown by the spirit-stalked Phantasmal Forest. Many knights of the Circle view themselves as inheritors of a legacy of shame. They aspire to the heroism of their storied ancestors and battle to absolve themselves of imagined failures. They throw themselves into crusades against foes, real and imagined, sacrificing their lives—and those of their people—for redemption and glory.

For all the Circle’s good intentions, these knights are cursed. Monsters and villains they’ve defeated reappear in the Shadowlands seeking vengeance. Most infamously, deep in the Phantasmal Forest lingers the evil that caused Avonleigh’s downfall: [**Ebonbane**](#ref:monster:6491352-ebonbane "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491352-ebonbane"), Darklord of the Shadowlands and the sapient sword of the Circle’s founder, Kateri Shadowborn.

## Domain Features {#rthw:shadowlands:DomainFeatures}

The Shadowlands is known for the following features:

**Bastions on the Borderlands.** The Circle seeks to reclaim a foothold in Avonleigh in a region called the Borderlands. They often reward allies with Bastions here (see [chapter 3](#rthw:ravenloft-adventures:HauntedBastions "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/ravenloft-adventures#HauntedBastions") and the [Dungeon Master’s Guide](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/dmg-2024) for details on [Bastions](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/dmg-2024/bastions)).

**The Circle.** The knights of the Circle (described in [chapter 3](#rthw:ravenloft-adventures:thecircle "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/ravenloft-adventures#thecircle")) make their home in this domain.

**Nidala’s Ruler.** Elena Faith-hold rules Nidala. But this knight is rarely present in the land, as she leads deadly quests beyond the domain’s borders (see “[Faith-hold’s Crusades](#rthw:shadowlands:faithholdscrusades "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/shadowlands#faithholdscrusades")”).

## Locations in the Shadowlands {#rthw:shadowlands:LocationsintheShadowlands}

The Shadowlands is a dualistic domain: Avonleigh remains an overtly haunted wilderness home to lurking evils, while Nidala touts itself as the virtuous opposite. But the land’s harmony is artificial, its people forced to smile while trapped in the service of Elena Faith-hold and her sycophants. Accordingly, the domain’s conflict isn’t one of good versus evil, but rather of overt and covert evils.

The Phantasmal Forest is detailed below, and other notable locations are summarized on the [Shadowlands Locations table](#rthw:shadowlands:shadowlandslocations "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/shadowlands#shadowlandslocations").

### Phantasmal Forest {#rthw:shadowlands:PhantasmalForest}

The Phantasmal Forest dominates the haunted land of Avonleigh, a shifting, surreal woodland cloaked by perpetual night. A dreamlike place controlled by _Ebonbane_, the forest changes constantly, and locations within drift like flotsam on a dark sea. The River Avalon and the King’s Highway—an overgrown route of misaligned stones—enter the forest, but within the woods they circle endlessly and never leave. Only those descended from the Circle’s founding members can navigate the Phantasmal Forest without becoming lost. All others wander at _Ebonbane_’s whim, becoming prey for the wolves, corrupted fey, cursed knights, or wicked souls that haunt the forest.

[![Map 2.28: Shadowlands View Player Version (Artist: Marco Bernardini)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/map-15-01.shadowlands.jpg)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/map-15-01.shadowlands.jpg)

**Shadowlands Locations**

Elena keeps this a secret and sacrifices a dozen villagers to the creature every three years. |

The Circle grants these holdings to members and allies who swear to restore them as bastions of light.                                                                                                   |

## Ebonbane {#rthw:shadowlands:Ebonbane}

Darklord of Endless Vengeance

[![(Artist: Matthew G. Lewis)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/15-003.ebonbane.jpg)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/15-003.ebonbane.jpg)

> “Questing knights? Champions of the realm? Look upon thy sterling souls. Tell me, heroes, by what fair deeds art thou known in this rotted world?”
>
> —Ebonbane

[**Ebonbane**](#ref:magic_item:11610583-ebonbane "https://www.dndbeyond.com/magic-items/11610583-ebonbane") is an evil, sapient blade that seeks to annihilate the legacy of the Shadowlands’ greatest hero and her allies. This includes all with the Shadowborn name and every member of the Circle.

_Ebonbane_ is a magic weapon (see “[Ebonbane as a Magic Item](#rthw:shadowlands:ebonbaneasamagicitem "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/shadowlands#ebonbaneasamagicitem")” later in this section), but within Shadowborn Manor, it becomes a creature that can move on its own (see the **Ebonbane** stat block). Beyond the manor, it doesn’t use its stat block—it requires a wielder to work its evil in the world.

Many who attempt to attune to the weapon are slain outright by its evil. Those who do manage to wield _Ebonbane_ must endure the Darklord’s constant demands and risk becoming its pawn (see “[Sentient Magic Items](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/dmg-2024/treasure#sentientmagicitems)” in the [Dungeon Master’s Guide](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/dmg-2024)). If unattended outside Shadowborn Manor, _Ebonbane_ eventually finds its way back there. No one can carry _Ebonbane_ out of the Shadowlands. If someone tries, the sword vanishes and reappears in Shadowborn Manor.

_Ebonbane_ has a flamboyant personality and a penchant for the dramatic and sadistic. It has no regard for life and delights in animating the corpses of foes, then destroying them in front of their allies. When it speaks, it uses language that mocks the elevated speech of knights.

### [Ebonbane](#ref:monster:6491352-ebonbane "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491352-ebonbane") {#rthw:shadowlands:Ebonbanerefmonster6491352ebonbanehttpswwwdndbeyondcommonsters6491352ebonbane}

Small Construct, Chaotic Evil

**AC** 17 **Initiative** +14 (24)

**HP** 130 (29d6 + 29)

**Speed** 5 ft., Fly 50 ft. (hover)

|     |     | Mod | Save |
| --- | --- | --- | ---- |
| STR | 18  | +4  | +4   |
| DEX | 18  | +4  | +4   |
| CON | 13  | +1  | +6   |

|     |     | Mod | Save |
| --- | --- | --- | ---- |
| INT | 17  | +3  | +3   |
| WIS | 14  | +2  | +7   |
| CHA | 19  | +4  | +4   |

**Skills** [**Arcana**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#skills) +8, [**History**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#skills) +8, [**Perception**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#skills) +7

**Resistances** Bludgeoning, Fire, Piercing, Psychic, Slashing

**Immunities** Poison, Necrotic; [**Charmed**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#charmedcondition), [**Deafened**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#deafenedcondition), [**Exhaustion**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#exhaustioncondition), [**Frightened**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#frightenedcondition), [**Paralyzed**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#paralyzedcondition), [**Petrified**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#petrifiedcondition), [**Poisoned**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#poisonedcondition)

**Senses** [**Truesight**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#truesight) 120 ft; Passive Perception 17

**Languages** Common; telepathy 10 ft.

**Challenge** 13 (XP 10,000, or 11,500 in domain; PB +5)

#### Traits {#rthw:shadowlands:Traits}

**_Darklord Restoration._** If Ebonbane dies, it revives with all its Hit Points in 1d10 weeks, teleporting somewhere in Shadowborn Manor. Until it revives, Ebonbane acts as a [**+3 Longsword**](#ref:magic_item:5320-longsword-3 "https://www.dndbeyond.com/magic-items/5320-longsword-3") when wielded by a creature.

**_Legendary Resistance (3/Day, or 4/Day in Domain)._** If Ebonbane fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

**_Magic Resistance._** Ebonbane has [**Advantage**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#advantage) on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

#### Actions {#rthw:shadowlands:Actions}

**_Multiattack._** Ebonbane makes three Darkflame Slash attacks. It can replace one of these attacks with a use of Possess Dead if available.

**_Darkflame Slash._** _Melee or Ranged Attack Roll:_ +9, reach 5 ft. or range 90 ft. _Hit:_ 9 (1d10 + 4) Slashing damage plus 10 (3d6) Necrotic damage.

**_Possess Dead (Recharge 5–6)._** Ebonbane raises a Medium or Small Humanoid corpse within 5 feet of itself and possesses it. The corpse wields Ebonbane and is under its control. Ebonbane gains 50 [**Temporary Hit Points**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#temporaryhitpoints), and its statistics are the same, except its Speed increases to 30 feet, and it can speak through the corpse using any language the corpse knew in life.

The possession lasts until Ebonbane drops to 0 Hit Points or Ebonbane ends the possession as a Bonus Action. Once the possession ends, Ebonbane can’t possess the corpse again. The corpse crumbles to dust 24 hours after the possession ends.

**_Worthy Wielder._** _Charisma Saving Throw:_ DC 17, one willing Humanoid within 5 feet. _Failure:_ 36 (8d8) Force damage. If this damage reduces the target to 0 Hit Points, Ebonbane devourers its soul. A creature whose soul has been devoured by Ebonbane can be restored to life only by a [**Wish**](#ref:spell:2619213-wish "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619213-wish") spell. _Success:_ The target attunes to Ebonbane and can wield the sword (see “[Ebonbane as a Magic Item](#rthw:shadowlands:ebonbaneasamagicitem "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/shadowlands#ebonbaneasamagicitem")”).

#### Reactions {#rthw:shadowlands:Reactions}

**_Parry._** _Trigger:_ Ebonbane is hit by a melee attack roll. _Response:_ Ebonbane adds 5 to its AC against that attack, possibly causing it to miss.

#### Legendary Actions {#rthw:shadowlands:LegendaryActions}

Legendary Action Uses: 3 (4 in Domain). Immediately after another creature’s turn, Ebonbane can expend a use to take one of the following actions. Ebonbane regains all expended uses at the start of each of its turns.

**_Retaliate._** Ebonbane moves up to half its Speed and makes one Darkflame Slash attack.

**_Runic Flare._** _Constitution Saving Throw:_ DC 17, each creature of Ebonbane’s choice in a 30-foot [**Emanation**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#emanationareaofeffect) originating from Ebonbane. _Failure:_ The target has the [**Blinded**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#blindedcondition) condition and repeats the save at the end of each of its turns. The target succeeds automatically after 1 minute. _Failure or Success:_ Ebonbane can’t take this action again until the start of its next turn.

### Ebonbane’s Tale {#rthw:shadowlands:EbonbanesTale}

Kateri Shadowborn was a great hero who, alongside her order of valorous knights called the Circle, spent her life in service of good. Among her greatest deeds was leading an army against a nation whose king had been possessed by a fiend. She defeated the fiend, though doing so caused her magic sword to shatter.

After a life of great deeds, Kateri Shadowborn retired to live in peace with her family at Shadowborn Manor. But the hero had made many enemies. Thinking her vulnerable, wicked cultists recovered the pieces of Kateri’s broken sword and conjured the lingering malice of the evils she had thwarted. These the cultists forged into a terrible weapon, _Ebonbane_—and they became its first victims.

Animated by hatred for Kateri and her allies, _Ebonbane_ took control of its creators and became a curse on the world. For years it worked to destroy what Kateri had created, ruin what she loved, and slaughter those who aided her. Many times the evil sword’s wielder was captured, but none ever suspected that the weapon itself was behind the grisly crimes.

Finally, in the hands of an unassuming monk, _Ebonbane_ found its way to Shadowborn Manor, where grim news had isolated Kateri and worn her down. Aged but still a mighty knight, Kateri recognized _Ebonbane_’s threat, and a great battle ensued. During the clash, Kateri kept _Ebonbane_’s attention and ensured her family and friends escaped the manor. When only the hero and the wicked sword remained, Kateri summoned her remaining might into a blow to destroy _Ebonbane._ But the wicked sword proved too powerful. Kateri’s blade shattered, and _Ebonbane_ struck down the legendary knight. Exalting in its victory, the evil weapon possessed Kateri’s body and pursued her fleeing family. But as it did so, it witnessed its quarry fading into the rising Mists.

When the Mists receded, _Ebonbane_ found itself in a realm where the residents regarded the ancestors of Kateri Shadowborn and her fellow knights as heroes. Thrilled to continue its spree, _Ebonbane_ sought to leave Shadowborn Manor, but it had no one to carry it beyond the grounds. Now, the evil blade seethes in frustration, waiting for a worthy bearer to carry it into the world so it might destroy all the good that came from Kateri’s work.

### Ebonbane as a Magic Item {#rthw:shadowlands:EbonbaneasaMagicItem}

_Ebonbane_’s magic weapon form is described below.

---

#### [Ebonbane](#ref:magic_item:11610583-ebonbane "https://www.dndbeyond.com/magic-items/11610583-ebonbane") {#rthw:shadowlands:Ebonbanerefmagicitem11610583ebonbanehttpswwwdndbeyondcommagicitems11610583ebonbane}

Weapon (Longsword), Artifact (Requires Attunement)

The Darklord of the Domain of Dread known as the Shadowlands is _Ebonbane_, a sapient sword. [**Ebonbane**](#ref:monster:6491352-ebonbane "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491352-ebonbane") uses its monster stat block while in Shadowborn Manor.

**_Bound to the Shadowlands._** When you enter a space outside of the Shadowlands, your Attunement immediately ends and _Ebonbane_ teleports to somewhere in Shadowborn Manor.

**_Insatiable Rage._** The sword demands destruction. If the sword hasn’t slain a Celestial or a Humanoid for 3 days, you make a DC 17 Charisma saving throw at the next dawn. On a successful save, you take 8d8 Force damage. On a failed save, you are dominated by the sword, as if by the [**Dominate Monster**](#ref:spell:2619147-dominate-monster "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619147-dominate-monster") spell, and the sword demands the blood of a Celestial or a Humanoid. The spell effect ends when the sword’s demand is met.

**_Magic Weapon._** You gain a +3 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. When you hit a Celestial or a Humanoid with it, that attack also deals 3d6 Necrotic damage.

While you hold this weapon, you have [**Advantage**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#advantage) on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

**_Sentience._** _Ebonbane_ is a sentient Chaotic Evil weapon with an Intelligence of 17, a Wisdom of 14, and a Charisma of 19. It has hearing and [**Truesight**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#truesight) out to 120 feet. The weapon speaks Common and can communicate with its wielder telepathically. While you are attuned to it, _Ebonbane_ also understands every language you know.

**_Personality._** _Ebonbane_ was created to kill the paladin Kateri Shadowborn, and it still possesses a burning hatred for goodly knights. _Ebonbane_ revels in seeing good defeated and hope vanquished. The sword bonds with any wielder that assists in its goals but always views it wielder as a lackey.

**_Destroying Ebonbane._** The only way to destroy _Ebonbane_ is to forge a weapon from the [Four Keys](#rthw:shadowlands:questofthefourkeys "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/shadowlands#questofthefourkeys") and reduce _Ebonbane_ to 0 Hit Points with it (see the **Ebonbane** stat block).

---

### Ebonbane’s Domain {#rthw:shadowlands:EbonbanesDomain}

The Shadowlands is altered by _Ebonbane_’s presence, creating the following effects:

**Closing the Borders.** While in its domain, _Ebonbane_ can close or open the borders of the Shadowlands at will. While the borders are closed, whirling blades of magic fly through the Mists surrounding the Shadowlands. A creature that enters the Mists for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there must succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw or take 3d10 Force damage. A creature makes this save only once per turn.

**Haunted Woods.** The forest within 1 mile of _Ebonbane_’s lair is wreathed in a powerful illusion. Whenever a creature other than _Ebonbane_ or the sword’s allies finishes a Short or Long Rest in that area, it must succeed on a DC 15 Intelligence saving throw, or it is lost in the forest, always finding itself at the location it started in until it finishes a Short or Long Rest.

**Turning Weapons.** While in its lair, _Ebonbane_ can transform nonmagical [**Greatswords**](#ref:equipment:22-greatsword "https://www.dndbeyond.com/equipment/22-greatsword") and [**Longswords**](#ref:equipment:4-longsword "https://www.dndbeyond.com/equipment/4-longsword") within 1 mile of the lair into [**Animated Flying Swords**](#ref:monster:5194895-animated-flying-sword "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5194895-animated-flying-sword") by completing a 24-hour ritual.

If _Ebonbane_ is destroyed, these effects end immediately.

### Ebonbane’s Lair {#rthw:shadowlands:EbonbanesLair}

_Ebonbane_ remains imprisoned in Shadowborn Manor, a fortified estate hidden in the Phantasmal Forest. The grounds are strewn with the bodies of those who sought the legendary blade and failed.

#### Shadowborn Manor {#rthw:shadowlands:ShadowbornManor}

Though abandoned, Shadowborn Manor remains in decent repair. The estate is depicted on [map 2.29](#rthw:shadowlands:map229shadowbornmanor "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/shadowlands#map229shadowbornmanor") and has the following features:

**Dungeon.** The Circle understood that some evils needed to be contained. A secret stairway in the east wing leads to a dungeon that has remained hidden from _Ebonbane._

**Great Hall.** This hall hosts the round table where members of the Circle once met. _Ebonbane_ poses the bodies of knights here to possess as it pleases.

**Lady’s Chambers.** Kateri Shadowborn’s armored corpse lies in the largest bedroom on the second floor. It is _Ebonbane_’s favorite body to reanimate, and if destroyed, it reappears in this chamber.

## Adventures in the Shadowlands {#rthw:shadowlands:AdventuresintheShadowlands}

Adventures set in the Shadowlands feature individuals striving to prove their worth or superiority. Characters might be welcome to join the knights of the Circle, or perhaps they belong to families with heroic histories. Such ties could connect characters to the domain’s history and future quests. Use this section to develop horror adventures in this domain.

[![The remains of failed quests and fallen knights lie near Shadowborn Manor in the Phantasmal Forest (Artist: Luca Bancone)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/15-004.phantasmal-forest.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/15-004.phantasmal-forest.png)

### Horror in the Shadowlands {#rthw:shadowlands:HorrorintheShadowlands}

Adventures in the Shadowlands often include the following elements.

#### Faith-hold’s Crusades {#rthw:shadowlands:FaithholdsCrusades}

Elena Faith-hold rules Nidala, crushing its people under the weight of her intolerance and need to maintain her virtuous reputation. While she doesn’t lead the Circle, she is its most respected member.

Elena leads forays of knights into the Mists on lengthy quests to defeat wicked foes in mysterious lands. An invitation to join one of Elena’s crusades is a great honor and a death sentence. Whenever Elena returns from the Mists, she always does so alone, claiming to be the sole survivor of a great victory.

Elena Faith-hold isn’t a Darklord, but should someone ever destroy _Ebonbane_, she might ascend to that position.

#### Quest of the Four Keys {#rthw:shadowlands:QuestoftheFourKeys}

One can destroy _Ebonbane_ permanently using the sword of Kateri Shadowborn. However, the Dark Powers shattered her sword and scattered its pieces. These fragments are known as the Four Keys—emblems of Kateri’s valor and faith. Each embodies a different virtue and one of the four elements.

**_The Keys’ Locations._** The Four Keys might appear anywhere in the Shadowlands or other domains. The ghost of Kateri Shadowborn or lore hidden amid tragic sites might point toward the keys.

**_Using the Keys._** Should the characters collect the Four Keys, they can reforge them into a weapon that—if used to reduce [_Ebonbane_](#rthw:shadowlands:ebonbanestatblock "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/shadowlands#ebonbanestatblock") to 0 Hit Points—negates its Darklord Restoration trait. It’s up to you whether this ends the Darklord’s threat or unleashes a greater evil bound within.

### Shadowlands Campaign Arc {#rthw:shadowlands:ShadowlandsCampaignArc}

Campaigns in the Shadowlands often involve quests that reveal evils steeped in tragedies and abuses of power. A campaign here might follow this outline:

**Levels 1–4.** The characters aid members of the Circle in defeating a dangerous [**Basilisk**](#ref:monster:5194919-basilisk "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5194919-basilisk") in Nidala. Impressed, the knights charge the characters with reclaiming a fort in the Borderlands from a wicked knight. The knight—a Circle member who died trying to recover Kateri Shadowborn’s sword—is now a [**Revenant**](#ref:monster:5195182-revenant "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195182-revenant"). Once the knight is defeated, the Circle gives the characters its fort as a Bastion ([detailed](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/dmg-2024/bastions) in the [Dungeon Master’s Guide](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/dmg-2024)).

**Level 5–8.** In their Bastion, the characters find a piece of a broken sword. The spirit of Kateri Shadowborn appears to the most virtuous character and asks for their help freeing her spirit and defeating _Ebonbane._ She shares the details in the “[Quest of the Four Keys](#rthw:shadowlands:questofthefourkeys "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/shadowlands#questofthefourkeys")” section. The characters begin a journey across the Shadowlands and beyond to recover the other three sword fragments.

**Levels 9–11.** Once the characters have the Four Keys, Kateri’s spirit instructs them to travel to the Stone Circle in the Phantasmal Forest, where the sword can be magically reforged as a [**Holy Avenger**](#ref:magic_item:9228774-holy-avenger "https://www.dndbeyond.com/magic-items/9228774-holy-avenger"). With this weapon, the characters journey to Shadowborn Manor and face [**Ebonbane**](#ref:monster:6491352-ebonbane "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491352-ebonbane").

### The Shadowborn Sword {#rthw:shadowlands:TheShadowbornSword}

Adventure for Level 10 Characters

**Situation.** A knight seeks to prove herself by finding a hero’s lost sword.

**Hook.** The human knight Lucia Lambert (Medium, Lawful Good [**Questing Knight**](#ref:monster:5195177-questing-knight "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195177-questing-knight")) invites the characters to join her mission to recover the lost sword of the hero Kateri Shadowborn. In return, she’ll reward them with 4,000 GP—or double that amount in additions to the characters’ Bastions.

[![Map 2.29: Shadowborn Manor View Player Version (Artist: Pedro Cardoso)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/map-15-02.shadowborn-manor.jpg)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/map-15-02.shadowborn-manor.jpg)

#### Encounters {#rthw:shadowlands:Encounters}

The adventure starts at the edge of the Phantasmal Forest and consists of these encounters.

**_Phantasmal Forest._** The journey to Shadowborn Manor is 18 miles, with the forest’s density and perpetual [**Darkness**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#darkness) limiting characters to a [Slow pace](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/br-2024/playing-the-game#travelpace). As Lucia’s family members have belonged to the Circle since its founding, she can navigate the forest at a Normal pace, so the journey takes only 8 hours.

**_Fallen Knight._** Outside the manor, a [**Death Knight Aspirant**](#ref:monster:5194962-death-knight-aspirant "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5194962-death-knight-aspirant") wearing the armor of a Circle knight bars the path and warns characters not to enter. A Good character who succeeds on a DC 16 Charisma ([**Persuasion**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#skills)) check can convince the corpse to let them pass; otherwise, it attacks those who try to enter.

**_Shadowborn Manor._** Armored corpses lie about Shadowborn Manor (use map 2.29). If the characters disturb them or enter the great hall, five rise as [**Strahd Skeletons**](#ref:monster:6491389-strahd-skeleton "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491389-strahd-skeleton") (see [chapter 5](#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:strahdskeleton "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/denizens-of-the-mists#strahdskeleton")).

**_Shadowborn’s Ghost._** The Lawful Good [**Ghost**](#ref:monster:5195008-ghost "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195008-ghost") of Kateri Shadowborn haunts the manor. If the characters seem near defeat, she appears and can distract _Ebonbane_ or lead them to the hidden dungeon.

**_Ebonbane._** [**Ebonbane**](#ref:monster:6491352-ebonbane "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491352-ebonbane") (see earlier in [this chapter](#rthw:shadowlands:Ebonbane "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/shadowlands#Ebonbane")) lies in the great hall. If with the characters, Lucia claims the sword and is stricken dead by _Ebonbane_, who animates her body. Otherwise, _Ebonbane_ animates another corpse. The Darklord tries to convince the characters to take it from the manor so it can slay their foes. If they reject it, _Ebonbane_ fights.

**_Conclusion._** Should the characters escape Shadowborn Manor, each of them earns a bonus 3,100 XP. If they don’t take _Ebonbane_, Kateri’s ghost appears to them the following night and explains that _Ebonbane_’s evil isn’t ended. She goes explains the Darklord’s history and how to destroy it (see “[Quest of the Four Keys](#rthw:shadowlands:questofthefourkeys "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/shadowlands#questofthefourkeys")”). The Circle rewards the characters in Lucia’s stead if she is slain.

</CHAPTER>

<CHAPTER id="rthw:sithicus" title="Sithicus">

# Sithicus {#rthw:sithicus:Sithicus}

Domain of the Soul’s Shadow

> #### **Darklord:** [Lord Loren Soth](#rthw:sithicus:LordSoth "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/sithicus#LordSoth") {#rthw:sithicus:LordSoth}
>
> **Genre:** [Dark fantasy](#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:darkfantasy "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/creating-domains-of-dread#darkfantasy")
>
> **Hallmarks:** Cataclysmic fire, malicious shadows, tormented memories, twisted fantasy
>
> **Mist Talismans:** Black rose, burnt armor, scrap of black fabric, three thorns
>
> **Aligned Tarokka Card:** Paladin
>
> **Opposed Tarokka Card:** Innocent

[![(Artist: Pam Wishbow)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/16-001.paladin-tarokka.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/16-001.paladin-tarokka.png) [![](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/16-002.innocent-tarokka.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/16-002.innocent-tarokka.png)

Whatever Sithicus was or could have been, it will never be. The dramatic ruins of a fabulous elven realm cover a land realm forested by gigantic trees and burning with the flames of a forgotten magical disaster. Scattered communities appear among the dilapidation, the domain’s predominantly elf population living like strangers amid structures to which they have no connection. At dusk, people withdraw, hiding from the domain’s true residents: the shadows.

By night, the shadows of Sithicus reenact forgotten lives or mimic the deeds of questing knights, devoted lovers, and lurking monsters. Most of these shadows are harmless, if unnerving, and seem not to notice other beings. Some, however, resent the domain’s other residents and torment the living.

Though few in the domain realize it, Sithicus has ties to the world of Krynn on the Material Plane. Ruins suggest the work of elves from that world, while the night sky blazes with the five-headed dragon constellation of the deity Takhisis. As on Krynn, the black moon Nuitari is visible only to evil beings. But the domain’s clearest tie to Krynn is its Darklord, the accursed knight [**Lord Soth**](#ref:monster:6491370-lord-soth-of-sithicus "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491370-lord-soth-of-sithicus").

## Domain Features {#rthw:sithicus:DomainFeatures}

Sithicus is known for the following features:

**Bound to Krynn.** Sithicus is a warped reflection of the lands of Krynn. This world and its people, such as kender, are described in [Dragonlance: Shadow of the Dragon Queen](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/sotdq).

**Cataclysmic Fire.** Accursed flames blaze amid prominent ruins and turn shadows into monsters drawn from Lord Soth’s past.

**Living Shadows.** Shadows in Sithicus move on their own. Most are harmless, but some are deadly creatures such a [**Shadows**](#ref:monster:5174958-shadow "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5174958-shadow") or [**Shadow Demons**](#ref:monster:5195200-shadow-demon "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195200-shadow-demon").

**Soth’s Traitor.** Lord Soth’s undead soldiers hunt for the ghostly knight Caradoc, whom Soth blames for his imprisonment in Sithicus.

## Locations in Sithicus {#rthw:sithicus:LocationsinSithicus}

Two significant features of Sithicus are detailed below, and other notable locations are summarized on the [Sithicus Locations table](#rthw:sithicus:sithicuslocations "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/sithicus#sithicuslocations").

### Endless Ruins {#rthw:sithicus:EndlessRuins}

Sithicus lies blanketed in endless ruins. Ancient forests rise from them, rivers flow in their broken avenues, and whole mountain ranges are sculpted with crumbled towers. These structures suggest the work of a vast, magical elven nation, but all evidence of these people has been reduced to enigmatic scraps of art and lore. At the heights of crumbling towers or in empty crypts blaze violet, cataclysmic fire (see “[Cataclysmic Flames](#rthw:sithicus:cataclysmicflames "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/sithicus#cataclysmicflames")”). In rare cases, these phantasmal flames reveal glimpses of Lord Soth’s past and details that the clever might use to win the Darklord’s favor.

### Great Chasm {#rthw:sithicus:GreatChasm}

The Great Chasm gapes in Sithicus like a wound. None can say how deep it goes, as light fails to pierce more than a few dozen feet into the ravine. Those who descend deeper vanish into the shadows and rarely return. Those who do tell of a malicious darkness beneath the domain, a cacophony of hateful voices, and shadows that hunger.

Hidden amid ruins spilling into the chasm is the home of Inza Kulchevich, a hateful witch who can speak to shadows and believes all virtue is a lie. Despite her cynicism, she might perform prophetic fortune-telling or share strange lore in return for her visitors’ shadows.

[![Map 2.30: Sithicus View Player Version (Artist: Pedro Cardoso)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/map-16-01.sithicus.jpg)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/map-16-01.sithicus.jpg)

**Sithicus Locations**

| Location                           | Description                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Giant’s Cloak                      | Throughout the Giant’s Cloak forest are petrified trees carved with strange runes and weeping tar-like sap. Stone giant hermits tend these groves and set deadly traps against trespassers. |
| Har-Thelen                         | Har-Thelen is largely abandoned. Its gates stand open, and only a few hundred people reside at its center. By night, stray shadows work and live among the abandoned structures.            |
| Hroth                              | The decrepit town of Hroth is built amid giant swamp trees, many of which lean at precarious angles. The bogs nearby are said to be magic and can return to life those buried within.       |
| Iron Warden Inn                    | The Iron Warden Inn is closed by day, but at night, those with enough wealth to buy entry gamble at games of cards and death’s-head dice. Sometimes the dead come to play.                  |
| Kendralind                         | A hidden village of faded tree houses, huts, and burrows, Kendralind is home to a few dozen kender vampires. The residents are equally delighted by games, whimsical tales, and bloodshed.  |
| Lake of Glass                      | The Lake of Glass moves like water but is as solid as glass. At night, the lake reflects the hidden moon, Nuitari, and magic cast within its reflected light is empowered but cursed.       |
| Mal-Erek                           | Forgotten scholars built Mal-Erek amid giant trees. Now only squatters and obsessed scholars reside here, with few noticing the decay of the vaults and archives around them.               |
| Merchant’s Slash                   | The Merchant’s Slash trail is littered with the wreckage of merchant and traveler caravans. Some are still occupied by eccentric traders selling eerie wares from strange lands.            |
| [Nedragaard Keep](#rthw:sithicus:nedragaardkeep "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/sithicus#nedragaardkeep") | The towering fortress of Lord Soth is strangled by black thorns and blazes with cataclysmic flame. Within, undead knights and spectral elves reenact and recite Soth’s great failures.      |
| Sorrow                             | A hidden prison for the living guarded by the dead, Sorrow accepts mysterious transfers from beyond the Mists. Many thought dead in other domains are imprisoned here.                      |
| Veldrava                           | A dismal work camp stands at the entrance to a maze of unfathomably deep salt mines. Caustic minerals burn explorers who seek the source of whispers from the depths.                       |

## Lord Soth {#rthw:sithicus:LordSoth}

Darklord Cursed by Memories

[![(Artist: Cynthia Sheppard)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/16-003.lord-soth-of-sithicus.jpg)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/16-003.lord-soth-of-sithicus.jpg)

> “Explain why you have interrupted my reverie, or I will turn your waking hours into nightmares.”
>
> —Lord Soth

Lord Loren Soth seethes within a realm that mocks and frustrates him. Having known the rigid standards of knighthood and warfare, Soth finds Sithicus empty and chaotic, his people apathetic and undisciplined. The elven beauty that once captivated him lies ruined, the land burns with the flames of Krynn’s Cataclysm, and the realm’s shadows remind Soth of his past failures. Worse, no worthy foes exist to challenge him. So Soth broods on his throne in Nedragaard Keep, haunted by banshees that sing the tale of his disgrace and by rotted, undead copies of the knights who once served him.

Lord Soth cares nothing for his domain. But should noteworthy threats or remarkable individuals appear, he seeks to crush or enlist them. The only exception is the spirit of his treacherous former ally, Caradoc. Soth’s undead servants and his werebadger seneschal, Azrael Dax, scour the land for the elusive ghost.

Soth shares his imprisonment in Sithicus with all in the domain by keeping its borders perpetually closed. Only those who rouse him to activity or invade Nedragaard Keep might convince him to let them escape. This risks provoking the mighty death knight’s wrath, but Soth still thinks of himself as a true knight—he might assist those who present themselves as honorable warriors or show knowledge of his home (see “[Influencing Lord Soth](#rthw:sithicus:influencinglordsoth "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/sithicus#influencinglordsoth")”).

### [Lord Soth of Sithicus](#ref:monster:6491370-lord-soth-of-sithicus "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491370-lord-soth-of-sithicus") {#rthw:sithicus:LordSothofSithicusrefmonster6491370lordsothofsithicushttpswwwdndbeyondcommonsters6491370lordsothofsithicus}

Medium Undead, Lawful Evil

**AC** 18 **Initiative** +6 (16)

**HP** 228 (24d8 + 120)

**Speed** 30 ft.

|     |     | Mod | Save |
| --- | --- | --- | ---- |
| STR | 22  | +6  | +6   |
| DEX | 11  | +0  | +6   |
| CON | 20  | +5  | +5   |

|     |     | Mod | Save |
| --- | --- | --- | ---- |
| INT | 12  | +1  | +1   |
| WIS | 16  | +3  | +9   |
| CHA | 20  | +5  | +11  |

**Immunities** Immunities Necrotic, Poison; [**Exhaustion**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#exhaustioncondition), [**Frightened**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#frightenedcondition), [**Poisoned**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#poisonedcondition)

**Senses** [**Darkvision**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#darkvision) 120 ft.; Passive Perception 13

**Languages** Common, Infernal

**Challenge** 19 (XP 22,000, or 25,000 in domain; PB +6)

#### Traits {#rthw:sithicus:Traits}

**_Darklord Restoration._** If Lord Soth dies, he revives with all his Hit Points in 1d10 weeks somewhere in Sithicus.

**_Legendary Resistance (3/Day, or 4/Day in Domain)._** If Lord Soth fails a saving throw, he can choose to succeed instead.

**_Magic Resistance._** Lord Soth has [**Advantage**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#advantage) on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

**_Marshal Undead._** Undead creatures of Lord Soth’s choice (excluding himself) in a 60-foot [**Emanation**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#emanationareaofeffect) originating from him have [**Advantage**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#advantage) on attack rolls and saving throws. Lord Soth can’t use this trait if he has the [**Incapacitated**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#incapacitatedcondition) condition.

#### Actions {#rthw:sithicus:Actions}

**_Multiattack._** Lord Soth makes three Forsaken Brand attacks.

**_Forsaken Brand._** _Melee Attack Roll:_ +12, reach 5 ft. _Hit:_ 10 (1d8 + 6) Slashing damage plus 13 (3d8) Necrotic damage.

**_Cataclysmic Fire (Recharge 5–6)._** _Dexterity Saving Throw:_ DC 19, each creature in a 20-foot-radius [**Sphere**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#sphereareaofeffect) centered on a point Lord Soth can see within 120 feet. _Failure:_ 24 (7d6) Fire damage plus 24 (7d6) Necrotic damage. _Success:_ Half damage.

**_Face of Death (1/Day)._** _Charisma Saving Throw:_ DC 19, each creature in a 60-foot [**Emanation**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#emanationareaofeffect) originating from Lord Soth. _Failure:_ 22 (4d10) Psychic damage, and the creature has the [**Frightened**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#frightenedcondition) condition. _Success:_ Half damage only. _Failure or Success:_ If this damage reduces the target to 0 Hit Points, the target dies.

#### Bonus Actions {#rthw:sithicus:BonusActions}

**_Commanding Magic (3/Day)._** Lord Soth casts [**Dispel Magic**](#ref:spell:2619103-dispel-magic "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619103-dispel-magic"), [**Hold Person**](#ref:spell:2619153-hold-person "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619153-hold-person"), or [**Banishment**](#ref:spell:2618906-banishment "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618906-banishment") (level 5 version), using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 19).

#### Legendary Actions {#rthw:sithicus:LegendaryActions}

Legendary Action Uses: 3 (4 in Domain). Immediately after another creature’s turn, Soth can expend a use to take one of the following actions. Soth regains all expended uses at the start of each of his turns.

**_Punish._** Lord Soth moves up to half his Speed, and he makes one Forsaken Brand attack.

**_Soth’s Command._** Lord Soth casts [**Command**](#ref:spell:2618985-command "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618985-command") (level 3 version), using the same spellcasting ability as Commanding Magic. Lord Soth can’t take this action again until the start of his next turn.

> #### Villain of Two Worlds {#rthw:sithicus:lordsoth:6491370-lord-soth-of-sithicus:VillainofTwoWorlds}
>
> Lord Soth features in adventures in both the Dragonlance and Ravenloft campaign settings. If you want to give Soth a unique relationship to the Domains of Dread, consider these possibilities:
>
> - The nature of Soth’s curse creates aspects of the death knight in both Krynn and Sithicus. When Soth broods in his fortress in Krynn, he remains active in Sithicus. When the evil god, Takhisis, calls for his service on Krynn, Soth enters a magical torpor in his fortress in Sithicus.
> - Soth traveled from Krynn to Sithicus and is destined to return. If he leaves Sithicus, the domain might be destroyed, or a villain like Inza Kulchevich might take over.
> - Soth was trapped in Sithicus, escaped, and was trapped again, perpetuating a cycle of despair.
>
> Soth’s story and where characters encounter him are for you to detail in your adventures.

### Lord Soth’s Tale {#rthw:sithicus:LordSothsTale}

Lord Soth was given a quest to save the people of his world, Krynn, from the wrath of the gods. Possessed by baseless paranoia and possessiveness of his elf wife, Soth forsook that quest, and the world was devastated in a great Cataclysm. In punishment, Soth was resurrected as a death knight and, for centuries, brooded on his disgrace in the charred ruins of his fortress, Dargaard Keep.

When the evil god Takhisis whispered to Soth, promising to restore his glory and avenge him against the heroic knights who banished him long ago, Soth answered and served Takhisis. During this time, he called on his undead servants, including the ghost of the knight Caradoc. Seeking to forge a new knighthood of loyal dead, Soth became obsessed with Dragon Highlord Kitiara Uth Matar and charged Caradoc with claiming her soul. When Kitiara died in battle, Caradoc refused to capture her spirit unless Soth bargained with Takhisis to restore Caradoc to life. Enraged, Soth tried to destroy Caradoc as the Mists rose around them.

When the Mists faded, Soth found himself in the domain of [Barovia](#rthw:barovia "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/barovia"). For a time, he found an ally in [**Count Strahd von Zarovich**](#ref:monster:6491390-strahd-von-zarovich "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491390-strahd-von-zarovich"), but the two villains couldn’t abide one another for long. Soth eventually pursued rumors of his treacherous servant, Caradoc, into the Mists. When the Mists parted again, the domain of Sithicus spread before him.

### Lord Soth’s Domain {#rthw:sithicus:LordSothsDomain}

Sithicus is altered by Lord Soth’s presence, creating the following effects:

**Closing the Borders.** While in his domain, Lord Soth can close or open the borders to Sithicus. While the borders are closed, purple flames fill the Mists surrounding Sithicus. A creature that enters the Mists for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there takes 5 (1d10) Fire damage plus 5 (1d10) Necrotic damage.

**Fearless Soldiers.** Undead allies of Lord Soth have Immunity to the [**Frightened**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#frightenedcondition) condition.

**Guilt of Sithicus.** Few sleep soundly in Sithicus. Whenever a creature other than Lord Soth and his allies finishes a Long Rest in the domain, the creature must succeed on a DC 10 Constitution saving throw or gain 1 [**Exhaustion**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#exhaustioncondition) level.

If Lord Soth dies, these effects end immediately.

### Lord Soth’s Lair {#rthw:sithicus:LordSothsLair}

[![Nedragaard Keep (Artist: Titus Lunter)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/16-004.nedagaard-keep.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/16-004.nedagaard-keep.png)

Lord Soth rules from Nedragaard Keep, a twisted, copy of his accursed fortress on Krynn, Dargaard Keep. Nedragaard Keep grows and withers over time like a living thing. Undead soldiers patrolling the keep regularly forget their duties or collapse into lifelessness. The disorder within the rigid death knight’s fortress endlessly frustrates Lord Soth.

#### Nedragaard Keep {#rthw:sithicus:NedragaardKeep}

Nedragaard Keep is a towerlike fortress of crumbling, flame-scarred stone. Prominent locations in the keep are depicted on [map 2.31](#rthw:sithicus:map231nedragaardkeep "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/sithicus#map231nedragaardkeep") and have the following features:

**Gatehouse.** Undead soldiers guard the gates to Nedragaard Keep, demanding to know trespassers’ identities. Those who identify themselves with the proper passphrase, such as “a seeker of the rose” or “a servant of Nightlund’s lord,” are admitted. Stairs beyond the gate climb several floors to the top of the keep’s walls.

**Garden.** Gardens on the keep’s second floor are overgrown with thorny plants—use the rules for [razorvine](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/dmg-2024/dms-toolbox#razorvine) from the [Dungeon Master’s Guide](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/dmg-2024). From here spread massive vines that bloom with black roses and strangle the entire castle.

**Throne Room.** High in the keep is Soth’s throne room. Here Lord Soth spends much of his time dwelling on failures and twisted fantasies. Thirteen [**Banshees**](#ref:monster:5194916-banshee "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5194916-banshee") haunt the keep, and at any time, at least three linger here, singing of Soth’s disgrace.

## Adventures in Sithicus {#rthw:sithicus:AdventuresinSithicus}

Adventures set in Sithicus feature mysterious shadows, grim ruins, and strange foes from the warped memories of Lord Soth. Use this section to develop horror adventures in this domain.

### Horror in Sithicus {#rthw:sithicus:HorrorinSithicus}

Adventures in Sithicus often include the following elements.

#### Cataclysmic Flames {#rthw:sithicus:CataclysmicFlames}

Illusory violet flames burn across Sithicus—fires from the Cataclysm that devastated Krynn. Powerful shadows guard prominent, bonfire-like pillars of these flames. These shadows might use the stat blocks of any monster, but they resemble dragons, knights, and figures from Soth’s past.

Whenever someone defeats one of these guardians, the flame it protected reveals an illusory scene from the Darklord’s past before vanishing. Any character who witnesses such a scene learns something of Soth’s history, the world he comes from, or the knighthood he once belonged to. One of the viewers then gains the Charm of the Black Rose (see “[Supernatural Gifts](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/dmg-2024/dms-toolbox#supernaturalgifts)” in the [Dungeon Master’s Guide](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/dmg-2024) for additional details).

---

##### Charm of the Black Rose {#rthw:sithicus:CharmoftheBlackRose}

_Supernatural Gift (Charm)_

You can expend this charm to gain one of the following effects:

- You have [**Advantage**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#advantage) on ability checks made to influence [**Lord Soth’s**](#ref:monster:6491370-lord-soth-of-sithicus "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491370-lord-soth-of-sithicus") attitude for 24 hours.
- You cast [**Dissonant Whispers**](#ref:spell:2619104-dissonant-whispers "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619104-dissonant-whispers") (level 5 version, spell save DC 17).

The Charm vanishes once you use either effect.

---

#### Influencing Lord Soth {#rthw:sithicus:InfluencingLordSoth}

Lord Soth is typically [**Hostile**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#hostileattitude) to strangers, but characters can adjust his attitude to [**Indifferent**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#indifferentattitude) by succeeding on a DC 20 Charisma ([**Deception**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#skills) or [**Persuasion**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#skills)) check. Soth might employ characters he deems worthy on quests, such as the hunt for the ghost Caradoc. Making a second successful DC 20 Charisma ([**Deception**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#skills) or [**Persuasion**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#skills)) check while offering Soth something he covets can improve Soth’s attitude to [**Friendly**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#friendlyattitude) for a short time, during which he might let others leave his domain.

#### Living Shadows {#rthw:sithicus:LivingShadows}

Shadows in Sithicus often act with a life of their own. Roll on or choose a result from the Shadows of Sithicus table to inspire these shapes’ behavior.

**Shadows of Sithicus**

| 1d6 | The Shadows Behave As…                         |
| --- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| 1   | An elf desperately offering a swaddled bundle. |
| 2   | Glimpses of skeletal warriors or horses.       |
| 3   | Knights in battle or in the midst of a siege.  |
| 4   | Peasants being consumed by shadowy flames.     |
| 5   | Marching soldiers with dragon-like features.   |
| 6   | Solemn elf priests being ambushed by ogres.    |

#### Sithicus Campaign Arc {#rthw:sithicus:SithicusCampaignArc}

Campaigns set in Sithicus often involve trying to gain Lord Soth’s favor and win escape from the domain. A campaign here might follow this outline:

**Levels 1–4.** Azrael Dax, Lord Soth’s werebadger seneschal, brusquely recruits the characters to hunt down deadly shadows. These shadows take the form of and behave as noble knights.

**Level 5–9.** Impressed by the characters, Azrael sends them to Inza Kulchevich to ask the witch to use her powers to find Lord Soth’s elusive former servant, Caradoc. Inza can do this, but first she requires the characters to collect the cataclysmic flame from three ruins across the domain in a magical iron pendant. Each flame is guarded by a shadow creature that resembles some foe from Soth’s twisted memories—like a lance-wielding [**Warrior Commander**](#ref:monster:5195258-warrior-commander "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195258-warrior-commander") or a pompous [**Archpriest**](#ref:monster:5194903-archpriest "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5194903-archpriest").

**Levels 10–14.** Inza uses the pendant to reveal that Caradoc’s soul is trapped in a black sapphire that Azrael already possesses. The characters must recover the gem. They might then infiltrate Nedragaard Keep to offer it to [**Lord Soth**](#ref:monster:6491370-lord-soth-of-sithicus "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491370-lord-soth-of-sithicus"). Soth is fickle though, and this approach might end in a confrontation with the death knight.

[![Map 2.31: Nedragaard Keep View Player Version (Artist: NerdyMaps)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/map-16-02.nedragaard-keep.jpg)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/map-16-02.nedragaard-keep.jpg)

### Shadow of the Black Rose {#rthw:sithicus:ShadowoftheBlackRose}

Adventure for Level 14 Characters

**Situation.** The characters seek to escape Sithicus or the Domains of Dread.

**Hook.** Inza Kulchevich (Medium, Neutral Evil [**Death Cultist**](#ref:monster:5194960-death-cultist "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5194960-death-cultist")) offers to tell the characters how to escape Sithicus if they recover a magical gem from Lord Soth’s seneschal, Azrael Dax.

[![Map 2.31: Sithicus Ruins View Player Version (Artist: NerdyMaps)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/map-16-03.sithicus-ruins.jpg)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/map-16-03.sithicus-ruins.jpg)

#### Encounters {#rthw:sithicus:Encounters}

The adventure consists of these encounters.

**_Inza’s Quest._** The witch Inza loathes Lord Soth. She knows he has tasked Azrael with recovering a magical gem that holds the spirit of the Darklord’s treacherous former ally, the knight Caradoc. Inza gives the characters an iron pendant bearing an image of a rose that’s missing its central gem. She asks them to follow Azrael to a ruin in the Misttop Mountains, where he hunts the missing gem, and recover it before him.

**_Inza’s Secret._** Inza doesn’t share that she seeks to release Caradoc to provoke Soth into a conflict with the characters.

**_Searching the Ruins._** The ruins where Azrael hunts for the gem appear on map 2.31. For every 10 minutes the characters are exploring, roll 1d6 on the table below for an encounter. For each previous encounter rolled on this table, add 1 to the result.

**Encounters in the Ruins**

| 1d6 | Encounter                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| --- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1–2 | [**Death Knight Aspirant**](#ref:monster:5194962-death-knight-aspirant "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5194962-death-knight-aspirant") and two [**Banshees**](#ref:monster:5194916-banshee "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5194916-banshee") |
| 3–4 | Two [**Relentless Nightmares**](#ref:monster:6491384-relentless-nightmare "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491384-relentless-nightmare") (see [chapter 5](#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:relentlessnightmare "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/denizens-of-the-mists#relentlessnightmare")) |
| 5   | A [**Gulthias Blight**](#ref:monster:5195067-gulthias-blight "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195067-gulthias-blight") covered in black roses                                                                                                    |
| 6   | Kender Nosferatu (see below)                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| 7   | Shadow Highlord (see below)                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| 8+  | Azrael Dax (see below)                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |

**_Kender Nosferatu._** A morbidly whimsical pair of [**Vampire Nosferatu**](#ref:monster:6491398-vampire-nosferatu "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491398-vampire-nosferatu") (see [chapter 5](#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:vampirenosferatu "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/denizens-of-the-mists#vampirenosferatu")) pesters the characters, hoping to be entertained. If the characters don’t keep them amused, the nosferatu attack. Because these monsters were kender in life—mischievous folk from the world of Krynn—they are Small.

**_Shadow Highlord._** A dragon rider made of shadows guards a pillar of illusory violet flame. It reflects one of Lord Soth’s warped memories and uses the stat blocks of a [**Dullahan**](#ref:monster:6491351-dullahan "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491351-dullahan") (see [chapter 5](#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:dullahan "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/denizens-of-the-mists#dullahan")) riding a [**Young Blue Dragon**](#ref:monster:5195278-young-blue-dragon "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195278-young-blue-dragon"), followed by a withered [**Death’s Head**](#ref:monster:6491350-deaths-head "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491350-deaths-head") (see [chapter 5](#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:deathshead "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/denizens-of-the-mists#deathshead")). The monsters are [**Hostile**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#hostileattitude). If they’re defeated, the nearby pillar of flames shows a scene of Lord Soth being knighted and grants a character the benefits noted in “[Cataclysmic Flames](#rthw:sithicus:cataclysmicflames "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/sithicus#cataclysmicflames").” If you roll this encounter a second time, treat it as a meeting with Azrael Dax.

**_Azrael Dax._** Azrael Dax is Lord Soth’s dwarf seneschal and a murderous werebadger (use the [**Werebear**](#ref:monster:5195263-werebear "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195263-werebear") stat block). Azrael and the six [**Strahd Skeletons**](#ref:monster:6491389-strahd-skeleton "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491389-strahd-skeleton") (see [chapter 5](#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:strahdskeleton "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/denizens-of-the-mists#strahdskeleton")) attending him are Hostile. If reduced to 50 Hit Points or fewer, Azrael bargains for his life and offers the characters the black sapphire they’re looking for, which he’s been hiding from Soth for moons. After this, don’t roll for more encounters in the ruins.

**_Repairing the Pendant._** Placing the black gem in Inza’s iron amulet releases Caradoc (Neutral Evil [**Ghost**](#ref:monster:5195008-ghost "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195008-ghost")). The arrogant creature is [**Indifferent**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#indifferentattitude) to the characters. If they don’t free Caradoc, Inza does when the group returns the gem and pendant to her.

**_Soth Appears._** Three rounds after Caradoc is freed, [**Lord Soth of Sithicus**](#ref:monster:6491370-lord-soth-of-sithicus "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491370-lord-soth-of-sithicus") (see earlier in [this chapter](#rthw:sithicus:LordSoth "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/sithicus#LordSoth")) appears from the shadows. Soth fights Caradoc and mistakes the characters for the ghost’s allies. A character might convince him otherwise—see “[Influencing Lord Soth](#rthw:sithicus:influencinglordsoth "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/sithicus#influencinglordsoth").”

**_Escape._** Characters who flee or defeat Lord Soth gain an additional 6,200 XP. Those who change the Darklord’s attitude to [**Friendly**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#friendlyattitude) or help him defeat Caradoc can convince him to let them leave Sithicus. Defeating Soth also causes the domain’s borders to open. If the characters confront Inza about her method for leaving Sithicus, she cryptically explains that the only route to do so leads through Soth, encouraging them to seek the Darklord’s aid or confront the death knight again.

</CHAPTER>

<CHAPTER id="rthw:tepest" title="Tepest">

# Tepest {#rthw:tepest:Tepest}

Domain of Nature’s Cruel Secrets

> #### **Darklord:** [Mother Lorinda](#rthw:tepest:MotherLorinda "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/tepest#MotherLorinda") {#rthw:tepest:MotherLorinda}
>
> **Adventure Genre:** [Folk horror](#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:folkhorror "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/creating-domains-of-dread#folkhorror")
>
> **Hallmarks:** Fey bargains, rural cults, secret sacrifices, sinister festivals
>
> **Mist Talismans:** Bloodstained farm implement, dried crown of white camellias, straw doll
>
> **Aligned Tarokka Card:** Druid
>
> **Opposed Tarokka Card:** Executioner

[![(Artist: Pam Wishbow)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/17-001.druid-tarokka.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/17-001.druid-tarokka.png) [![](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/17-002.executioner-tarokka.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/17-002.executioner-tarokka.png)

All is well in Tepest. Fields shimmer with bountiful harvests, and horned village children recite sing-song rhymes. But those who linger among this land’s pastures and colorful cottages can’t escape the feeling of being watched or the impression that strange forms move amid the fields. Locals dismiss such worries as the work of fey tricksters, but their smiles fail to mask the desperation in their eyes.

Brutality wears a welcoming face in Tepest, a truth embodied by the ancient hag Lorinda, who betrayed her coven in pursuit of adoration. Taking the guise of a deity called Mother, [**Lorinda**](#ref:monster:6491377-mother-lorinda "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491377-mother-lorinda") adopted the village of Viktal, protecting its people from nature’s whims so they can worship her even as they sacrifice themselves to feed her monstrous offspring. In the wilderness beyond, resentful fey watch and plot, offering cruel bargains to those who stray beyond Mother’s sight. The people of Viktal do what they must to survive, using tradition to cloak their fear and complicity in a cycle of murder. Strangers become symbols of hope for Viktal’s citizens—welcome alternatives to slaughtering their families in Mother’s name.

## Domain Features {#rthw:tepest:DomainFeatures}

Tepest is known for the following features:

**Children of the Fey.** Few children are born in Viktal. Would-be parents must bargain with Mother or the fey to bring them a child.

**Fey Threats.** Caves dot the land, connecting to depths where dangerous fey dwell. The people of Viktal fear them and blame them for every ill.

**The Last Village.** Viktal is the only community in Tepest. The others displeased Mother and suffered terrible fates.

**Mother.** Viktal’s residents devoutly follow the optimistic faith of the nature deity called Mother.

**Mother’s Minders.** Mother’s most zealous faithful are called Mother’s Minders. These devotees sacrifice their left eyes to Mother to show their faith.

**The Tithe.** Viktal’s festivals include a fertility celebration called the Tithe that occurs once a season.

## Locations in Tepest {#rthw:tepest:LocationsinTepest}

The valley of Tepest is rocky, ill-suited to farming, and plagued by dangerous fey. Nevertheless, those who worship Mother are protected from the worst of the land’s dangers. Mother’s Sight and Viktal are detailed below, and other notable locations are summarized on the [Tepest Locations table](#rthw:tepest:tepestlocations "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/tepest#tepestlocations").

### Mother’s Sight {#rthw:tepest:MothersSight}

A mile outside Viktal, in a field apart from the surrounding farms, stands Mother’s Sight: an array of rune-etched standing stones. These stones rise as tall as thirty feet, and several have pieces that defy gravity. Within the central and largest stone floats a disk reminiscent of a great eye.

Here the people come to worship, celebrate, and sacrifice. Colorful crafts adorn long tables, where the villagers play games and feast in celebration of Mother’s bounty. Meals here are tasty, and guests are encouraged to eat and drink beyond their fill.

During rituals here, Viktal’s community leaders give thanks to Mother before a dramatic fire surrounded by an eight-foot scaffold. (See “[The Tithe](#rthw:tepest:thetithe "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/tepest#thetithe")” adventure for additional details.)

### Viktal {#rthw:tepest:Viktal}

Mother ensures peace in Viktal. The village consists of a few dozen cottages, a market square, and an inn on the banks of Lake Kronov. Wicker scarecrows guard the rich fields blessed by Mother, and friendly people go about their daily lives. Cheery villagers welcome visitors, show them hospitality, and demonstrate interest in their stories.

[![Map 2.32: Tepest View Player Version (Artist: Jared Blando)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/map-17-01.tepest.jpg)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/map-17-01.tepest.jpg)

**Tepest Locations**

| Location       | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Arkenheights   | Mysterious valleys hide amid the forested Arkenheights mountains. Each is home to territorial fey who know the strange histories and mystical properties that linger in each.                                                                                                  |
| Blackroot      | A gigantic evil [**Treant**](#ref:monster:5195236-treant "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195236-treant") called Blackroot roots amid the stone circles of an ancient order of druids. Blackroot hoards the druids’ magic and protects its glade with its deadly saplings. |
| Briggdarrow    | This ruined village of Briggdarrow is overgrown by a toxic, vision-inducing fungus. Eerie fungal beings emerge from the ruins by night to spread the infestation beyond the village.                                                                                           |
| Cas Island     | A ruined fortress covers most of Cas Island. Within it lies a mysterious magical relic, but the waters around the island are guarded by a notorious, crocodilian lake monster, the Avanc.                                                                                      |
| The Cauldron   | A fey witch drowned in this pool long ago. Now, any corpse bathed in its magical waters returns to life—but the spirit inhabiting the body never matches the original owner’s.                                                                                                 |
| Goblinwood     | People-eating goblins lurk in the Goblinwood. They attack trespassers, but a curse affecting the goblins prevents them from seeing anyone wearing a cap of a certain color.                                                                                                    |
| Kellee         | The walled village of Kellee once worshipped Mother, but something went wrong. Now, Lorinda’s forsaken followers haunt the place, and neither she nor her current worshippers dare approach.                                                                                   |
| The Lost Court | By day, this idyllic valley is serene and filled with friendly animals. At night, the ground turns to mud and brambles, from which rise the transformed victims of fey curses.                                                                                                 |
| Mount Arak     | Beneath Mount Arak lies a hidden realm of the fey. The goodly Queen Maeve and wicked Prince Loht jointly rule their people. The fey resent the surface folk for ancient slights.                                                                                               |
| Nobody’s Inn   | Fey creatures avoid this sturdy, welcoming Nobody’s Inn. Few travel so far from Viktal, but those who do are welcomed by Bryonna, the inn’s gregarious but unnerving skeleton proprietor.                                                                                      |
| Seer’s Glass   | The mountain lake called Seer’s Glass has prophetic powers. Those who gaze on their reflection in it see their past by day and their future by night.                                                                                                                          |

## Mother Lorinda {#rthw:tepest:MotherLorinda}

Darklord Who Demands Adoration

[![(Artist: Brian Valenzuela)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/17-003.mother-lorinda.jpg)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/17-003.mother-lorinda.jpg)

> “What precocious moppets you are! Little ones who show Mother love get rewarded, but bad children get punished. Which sorts of tots are you?”
>
> —Mother Lorinda

Mother Lorinda desires a family over all else, not realizing she’s destroyed every family she’s ever had. A creator of monstrosities, this ancient green hag obsesses over unnatural maternalistic pursuits.

Over generations, Tepest’s villagers have come to view Lorinda not as a powerful witch, but as a god of the land and fertility called Mother. Lorinda doesn’t dissuade her fragile mortal followers from their baseless cult practices. The villagers provide willing sacrifices for the hag’s flawed magical attempts to create life, and their adoration gradually soothes the violent, magical outbursts that follow her failures.

Lorinda’s walking tower of bones, the Gurgyl, ranges across Tepest. Those who seek her here find a distracted but deceptively cunning hag clinging to grotesque dolls of her family. She laments the loss of her sisters, Laveeda and Leticia, never acknowledging that they remain alive as her prisoners. She often speaks of her daughter, Laoirse (pronounced “LUR-shuh”)—the name she uses over and over again for each of her monstrous creations.

When Lorinda visits Viktal, she appears in her illusory guise as Mother, an ancient, powerful woman wearing a mothlike cloak and bearing a branch with burning limbs. She calls on the people to prove their love for her through sacrifice, whether of food and crafts, their left eyes, or their lives. Sometimes her arrival is sudden and terrifying, such as when she magically appears to crawl from one of her followers’ empty eye sockets.

Lorinda seeks new ways to create a permanent family. This might involve great sacrifices, stolen fey magic, strange adoptions, or all manner of supernatural bargains.

### [Mother Lorinda](#ref:monster:6491377-mother-lorinda "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491377-mother-lorinda") {#rthw:tepest:MotherLorindarefmonster6491377motherlorindahttpswwwdndbeyondcommonsters6491377motherlorinda}

Medium Fey, Neutral Evil

**AC** 18 **Initiative** +7 (17)

**HP** 105 (14d8 + 42)

**Speed** 30 ft., Swim 30 ft.

|     |     | Mod | Save |

**Skills** [**Arcana**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#skills) +7, [**Deception**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#skills) +5, [**Perception**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#skills) +6, [**Stealth**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#skills) +4
