#### Ancient Altar {#rthw:ravenloft-adventures:AncientAltar}

Level 9 Bastion Facility

**Prerequisite:** None  
**Space:** Cramped  
**Hirelings:** 1  
**Order:** [Empower](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/dmg-2024/bastions#empower)

An Ancient Altar is a solemn chamber where you can make offerings to mysterious forces.

**_Empower: Purge Haunted Facility._** You commission your hireling to lead a ritual that takes 7 days, during which time you must remain in the Bastion. At the end of the ritual, you must offer a worthy sacrifice, which can be monetary (1,000 GP) or blood (the fresh corpse of at least one Large creature or four Medium creatures that aren’t Constructs or Undead). If you make a blood sacrifice, roll on the [Bastion Hauntings table](#rthw:ravenloft-adventures:bastionhauntings "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/ravenloft-adventures#bastionhauntings"). Once the ritual is complete, the sacrifice is destroyed. Choose a Haunted special facility in this Bastion or in a Bastion connected to this one; that facility is no longer Haunted.

**_Blasphemous Charm._** After spending a Long Rest in your Ancient Altar, you gain a magical Charm that lasts for 7 days or until you use it. You can use the Charm as a [**Magic**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#magicaction) action to cast [**Hunger of Hadar**](#ref:spell:2619162-hunger-of-hadar "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619162-hunger-of-hadar") without requiring Material components. You can’t gain this Charm again while you have it.

---

#### Cabinet of Curiosities {#rthw:ravenloft-adventures:CabinetofCuriosities}

Level 9 Bastion Facility

**Prerequisite:** None  
**Space:** Cramped  
**Hirelings:** 1  
**Order:** [Trade](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/dmg-2024/bastions#trade)

A Cabinet of Curiosities is a small salon, closet space, or antechamber where you can keep and catalog peculiar objects and fascinating oddities.

**_Trade: Acquire Curios._** When you issue the Trade order to this facility, you supply this facility’s hireling with a certain amount of gold and commission them to purchase strange items from unusual sources. It takes 28 days for the hireling to return to the Bastion with one or more magic items for you. Your investment determines the rarity of these items, and the quantity of magic items depends on the number of Haunted special facilities in your Bastion at the time of the hireling’s return, as shown on the Curio Investment and Curios Collected tables.

**Curio Investment**

| Investment | Item Rarity |
| ---------- | ----------- |
| 150 GP     | Common      |
| 600 GP     | Uncommon    |
| 6,000 GP   | Rare        |
| 60,000 GP  | Very Rare   |

**Curios Collected**

| Haunted Facilities | Magic Items Acquired | Cursed Item Chance (1d100) |
| ------------------ | -------------------- | -------------------------- |
| 0                  | 1                    | —                          |
| 1–2                | 1–2 (flip a coin)    | 01–10                      |
| 3–5                | 1d3                  | 01–20                      |
| 6                  | 1d4                  | 01–25                      |

To determine how many magic items your hireling brings back, count the Haunted special facilities in your Bastion, then roll the die indicated in the Magic Items Acquired column on the Curios Collected table. The DM rolls on the Cursed Item Chance (1d100) column to determine whether one of the magic items carries a curse. The DM chooses which item is cursed and establishes the nature of the curse.

For each magic item acquired, roll on a table in the “[Random Magic Items](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/dmg-2024/random-magic-items)” section in the [Dungeon Master’s Guide](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/dmg-2024) of the corresponding rarity to determine what the item is. (Select the treasure theme randomly.)

---

[![Spirits and grim secrets haunt Bastions in the Demiplanes of Dread (Artist: Pedro Cardoso)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/20-011.demiplanes-of-dread-bastion.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/20-011.demiplanes-of-dread-bastion.png)

#### Infirmary {#rthw:ravenloft-adventures:Infirmary}

Level 9 Bastion Facility

**Prerequisite:** Proficiency in the [**Medicine**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#skills) skill  
**Space:** Roomy  
**Hirelings:** 2  
**Order:** [Craft](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/dmg-2024/bastions#craft)

An Infirmary provides emergency healing and continual care to injured or sick Bastion occupants.

**_Craft Options._** When you issue the Craft order to this facility, choose one of the following options:

**Craft: Antitoxin.** You commission the facility’s hirelings to craft two vials of [**Antitoxin**](#ref:equipment:520-antitoxin "https://www.dndbeyond.com/equipment/520-antitoxin"). The work takes 7 days and costs no money. You can spend 50 GP during the creation process to enhance one of the vials of Antitoxin, or 100 GP to enhance both. An enhanced Antitoxin ends the [**Poisoned**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#poisonedcondition) condition on the creature that drinks it. An enhanced Antitoxin loses this enhancement after 28 days.

**Craft: Enhanced Potion of Healing.** You commission this facility’s hirelings to increase the potency of up to two [**Potions of Healing**](#ref:magic_item:8960641-potion-of-healing "https://www.dndbeyond.com/magic-items/8960641-potion-of-healing"). You must provide the potions to be enhanced, and the process takes 14 days to complete. A _Potion of Healing_ becomes a [**Potion of Healing (greater)**](#ref:magic_item:5133-potion-of-healing-greater "https://www.dndbeyond.com/magic-items/5133-potion-of-healing-greater"). When you reach level 13 you can provide up to two _Potions of Healing_ (greater), each of which becomes a [**Potion of Healing (superior)**](#ref:magic_item:5134-potion-of-healing-superior "https://www.dndbeyond.com/magic-items/5134-potion-of-healing-superior").

**_Triage._** When your Bastion is attacked and you roll a number of dice to determine how many Bastion Defenders are lost, you can reroll a number of those dice equal to the number of hirelings this facility has. You must use the new roll.

**_Enlarging the Facility._** You can enlarge your Infirmary to a Vast facility by spending 2,000 GP. If you do so, the Infirmary gains two hirelings, and the number of Antitoxins or _Potions of Healing_ you can enhance at a time increases to four.

---

#### Lightning Generator {#rthw:ravenloft-adventures:LightningGenerator}

Level 13 Bastion Facility

**Prerequisite:** None  
**Space:** Roomy  
**Hirelings:** 1  
**Order:** [Empower](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/dmg-2024/bastions#empower)

A Lightning Generator can transform atmospheric electricity to serve a variety of useful functions.

**_Charm of Electromancy._** After spending a Long Rest in your Lightning Generator, you take 8d6 Lightning damage and you gain a magical Charm that lasts for 7 days (see the [Dungeon Master’s Guide](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/dmg-2024) for rules on [Charms](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/dmg-2024/dms-toolbox#charms)). The Charm has 3 charges. You can expend 1 charge from the Charm to cast the [**Telekinesis**](#ref:spell:2619157-telekinesis "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619157-telekinesis") spell. Once all its charges are expended, the Charm vanishes from you.

**_Revivification._** When you cast the spell [**Raise Dead**](#ref:spell:2618922-raise-dead "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618922-raise-dead") and [**Resurrection**](#ref:spell:2618953-resurrection "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618953-resurrection") while in this facility, the cost of that spell’s Material components are reduced by 1,000 GP (minimum of 0).

**_Empower: Lightning Life._** The facility’s hireling channels the Generator’s energy to cast [**Animate Objects**](#ref:spell:2618855-animate-objects "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618855-animate-objects"), targeting one Large or Huge object of your choice in the Bastion. The spell’s duration is 7 days and doesn’t require [**Concentration**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#concentration).

---

#### Liminal Space {#rthw:ravenloft-adventures:LiminalSpace}

Level 17 Bastion Facility

**Prerequisite:** None  
**Space:** Vast  
**Hirelings:** 1  
**Order:** [Recruit](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/dmg-2024/bastions#recruit)

Your Bastion becomes connected to an unfathomable demiplane filled with vast, empty spaces and strange beings. This special facility doesn’t take up space in your Bastion; instead, the entrance to this facility appears in the closets, crawlspaces, and shadows of your Bastion’s other basic and special facilities. The hireling in charge of this facility protects the Bastion’s inhabitants from stray entities that slip out from the demiplane. This facility always counts as Haunted.

**_Dark Bargains._** You can enter this facility and wander within for 7 days, consulting and bargaining with the strange entities there. If you leave the Bastion during this time, you gain no benefit. At the end of the seventh day, you gain a Dark Gift feat of your choice (see [chapter 1](#rthw:character-options:darkgifts "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/character-options#darkgifts")). You can only have one feat from this benefit at a time; if you use this benefit when you already have a feat from it, the feat you gain at the end of the seven days replaces any feat previously gained from use of this facility.

**_Recruit: Stranger._** When you issue the Recruit order to this facility, you instruct the facility’s hireling to conduct a ritual and petition an entity from the demiplane for aid. This ritual takes 7 days and costs 1,000 GP. At the ritual’s end, roll any die. On an odd number, the summoned entity refuses your request and kills the hireling, and this facility can’t be used until your next Bastion turn, at which point the hireling is replaced at no cost to you; on an even number, the summoned entity agrees to your request and takes up residence in your Liminal Space.

While residing in your Liminal Space, an entity counts as a Bastion Defender, and if your Bastion is attacked, each entity in your Liminal Space reduces by 1 the number of dice you roll to determine how many Bastion Defenders are lost in the attack. You can choose not to count the entity as a Bastion Defender, in which case you can’t call on it to defend the Bastion; instead, the entity acts according to its nature, using the [**Unspeakable Horror**](#ref:monster:6491396-unspeakable-horror "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491396-unspeakable-horror") stat block (see [chapter 5](#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:unspeakablehorror "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/denizens-of-the-mists#unspeakablehorror")). You can have up to three entities in your Liminal Space at a time. Deduct any you lose from your Bastion Defenders roster.

---

#### Rookery {#rthw:ravenloft-adventures:Rookery}

Level 5 Bastion Facility

**Prerequisite:** None  
**Space:** Cramped  
**Hirelings:** 1  
**Order:** [Craft](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/dmg-2024/bastions#craft)

A number of ravens equal to your character level roost in a Rookery. Whenever a creature enters the facility, the birds uncannily track its movement, an unfathomable intelligence behind their beady eyes.

**_Craft: Mist Talisman._** When you issue the Craft order to this facility, you can commission the hireling to send ravens to various contacts in a Domain of Dread you have either visited previously or heard about from a creature that has been within said domain. This work takes 21 days, during which time no other activity can occur within this facility.

At the end of this period, the hireling produces a Mist talisman (see the [introduction](#rthw:domains-of-dread:misttalismans "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/domains-of-dread#misttalismans")) linked to the chosen Domain of Dread.

**_Messenger Ravens._** Whenever you finish a Long Rest in your Bastion, you can send one raven bearing a written message of 25 words or fewer to a creature you have met or a creature described to you by someone who has met it. After receiving this message, the recipient can reply in a like manner, attaching their response to the raven. Regardless of whether or not the recipient responds, the raven returns to the rookery after 7 days have passed.

You can send a message via raven in this way across any distance, though the message recipient must be on the same plane of existence as your Bastion or in a demiplane linked to yours by the Mists of Ravenloft. A messenger raven delivers the message regardless of any magical wards or other interposing forces, including the Mists and closed borders of a Domain of Dread. If the raven is unable to deliver your message, it returns to your rookery after 7 days with your original message still attached.

---

#### Séance Parlor {#rthw:ravenloft-adventures:SanceParlor}

Level 5 Bastion Facility

[![Divination tools, such as spirit boards and tarokka decks, are common features of seance parlors (Artist: CoupleOfKooks)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/20-012.spirit-board-on-table.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/20-012.spirit-board-on-table.png)

**Prerequisite:** None  
**Space:** Cramped  
**Hirelings:** 1  
**Order:** [Research](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/dmg-2024/bastions#research)

The veil between the world of the living and the dead grows thin in a Séance Parlor.

**_Research: Fortune Telling._** When you issue the Research order to this facility, you commission its hireling to read your fortune by casting bones, interpreting tea leaves, performing a tarokka reading, or using some other means. After your fortune is read, you gain [**Heroic Inspiration**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#heroicinspiration). You can’t gain this benefit again until you finish a Long Rest.

**_Speak with Dead._** After spending a Long Rest in your Séance Parlor, you can cast [**Speak with Dead**](#ref:spell:2619068-speak-with-dead "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619068-speak-with-dead") immediately without expending a spell slot or needing Material components. When you cast it in this way, you can target any deceased creature whose name you know, as long as you have a piece of its remains (such as ashes or a bone) or an object that was important to the creature in life (such as a brooch or signature weapon). The target speaks through an implement in the Séance Room such as a crystal ball or spirit board.

---

#### Spirit Vault {#rthw:ravenloft-adventures:SpiritVault}

Level 13 Bastion Facility

**Prerequisite:** None  
**Space:** Roomy  
**Hirelings:** 1  
**Order:** [Research](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/dmg-2024/bastions#research)

A Spirit Vault is magically warded to imprison and exorcise malevolent spirits and other supernatural forces. Haunted portraits, cursed relics, and other eerie curios line the shelves of this dark vault. This facility always counts as Haunted.

**_Esoteric Knowledge._** After spending a Long Rest in your Spirit Vault, you gain one of the following magical Charms:

**Charm of Exorcism.** You can use the Charm as a [**Magic**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#magicaction) action to cast [**Dispel Evil and Good**](#ref:spell:2619096-dispel-evil-and-good "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619096-dispel-evil-and-good") or [**Remove Curse**](#ref:spell:2618943-remove-curse "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618943-remove-curse") without requiring Material components.

**Charm of Malediction.** You can use the Charm as a Magic action to cast [**Hex**](#ref:spell:2618988-hex "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618988-hex") (level 3 version) or [**Bestow Curse**](#ref:spell:2618923-bestow-curse "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618923-bestow-curse") without requiring Material components.

The Charm lasts for 7 days or until you use it. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for the Charm’s spells (choose each time you gain this Charm).

**_Research: Ask the Occult._** When you issue the Research order to this facility, you or its hireling study the various relics and question the imprisoned entities within your Spirit Vault. This work takes 7 days. At the end of this time, roll 1d6. On a 1, the work is psychically taxing; if you did the research, you take 6d6 Psychic damage, and if the hireling did the research, they immediately die, and this facility can’t be used again until your next Bastion turn. Otherwise, you or the hireling gain information as if you had successfully cast the [**Contact Other Plane**](#ref:spell:2619052-contact-other-plane "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619052-contact-other-plane") spell. The hireling shares any information they learned with you the next time you speak.

</CHAPTER>

--- 

<CHAPTER id="rthw:creating-domains-of-dread" title="Creating Domains Of Dread">

# Chapter 4: Creating Domains of Dread {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:Chapter4CreatingDomainsofDread}

## Chapter 4 Creating Domains of Dread {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:Chapter4CreatingDomainsofDread}

[![A hexblood witch in the domain of Tepest conjures visions of adventurers’ fatal fates (Artist: Sean A. Murray)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/21-001.hexblood-witch.jpg)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/21-001.hexblood-witch.jpg)

Any fear might find terrible life amid the Domains of Dread. Each domain highlights its own distinctive terror or flavor of the macabre. [Chapter 2](#rthw:domains-of-ravenloft "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/domains-of-ravenloft") presents numerous Domains of Dread and their respective Darklords, but you can blend legendary evils, unexpected monstrosities, and grim settings into your own horrifying creations.

This chapter explores how to create a Domain of Dread, starting with defining its Darklord, the villain at the domain’s heart. Descriptions of various genres of horror also provide details to guide and inspire your creations.

> #### Tarokka and Random Tables {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:creatingdomainsofdread:TarokkaandRandomTables}
>
> This section provides random tables compatible with the tarokka deck (see [appendix A](#rthw:tarokka-deck "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/tarokka-deck")). Here’s how to use the tarokka deck—or playing cards—instead of a d10 to generate random results:
>
> **1: Remove the High Deck.** Remove all high deck cards, leaving only cards numbered one through nine plus the master of the suit.
>
> **2: Draw a Card.** Ensure the deck is well shuffled, then draw from the top.
>
> **3: Consult a Table.** Reference the card’s number to find your result on a table; in the tarokka deck, the master of a suit counts as a ten.
>
> When using the tarokka deck, you can let the card’s suit add extra dimension to your results. The four of coins might encourage you to link that aspect of the Darklord to wealth, while the four of swords could provide an interpretation rooted in violence. Appendix A details interpretations of the tarokka deck’s cards.

## Creating a Darklord {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:CreatingaDarklord}

Domains are reflections of and prisons for the Darklords they confine. To devise a Domain of Dread, first consider its central antagonist and prisoner: its Darklord. The following sections detail how to develop a Darklord as a focal antagonist in your horror adventures.

### Building Your Darklord {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:BuildingYourDarklord}

A Darklord’s memories, desires, mistakes, and evil deeds shape a domain and its inhabitants. This chapter presents tables with suggested questions and motifs related to a Darklord’s past and personality. Choose or randomly generate prompts to develop your Darklord further, or use the table entries as inspiration.

To build a Darklord, follow these steps:

**Step 1: Choose Genres.** What horror genres does your Darklord fit into? Use those genres’ principles to help develop your Darklord.

**Step 2: Determine Their Past.** Who was the Darklord before they turned to irredeemable evil? What ambitions and flaws drove them to commit heinous acts? How did the Darklord first attract the attention of the Dark Powers? The “[Darklord’s Past](#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:darklordspast "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/creating-domains-of-dread#darklordspast")” section provides a multitude of prompts to inspire your Darklord’s origin story.

**Step 3: Determine Their Identity.** What monstrous form does your Darklord’s evil take? Turn to each genre chosen in step 1, then consult that genre’s respective “Villain Identities” and “Villain Torments” sections. Feel free to mix and match the tables from different genres to achieve your desired feel.

### Genres of Horror {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:GenresofHorror}

Horror stories span a wide variety of genres. One tale might explore the grotesque, warping flesh and bone into perversions of the living; another might be fantastical and philosophical, using restless ghosts to examine the nature of the soul.

Before you begin building a Darklord, consider which genres of horror you’d like to explore. The Genres of Horror table describes the six major genres of horror explored later in this chapter and their common motifs. If you’re uncertain where to start, use the table to identify which motifs interest, excite, or inspire fear in you. The sections later in the chapter also detail each genre’s core principles, which drive how you develop the Darklord, the domain, and the adventures within.

These genres aren’t mutually exclusive. Feel free to blend themes from different genres to create a unique and terrifying story. The end of this chapter briefly describes a handful of additional genres for consideration.

**Genres of Horror**

| Genre                          | Characters in Stories of This Genre …   | Common Motifs                                         |
| ------------------------------ | --------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| [Body horror](#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:bodyhorror "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/creating-domains-of-dread#bodyhorror")     | Explore the unpredictability of flesh.  | Gore, loss of bodily autonomy, parasitic infestations |
| [Cosmic horror](#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:cosmichorror "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/creating-domains-of-dread#cosmichorror") | Face incomprehensible insignificance.   | Faceless terrors, infinite voids, unblinking eyes     |
| [Dark fantasy](#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:darkfantasy "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/creating-domains-of-dread#darkfantasy")   | Battle grim evils and wicked magic.     | Antiheroes, evil witchcraft, misty forests            |
| [Folk horror](#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:folkhorror "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/creating-domains-of-dread#folkhorror")     | Unmask ancient taboos and traditions.   | Cryptic legends, masked cults, secluded towns         |
| [Ghost stories](#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:ghoststories "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/creating-domains-of-dread#ghoststories") | Examine mortality and tragic histories. | Decrepit mansions, incorporeal haunts, old ruins      |
| [Gothic horror](#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:gothichorror "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/creating-domains-of-dread#gothichorror") | Confront passions and evils within.     | Ancient castles, strong emotions, tarnished splendor  |

### Darklord’s Past {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:DarklordsPast}

Every Darklord has committed irredeemable acts that attract the attention of the Dark Powers. Yet Darklords are still individuals who, at one point, had a home, childhood, and family. The following sections each examine a different aspect of the Darklord’s life prior to imprisonment.

#### Past Life {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:PastLife}

What circumstances and choices pushed the Darklord down their twisted path? Choose or randomly generate at least three questions from the Past Life table to answer. If you generate the same question again, use the question one above or below the entry instead.

**Past Life**

| 1d10 | Question                                                                       |
| ---- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| 1    | Does the Darklord feel that they have any hope of redemption? Do they want it? |
| 2    | How did the Darklord react when challenged?                                    |
| 3    | What ideal or philosophy governs the Darklord’s greater actions?               |
| 4    | What locations and circumstances shaped the Darklord’s adolescence?            |
| 5    | What pushed the Darklord to continue committing heinous acts?                  |
| 6    | What person, place, or object does the Darklord desire most?                   |
| 7    | What was the first depraved act the Darklord committed?                        |
| 8    | Whose respect did the Darklord crave?                                          |
| 9    | Who hurt the Darklord?                                                         |
| 10   | Who loved the Darklord?                                                        |

#### Dark Catalyst {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:DarkCatalyst}

Negative emotions can twist one’s ideals into something sinister. Choose or randomly generate at least one prompt from the Dark Catalyst table to develop what encouraged the Darklord’s corruption.

**Dark Catalyst**

| 1d10 | Something in the Darklord’s Past …                                         |
| ---- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1    | Caused them to obsess over control.                                        |
| 2    | Celebrated the Darklord’s heinous activities.                              |
| 3    | Drove them toward bloodthirsty revenge.                                    |
| 4    | Enabled their indulgence and vices.                                        |
| 5    | Escalated their violent tendencies.                                        |
| 6    | Fueled an all-consuming fear of loss.                                      |
| 7    | Pushed them to turn to a greater power.                                    |
| 8    | Removed their empathy for others.                                          |
| 9    | Sowed paranoia, encouraging them to constantly test their allies’ loyalty. |
| 10   | Spurred them to pursue perfection.                                         |

#### Wicked Ambitions {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:WickedAmbitions}

All Darklords have a core ambition or goal that drives them to commit evil acts. These unobtainable goals fueled their corruption and motivate the Darklords’ conflicts with adventurers in their domains. Choose or randomly generate such a goal from the Wicked Ambitions table.

**Wicked Ambitions**

| 1d10 | The Darklord …                                            |
| ---- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1    | Seeks an apprentice or inheritor.                         |
| 2    | Explores ways to forget the past.                         |
| 3    | Longs for divine or otherworldly power.                   |
| 4    | Pursues ways to relieve themself of loneliness.           |
| 5    | Relentlessly pursues the reincarnation of a loved one.    |
| 6    | Searches for an object or artifact.                       |
| 7    | Seeks vengeance against a person or ideal.                |
| 8    | Struggles to cheat death.                                 |
| 9    | Wants to be a hero—but one who is twisted to the extreme. |
| 10   | Wishes to be beautiful and admired.                       |

#### Intervention of the Dark Powers {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:InterventionoftheDarkPowers}

Consider how the Darklord attracted the attention of the Dark Powers. On the completion of an act of remarkable depravity, the Mists claim the Darklord—and perhaps their home—imprisoning them in a new Domain of Dread. The deed that ultimately causes a villain to be claimed by the Mists needn’t be devastating, but it should represent an evil novel enough for the Dark Powers to take note. Use the Darklords’ tales from [chapter 2](#rthw:domains-of-ravenloft "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/domains-of-ravenloft") to inspire how a Darklord might be claimed by the Mists.

### Birth of a Darklord {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:BirthofaDarklord}

Now trapped in a domain tailor-made to be their prison, the Darklord is immortal, and their greatest desire is just out of reach. At this point, you should have an idea of who the Darklord is, what they did, what form their evil takes, and how they came to the attention of the Dark Powers.

Now consider how the Darklord’s evil manifests in their domain and how it brings them into conflict with the adventurers and the domain’s inhabitants.

#### Monstrous Identities {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:MonstrousIdentities}

Some Darklords undergo harrowing transformations on their imprisonment, as the Dark Powers warp those Darklords’ forms to reflect their evil. Alternatively, the Darklord might have been a monster to begin with, or perhaps they gained their form and powers through their deeds or a curse.

Consider how your Darklord is viewed by inhabitants of their domain. Reference the genres of horror that your Darklord fits into (later in [this chapter](#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:GenresofHorror "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/creating-domains-of-dread#GenresofHorror")), and use a genre’s “Villain Identities” and “Villain Torments” sections to shape the Darklord’s monstrousness. The “Villain Identities” sections provide options for the Darklord’s primary identity or form while within their domain, while the “Villain Torments” sections provide torturous twists that the Dark Powers might employ to torment the Darklord and reflect their evil.

#### Finishing Touches {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:FinishingTouches}

The story of a Darklord entwines with those of the adventurers and the domain itself. As you finish fleshing out your Darklord’s details, consider the following options to further connect the Darklord to their domain and the adventures within it.

**_Endless Torment._** In every domain, its Darklord’s greatest desire remains in view but ever out of reach. How does your Darklord’s torment remain central to and unignorable in the story?

**_Misty Borders._** The [Mists of Ravenloft](#rthw:domains-of-dread:themists "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/domains-of-dread#themists") surround each Domain of Dread. The Dark Powers afford Darklords some control over the Mists bordering their domains. Does your Darklord allow the Mists to function undisturbed, or do the Mists also reflect the Darklord’s nature, perpetuating the cycle of torment?

**_Supporting Cast._** Consider what NPC types support the Darklord, exacerbate their threat, or oppose them. How do the inhabitants of the domain play into the Dark Powers’ plans, taking the Darklord’s situation from bad to worse?

## Creating a Domain {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:CreatingaDomain}

[![Domains of Dread might be any size or shape and can draw inspiration from any horror genre (Artist: Chris Seaman)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/21-002.different-domains-of-dread.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/21-002.different-domains-of-dread.png)

Once you’ve developed a terrifying Darklord, start shaping that Darklord’s unique Domain of Dread. Everything in this realm is inspired by the Darklord’s torment or personalized to it.

This section provides guidelines to help you create a suitably terrifying and tragic Domain of Dread.

### Building a Domain {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:BuildingaDomain}

Similar to building a Darklord, you can choose or randomly generate prompts from the tables below to flesh out the domain’s details.

To build a Domain of Dread, follow these steps:

**Step 1: Choose Genres.** Most Domains of Dread are inspired by the same horror genres that shape their imprisoned Darklord, but feel free to mix in new genre elements.

**Step 2: Develop Details.** What are the distinctive elements of the domain? How do these elements reflect and twist the Darklord’s past, furthering the Darklord’s torment? The “Dread Details” section contains several tables with prompts to tailor your domain to its central prisoner.

**Step 3: Create Adventures.** What adventures will the characters have in this domain? Turn to the genres chosen in step 1, and consult their “Adventure Hooks” and “Adventure Settings” sections to inspire your adventures.

**Step 4: Choose Monsters.** The genres later in [this chapter](#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:GenresofHorror "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/creating-domains-of-dread#GenresofHorror") each include a table suggesting a plethora of monsters that suit the genre’s sensibilities. Consult those monster tables, and choose which terrifying creatures will haunt the characters in the domain. If none of the suggested monsters fit your ideas, you can reskin or alter the suggested monsters or choose ones that do.

### Dread Details {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:DreadDetails}

The domain’s buildings, natural elements, landmarks, and creatures reflect the Darklord’s vile past. This section provides prompts for developing elements of your domain and connecting those specifics to the imprisoned Darklord.

Don’t get bogged down with the particulars of a working society. Things like weather, ecosystems, and agriculture needn’t follow logic in a domain. Mundane details can fade into the background as your adventures focus on the domain’s threats.

#### Domain Elements {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:DomainElements}

Above all else, a domain is a torturous prison for its Darklord. Visceral sights, sounds, and smells within the domain should hint at the Darklord’s past villainy or serve as a means for the Dark Powers to torment the domain’s central prisoner.

Choose or randomly generate at least three questions from the Domain Elements table to answer. If you generate the same question again, use the question one above or below the entry instead. Don’t be afraid to combine details in unexpected ways—the more unnatural or off-putting, the better.

**Domain Elements**

| 1d10 | Question                                                                                                               |
| ---- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1    | What sounds, smells, colors, or symbols pervade the domain?                                                            |
| 2    | Where do the Mists appear besides the domain’s borders? What shapes and sounds haunt the Mists in and near the domain? |
| 3    | What is visible in the sky? Is there a day-and-night cycle? What’s the weather like?                                   |
| 4    | What is the domain culture’s general attitude toward the Darklord?                                                     |
| 5    | What does the domain culture fear or consider taboo?                                                                   |
| 6    | What does the domain culture celebrate?                                                                                |
| 7    | What is scarce in the domain, and how do the inhabitants compensate for this?                                          |
| 8    | What do buildings in the domain look like? Are they new or old?                                                        |
| 9    | What biome is the domain’s environment (e.g., arctic, desert, forest)?                                                 |
| 10   | What justifications do the inhabitants use, if any, to pretend nothing is wrong in the domain?                         |

#### Darklord’s Shadows {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:DarklordsShadows}

A domain’s features are constant, painful, and symbolic reminders of the Darklord’s wicked past. Choose or randomly generate at least one prompt from the Darklord’s Shadows table to develop how the domain reflects the Darklord’s history. Consider connecting the results to your answers to the questions in “Domain Elements.”

**Darklord’s Shadows**

| 1d10 | The Domain Reflects …                                       |
| ---- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1    | A taboo the Darklord broke.                                 |
| 2    | Someone the Darklord killed.                                |
| 3    | Someone or something the Darklord loved—and lost.           |
| 4    | Esoteric knowledge the Darklord sought but couldn’t obtain. |
| 5    | A tradition sacred to the Darklord’s home.                  |
| 6    | An act of extreme violence the Darklord committed.          |
| 7    | The Darklord’s greatest temptation.                         |
| 8    | Someone the Darklord betrayed.                              |
| 9    | The Darklord’s greatest fear.                               |
| 10   | Evidence of the Darklord’s vilest act.                      |

## Unleash Your Horror {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:UnleashYourHorror}

At this point, you should have a wealth of information about your Darklord and their domain. Review your notes, connect elements, establish recurring themes, and consider ways to foreshadow circumstances that adventures might focus on. You don’t need to have answers for every question now; you can define many details during adventures or by focusing on elements your players gravitate toward. For examples of fully detailed Darklords and domains, see [chapter 2](#rthw:domains-of-ravenloft "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/domains-of-ravenloft").

## Genres of Horror {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:GenresofHorror}

The following sections provide overviews of several genres of horror. Use these to inspire adventures, Darklords, and Domains of Dread of your own creation or to further detail the domains presented in [chapter 2](#rthw:domains-of-ravenloft "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/domains-of-ravenloft"). Mix and match elements from different genres to create your own uniquely terrifying combinations.

---

### Body Horror {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:BodyHorror}

[![(Artist: Ivan Shavrin)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/21-003.body-horror.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/21-003.body-horror.png)

Body horror examines the fear of our failing anatomies. Tales in this genre explore the unpredictability of flesh—that robust health might be an illusion and that we might be incubating what will devour us. Examples include _Alien_ and _The Fly_.

#### Body Horror Principles {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:BodyHorrorPrinciples}

Consider the following principles when creating Darklords and domains with body horror themes:

**Depth of Transformation.** Physical transformations are common and might affect more than bodies. Objects, architecture, and the natural world might be also anthropomorphized.

**Flesh Aberrations.** Characters suffer aberrant or excessive growth, whether of organs, discordant appendages, or unnatural materials.

**Gore Is a Byproduct.** Though gore might take center stage in body horror stories, it’s often a side effect of stories about fear of change, difference, mortality, physical harm, or disease.

**Gore Isn’t Required.** Body horror doesn’t need to be messy. Swapping bodies, turning to stone, or gaining one’s ideal form might feature in this genre.

**Real Disabilities Aren’t Horrifying.** Body horror has a history of portraying disability as monstrous. Avoid this trope.

#### Body Horror Villains {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:BodyHorrorVillains}

A physical transformation doesn’t make someone a villain. Villains in body horror adventures cultivate evil in tandem with the aberrant transformations afflicting their form and surroundings.

##### Villain Identities {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:VillainIdentities}

Villains of this genre are often tragic figures, whether they’re cultists enduring forced metamorphosis or scientists trying to extend their lives. Choose from or roll on the Body Horror Villains table to inspire villains appropriate to this genre.

**Body Horror Villains**

| 1d10 | The Villain Is …                                                                           |
| ---- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| 1    | An abandoned homunculus made in the image of its creator’s child.                          |
| 2    | A scientist who, hoping to keep their spouse alive, grafts their spouse to their own body. |
| 3    | A fungal mass that grows more intelligent with every sapient life it engulfs.              |
| 4    | A guardian angel possessed by the vile blood of the demons it has slain.                   |
| 5    | A dying ruler obsessed with creating a new body so they can continue their reign.          |
| 6    | A cancer possessed by the mind of a dead mage that seeks to regrow their body.             |
| 7    | A monarch who feeds their cannibal children, no matter the cost.                           |
| 8    | The priests of a forgotten god, who try to raise their deity from the faithful’s flesh.    |
| 9    | A house that remembers its tenants and will do anything to regain them.                    |
| 10   | A grieving mortician who sculpts every face they encounter into that of their lost love.   |

##### Villain Torments {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:VillainTorments}

Villains in this genre simultaneously draw power from and are tormented by supernatural and physiological aberrance. Choose from or roll on the Body Horror Torments table to determine what abhorrent affliction plagues the villain.

**Body Horror Torments**

| 1d10 | The Villain …                                                               |
| ---- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1    | Possesses a bestial mouth in their torso.                                   |
| 2    | Is pockmarked with eyes that never close.                                   |
| 3    | Grows tooth-filled cysts on their limbs.                                    |
| 4    | Is plagued by an ever-growing fungal mass sprouting from their extremities. |
| 5    | Restitches their body together.                                             |
| 6    | Has parasites writhing beneath their skin.                                  |
| 7    | Can dissolve their physical form at will.                                   |
| 8    | Is gravid with bulbous egg sacs.                                            |
| 9    | Aches with a ceaseless hunger.                                              |
| 10   | Can’t control their transformation into a beast and back.                   |

#### Body Horror Adventures {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:BodyHorrorAdventures}

Adventures in body horror realms often become tests of endurance, whether characters are attempting to hold out until rescue arrives or endeavoring to mount a rescue themselves. Alternatively, adventures might have an investigative feel, requiring the heroes to uncover the dark secret that lies beneath the mundane.

##### Adventure Hooks {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:AdventureHooks}

Body horror plots often explore the unpredictability of life and discordance between mind and body. Choose from or roll on the Body Horror Plots table to inspire your body horror adventures.

**Body Horror Plots**

| 1d10 | Adventure Plots                                                                   |
| ---- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1    | A malevolent curse is transforming the village’s children into misshapen statues. |
| 2    | Guests of a popular local dinner party keep succumbing to autophagia.             |
| 3    | Corpses of beasts—mutated and halfway human—are left at the forest’s edge.        |
| 4    | Every night, one townsperson melts.                                               |
| 5    | Fiends have infiltrated a community by wearing the corpses of the deceased.       |
| 6    | Fleshy catacombs open beneath a town.                                             |
| 7    | A neighborhood is filled with derelict houses composed entirely of mimics.        |
| 8    | The corpse of a monstrous leviathan has washed ashore, entrails still moving.     |
| 9    | A virulent infestation uses the townsfolk as incubators for giant insects.        |
| 10   | Something is stealing the tongues of the city guards.                             |

##### Adventure Settings {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:AdventureSettings}

Body horror can occur anywhere, from mundane settings to unsettling locales. Choose from or roll on the Body Horror Settings table to inspire locations for your adventures.

**Body Horror Settings**

| 1d10 | The Adventure Takes Place In …                                                 |
| ---- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| 1    | A vine-covered, ostensibly abandoned prison or asylum.                         |
| 2    | The cavernous gut of a dead behemoth.                                          |
| 3    | A sprawling university, older than the town surrounding it.                    |
| 4    | A city of red muscle, with bleeding eyes embedded in hair-strangled buildings. |
| 5    | A forest of burnt pines draped in gore.                                        |
| 6    | A derelict laboratory with old experiments floating in containment tubes.      |
| 7    | A slaughterhouse, larger than it appears on the outside and full of victims.   |
| 8    | A suddenly empty mortuary.                                                     |
| 9    | An old church sitting astride a warren of ancient tunnels.                     |
| 10   | A vibrant garden sprouting from a mound of putrid corpses.                     |

#### Body Horror Monsters {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:BodyHorrorMonsters}

Any monster might become the focus of a body horror plot. Know what your players anticipate so you can distort those expectations. A poised elf revealed to be a husk puppeted by sapient worms can prove as frightening as any eldritch horror. The Body Horror Monsters table presents monsters particularly appropriate to such adventures. Unless otherwise noted, creatures in this table appear in the [Monster Manual](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/mm-2024).

### Cosmic Horror {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:CosmicHorror}

[![(Artist: Ivan Shavrin)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/21-004.cosmic-horror.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/21-004.cosmic-horror.png)

Cosmic horror revolves around the fear of personal insignificance. The genre, inspired by stories of the Cthulhu Mythos, is predicated on the idea of entities so vast and so genuinely beyond our comprehension that we can’t fathom their simplest motivations. To see them is to become lost in their magnitude and the evidence that we have never and could never matter to the cosmos at large. Examples include _Annihilation_ and _Stalker._

#### Cosmic Horror Principles {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:CosmicHorrorPrinciples}

Consider the following principles when creating Darklords and domains with cosmic horror themes:

**Fear the Unknown.** Be vague. Cosmic horror emerges through imagination and the indescribable, not through details.

**Iconography.** Cults, forbidden books, and strange symbols form the cornerstones of cosmic horror.

**Inscrutable Forces.** Cosmic horror is about alien forces driven by motivations humans can’t understand. There is no good or evil, no law or chaos.

**Marginalization Isn’t Horror.** The genre has a history of framing marginalized demographics as monstrous and stigmatizing mental illness. Avoid those tropes.

**Remove the Familiar.** Cosmic horror makes characters feel gradually unmoored from reality.

#### Cosmic Horror Villains {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:CosmicHorrorVillains}

Despite the genre’s grand magnitude, villains of cosmic horror are still often individual beings. Godlike terrors and inscrutable forces might pull the strings with their unknowable goals, but the antagonists the characters face are concrete, fallible people.

##### Villain Identities {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:VillainIdentities}

Cosmic horror villains often perpetrate horrors as they strive for outcomes they can’t articulate. Choose from or roll on the Cosmic Horror Villains table to inspire villains appropriate to this genre.

**Cosmic Horror Villains**

| 1d10 | The Villain Is …                                                                        |
| ---- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1    | A smiling minstrel whose music drives listeners to murder.                              |
| 2    | A priest obsessed with creating a shelter safe from the coming apocalypse.              |
| 3    | A mayor who will do anything to ensure citizens finish a sacred transformation.         |
| 4    | An astronomer broken and enraptured by what they saw in the stars.                      |
| 5    | A scientist striving to make their body the perfect host for an ageless being.          |
| 6    | A coroner who believes the bodies they autopsy contain secret messages.                 |
| 7    | The head librarian of an ancient sect, who seeks secrets hidden within their peers.     |
| 8    | A spoiled noble who intends to raise a cult to feed to residents of an alien dimension. |
| 9    | A researcher knowingly incubating a powerful entity within themself.                    |
| 10   | A hierophant seeking a doorway to an alien realm to bring about a new world.            |

##### Villain Torments {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:VillainTorments}

Villains in this genre are endowed with unnatural powers stemming from their studies or granted by alien forces. Choose from or roll on the Cosmic Horror Torments table to determine what alien or psychological torment plagues the villain.

**Cosmic Horror Torments**

| 1d10 | The Villain …                                                               |
| ---- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1    | Is haunted by otherworldly masters that whisper from reflective surfaces.   |
| 2    | Sees multiple dimensions at once.                                           |
| 3    | Is transforming into a long-extinct being.                                  |
| 4    | Screams messages from the far-flung future.                                 |
| 5    | Absorbs the words out of books.                                             |
| 6    | Drains any object they focus on of all but one portentous color.            |
| 7    | Finds their body warped to match that of the last person they talked with.  |
| 8    | Incubates an alien symbiote in their brain.                                 |
| 9    | Sleepwalks, drawing the same symbol on every surface they come across.      |
| 10   | Obsesses over music, shifting their form to embody whatever song they hear. |

#### Cosmic Horror Adventures {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:CosmicHorrorAdventures}

Adventures in cosmic horror realms are bleak, desperate affairs, where the best one can hope for is to survive relatively intact. There is no stopping the ultimate evil, but characters might aspire to seal it away temporarily.

##### Adventure Hooks {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:AdventureHooks}

Cosmic horror adventures often deal with how alien forces might alter us, perverting our expectations and separating us from what makes us human. Choose from or roll on the Cosmic Horror Plots table to inspire your cosmic horror adventures.

**Cosmic Horror Plots**

| 1d10 | Adventure Hook                                                                                                            |
| ---- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1    | A child has gone missing in the impossibly vast space beneath their bed.                                                  |
| 2    | Something drags a coastal town’s inhabitants out in the night, garbs them in silver, and leads them to the surf to drown. |
| 3    | A wandering minstrel plays music that robs entire cities of sleep.                                                        |
| 4    | Local bakers have started making pies filled with a delicious, luminescent, alien, blue goo.                              |
| 5    | A sapient, unholy tome will do anything to reach a group of cultists.                                                     |
| 6    | The inheritors of an ancient sect are transforming into astral horrors.                                                   |
| 7    | Animals in the local forest have started going to a specific charred grove to die.                                        |
| 8    | Colossal statues surrounding the city move only during dusk and dawn.                                                     |
| 9    | The characters must survive an evening in a sinking ancestral home.                                                       |
| 10   | A new wing in the academy’s library has appeared, filled with blank books.                                                |

##### Adventure Settings {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:AdventureSettings}

Cosmic horror frequently takes place in settings that imply access to hidden knowledge or in unnatural, logic-defying dimensions far removed from reality. Choose from or roll on Cosmic Horror Settings table to inspire locations for your adventures.

**Cosmic Horror Settings**

| 1d10 | The Adventure Takes Place In …                                             |
| ---- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1    | A lavish manor devoid of people—save for staff who swear the lord is busy. |
| 2    | A narrow chapel in the woods, whose bell rings ceaselessly.                |
| 3    | A hidden ward of a decrepit university.                                    |
| 4    | A dimension of featureless white, broken up only by staring eyes.          |
| 5    | The ninth basement beneath an otherwise normal family home.                |
| 6    | A small inn in the mountains that smells perpetually of brine.             |
| 7    | An ambulatory forest riddled with carvings of unblinking eyes.             |
| 8    | A sewage system that predates its city.                                    |
| 9    | A coastline slowly being consumed by an obsidian sea.                      |
| 10   | A decrepit lighthouse whose light flickers on at strange intervals.        |

#### Cosmic Horror Monsters {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:CosmicHorrorMonsters}

Monsters in cosmic horror adventures are often strange beings that enact bizarre changes on their victims. The Cosmic Horror Monsters table presents monsters particularly appropriate to such adventures. Unless otherwise noted, creatures in this table appear in the [Monster Manual](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/mm-2024).

| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

### Dark Fantasy {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:DarkFantasy}

[![(Artist: Ivan Shavrin)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/21-005.dark-fantasy.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/21-005.dark-fantasy.png)

The dark fantasy genre features fantasy worlds where grim themes, nihilistic plots, or horrifying elements inform their stories. Any tale featuring both supernatural elements and horror themes might constitute dark fantasy, whether it’s a fantasy story steeped in dread or an otherwise realistic world that features a supernatural terror. Examples include _The Dark Tower_ and _Pan’s Labyrinth._

#### Dark Fantasy Principles {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:DarkFantasyPrinciples}

Consider the following principles when creating Darklords and domains with dark fantasy themes:

**Evil Sometimes Triumphs.** Good doesn’t always win. Evil individuals with great power and unopposed schemes might prosper.

**Low Magic.** Magic and magic items might be rarer or require a bargain or sacrifice to use.

**Morally Gray.** The lines between good and evil are blurred. Choices involve deciding on the least bad outcome available.

**Nefarious Deeds.** Corruption and suspicion flourish among organizations and individuals.

**Reluctant Heroes.** Antiheroes are common—characters tainted by the world’s evil or those who refuse to be considered heroes.

#### Dark Fantasy Villains {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:DarkFantasyVillains}

Sinister individuals leave their marks on dark fantasy domains, whether with oppressive architecture, unavoidable propaganda, or scars on an exploited environment.

##### Villain Identities {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:VillainIdentities}

Villains occupy places of influence in dark fantasy domains. Choose from or roll on the Dark Fantasy Villains table to inspire villains appropriate to this genre.

**Dark Fantasy Villains**

| 1d10 | The Villain Is …                                                                   |
| ---- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1    | A machine that believes it’s a resurrected tyrant and seeks to rebuild its empire. |
| 2    | The leader of a subterranean people who plots to blot out the sun’s searing light. |
| 3    | A high priest intent on shifting an entire nation into their god’s realm.          |
| 4    | A desperate general who unleashes otherworldly war machines.                       |
| 5    | A massive treant who has allied with raiders and seeks to fell every forest.       |
| 6    | A sage who solves an endless war by preventing anyone from dying.                  |
| 7    | An eternal royal whose immortality relies on the blood of angels.                  |
| 8    | A criminal kingpin who burns opponents into psychoactive spirit dust.              |
| 9    | An ancient dragon whose godlike magic drains the domain of life.                   |
| 10   | A god who killed all their peers and now rules the mortal realm.                   |

##### Villain Torments {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:VillainTorments}

In dark fantasy adventures, a villain’s power is often rooted in the villain’s own suffering. Choose from or roll on the Dark Fantasy Torments table to determine how this power tragically works against the villain.

**Dark Fantasy Torments**

| 1d10 | The Villain …                                                                      |
| ---- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1    | Uncontrollably damages everything they care about.                                 |
| 2    | Manufactures catastrophes to distract from their own ineptitude.                   |
| 3    | Is surrounded by power-hungry spies and saboteurs, fueling the villain’s paranoia. |
| 4    | Seeks the pleasure of lost glories.                                                |
| 5    | Is surrounded by sycophants whose constant praise makes every success feel hollow. |
| 6    | Is plagued by a cursed family legacy.                                              |
| 7    | Is hounded by rivals and baseless mockery.                                         |
| 8    | Must sacrifice those they love to maintain their facade of power.                  |
| 9    | Is praised by society for a deed they never truly accomplished.                    |
| 10   | Elicits excessive fear and reverence, resulting in their isolation.                |

#### Dark Fantasy Adventures {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:DarkFantasyAdventures}

Adventures in dark fantasy domains involve desperate or reluctant heroes resisting evil. Even in the grimmest settings, desperation and hope fan the flames of resistance.

##### Adventure Hooks {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:AdventureHooks}

Plots in dark fantasy adventures range from street-level depravity to world-ruining conspiracies. Choose from or roll on the Dark Fantasy Plots table to inspire your dark fantasy adventures.

**Dark Fantasy Plots**

| 1d10 | Adventure Hook                                                                             |
| ---- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| 1    | A beholder-shaped statue has come to life and begun terrorizing the city.                  |
| 2    | A portal to a demonic realm has opened in the mouth of an innocent acolyte.                |
| 3    | A sapient virus is turning the inhabitants of a village into shadows.                      |
| 4    | Giant spiders have declared war on all bipedal creatures.                                  |
| 5    | A coven plans to use a volcano as a massive cauldron for a catastrophic spell.             |
| 6    | The nation’s beloved monarch was recently revealed to be a lich.                           |
| 7    | A malevolent phantom haunts the moon, raising corpses bathed in its light as undead.       |
| 8    | A sentient weapon transforms its surroundings into a mockery of the war it last fought in. |
| 9    | A factory distills souls into a powerful wish-granting elixir.                             |
| 10   | An expanding labyrinth has just swallowed another neighborhood.                            |

##### Adventure Settings {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:AdventureSettings}

Evil is entrenched in dark fantasy domains, reflected by their grandiose adventure locales. Choose from or roll on the Dark Fantasy Settings table to inspire locations for your adventures.

**Dark Fantasy Settings**

| 1d10 | The Adventure Takes Place In …                                              |
| ---- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1    | The floating and fallen ruins of a magical megastructure.                   |
| 2    | A blood-soaked swamp.                                                       |
| 3    | A tower that pierces a magical ley line, draining its power.                |
| 4    | A criminal consortium’s lavish academy.                                     |
| 5    | A forest where every tree grows from the body of a mummified hero.          |
| 6    | An empire covered in the watchful religious symbols of an all-seeing deity. |
| 7    | A fortress with seven locked gates that seal off the underworld.            |
| 8    | A country devastated by the fallout of weapons used in an age-old war.      |
| 9    | A town threatened by an unstoppable, slowly encroaching infection.          |
| 10   | A city adrift on a sea full of primeval predators.                          |

#### Dark Fantasy Monsters {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:DarkFantasyMonsters}

Any monster can find a place in a dark fantasy plot. D&D’s most iconic threats—such as dragons and beholders—are particularly appropriate to horror-tinged tales, as are any other supernatural foes. The Dark Fantasy Monsters table presents monsters particularly appropriate to such adventures. Unless otherwise noted, creatures in this table appear in the [Monster Manual](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/mm-2024).

### Folk Horror {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:FolkHorror}

[![(Artist: Ivan Shavrin)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/21-006.folk-horror.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/21-006.folk-horror.png)

Folk horror adventures involve traditions, beliefs, and perceptions that are passed down through generations and take terrifying twists. For those who ascribe to hidden traditions, sacrifices to strange gods or placations to lurking monsters are everyday events. For outsiders, though, these practices reveal the subjectivity of normalcy and societal truth. Examples include _Midsommar and The Wicker Man._

#### Folk Horror Principles {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:FolkHorrorPrinciples}

Consider the following principles when creating Darklords and domains with folk horror themes:

**Isolation Begets Weirdness.** Strange and potentially dangerous traditions flourish in isolated or private communities.

**Perversion of Community.** Communities in folk horror stories often are a grim mirror of an aspect of accepted society. They often dramatically use outsiders or purge nonbelievers.

**Relative Truth.** Beliefs highlighted in folk horror stories might not be true.

**Secret Traditions.** Community members typically hide their beliefs, perhaps by physically obscuring them or manipulating others in power.

**Strangeness in Specificity.** Art, symbols, tools, celebrations, and other trappings of belief make a community’s traditions more specific and eerie.

#### Folk Horror Villains {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:FolkHorrorVillains}

Antagonistic forces in folk horror usually are community leaders—paragons of the strange beliefs central to the horror’s narrative. Outsiders might have a chance to adopt the community’s ways, but otherwise locals consider them heretics or corrupting elements.

##### Villain Identities {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:VillainIdentities}

Folk horror villains are manipulative, leading others to follow inscrutable traditions. Choose from or roll on the Folk Horror Villains table to inspire villains appropriate to this genre.

**Folk Horror Villains**

| 1d10 | The Villain Is …                                                                 |
| ---- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1    | A secluded temple’s high priest who needs to find the perfect sacrifice.         |
| 2    | An erinyes that appears when youngsters speak a rhyme into a darkened mirror.    |
| 3    | A night hag that dwells in the dreams of those who drink a special ergot tea.    |
| 4    | A shape-shifter that takes on the appearance of the last person it fed on.       |
| 5    | A wicker giant that animates during the new moon, punishing the unwary.          |
| 6    | A mayor who behaves in archaic ways so villagers don’t enrage an ancient ghost.  |
| 7    | A treant who demands corpses to replace trees cleared by a town’s construction.  |
| 8    | A mysterious robed figure who wears a horned mask and leads a silent cult.       |
| 9    | A bloodthirsty forest guardian that resembles a deer with two heads.             |
| 10   | A shadow that appears only when individuals look away from the woods’ tree line. |

##### Villain Torments {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:VillainTorments}

Folk horror villains have been consumed by the traditions or land they embody, causing them to fail in their duties or their rites to spin out of control. Choose from or roll on the Folk Horror Torments to determine how these twisted traditions torment the villain.

**Folk Horror Torments**

| 1d10 | The Villain …                                                                        |
| ---- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| 1    | Knows the beliefs are false but keeps up the facade to maintain power.               |
| 2    | Adheres to an ancient faith and desperately works to convert nonbelievers.           |
| 3    | Seeks to transform their body into a vessel or gate for the subject of their belief. |
| 4    | Now appears as a bloodthirsty amalgamation of various forest creatures.              |
| 5    | Uncontrollably utters prophecies.                                                    |
| 6    | Is haunted by judgmental ancestral spirits.                                          |
| 7    | Can appear only at dawn and dusk.                                                    |
| 8    | Has partially melded into a hallowed tree.                                           |
| 9    | Is being consumed by fungi.                                                          |
| 10   | Can no longer commune with their deity, driving them to ever bloodier sacrifices.    |

#### Folk Horror Adventures {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:FolkHorrorAdventures}

In folk horror tales, characters often discover that their beliefs aren’t as universally held as they assumed—and provide no defense against those who reject those beliefs.

##### Adventure Hooks {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:AdventureHooks}

Folk horror plots often involve outsiders to a group discovering unsettling practices or traditions. Choose from or roll on the Folk Horror Plots to inspire your folk horror adventures.

**Folk Horror Plots**

| 1d10 | Adventure Hook                                                                         |
| ---- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1    | Anyone entering the city on horseback is imprisoned and sentenced to death.            |
| 2    | A cult requests help summoning a demonic force to combat a greater evil.               |
| 3    | The townspeople protect a violent hag, whom they call “grandmother.”                   |
| 4    | After an estate party, the residents adopt the characters, refusing to let them leave. |
| 5    | The characters bear an uncanny resemblance to the founders of a secret village.        |
| 6    | Townsfolk disappear for days before reappearing with missing memories.                 |
| 7    | Strangers hand out wax earplugs to protect others from “the choir.”                    |
| 8    | Every night, parents let their children follow floating lights into the forest.        |
| 9    | Villagers physically can’t stop smiling.                                               |
| 10   | Anyone who stays in the village overnight loses their shadow to the looming woods.     |

##### Adventure Settings {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:AdventureSettings}

Folk horror stories often take place in isolated or rural areas, but they could be set anywhere insular communities thrive or traditions stagnate. Choose from or roll on the Folk Horror Settings to inspire locations for your adventures.

**Folk Horror Settings**

| 1d10 | The Adventure Takes Place In …                                                      |
| ---- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1    | A copse of dense, blackened woods.                                                  |
| 2    | A mansion built around a stone circle.                                              |
| 3    | A field where paths grow in corridor-like patterns leading to a ruin at the center. |
| 4    | A telepathic collective that townsfolk join by ingesting a rare fungus.             |
| 5    | A hag’s hut that stands atop a growing hill of rotten sweets.                       |
| 6    | A glacier that residents never leave.                                               |
| 7    | A cavern where the glowing bones of an otherworldly being jut from the walls.       |
| 8    | A countryside with stretches of hayfields and colorful barns.                       |
| 9    | Rival villages engaged in an age-old war.                                           |
| 10   | A deserted chapel that has been burned down and rebuilt a thousand times.           |

#### Folk Horror Monsters {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:FolkHorrorMonsters}

Eerie traditions and unnatural alliances with monsters fill folk horror tales. When certain behaviors have taken hold over generations, even the strangest practices and most dangerous beings might be accepted as part of society. The Folk Horror Monsters table presents monsters particularly appropriate to such adventures. Unless otherwise noted, creatures in this table appear in the [Monster Manual](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/mm-2024).
