### Ghost Stories {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:GhostStories}

[![(Artist: Ivan Shavrin)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/21-007.ghost-stories.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/21-007.ghost-stories.png)

Ghost stories number among the more psychologically elaborate genres of horror. Only by revealing tales of tragedy and past wrongs can heroes bring peace to forces that share their suffering with the living. Examples include _The Woman in Black_ and _The Haunting of Hill House._

#### Ghost Story Principles {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:GhostStoryPrinciples}

Consider the following principles when creating Darklords and domains inspired by ghost stories:

**Mirror of Humanity.** Ghosts are a way to examine the nature of the soul, mortality, and history.

**Naive Heroes.** Heroes are purehearted or unsuspecting individuals whose resolve is shaken by the story’s events. Look for ways to test heroes’ psychology with your hauntings.

**Resolving a Haunt.** Heroes need a way to put spirits to rest. Once you reveal the story, ensure the way to combat the haunting is clear.

**Specificity.** Even the smallest details can reveal a haunting’s story. A simple locket or portrait might contain clues that explain a haunting.

**Ties to the Living.** Personal ties give ghost stories weight. Consider connecting the heroes to spirits in ways they won’t predict, such as making a phantasmal villain a hero’s ancestor.

#### Ghost Story Villains {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:GhostStoryVillains}

In ghost stories, spirits often represent instruments of supernatural justice, causing those responsible for their deaths to suffer. Spirits also can represent grief and the need for closure.

##### Villain Identities {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:VillainIdentities}

While the villains in ghost stories are often spirits or haunted places, they also could be the individuals who provoked a haunting to begin with. Choose from or roll on the Ghost Story Villains table to inspire villains appropriate to this genre.

**Ghost Story Villains**

| 1d10 | The Villain Is …                                                                             |
| ---- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1    | A medium who gains power over spirits by feeding victims to them.                            |
| 2    | The spirit of a long-dead murderer who continues to kill in death.                           |
| 3    | A ghostly ancestor who refuses to relinquish control of their kin.                           |
| 4    | A priest who marks the unworthy for sacrifice to the cathedral’s hungry spirits              |
| 5    | A phantom rider who sweeps through the village, stealing away the living.                    |
| 6    | An unbound spirit that repeatedly manifests in victims’ nightmares.                          |
| 7    | The capricious phantasm of an amoral accident victim who torments the living.                |
| 8    | The spirit of a former tyrant who demands sacrifices from their old domain.                  |
| 9    | A ghost hunter who inflicts hauntings on clients—then charges to remove the spirits.         |
| 10   | The spirit of an evil captain who lurks near their wrecked vessel, sabotaging passing ships. |

##### Villain Torments {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:VillainTorments}

Whether they’re living monsters or ghosts, villains in ghost stories are the architects of their own tragedies. Choose from or roll on the Ghost Story Torments table to determine how the villain’s past painfully manifests.

**Ghost Story Torments**

| 1d10 | The Villain …                                                                        |
| ---- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| 1    | Can’t touch anyone without stealing a precious memory.                               |
| 2    | Can temporarily release spirits from the villain’s elaborate scars.                  |
| 3    | Is hounded by spirits that each represent an emotion the villain can no longer feel. |
| 4    | Drains the life from any animal they see.                                            |
| 5    | Has lost the ability to feel physical sensation.                                     |
| 6    | Can be seen only in reflective surfaces.                                             |
| 7    | Is bound within a building; leaving would permanently destroy them.                  |
| 8    | Turns to ash in sunlight.                                                            |
| 9    | Can communicate only through music and writing.                                      |
| 10   | Siphons the color from objects they possess.                                         |

#### Ghost Story Adventures {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:GhostStoryAdventures}

Ghost story adventures deal with learning the story behind a haunting and ultimately resolving it. They benefit from preserving the mystery behind a spirit’s motivations until the heroes discover the truth.

##### Adventure Hooks {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:AdventureHooks}

Though the structure—learn about a haunting and resolve it—might seem straightforward, ghost story plots can explore philosophical issues like the burden of ancestry and the nature of the soul. Choose from or roll on the Ghost Story Plots table to inspire your ghost stories.

**Ghost Story Plots**

| 1d10 | Adventure Hook                                                                        |
| ---- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1    | Murder victims linger as ghosts until someone solves their murders.                   |
| 2    | Bloody graffiti keeps appearing on the city’s walls.                                  |
| 3    | A stubborn miser must visit their haunted family home to put their family to rest.    |
| 4    | A mob of angry spirits besieges the local temple on the winter solstice each year.    |
| 5    | The adventurers must solve the murder of a ghost who can say only three words.        |
| 6    | A ship—with the same name as a vessel lost at sea decades prior—arrives at port.      |
| 7    | Rumors abound of a ritual allowing a living individual to trade places with the dead. |
| 8    | The ghosts of an actor’s rivals haunt the local theater.                              |
| 9    | A noble accidentally broke a family urn, unleashing their cruel ancestral spirits.    |
| 10   | Every full moon, spirits in a graveyard rise to seek vengeance for a mass crime.      |

##### Adventure Settings {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:AdventureSettings}

Ghost stories are intensely personal, and adventures within this genre take place in a setting dripping with tragic history. Choose from or roll on the Ghost Story Settings table to inspire locations for your adventures.

**Ghost Story Settings**

| 1d10 | The Adventure Takes Place In …                                                      |
| ---- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1    | A decrepit mansion where, for years, nobles killed the staff to keep their secrets. |
| 2    | A graveyard city-state where all living residents are grave keepers.                |
| 3    | An opulent yet abandoned library, filled with haunted artifacts.                    |
| 4    | The site of an ancient battle that permanently devastated the land.                 |
| 5    | A nation where the residents observe grueling rituals to appease the angry dead.    |
| 6    | An expansive forest in which a cruel noble once hunted the poor for sport.          |
| 7    | A ruined barn where dozens of remarkable animals lost their lives in a fire.        |
| 8    | A picturesque cliff where visiting couples often mysteriously fall to their deaths. |
| 9    | An attic in which a hateful spirit has been sealed for decades.                     |
| 10   | A dilapidated lighthouse overlooking a black-sand beach.                            |

#### Ghost Story Monsters {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:GhostStoryMonsters}

Creatures that embody or serve as a response to past tragedies often feature in ghost stories. Don’t limit yourself to incorporeal Undead when creating your own hauntings. The Ghost Story Monsters table presents monsters particularly appropriate to such adventures. ### Gothic Horror {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:GothicHorror}

[![(Artist: Ivan Shavrin)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/21-008.gothic-horror.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/21-008.gothic-horror.png)

Gothic horror deals with the terror within. It shatters the illusion of humanity by holding a mirror up to us and forcing us to examine what we truly are and what we pretend to be. In gothic horror, we—not some distant entity—are the architects of our destruction. Examples include _Dracula_ and _Frankenstein._

#### Gothic Horror Principles {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:GothicHorrorPrinciples}

Consider the following principles when creating Darklords and domains with gothic horror themes:

**Brave Heroes.** Gothic heroes are often virtuous, deeply passionate, or courageous. Adventures should test characters’ beliefs and morality.

**Foreboding.** Atmosphere and a sense of dread are key. Locations are often decrepit or foreboding.

**High Emotions.** Gothic stories include intense, exaggerated emotions. Romances, rivalries, and life-changing events are common.

**Sacrifice.** Sacrifices feature prominently in gothic stories. Give characters heart-wrenching choices.

**Unassuming, Unrepentant Villains.** Gothic villains are unrepentantly evil, but this shouldn’t be immediately obvious. Drop hints about your villain’s awful secrets before revealing them fully.

#### Gothic Horror Villains {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:GothicHorrorVillains}

Though thoroughly wicked, villains in gothic horror tales act reserved or unassuming until they reveal their true nature. Any intriguing figure with a dark secret can serve as a gothic horror villain.

##### Villain Identities {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:VillainIdentities}

Gothic villains are most effective when they are slowly revealed as shockingly cruel, immoral, or the antithesis of good. Choose from or roll on the Gothic Horror Villains table to inspire villains appropriate to this genre.

**Gothic Horror Villains**

| 1d10 | The Villain Is …                                                                 |
| ---- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1    | A reclusive noble who uses their vampiric reputation to terrorize their vassals. |
| 2    | A vain socialite who made a bargain with a fell power to retain their youth.     |
| 3    | A scientist obsessed with creating the perfect poison, machine, or life-form.    |
| 4    | A beloved magnate who abducts commoners to use in beauty rituals.                |
| 5    | A celebrity who murders openly but uses their charm to avoid repercussions.      |
| 6    | Someone who loves a monstrous creature and does anything to keep it safe.        |
| 7    | A wealthy heir who manipulates the ambitious into committing terrible deeds.     |
| 8    | A poisoner who seeks to manipulate history through targeted killings.            |
| 9    | An artist who concocts terrible accidents to inspire their art.                  |
| 10   | A monster hunter who accuses those they consider sinful of being monsters.       |

##### Villain Torments {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:VillainTorments}

Self-debasement and self-loathing lurk at the heart of gothic villains’ evil, whether they indulge in vices or are consumed with misanthropy. Choose from or roll on the Gothic Horror Torments table to determine how temptation and dramatic emotions torment the villain.

**Gothic Horror Torments**

| 1d10 | The Villain …                                                                   |
| ---- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1    | Inherited unlimited wealth, but all finery they wear turns into ash.            |
| 2    | Endlessly cries tears of blood.                                                 |
| 3    | Is covered in tattoos, which magically update to illustrate all their sins.     |
| 4    | Turns into a lead statue when the sun rises.                                    |
| 5    | Is incomparably beautiful, but locals perceive them as a beast.                 |
| 6    | Sees evidence of their impending doom everywhere.                               |
| 7    | Extinguishes any light shone on them.                                           |
| 8    | Can’t taste food.                                                               |
| 9    | Curses anyone they dance with.                                                  |
| 10   | Craves company but is cursed to forever wear a mask and obscure their identity. |

#### Gothic Horror Adventures {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:GothicHorrorAdventures}

The themes of gothic horror adventures center around shattering the lies we trick ourselves into believing. Ominous history, poetic tragedy, and supernatural forces are staples of gothic horror.

##### Adventure Hooks {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:AdventureHooks}

The dichotomy between goodness and evil, reckonings for wicked deeds, and dire choices are strong themes in gothic horror plots. Choose from or roll on the Gothic Horror Plots table to inspire your gothic horror adventures.

**Gothic Horror Plots**

| 1d10 | Adventure Hook                                                                          |
| ---- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1    | The city’s rulers secretly are warring hags, wererats, and vampires.                    |
| 2    | A scientist, never seen and known only through their writing, has disappeared.          |
| 3    | A repentant immortal requests help in losing centuries of painful memories.             |
| 4    | A beloved social figure turns into a murderous living doll every night.                 |
| 5    | A pair of spirits brings unspeakable tragedy to any romantic couple in town.            |
| 6    | A generational curse forces villagers to sacrifice themselves.                          |
| 7    | Every night, one random guest of an opulent inn chokes on their own blood.              |
| 8    | A serial killer impales victims on a certain monument in a cruel mockery of art.        |
| 9    | Terrible noises sound from a dilapidated mansion; those who visit are never seen again. |
| 10   | As the result of abhorrent experiments, blood-drained creatures roam the streets.       |

##### Adventure Settings {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:AdventureSettings}

Gothic horror settings have an underlying sinister air, and encounters often take place in forlorn structures where depravity runs rampant. Choose from or roll on the Gothic Horror Settings table to inspire locations for your adventures.

**Gothic Horror Settings**

| 1d10 | The Adventure Takes Place In …                                                         |
| ---- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1    | A lavish garden that siphons life from visitors to maintain its beauty.                |
| 2    | A ruined cathedral devoted to transforming a prophesied being.                         |
| 3    | A laboratory where preserved body parts carry the minds of their former owners.        |
| 4    | A forest of eternal night where bloodthirsty creatures live in fragile peace.          |
| 5    | A rectory where the stained glass windows hold the trapped souls of the pious.         |
| 6    | A city where all who die are cast in plaster and used to adorn the streets.            |
| 7    | An island where the inhabitants make sacrifices to avoid eerie transformations.        |
| 8    | An artist’s paradise where cruelties are elevated to terrible and beautiful art forms. |
| 9    | A castle in which visitors are transformed into objects or animals.                    |
| 10   | A ruined fortress haunted by a monstrous yet docile creature.                          |

#### Gothic Horror Monsters {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:GothicHorrorMonsters}

Creatures imbued with tragedy or abominable origins work well in gothic horror adventures. The Gothic Horror Monsters table presents monsters particularly appropriate to such adventures. ### Disaster Horror {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:DisasterHorror}

[![(Artist: Ivan Shavrin)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/21-009.disaster-horror.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/21-009.disaster-horror.png)

In disaster horror, the world has fallen to ruin or it’s getting there fast. The unthinkable has happened, and society is collapsing. In these tales, you might replace a monster or villain with cascading catastrophes like those brought about by a meteorite strike or volcanic eruption. Regardless of a hero’s power, the best-timed strike or the most powerful spell might not fix a city ruined by an earthquake or a world ravaged by plagues.

#### Disaster Horror Features {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:DisasterHorrorFeatures}

Consider the following principles when creating adventures with disaster horror themes:

**Nature of Disaster.** The disasters in your horror adventures need not be natural. Magical disruptions, temporal shifts, and violent interplanar rifts might sow supernatural chaos. Wars and relentless monster hordes—including legions of zombies or demons—also can cause domain-changing ruin.

**Society’s Downfall.** In disaster horror, society breaks down. Inns are closed, healers are few or overtaxed, and anarchy rises as governments crumble.

**What It Takes to Survive.** Scared innocents, opportunistic scavengers, and leaderless institutions (military or otherwise) seek to survive. The hopeless acts of others might prove more horrifying than the disaster.

---

### Occult Detective Stories {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:OccultDetectiveStories}

[![(Artist: Ivan Shavrin)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/21-010.occult-detective-stories.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/21-010.occult-detective-stories.png)

Occult detective stories straddle the line between fantasy, mystery, and horror. For the occult detective, solving paranormal mysteries is part of the job. In these adventures, supernatural criminals or monsters pursue nefarious ends while the characters act as detectives: interpreting events, seeking patterns, deducing goals, and ultimately putting an end to the threat. Investigation and cleverness take center stage in these adventures, although—as in the noir stories that inspire the genre—there’s plenty of room for action.

#### Occult Detective Story Features {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:OccultDetectiveStoryFeatures}

Consider the following principles when creating adventures with occult detective themes:

**Lighter Frights.** Occult detective adventures can be just as terrifying as other horror adventures but might be lighter in tone. Adventurers might encounter the results of horrific deeds rather than experiencing them firsthand and might face a foe only once they’re prepared.

**Supernatural Twists.** Consider how monsters, magic, or other supernatural forces might lend a thrilling twist to criminal enterprises. How will the characters catch an invisible assassin or a thief who pilfers extradimensional spaces?

**Threading Hints.** Once you know the villain’s mode of operation, consider how the villain might give themself away. Even if you’re not sure, listen to the characters’ plans and give them opportunities to feel brilliant in the course of their investigations.

---

### Psychological Horror {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:PsychologicalHorror}

[![(Artist: Ivan Shavrin)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/21-011.psychological-horror.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/21-011.psychological-horror.png)

Psychological horror stories create suspense by heightening or calling into question characters’ states of mind, emotions, and perceptions. These tales often highlight the difference between what characters think and how they behave.

#### Psychological Horror Features {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:PsychologicalHorrorFeatures}

Consider the following principles when creating adventures with psychological horror themes:

**Fears as Metaphors.** Common anxieties and fears can become metaphors for antagonists in psychological horror. Fear of judgment by one’s peers might manifest as a jury of nothics, while fear of change could be represented by a medusa that petrifies those who threaten the status quo.

**Mental Illness Isn’t Horror.** Some classic psychological horror tales stigmatize mental illness. Avoid this trope in your adventures.

**Unreliable Information.** Uncertainty and paranoia shape psychological horror stories. Characters might experience a deadly encounter only to wake up at the end, not having realized they were asleep. Before undermining characters’ senses, identify what’s driving these skewed perceptions and how characters might overcome them.

---

### Slasher Horror {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:SlasherHorror}

[![(Artist: Ivan Shavrin)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/21-012.slasher-horror.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/21-012.slasher-horror.png)

Slasher horror contends with relentless killers, which might be people or monsters. These adventures revel in grisly details, the suspense of an impending showdown with a powerful foe, and the fear that death waits right around the corner.

#### Slasher Horror Features {#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:SlasherHorrorFeatures}

Consider the following principles when creating adventures with slasher horror themes:

**Solo Antagonist.** Slasher horror stories typically include one major antagonist that threatens a group. This might be a particularly large or cunning beast, a murderer who terrorizes a neighborhood, a monster stalking a town, or a supernatural menace that spreads a signature cause of death.

**Targets.** Consider who the villain’s targets are and why the villain is preying on that group. Is it out of hunger or for revenge, or does the creature have a deep-seated need to kill?

**Violence and Infamy.** Antagonists in slasher horror are often infamous, akin to urban legends, with numerous victims. Consider how the killer avoids capture and what makes the killer’s actions warrant their infamy.

</CHAPTER>

<CHAPTER id="rthw:denizens-of-the-mists" title="Denizens Of The Mists">

# Chapter 5: Denizens of the Mists {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:Chapter5DenizensoftheMists}

## Chapter 5 Denizens of the Mists {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:Chapter5DenizensoftheMists}

[![A grim dullahan strikes down its victim, claiming another grisly death’s head as a follower (Artist: Sean A. Murray)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/22-001.grim-dullahan.jpg)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/22-001.grim-dullahan.jpg)

Terrors haunt the Mists. This chapter begins with advice to help you, the DM, use monsters to create frightful encounters. Following this is a collection of horrifying monsters and stalwart monster hunters for your adventures in the Domains of Dread.

## Horror Monsters {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:HorrorMonsters}

Cultivating mystery and menace around the monstrous foes in your adventures can be a simple matter. Here are techniques you can use to transform any monster into a horror to haunt characters’ nightmares.

### Monstrous Origins {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:MonstrousOrigins}

Unique monsters are singularly terrifying. Consider presenting the monster central to your adventures as a one-of-a-kind terror. Such a creature might be a fluke of nature, the product of insidious magic, a purposefully terrifying creation of the Dark Powers, or a being with an even more unsettling background. Use the tips for creating Darklords and drawing inspiration from different genres of horror in [chapter 4](#rthw:creating-domains-of-dread:GenresofHorror "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/creating-domains-of-dread#GenresofHorror") to create unique origins for the most important threats in your adventures.

Different origin stories suggest diverse paths for adventurers to follow when investigating these creatures, learning their weaknesses, and ensuring nothing like them ever menaces again.

### Terrifying Language {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:TerrifyingLanguage}

Describe monsters in vivid ways. A terror chasing characters could just “follow” them, but instead it might “wriggle,” “surge,” or “galumph” after them. Descriptive language underscores how a creature behaves and conjures a visceral description of the monster. Unexpected descriptions can emphasize a creature’s bizarre nature and unsettle the players. For example, it’s one thing to say a snake “slithers,” but another to say a sinister shadow or cruel witch does.

Use unsettling descriptions and similes. For example, a vine blight’s constricting vines might resemble “noose-like cords” or “oily digits.” Try less literal descriptions—even nonsensical ones. For example, a flesh golem might howl like “an earthquake in a mortuary” or “a charnel pit that’s learned to sob.”

### Notorious Monsters {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:NotoriousMonsters}

Treat creatures central to your horror adventures as infamous threats. The more you foreshadow their menace or reveal that they have threatened others before, the larger such creatures loom. Build dread by giving monsters reputations that suggest the monsters’ form, deeds, or peculiarities while letting players’ imaginations embellish details.

For example, tales might describe a skeletal horror that whistles cheerfully while committing brutal acts. Characters might hear rumors of the Whistling Fiend’s melodies becoming haunting earworms for survivors of the fiend’s attacks. A party seeking the monster might hear it whistling in the Mists long before they confront it. All that time, characters can speculate about their enemy’s nature, but ultimately the Whistling Fiend might be any threat you choose.

### Mysterious Monsters {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:MysteriousMonsters}

Use conflicting descriptions and strange behaviors to cultivate mystery around your monster. The less characters know about a creature, the more they’ll speculate about terrifying possibilities.

You can develop uncertainty about a creature even after it appears. Keep players guessing about an adventure’s threat by referring to a monster by a flavorful description rather than the name of its stat block. A “zombie” doesn’t sound like much of a threat, but a “stumbling mass of fetid skin and shattered bones” might be something else entirely.

### Weird Traits {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:WeirdTraits}

By adding unexpected traits to monster stat blocks, you can undermine players’ expectations of what a monster is and what it can do. Consider how you can use the [Creature Traits](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/dmg-2024/dms-toolbox#creaturetraits) list in the “[Creating a Creature](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/dmg-2024/dms-toolbox#creatingacreature)” section of the [Dungeon Master’s Guide](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/dmg-2024) to give familiar monsters horrifying twists.

### Putting It All Together {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:PuttingItAllTogether}

Combine the techniques in this section to create a unique terror. If you have ideas about what you want your monster to do, write them down. Then develop stories that connect those pieces or reinforce the type of horror you want to create.

[![A zombie beholder’s terror is transformed when the monster is recast as a flesh-stitched horror (Artist: Helge C. Balzer)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/22-002.zombie-beholder.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/22-002.zombie-beholder.png)

For example, perhaps you’ve got an idea for an arrogant mage who sought to prove he didn’t need his adventuring companions’ protection by constructing a suit of living armor. Considering the bizarre, magical whims of such a character, you choose a [**Zombie Beholder**](#ref:monster:5194922-beholder-zombie "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5194922-beholder-zombie") as the foundation for the mage’s animate armor. To reinforce its nature as a magical creation, you change the monster’s creature type from Undead to Construct and describe it as being made of stitched-together animal parts. Then you give it the Berserk and Magic Resistance traits of a [**Flesh Golem**](#ref:monster:5194997-flesh-golem "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5194997-flesh-golem"). The characters’ surprise at unexpectedly facing a beholder might be startling enough, but you add to your story that the mage has become trapped within his living armor as it hunts his former companions. Only by defeating the horror might the characters free what remains of the mage within, represented by the Emissary of Juiblex creature trait from the “[Creating a Creature](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/dmg-2024/dms-toolbox#creatingacreature)” section of the [Dungeon Master’s Guide](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/dmg-2024).

### Bodytaker Plants {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:BodytakerPlants}

Body-Snatching Alien Flora

**Habitat:** Forest, Grassland, Hill, Swamp; **Treasure:** Any

Bodytaker plants are intelligent organisms that originated on a long-ruined planet of the Material Plane. To outlive their doomed world, these enigmatic plants spread their seeds to the stars. In rare cases, their meteorite-like seeds fall to fertile worlds and take root. What emerges is a new bodytaker plant that seeks to grow and propagate until its kind dominates the entire world. As assistants, the plant creates eerie vegetative duplicates of the world’s inhabitants called bodytaker podlings. Podlings serve the bodytaker plants’ will, infiltrating societies and replacing the individuals they resemble. Ultimately, podlings seek to isolate inhabitants so they can become fertilizer for the bodytaker plant that created them or fodder for more podlings.

#### Bodytaker Podling {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:BodytakerPodling}

A bodytaker podling is a near-perfect replica of a creature consumed by a bodytaker plant. A podling possesses the appearance and memories of the being it duplicates, but it is entirely loyal to the bodytaker plant that created it. Fundamentally, a podling isn’t its own creature but an expendable appendage of a bodytaker plant.

Bodytaker podlings frequently exhibit behaviors that suggest their true nature. Most often, they miss the nuances of social interactions. Some might talk in a stilted, jerky cadence or refer to themselves in the third person. Close friends and family members of those replaced by a podling might realize that their loved one has changed, but few imagine the cause behind such a dramatic shift. A podling might try to avoid suspicion by claiming to be ill or redirect doubt by insisting others are behaving oddly. If confronted with evidence of its plant nature, or if caught tending to a bodytaker plant, the podling throws itself into battle and fights to the death.

Roll on or choose a result from the Podling Behaviors table to inspire the unusual habits a podling might demonstrate.

**Podling Behaviors**

| 1d6 | The Podling Exhibits the Strange Habit Of … |
| --- | ------------------------------------------- |
| 1   | Drinking water from dirty troughs.          |
| 2   | Eating one type of food for all meals.      |
| 3   | Excessive and unabashed sunbathing.         |
| 4   | Forgoing shoes to feel the dirt.            |
| 5   | Pausing and listening to unheard sounds.    |
| 6   | Whispering to flowers and houseplants.      |

[![A new bodytaker podling emerges from a bodytaker plant (Artist: Antonio José Manzanedo)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/22-004.bodytaker-podling-and-plant.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/22-004.bodytaker-podling-and-plant.png)

##### [Bodytaker Podling](#ref:monster:6491342-bodytaker-podling "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491342-bodytaker-podling") {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:BodytakerPodlingrefmonster6491342bodytakerpodlinghttpswwwdndbeyondcommonsters6491342bodytakerpodling}

Medium or Small Plant, Neutral Evil

**AC** 12 **Initiative** +0 (10)

**HP** 26 (4d8 + 8)

**Speed** 30 ft.

**STR** 16 (+3) | **DEX** 11 (+0) | **CON** 14 (+2) | **INT** 10 (+0) | **WIS** 10 (+0) | **CHA** 10 (+0)

**Skills** [**Deception**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#skills) +4

**Immunities** [**Charmed**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#charmedcondition), [**Frightened**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#frightenedcondition)

**Senses** [**Blindsight**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#blindsight) 30 ft.; Passive Perception 10

**Languages** Deep Speech plus one other language

**CR** 1/2 (XP 100; PB +2)

#### Traits {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:Traits}

**_Semblance of Life._** The podling is a physical copy of a creature digested by a [**Bodytaker Plant**](#ref:monster:6491341-bodytaker-plant "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491341-bodytaker-plant"). The podling has [**Advantage**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#advantage) on Charisma ([**Deception**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#skills)) checks made to pass as the digested creature. The podling melts into a slurry when it dies.

#### Actions {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:Actions}

**_Slam._** _Melee Attack Roll:_ +5, reach 5 ft. _Hit:_ 6 (1d6 + 3) Bludgeoning damage.

#### Bodytaker Plant {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:BodytakerPlant}

A bodytaker plant uses its powerful vines to capture victims or accept captives brought to it by podling servants. The plant drags prey into an attached pod where the captive is dissolved over the course of hours. After the process is complete, a duplicate of the captive emerges as a subservient podling. Nothing of the original creature remains, though its noncompostable gear might be recovered after the bodytaker plant is slain.

A bodytaker plant’s podlings are extensions of the plant’s will, and the plant has no qualms about sacrificing podlings or using them as shields in battle. While bodytaker plants can communicate telepathically, most do so only in desperate cases, preferring to speak through their podlings—potentially speaking through several at once.

A bodytaker plant grows where its seed fell from space, or it might later have its podlings relocate it to a hidden sanctuary. Roll on or choose a result from the Bodytaker Plant Sanctuary table to inspire where such a plant might grow.

**Bodytaker Plant Sanctuary**

| 1d4 | The Bodytaker Plant Grows In…           |
| --- | --------------------------------------- |
| 1   | A building converted into a greenhouse. |
| 2   | A hidden caldera or cenote.             |
| 3   | An overgrown circle of standing stones. |
| 4   | The sanctuary of a ruined cathedral.    |

Huge Plant, Neutral Evil

**AC** 16 **Initiative** −1 (9)

**HP** 138 (12d12 + 60)

**Speed** 10 ft., Climb 10 ft., Swim 10 ft.

**Vulnerabilities** Poison

**Immunities** [**Blinded**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#blindedcondition), [**Charmed**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#charmedcondition), [**Exhaustion**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#exhaustioncondition), [**Frightened**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#frightenedcondition), [**Prone**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#pronecondition)

#### Traits {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:Traits}

**_Podling Link._** The plant can see through and communicate telepathically with any of its podlings within 10 miles of it. When the plant dies, its podlings also die.

**_Rejuvenation._** If the plant dies, it revives with all its Hit Points in 1d10 days. This trait doesn’t function if the plant is reduced to 0 Hit Points by Poison damage or its remains are sprinkled with salt.

#### Actions {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:Actions}

**_Multiattack._** The plant makes three Vine attacks. It can replace one attack with a use of Entrapping Pod.

**_Vine._** _Melee Attack Roll:_ +7, reach 20 ft. _Hit:_ 17 (3d8 + 4) Slashing damage. If the target is a Large or smaller creature, it has the [**Grappled**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#grappledcondition) condition (escape DC 14) from one of four vines.

**_Entrapping Pod._** _Strength Saving Throw:_ DC 15, one Large or smaller creature the plant is grappling. _Failure:_ The target is pulled into the plant’s space, is no longer [**Grappled**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#grappledcondition), and is trapped in the plant’s pod. While trapped, the target has the [**Blinded**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#blindedcondition) and [**Paralyzed**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#paralyzedcondition) conditions, and it has [**Total Cover**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#cover) against attacks and other effects outside the pod. After 2d4 hours, the trapped target dies, and if it was a Humanoid, a [**Bodytaker Podling**](#ref:monster:6491342-bodytaker-podling "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491342-bodytaker-podling") resembling it emerges from the pod.

A creature outside the pod and within 5 feet of the plant can take an action to make a DC 14 Strength ([**Athletics**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#skills)) check. On a successful check, the target is removed from the pod, falls in a space within 5 feet of the plant, and has the [**Prone**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#pronecondition) condition. If the plant dies, the trapped target is no longer Blinded or Paralyzed and can escape from the pod using 5 feet of movement, exiting Prone.

#### Reactions {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:Reactions}

**_Transfer Harm._** _Trigger:_ An attack roll hits the plant while a podling is within 5 feet of the plant. _Response:_ The plant halves the damage it takes from that attack, and the podling takes the other half of the damage.

### Boneless {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:Boneless}

Flayed Flesh with Murderous Intent

**Habitat:** Any; **Treasure:** None

Boneless are the animate skins of crushed or flensed humanoids. They rise from the corpses of those who suffered brutal ends such as flaying, crushing, or cannibalism. These hateful skins might seek vengeance, constricting and smothering victims using their elastic bodies. Alternatively, necromancers might create boneless to serve as stealthy assassins.

Vile magic-users might order a boneless to hang like a grotesque banner or adorn a skeleton or zombie. When foes approach, the boneless peels away from its surroundings or undead ally to face them.

**AC** 12 **Initiative** +2 (12)

**Speed** 30 ft.

**Skills** [**Stealth**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#skills) +4

**Resistances** Bludgeoning

**Immunities** Poison; [**Exhaustion**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#exhaustioncondition), [**Poisoned**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#poisonedcondition)

**Senses** [**Darkvision**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#darkvision) 60 ft.; Passive Perception 10

**Languages** Understands Common but can’t speak

#### Traits {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:Traits}

**_Abduct._** The boneless needn’t spend extra movement to move a creature it is grappling.

**_Compression._** The boneless can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch without expending extra movement to do so.

#### Actions {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:Actions}

**_Smother._** _Melee Attack Roll:_ +4, reach 5 ft. _Hit:_ 7 (2d4 + 2) Bludgeoning damage. If the target is a Medium or smaller creature, it has the [**Grappled**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#grappledcondition) condition (escape DC 12). Until the grapple ends, the target has the [**Blinded**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#blindedcondition) and [**Restrained**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#restrainedcondition) conditions, is [**suffocating**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#suffocationhazard), and takes 7 (2d4 + 2) Bludgeoning damage at the start of each of the boneless’s turns. The boneless can smother only one creature at a time. While grappling a target, the boneless can’t take this action again.

#### Bonus Actions {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:BonusActions}

**_Unraveling Flesh (1/Day)._** _Wisdom Saving Throw:_ DC 11, each creature within 30 feet that can see the boneless. _Failure:_ The target has the [**Frightened**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#frightenedcondition) condition. _Failure or Success:_ The boneless moves up to its Speed without provoking [**Opportunity Attacks**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#opportunityattack).

A brain in a jar’s container might be an alien contraption, ostentatious glassware, or a mundane canister.

### Carrion Stalker {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:CarrionStalker}

Gut-Bursting Corpse Eater

**Habitat:** Swamp, Underdark, Urban; **Treasure:** None

[![(Artist: Leroy Steinmann)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/22-007.carrion-stalker.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/22-007.carrion-stalker.png)

Carrion stalkers are parasites that feed on corpses, infesting bodies with their maggot-like young. While stalkers can survive off corpses, they’re attracted to movement and ambush any who disturb them. The foul parasites attach to their prey, using their stingers to implant their larvae into living victims. If a carrion stalker doesn’t slay and consume its foe, its larvae grow rapidly within that creature. After a day of gestation, a larva bursts from its host as a mature carrion stalker in an eruption as horrifying as it is lethal.

Carrion stalkers have symbiotic relationships with [**carrion crawlers**](#ref:monster:5194938-carrion-crawler "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5194938-carrion-crawler"). Carrion crawlers won’t devour bodies infested by carrion stalkers, but they might pick up stalker larvae as they root among filth. The crawlers then spread these young, infecting sewers or graveyards with carrion stalkers. In return, carrion stalkers avoid preying on carrion crawlers.

Battlefields, mass graves, and similar sites make natural homes for carrion stalkers. While corpses left by plagues or wars might coax carrion stalkers into streets or alleys, these vile parasites rarely creep onto the surface unless they become an overwhelming infestation.

#### [Carrion Stalker](#ref:monster:6491345-carrion-stalker "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491345-carrion-stalker") {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:CarrionStalkerrefmonster6491345carrionstalkerhttpswwwdndbeyondcommonsters6491345carrionstalker}

**AC** 15 **Initiative** +3 (13)

**HP** 55 (10d4 + 30)

**Speed** 30 ft., Burrow 30 ft.

**STR** 6 (−2) | **DEX** 17 (+3) | **CON** 16 (+3) | **INT** 2 (−4) | **WIS** 13 (+1) | **CHA** 6 (−2)

**Senses** [**Tremorsense**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#tremorsense) 60 ft.; Passive Perception 11

**Languages** None

**CR** 3 (XP 700; PB +2)

#### Actions {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:Actions}

**_Multiattack._** The carrion stalker makes two Tentacle attacks and one Stinger attack.

**_Tentacle._** _Melee Attack Roll:_ +5, reach 5 ft. _Hit:_ 8 (2d4 + 3) Piercing damage, and the carrion stalker attaches to the target. While attached, the carrion stalker can’t make Tentacle attacks against other targets.

The carrion stalker can detach itself by spending 5 feet of movement. The target or a creature within 5 feet of it can detach the carrion stalker as an action.

**_Stinger._** _Melee Attack Roll:_ +5 (with [**Advantage**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#advantage) if the carrion stalker is attached to the target), reach 5 ft. _Hit:_ 7 (2d6) Poison damage, and the target is subjected to the following effect. _Constitution Saving Throw:_ DC 13. _Failure:_ The target has the [**Poisoned**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#poisonedcondition) condition. While Poisoned in this way, the target is infested with a carrion stalker larva. If the target is still Poisoned in this way after 24 hours, the effect ends as the larva becomes a fully grown **Carrion Stalker**, which bursts from the target’s chest and kills it.

### Carrionette {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:Carrionette}

Evil Toy Come to Life

**Habitat:** Urban; **Treasure:** [Implements](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/dmg-2024/random-magic-items#implementstables)

When evil energies infest a children’s toy box, once-beloved playthings can become cursed monsters. Such is the case of the carrionette, an animated doll or puppet that uses its sinister magic to swap bodies with a living person.

Carrionettes can hide in plain sight amid a jumbled toy chest or crate of disused trinkets. A carrionette might wait patiently for years to be picked up by an unsuspecting victim—preferably an adventurer, a trader, or someone else with autonomy and a sturdy body—only to crawl out of the looter’s backpack in the middle of the night for a harrowing sneak attack.

[![(Artist: Guilherme Motta)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/22-008.carrionette.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/22-008.carrionette.png)

**_Silver Needle._** _Melee Attack Roll:_ +4, reach 5 ft. _Hit:_ 1 Piercing damage plus 3 (1d6) Necrotic damage. If the target is a Humanoid not cursed by a carrionette, it is subjected to the following effect. _Charisma Saving Throw:_ DC 11. _Failure:_ The target is [**cursed**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#curses) for 1 minute. Until the curse ends, the target has the [**Poisoned**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#poisonedcondition) condition, and its Speed is reduced by 10 feet.

**_Soul Swap (Recharge 5–6)._** _Charisma Saving Throw:_ DC 11, one Humanoid the carrionette can see within 15 feet that is cursed by its Silver Needle. _Failure:_ The carrionette possesses the target’s body, and the target possesses the carrionette’s body and has the [**Unconscious**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#unconsciouscondition) condition for 1 hour. While possessing another body, the carrionette and target retain their alignments; personalities; Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores; and languages known. They otherwise adopt the other creature’s game statistics, though the target can’t use this Soul Swap action.

The possession is undone if the target (while in the carrionette’s body) deals damage to the carrionette (in the target’s original body) with its Silver Needle. If either body is destroyed, both the carrionette and the target die.

**_Petrifying Bite._** _Melee Attack Roll:_ +3, reach 5 ft. _Hit:_ 3 (1d4 + 1) Piercing damage plus 3 (1d6) Necrotic damage. If the target is a creature, it is subjected to the following effect. _Constitution Saving Throw:_ DC 11. _First Failure:_ The target has the [**Restrained**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#restrainedcondition) condition and repeats the save at the end of its next turn if it is still Restrained, ending the effect on itself on a success. _Second Failure:_ The target has the [**Petrified**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#petrifiedcondition) condition instead of the Restrained condition for 10 minutes, after which the effect ends on the target.

### Dullahan {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:Dullahan}

Vengeful Headless Hunter

**Habitat:** Grassland, Hill, Urban; **Treasure:** [Armaments](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/dmg-2024/random-magic-items#armamentstables)

Headless, undying warriors, dullahans arise from decapitated villains and murderously seek to recover their missing heads. In their endless hunts, they terrorize sites relevant to their crimes or near where they died, beheading anyone they believe responsible (or connected to those responsible) for their deaths. Aside from their lethal blades, dullahans terrorize foes with their terrifying wails and by throwing the flame-wreathed skulls of past victims. Many pursue their victims astride undead or fiendish steeds.

### Ez d’Avenir {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:EzdAvenir}

Wandering Monster Hunter

Ez d’Avenir first encountered monsters among her manipulative family, the Radanaviches, who posed as Vistani to prey on travelers. Among their foul deeds, the Radanavich family kidnapped Erasmus van Richten, the son of [**Rudolph van Richten**](#ref:monster:6491386-rudolph-van-richten "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491386-rudolph-van-richten") (detailed later in [this chapter](#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:rudolphvanrichten "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/denizens-of-the-mists#rudolphvanrichten")) and sold him to his death at the hands of the vampire Baron Metus. In the brief time Ez knew Erasmus, the youth spoke lovingly of a different sort of family than the one Ez knew. When Erasmus’s father tracked down Ez’s family and delivered her mother to justice, Ez didn’t stop the determined doctor.

[![(Artist: Rowan Holloway)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/22-012.raven-flying.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/22-012.raven-flying.png)

In the years that followed, Ez joined a true Vistani band and adopted the name d’Avenir. She traveled far but never found the sense of belonging Erasmus described. She sought out Rudolph van Richten and, after a wary introduction, came to study with the doctor. During that time, she reconnected with Erasmus, now a ghost. She learned priceless lessons from the van Richtens, but she eventually left their household to pursue her own destiny.

Ez’s skillful slaying of monsters and her bravery in the face of supernatural perils have earned her a reputation as a folk hero and Mist wanderer of note. Although her adventures have cost her dearly—she has lost valuable bounties, dear companions, and her leg from the knee down—Ez works tirelessly to eradicate evil and protect innocents. Armed with wisdom from her mentor, encouragement from her departed friend, and hope forged in the depths of her heart, Ez aspires to someday create a place that feels safe enough to call home.

Whether she’s hunting monsters or investigating mysteries, Ez carries Vistani music with her wherever she goes. She boasts a significant repertoire of songs from across the Land of the Mists, which she’s happy to perform for anyone who travels alongside her.

[![(Artist: Taras Susak)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/22-013.ez-davenir.jpg)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/22-013.ez-davenir.jpg)

### Gug {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:Gug}

Cavern-Stalking, Aberrant Glutton

**Habitat:** Underdark; **Treasure:** [Armaments](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/dmg-2024/random-magic-items#armamentstables)

[![(Artist: Audy Ravindra)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/22-016.gug.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/22-016.gug.png)

Gugs are gigantic, subterranean horrors with heads split by toothy, vertical maws. They are stealthy predators that favor humanoid prey. Gugs fear and hate [**ghouls**](#ref:monster:5195009-ghoul "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195009-ghoul"), perhaps because they compete to dominate the hidden necropolises and charnel depths of the Underdark, or for reasons related to a curse that forces gugs to dwell underground.

#### [Gug](#ref:monster:6491359-gug "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491359-gug") {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:Gugrefmonster6491359gughttpswwwdndbeyondcommonsters6491359gug}

Huge Aberration, Chaotic Evil

**AC** 16 **Initiative** +6 (16)

**HP** 250 (20d12 + 120)

**Speed** 40 ft.

**STR** 22 (+6) | **DEX** 15 (+2) | **CON** 23 (+6) | **INT** 7 (−2) | **WIS** 16 (+3) | **CHA** 11 (+0)

**Skills** [**Perception**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#skills) +7, [**Stealth**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#skills) +10

**Senses** [**Darkvision**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#darkvision) 120 ft.; Passive Perception 17

**Languages** Understands Deep Speech but can’t speak

**CR** 12 (XP 8,400; PB +4)

#### Traits {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:Traits}

**_Pack Tactics._** The gug has [**Advantage**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#advantage) on an attack roll against a creature if at least one of the gug’s allies is within 5 feet of the creature and the ally doesn’t have the [**Incapacitated**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#incapacitatedcondition) condition.

#### Actions {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:Actions}

**_Multiattack._** The gug makes two Claw attacks and uses Chew.

**_Claw._** _Melee Attack Roll:_ +10, reach 10 ft. _Hit:_ 22 (3d10 + 6) Slashing damage. If the target is a Medium or smaller creature, it has the [**Grappled**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#grappledcondition) condition (escape DC 16) from one of two claws.

**_Chew._** _Dexterity Saving Throw:_ DC 18, up to two Medium or smaller creatures [**Grappled**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#grappledcondition) by the gug. _Failure:_ The gug places the target in its mouth and chews. A chewed creature is no longer Grappled but has the [**Restrained**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#restrainedcondition) condition. While Restrained in this way, a target has [**Half Cover**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#cover) against attacks and other effects not originating from the gug and takes 10 (3d6) Piercing damage at the start of each of the gug’s turns. A gug can have a maximum of four creatures in its mouth at a time.

A creature in the gug’s mouth can take an action to make a DC 16 Strength ([**Athletics**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#skills)) check. On a successful check, the target is no longer Restrained and moves to an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the gug. If the gug dies, a target is no longer Restrained and can escape from the gug using 5 feet of movement, exiting with the [**Prone**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#pronecondition) condition.

### Jiangshi {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:Jiangshi}

Vindictive, Vitality-Sapping Corpse

**Habitat:** Any; **Treasure:** [Relics](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/dmg-2024/random-magic-items#relicstables)

When a soul becomes trapped within its corpse, its bitterness can reanimate its body, creating a jiangshi. These vengeful dead stalk their descendants, sowing terror and taking retribution for the slights or neglected burial rites that led to their cursed resurrections. Rigor mortis notoriously afflicts the limbs of jiangshi, causing them to hold their arms rigidly and to walk with a stiff gait. This, along with their flight, leads many to call them hopping vampires.

By day, jiangshi lurk within tombs or hidden ruins to avoid attention from the living. At night, they emerge to drain the life from those who dare wander in darkness. A Humanoid killed by a jiangshi rises as a life-hungry corpse that, if given the chance to slake its thirst, might also turn into jiangshi.

Medium Undead, Lawful Evil

#### Traits {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:Traits}

**_Jiangshi Weaknesses._** The jiangshi has these weaknesses:

**Fear of Its Own Reflection.** If the jiangshi sees its reflection, it immediately takes its Reaction, if available, to move as far from the reflection as possible.

**Susceptible to Holy Symbols.** While the jiangshi is wearing or touching a Holy Symbol, it loses its Immunity to the [**Frightened**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#frightenedcondition) condition and automatically fails saving throws to avoid or end the Frightened condition.

#### Actions {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:Actions}

**_Multiattack._** The jiangshi makes three Slam attacks and uses Consume Energy.

**_Slam._** _Melee Attack Roll:_ +8, reach 5 ft. _Hit:_ 13 (2d8 + 4) Bludgeoning damage.

**_Consume Energy._** _Constitution Saving Throw:_ DC 16, one creature the jiangshi can see within 30 feet. _Failure:_ 18 (4d8) Necrotic damage. _Success:_ Half damage. _Failure or Success:_ The jiangshi regains Hit Points equal to the Necrotic damage taken, the jiangshi’s Fly Speed increases to 20 feet until the end of its next turn, and it can take its Hungering Stride Bonus Action. A Humanoid reduced to 0 Hit Points by this damage rises at the end of the jiangshi’s turn as a [**Wight**](#ref:monster:5195269-wight "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195269-wight") under the jiangshi’s control. If this wight kills a Humanoid with its Life Drain action, the wight transforms into an independent **Jiangshi** 5 days later.

#### Bonus Actions {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:BonusActions}

**_Hungering Stride (Requires Consume Energy)._** The jiangshi takes the [**Dash**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#dashaction) action.

**_Shape-Shift._** The jiangshi [**shape-shifts**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#shapeshifting) into a Medium or Small Beast, Humanoid, or Undead creature, or it returns to its true form. Its game statistics, other than its size, are the same in each form. Any equipment it is wearing or carrying isn’t transformed.

### Loup Garou {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:LoupGarou}

Legendary Lycanthrope

**Habitat:** Forest, Swamp, Urban; **Treasure:** Any

Loup garou are powerful lycanthropes capable of transforming into hulking dire wolves. They actively seek to spread the curse of lycanthropy, creating packs of subservient werewolves that can reduce communities to ruins and ravage whole regions. The strain of lycanthropy spread by a loup garou is harder to cure than typical varieties. Only slaying a loup garou can free the monster’s victims from their affliction.

### Madam Eva {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:MadamEva}

Duplicitous Diviner

The mysterious fortune teller Madam Eva shrouds herself in a carefully woven web of lies. Though she appears to be in her seventies, she is much older. She sets herself apart from any group, guarding the secrets of her origins and centuries-spanning agendas.

Madam Eva is a legendary figure known across the Land of the Mists. Few can rival her skill at interpreting omens, reading tarokka cards, or taming spirits during séances. While the fortunes she shares might have double meanings, they’re never wrong. She is renowned for revealing when best to enter the Mists to escape a domain or reach an intended destination, leading many travelers to seek her on the shores of the Tser Pool in Barovia to seek her insights. She often hints at knowledge of the Mists’ secrets and the tales (and weaknesses) of Darklords, and she’s not above revealing them for a price. Madam Eva holds grudges and usually shares her secrets only with those who do her a favor first. Whatever she discovers might soon also be known by Barovia’s Darklord, with whom she shares age-old ties.

### Mi-Go {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:MiGo}

Brain-Robbing Alien Fungus

**Habitat:** Forest, Hill, Mountain, Underdark; **Treasure:** [Implements](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/dmg-2024/random-magic-items#implementstables)

Bizarre beings that profanely unite features of alien insects and otherworldly fungus, mi-go bend their unfathomable intellects toward colonizing worlds and controlling the inhabitants. They work with bizarre precision, learning all they can about how other creatures think and define identity. To this end, mi-go extract creatures’ brains for research and experimentation. Occasionally they swap brains between individuals, or they place stolen brains into the bodies of radically different creatures, then observe the results from afar.

Mi-go aren’t impeded by light, but they prefer the dark. They typically lurk in secluded caverns and amid remote heights.

**_Dazing Ray (Recharge 4–6)._** _Dexterity Saving Throw:_ DC 17, one creature the mi-go can see within 60 feet. _Failure:_ 22 (4d10) Lightning damage plus 10 (3d6) Force damage, and the target has the [**Stunned**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#stunnedcondition) condition until the end of the mi-go’s next turn.

**_Extract Brain (Requires Silver Canister)._** _Constitution Saving Throw:_ DC 17, one creature that is [**Grappled**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#grappledcondition) by the mi-go or that has the [**Stunned**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#stunnedcondition) condition. _Failure:_ 77 (14d10) Piercing damage. _Success:_ Half damage. _Failure or Success:_ If this damage reduces the target to 0 Hit Points, the mi-go kills it, removes its brain, and places the brain in its silver canister.

**_Spellcasting._** The mi-go casts one of the following spells, requiring no spell components and using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 17):

**1/Day Each:** [**Modify Memory**](#ref:spell:2619109-modify-memory "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619109-modify-memory"), [**Plane Shift**](#ref:spell:2618867-plane-shift "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618867-plane-shift") (self only)

### Mist Horror {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:MistHorror}

Shapeless Stalker in the Mists

**Habitat:** Any; **Treasure:** None

[![(Artist: Irina Nordsol)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/22-021.mist-horror.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/22-021.mist-horror.png)

The Mists separating the Domains of Dread are far from safe—or empty. Mist horrors are animate clouds of vapor, barely perceptible within the Mists. In the presence of creatures, these vaporous terrors take the shape of their viewers’ greatest fears. Such appearances are subjective, and anyone who views a mist horror sees it in the way that terrifies them most. A mist horror outside the Mists swiftly loses cohesion and collapses into harmless vapor.

Large Undead, Chaotic Evil

**AC** 13 **Initiative** +2 (17)

**HP** 45 (7d10 + 7)

**Speed** 25 ft., Fly 25 ft. (hover)

Traveler Between Domains

### Mordenheim’s Monster {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:MordenheimsMonster}

Masterwork of Stolen Flesh

**Habitat:** Urban; **Treasure:** [Individual](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/dmg-2024/creating-adventures#individualtreasure)

The creations of [**Dr. Viktra Mordenheim**](#ref:monster:6491399-viktra-mordenheim "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491399-viktra-mordenheim"), Darklord of Lamordia, defy reason and classification as mere flesh golems. As she seeks to re-create her masterpiece, the Unbreakable Heart, Mordenheim has refined the creation of beings that are much more than the sum of their rotting parts. Known as Mordenheim’s monsters, these collections of body parts are reanimated into striking, mighty, thinking beings with wills of their own. While some might be convinced to serve their creator, others seek to recover some semblance of the lives they remember in fractured memories. Still others believe that they are something new and greater than what they were before and seek to create a new life—whether on their own or at the expense of communities that shun and fear them.

[![(Artist: Marie Magny)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/22-023.mordenheims-monster.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/22-023.mordenheims-monster.png)

#### Traits {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:Traits}

**_Greater Lightning Absorption._** Whenever the monster is subjected to Lightning damage, it regains a number of Hit Points equal to the Lightning damage dealt, and its Speed increases by 40 feet until the end of its next turn.

**_Immutable Form._** The monster can’t [**shape-shift**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#shapeshifting).

**_Magic Resistance._** The monster has [**Advantage**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#advantage) on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

If the target is a Medium or smaller creature, it has the [**Grappled**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#grappledcondition) condition (escape DC 18) from one of two hands.

**_Crush._** _Strength Saving Throw:_ DC 18, one creature [**Grappled**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#grappledcondition) by the monster. _Failure:_ 13 (2d6 + 6) Bludgeoning damage plus 7 (2d6) Lightning damage, and the target has the [**Restrained**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#restrainedcondition) condition. While Restrained, the target is [**suffocating**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#suffocationhazard).

**_Violent Leap._** The monster spends 10 feet of movement to jump to a space within 40 feet that contains one or more Medium or smaller creatures. _Dexterity Saving Throw:_ DC 18, each creature in the monster’s destination space. _Failure:_ 14 (4d6) Bludgeoning damage, and the target has the [**Prone**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#pronecondition) condition. _Failure or Success:_ The target moves to the nearest unoccupied space.

### Necrichor {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:Necrichor}

Reanimated Blood of an Evil Entity

**Habitat:** Underdark, Urban; **Treasure:** None

Necrichors are beings of sapient blood spawned from magical corruption, such as the gore of an obscene deity or a failed lich. They aspire to steal living bodies to fulfill megalomaniacal goals. Necrichors leave a trace of their essence within those they control, making necrichors difficult to destroy.

[![(Artist: David Astruga)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/22-024.necrichor.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/22-024.necrichor.png)

#### [Necrichor](#ref:monster:6491378-necrichor "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491378-necrichor") {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:Necrichorrefmonster6491378necrichorhttpswwwdndbeyondcommonsters6491378necrichor}

Medium Undead, Lawful Evil

**AC** 14 **Initiative** +3 (13)

**HP** 85 (10d8 + 40)

**Speed** 20 ft., Climb 20 ft.

**STR** 8 (−1) | **DEX** 16 (+3) | **CON** 18 (+4) | **INT** 17 (+3) | **WIS** 13 (+1) | **CHA** 10 (+0)

**Resistances** Acid, Necrotic

**Immunities** Poison; [**Blinded**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#blindedcondition), [**Charmed**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#charmedcondition), [**Deafened**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#deafenedcondition), [**Exhaustion**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#exhaustioncondition), [**Frightened**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#frightenedcondition), [**Grappled**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#grappledcondition), [**Paralyzed**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#paralyzedcondition), [**Poisoned**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#poisonedcondition), [**Prone**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#pronecondition), [**Restrained**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#restrainedcondition)

**Senses** [**Blindsight**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#blindsight) 120 ft.; Passive Perception 11

**Languages** Common plus two other languages; telepathy 120 ft.

**CR** 7 (XP 2,900; PB +3)

#### Traits {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:Traits}

**_Amorphous._** The necrichor can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch without expending extra movement to do so.

**_Legendary Resistance (2/Day)._** If the necrichor fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

**_Reborn by Blood._** If destroyed, the necrichor revives with all its Hit Points in 1d10 days in the nearest unoccupied space next to a creature of its choice that it has previously possessed with its Blood Puppeteering action. This trait doesn’t function if the destroyed necrichor’s remains are in a vessel affected by the [**Hallow**](#ref:spell:2619138-hallow "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619138-hallow") spell or if all the necrichor’s previous Blood Puppeteering targets are dead.

**_Spider Climb._** The necrichor can climb difficult surfaces, including along ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.

#### Actions {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:Actions}

**_Multiattack._** The necrichor makes two Necrotic Burst attacks.

**_Necrotic Burst._** _Melee or Ranged Attack Roll:_ +6, reach 5 ft. or range 120 ft. _Hit:_ 12 (2d8 + 3) Force damage plus 11 (2d10) Necrotic damage, and the target has the [**Poisoned**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#poisonedcondition) condition until the start of the necrichor’s next turn. While Poisoned, the target can’t regain Hit Points.

**_Blood Puppeteering (Recharge 6)._** _Constitution Saving Throw:_ DC 15, one [**Bloodied**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#bloodied) creature within 5 feet. Constructs and Undead automatically succeed on this save. _Failure:_ The target is possessed by the necrichor; the necrichor disappears, and the target has the [**Incapacitated**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#incapacitatedcondition) condition and loses control of its body. The necrichor now controls the target’s body, but the target retains awareness. The necrichor can’t be targeted by any attack, spell, or other effect except ones that specifically target Undead. The necrichor’s game statistics are the same, except it uses the possessed target’s Speed and Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution scores.

The possession lasts until the target drops to 0 Hit Points or the necrichor leaves it as a Bonus Action. When the possession ends, the necrichor appears in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the target, and the target is immune to this necrichor’s Blood Puppeteering for 24 hours.

_Success:_ The target is immune to this necrichor’s Blood Puppeteering for 24 hours.

### Nightgaunt {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:Nightgaunt}

Faceless Fearmonger from the Far Realm

**Habitat:** Mountain, Underdark; **Treasure:** [Implements](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/dmg-2024/random-magic-items#implementstables), [Individual](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/dmg-2024/creating-adventures#individualtreasure)

Inscrutable, gargoyle-like fiends, nightgaunts soar over subterranean mountain ranges and the skies of alien worlds. These hunters are infamous for abducting victims and dropping them from incredible heights. Those who have escaped nightgaunts describe the touch of their razor-like claws as “tickling” in a way that causes every sense to scream.

A nightgaunt’s head is a smooth, horned polyp. Before a nightgaunt kills, its head splits apart, revealing an otherworldly glow deep within.

**_Tickle._** _Wisdom Saving Throw:_ DC 16, one creature [**Grappled**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#grappledcondition) by the nightgaunt. _Failure:_ The target has the [**Incapacitated**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#incapacitatedcondition) condition until the start of the nightgaunt’s next turn.

### Priest of Osybus {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:PriestofOsybus}

Necromancer Cursed by Dark Powers

**Habitat:** Any; **Treasure:** Any

[![(Artist: Polar Engine)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/22-026.priest-of-osybus.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/22-026.priest-of-osybus.png)

The priests of Osybus are evil necromancers who steal souls to fuel their malevolent magic. Thanks to a foul bargain made with dread powers, these priests can defy death by transforming into undead.

Centuries ago, Osybus, a mysterious figure of immense ambition and evil, founded the order of priests that now bears his name. Osybus sought to use others’ souls to achieve immortality. He forged pacts with any entity that promised him more power, and he delved into any eldritch secret that could possibly prolong his life. He became a devotee of the Dark Powers and tapped into their immortal malice to fuel his apotheosis. As his power grew, he shared his secrets with disciples who wished to defy death in exchange for their worship.

Osybus achieved his goal and became a lich of almost godly power. He rewarded his disciples with a trace of his power in the form of shadowy tattoos. Osybus’s boon gave his priests the ability to steal souls and to cheat death by transforming into undead horrors.

The threat posed by Osybus and his disciples raised alarms far and wide. The Ulmist Inquisition—which at the time counted then-mortal Count Strahd von Zarovich as an ally—faced Osybus in battle. Fearing that their master eventually would consume their souls, Osybus’s disciples aided the inquisition by destroying Osybus’s physical form. As Osybus perished, he cursed his former allies: Their immortality would fail them eventually, and he would become one of the Dark Powers.

[![A Soul Tattoo on the Flesh of a Priest of Osybus (Artist: Jane Katsubo)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/22-027.soul-tattoo.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/22-027.soul-tattoo.png)

To rid themselves of this curse, Osybus’s former devotees turned to the same Dark Powers with whom their master had communed. They received a mission: Provide a mighty noble to serve as an earthly vessel for the Dark Powers to enter the world and conquer it. They found a suitable vessel in [**Strahd von Zarovich**](#ref:monster:6491390-strahd-von-zarovich "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491390-strahd-von-zarovich"). Working in shadows and through intermediaries, the priests whispered hatred to the count. Once the priests corrupted Strahd’s heart, they laid the path before him that led to his fall into vampirism.

But Osybus hadn’t lied; he became one of the Dark Powers. Those powers conjured a misty prison to contain the newly immortal Strahd, thereby stymieing the priests’ ambitions to use the count as a weapon of conquest.

The priests of Osybus still seek to unleash Strahd from the Mists, often using adventurers as pawns. They continue to bear their hated founder’s name, for they know it is his original gift that gives them their horrific powers.

**_Tattoo of Osybus._** If damage reduces the priest to 0 Hit Points, it receives a random boon. Roll 1d6 to determine the boon the priest receives. The priest revives at the start of its next turn with half its Hit Points, and its creature type is now Undead.

**1: Dread Boon.** An aura of dread fills a 15-foot [**Emanation**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#emanationareaofeffect) originating from the priest. _Wisdom Saving Throw:_ DC 15, each non-Undead creature that starts its turn in the Emanation. _Failure:_ The target has the [**Frightened**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#frightenedcondition) condition until the start of its next turn

**2: Ectoplasmic Boon.** Sticky ectoplasm slows creatures in a 15-foot [**Emanation**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#emanationareaofeffect) originating from the priest. _Strength Saving Throw:_ DC 15, each creature that starts its turn in the Emanation. _Failure:_ The target’s Speed is reduced by 10 feet until the start of its next turn.

**3: Vampiric Boon.** When the priest deals Necrotic damage to a creature, the priest gains [**Temporary Hit Points**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#temporaryhitpoints) equal to the damage dealt.

**4: Blazing Boon.** The priest has a Fly Speed of 30 feet and Immunity to Fire damage.

**5: Spectral Boon.** The priest has Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage, and it has Vulnerability to Radiant damage. Additionally, the priest can move through other creatures and objects as if they were [**Difficult Terrain**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#difficultterrain). It takes 5 (1d10) Force damage if it ends its turn inside an object.

**6: Deathly Boon.** When the priest revives with this boon, all corpses of Small or Medium Humanoids in a 30-foot [**Emanation**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#emanationareaofeffect) originating from the priest rise as [**Skeletons**](#ref:monster:4775841-skeleton "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/4775841-skeleton") under the priest’s control. Additionally, at the end of each of the priest’s turns, each non-Undead creature in a 5-foot Emanation originating from the priest takes 5 (1d10) Necrotic damage.

The priest dies and this trait doesn’t function if the priest receives a boon it already has or the priest’s tattoo of Osybus is destroyed. The tattoo is destroyed only if the priest takes 15 damage or more on a single turn while the priest has 0 Hit Points.

If this damage reduces a Medium or smaller creature to 0 Hit Points, the creature dies, and its soul becomes trapped in a soul tattoo on the priest’s body. The soul is freed if the priest dies.

**_Necrotic Bolt._** _Ranged Attack Roll:_ +7, range 120 ft. _Hit:_ 30 (4d12 + 4) Necrotic damage, and the target can’t regain Hit Points until the start of the priest’s next turn.

The shadow takes its turn immediately after the priest on the same Initiative count, and it obeys the priest. The shadow remains animate until it is destroyed, it is more than 120 feet from the priest, the priest dies, or the priest uses this Bonus Action again.
