### Rudolph van Richten {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:RudolphvanRichten}

Cursed Vampire Hunter

In better days, Rudolph van Richten lived with his wife, Ingrid, and son, Erasmus, in their family home outside Rivalis in the domain of [Darkon](#rthw:darkon "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/darkon"). The brash doctor Rudolph ran afoul of the Radanaviches, a family of brigands disguised as Vistani travelers. When the doctor refused to treat one of the family’s mortally ill members, the group’s leader, Irena Radanavich, ordered her band to kidnap Rudolph’s son. She then sold the young man to the vampire Baron Metus. Rudolph pursued the Radanaviches, shattered their criminal operation, and brought Irena to justice, but not before suffering her curse: “Live you always among monsters, and see everyone you love die beneath their claws.”

By the time Rudolph tracked down his missing son, the curse had already taken hold: Erasmus had been transformed into Metus’s vampire spawn. Rudolph put an end to his son’s suffering by pounding a wooden stake through the youth’s chest.

This violent deed begat more bloodshed: Baron Metus avenged his slain servant by killing Rudolph’s wife, Ingrid. Though Rudolph eventually slew the evil baron, he remains haunted by the horror of his family’s destruction.

Rudolph has committed himself to unmasking the evils lurking amid the Land of the Mists, hunting monsters, ending curses, and providing others with tools to do the same. His reputation and writings have spread among the domains. His published works, such as _Van Richten’s Guide to Vampires_ and _Van Richten’s Guide to Werebeasts_, have earned him both adherents and disdain among scholarly communities. Nevertheless, his good works have touched lives and earned him allies far and wide.

Rudolph lives in Mordentshire in the domain of [Mordent](#rthw:mordent "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/mordent"). From his modest herbalist’s shop, he corresponds with scholars and monster hunters across the domains, researches horrific creatures, and crafts tools to combat evil. Frequently he travels to other domains to conduct research or aid friends.

Over the years, Rudolph has adventured alongside heroes like monster hunter George Weathermay and detectives Alanik Ray and Arthur Sedgewick. A new generation of heroes, including the [**Ez d’Avenir**](#ref:monster:6491354-ez-davenir "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491354-ez-davenir") and [**Gennifer**](#ref:monster:6491356-gennifer-weathermay-foxgrove "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491356-gennifer-weathermay-foxgrove") and [**Laurie Weathermay-Foxgrove**](#ref:monster:6491368-laurie-weathermay-foxgrove "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491368-laurie-weathermay-foxgrove"), have learned from the doctor and continue his fight against evil.

Unbeknownst to Rudolph, Erasmus watches over his father. The spirit of the artistic and thoughtful young man haunts the elder van Richten and aids him and his father’s allies with subtle direction and encouragement.

Rudolph knows that his age or vocation will eventually put an end to his endeavors. Increasingly he turns his research toward [Barovia](#rthw:barovia "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/barovia") and its vampire overlord, [**Strahd von Zarovich**](#ref:monster:6491390-strahd-von-zarovich "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491390-strahd-von-zarovich"), believing they hold keys to undoing myriad evils across the Land of the Mists.

#### Bonus Actions {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:BonusActions}

**_Occult Aid (2/Day)._** Rudolph casts [**Cure Wounds**](#ref:spell:2619079-cure-wounds "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619079-cure-wounds"), [**Dispel Evil and Good**](#ref:spell:2619096-dispel-evil-and-good "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619096-dispel-evil-and-good"), or [**Sanctuary**](#ref:spell:2619003-sanctuary "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619003-sanctuary"), using Wisdom as the spellcasting modifier (spell save DC 15).

### Shoggoth {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:Shoggoth}

Hulking, Amorphous Predator

**Habitat:** Arctic, Coastal, Swamp, Underdark; **Treasure:** None

Shoggoths are massive, undulating horrors possessed of ancient and cruel intellects. Created by [**elder things**](#ref:monster:6491353-elder-thing "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491353-elder-thing") (detailed in [this chapter](#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:elderthing "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/denizens-of-the-mists#elderthing")), the first shoggoths created cyclopean cities and performed dangerous labor in forgotten ages. Eventually, the shoggoths grew stronger and overthrew their makers. Since then, shoggoths have lurked in the ruins of their ancient cities and in hidden places across the multiverse. They tend to brood in remote, icy reaches where their bodies are invigorated by the blistering cold.

[![(Artist: Diana Franco)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/22-030.shoggoth.jpg)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/22-030.shoggoth.jpg)

#### [Shoggoth](#ref:monster:6491388-shoggoth "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491388-shoggoth") {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:Shoggothrefmonster6491388shoggothhttpswwwdndbeyondcommonsters6491388shoggoth}

Huge Aberration, Chaotic Evil

**AC** 15 **Initiative** +7 (17)

**HP** 172 (15d12 + 75)

**Speed** 30 ft., Climb 30 ft., Swim 30 ft.

**STR** 22 (+6) | **DEX** 16 (+3) | **CON** 21 (+5) | **INT** 20 (+5) | **WIS** 17 (+3) | **CHA** 8 (−1)

**Resistances** Bludgeoning, Piercing, Slashing

**Immunities** Cold; [**Grappled**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#grappledcondition), [**Prone**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#pronecondition), [**Restrained**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#restrainedcondition)

**Senses** [**Darkvision**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#darkvision) 120 ft.; Passive Perception 13

**Languages** Deep Speech; telepathy 60 ft.

**CR** 11 (XP 7,200; PB +4)

#### Traits {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:Traits}

**_Amphibious._** The shoggoth can breathe air and water.

**_Mimicry._** The shoggoth can mimic voices and animal sounds. A creature that hears this mimicry can tell it is an imitation only with a successful DC 13 Wisdom ([**Insight**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#skills)) check.

**_Susceptible to Charm._** The shoggoth has [**Disadvantage**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#disadvantage) on saving throws to avoid or end the [**Charmed**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#charmedcondition) condition.

#### Actions {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:Actions}

**_Multiattack._** The shoggoth makes three Pseudopod attacks. It can replace one attack with a use of Suction Burst if available.

**_Pseudopod._** _Melee Attack Roll:_ +10, reach 15 ft. _Hit:_ 15 (2d8 + 6) Bludgeoning damage plus 11 (2d10) Thunder damage, and the creature has the [**Grappled**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#grappledcondition) condition (escape DC 16) from one of four pseudopods.

**_Suction Burst (Recharge 4–6)._** _Strength Saving Throw:_ DC 18, one creature [**Grappled**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#grappledcondition) by the shoggoth. _Failure:_ 22 (4d10) Thunder damage, and the target is repelled from the shoggoth. The target no longer has the Grappled condition, is pushed up to 30 feet straight away from the shoggoth, and has the [**Deafened**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#deafenedcondition) and [**Stunned**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#stunnedcondition) conditions until the end of its next turn. _Success:_ Half damage only.

#### Reactions {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:Reactions}

**_Cold Sprint._** _Trigger:_ The shoggoth is subjected to Cold damage. _Response:_ The shoggoth moves up to its Speed and can make one Pseudopod attack with [**Advantage**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#advantage).

### Star Spawn Emissaries {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:StarSpawnEmissaries}

Colossal, Shape-Shifting Alien Colonizers

**Habitat:** Any; **Treasure:** Any

Star spawn emissaries are the fingers of alien realms, digits that tip the scales of reality toward terror. Heralded by ominous astrological events, these ravenous invaders make worlds ready for their unimaginable masters. Employing two malleable forms, emissaries undermine perceptions of order, trust, and reality on global scales, readying worlds for sanity-shattering revelations and cascading apocalypses.

#### Lesser Star Spawn Emissary {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:LesserStarSpawnEmissary}

A star spawn emissary’s lesser form allows it to appear as another creature. Emissaries readily appear as people, animals, or other creatures—the more unassuming, the better. Should an emissary’s true form be revealed and defeated, its greater form appears and seeks revenge moments or days later.

[![Front to Back: Lesser Star Spawn Emissary and Greater Star Spawn Emissary (Artist: Antonio José Manzanedo)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/22-031.greater-star-spawn-emissary.jpg)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/22-031.greater-star-spawn-emissary.jpg)

#### Traits {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:Traits}

#### Actions {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:Actions}

**_Multiattack._** The emissary makes three attacks, using Lashing Maw or Invert Flesh in any combination.

**_Lashing Maw._** _Melee Attack Roll:_ +11, reach 15 ft. _Hit:_ 16 (2d10 + 5) Piercing damage plus 13 (3d8) Acid damage.

**_Invert Flesh._** _Constitution Saving Throw:_ DC 21, one creature the emissary can see within 120 feet. _Failure:_ 29 (4d10 + 7) Force damage.

#### Bonus Actions {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:BonusActions}

**_Shape-Shift._** The emissary [**shape-shifts**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#shapeshifting) into a Small or Medium creature, or it returns to its true form. Its game statistics, other than its size, are the same in each form. Any equipment it is wearing or carrying isn’t transformed.

#### Legendary Actions {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:LegendaryActions}

Legendary Action Uses: 3 (4 in Lair). Immediately after another creature’s turn, the emissary can expend a use to take one of the following actions. The emissary regains all expended uses at the start of each of its turns.

**_Teleporting Lash._** The emissary teleports up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space it can see and makes one Lashing Maw attack.

**_Twist._** The emissary uses Invert Flesh.

**_Warp Body._** _Constitution Saving Throw:_ DC 21, one creature the emissary can see within 30 feet. _Failure:_ 27 (6d8) Force damage, and the target has the [**Stunned**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#stunnedcondition) condition until the start of its next turn. _Failure or Success:_ The emissary can’t take this action again until the start of its next turn.

#### Greater Star Spawn Emissary {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:GreaterStarSpawnEmissary}

An emissary’s greater form is a destructive abomination. This massive amalgamation of violent flesh is composed of the meat and voices of every form the emissary has ever mimicked. Only once this greater form is destroyed is the emissary defeated.

**_Legendary Resistance (3/Day, or 4/Day in Lair)._** If the emissary fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

#### Actions {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:Actions}

**_Lashing Maw._** _Melee Attack Roll:_ +14, reach 15 ft. _Hit:_ 33 (4d12 + 7) Piercing damage plus 18 (4d8) Acid damage.

**_Coagulated Nodule._** _Ranged Attack Roll:_ +15, range 120 ft. _Hit:_ 44 (8d8 + 8) Acid damage.

**_Unearthly Bile (Recharge 5–6)._** _Dexterity Saving Throw:_ DC 23, each creature in a 30-foot-radius Sphere centered on a point the emissary can see within 120 feet. _Failure:_ 54 (12d8) Acid damage, and a [**Gibbering Mouther**](#ref:monster:5195034-gibbering-mouther "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5195034-gibbering-mouther") appears in an unoccupied space within 30 feet of the target. The mouthers take their turn immediately after the emissary on the same Initiative count. Each mouther fights until destroyed. _Success:_ Half damage only.

#### Legendary Actions {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:LegendaryActions}

Legendary Action Uses: 3 (4 in Lair). Immediately after another creature’s turn, the emissary can expend a use to take one of the following actions. The emissary regains all expended uses at the start of each of its turns.

**_Forced Mutations._** _Charisma Saving Throw:_ DC 23, up to two creatures the emissary can see within 30 feet. _Failure:_ The target has the [**Paralyzed**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#paralyzedcondition) condition until the end of its next turn. _Failure or Success:_ The emissary can’t take this action again until the start of its next turn.

**_Teleporting Lash._** The emissary can teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space it can see, and it makes one Lashing Maw attack.

#### Star Spawn Emissary Lairs {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:StarSpawnEmissaryLairs}

A star spawn emissary’s lair takes on macabre bodily features. A ruined watchtower might become a spire of pulsating flesh, or an abandoned mineshaft might transform into a maze of sticky, muscular innards.

The region containing a star spawn emissary’s lair becomes twisted by its presence, creating the following effects:

**Cosmic Transformation.** When a creature in the lair [**shape-shifts**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#shapeshifting) to its true form, creatures in a 10-foot [**Emanation**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#emanationareaofeffect) originating from the shape-shifter take 10 (3d6) Force damage.

**Terrifying Topography.** Terrain in the lair is transformed into a mockery of flesh with unsettling features like thick veins, lolling tongues, and pulsating orifices. Creatures of the emissary’s choice within 1 mile of the lair have [**Disadvantage**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#disadvantage) on saving throws to avoid or end the [**Frightened**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#frightenedcondition) condition while in that area.

If the star spawn emissary dies or moves its lair elsewhere, these effects end immediately.

### Strahd Skeleton {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:StrahdSkeleton}

Skeletal Soldier of the First Vampire

**Habitat:** Planar (Shadowfell), Underdark, Urban; **Treasure:** None

[![(Artist: David Astruga)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/22-032.strahd-skeleton.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/22-032.strahd-skeleton.png)

Vampires sometimes turn mortal servants unworthy of the gift of vampirism into skeletal soldiers. Known as Strahd skeletons—in recognition of the lord of Barovia who first created them—these silent, capable undead soldiers wield vampiric blades. Strahd skeletons that whet their blades in blood often carry their weapons back to their vampire lords. Tales disagree on whether vampires can feed from these bloody blades or merely revel in the sacrifice.

#### Traits {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:Traits}

**_Swarm._** The swarm can occupy another creature’s space and vice versa, and it can move through any opening large enough for a Tiny creature. The swarm can’t regain Hit Points or gain [**Temporary Hit Points**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#temporaryhitpoints).

#### Actions {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:Actions}

**_Infestation._** _Melee Attack Roll:_ +4, reach 5 ft. _Hit:_ 12 (4d4 + 2) Poison damage, or 7 (2d4 + 2) Poison damage if the swarm is [**Bloodied**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#bloodied), and the target has the [**Poisoned**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#poisonedcondition) condition. If the target remains Poisoned in this way after 1 hour, it is subjected to the following effect. _Constitution Saving Throw:_ DC 11. _Failure:_ Roll 1d6: on a **1–2**, the target has the [**Blinded**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#blindedcondition) condition; on a **3–4**, the target’s Hit Point maximum decreases by 5 (1d10); on a **5–6**, the target gains 1 [**Exhaustion**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#exhaustioncondition) level. The effect lasts until the Poisoned condition ends. _Success:_ The Poisoned condition ends.

### Ulmist Inquisitors {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:UlmistInquisitors}

Zealous Vanquishers of Evil Intent

**Habitat:** Any; **Treasure:** Any

[![Left to Right: Inquisitor of the Tome, Inquisitor of the Sword, and Inquisitor of the Mind Fire (Artist: Polar Engine)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/22-035.ulmist-inquisitors.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/22-035.ulmist-inquisitors.png)

“Evil lurks everywhere. With our minds, we will unearth it, we will plumb its depths, and we will annihilate it.” With those words, the psychically gifted priest Ulmed founded the Ulmist Inquisition, an order of psionic inquisitors that seeks to uncover and extinguish the wickedness lurking deep in people’s hearts. From the depraved city of Malitain on the Material Plane, the inquisition sends its members throughout the multiverse seeking to thwart the work of malevolent cults, reality-defying horrors, and the evil inherent to mortals. Sects of the inquisition exist within the Domains of Dread, working either in hidden cabals or infiltrating other faiths, such as the Church of Ezra.

The Ulmist Inquisition is organized into three orders named for Ulmed’s companions: the Order of Cosima, the Order of Ansel, and the Order of Tristian. Each order specializes in a different psionic power, and each bears a different symbol on its coat of arms. Some inquisitors entertain friendly rivalries with their fellows from other orders, but most put aside their grudges—at least temporarily—to work together against evil.

#### Inquisitor of the Mind Fire {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:InquisitoroftheMindFire}

The Order of Cosima harnesses the Mind Fire—their name for the fire of thought that blazes within each person’s mind. Inquisitors of this order use their psychic powers to read thoughts, reshape memories, and dominate the recalcitrant. They represent their order with the symbol of a burning eye.

**Immunities** [**Charmed**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#charmedcondition), [**Frightened**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#frightenedcondition)

**_Silvered Longsword._** _Melee Attack Roll:_ +8, reach 5 ft. _Hit:_ 14 (2d8 + 5) Slashing damage plus 4 (1d8) Psychic damage, and the target has the [**Frightened**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#frightenedcondition) condition until the start of the inquisitor’s next turn. _Critical Hit:_ If the target is a [**shape-shifted**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#shapeshifting) creature, it takes an additional 4 (1d8) Slashing damage.

**_Inquisitor’s Command (Recharge 5–6)._** _Wisdom Saving Throw:_ DC 16, each creature of the inquisitor’s choice that it can see within 60 feet. _Failure:_ The target has the [**Charmed**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#charmedcondition) condition until the start of the inquisitor’s next turn. On the Charmed target’s turn, the inquisitor can telepathically control the target’s move and make the target take the [**Attack**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#attackaction) action (the inquisitor chooses the target), the [**Dash**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#dashaction) action, or no action.

**_Mind Fire._** _Intelligence Saving Throw:_ DC 16, one creature the inquisitor can see within 120 feet. _Failure:_ 9 (1d8 + 5) Psychic damage, and the target has the [**Stunned**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#stunnedcondition) condition until the start of the inquisitor’s next turn.

### Vampires {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:Vampires}

Monstrous Life Drinkers

**Habitat:** Underdark, Urban; **Treasure:** Any

Horrific varieties of blood-drinking vampires spread their wickedness across the Domains of Dread.

#### Vampire Nosferatu {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:VampireNosferatu}

Nosferatu are vicious, feral hunters cursed with a primal offshoot of the curse of vampirism. These ravenous, graceless predators stalk the night, desperately seeking blood and barely remembered comforts of life.

Nosferatu feed on anything with blood. Heaps of mutilated rats, stables turned into slaughterhouses, and fields covered in massacred livestock might mark a nosferatu’s presence. Nosferatu lurk in forgotten places scoured of the living, such as charnel caves, cursed ruins, and desecrated barrow mounds.

For a few moments after feeding, nosferatu become lucid enough to recollect glimpses of their past lives. Even in these instances, though, they remain duplicitous schemers.

#### Traits {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:Traits}

**_Blood Frenzy._** The nosferatu has [**Advantage**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#advantage) on attack rolls against any creature that doesn’t have all its Hit Points.

**_Regeneration._** The nosferatu regains 10 Hit Points at the start of each of its turns if it has at least 1 Hit Point. If the nosferatu takes Radiant damage, this trait doesn’t function on the nosferatu’s next turn.

**_Spider Climb._** The nosferatu can climb difficult surfaces, including along ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.

**_Sunlight Hypersensitivity._** The nosferatu takes 20 Radiant damage if it starts its turn in sunlight. While in sunlight, it has [**Disadvantage**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#disadvantage) on attack rolls and ability checks.

**_Claw._** _Melee Attack Roll:_ +8, reach 5 ft. _Hit:_ 9 (1d8 + 5) Slashing damage.

**_Bloodthirsty Slash._** _Trigger:_ A [**Bloodied**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#bloodied) creature the nosferatu can see within 40 feet takes damage. _Response:_ The nosferatu moves up to its Speed without provoking [**Opportunity Attacks**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#opportunityattack) and makes a Claw attack against the triggering creature.

#### Vampire Mind Flayer {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:VampireMindFlayer}

Vampire mind flayers originate from the alien domain of [Bluetspur](#rthw:other-domains-of-dread:Bluetspur "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/other-domains-of-dread#Bluetspur") (see “[Other Domains of Dread](#rthw:other-domains-of-dread "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/other-domains-of-dread")” in chapter 2). In seeking a cure for their degenerating elder brain, the illithids of that realm tried radical experiments. The results were mind flayer tadpoles infected with vampirism. These terrors developed into mature mind flayers capable of harvesting psychic sustenance from sapient minds. After feeding on psionic energies, vampire mind flayers return to Bluetspur and are reabsorbed by the elder brain, releasing stolen psionic essences amid a hormone brine.

Vampire mind flayers are bestial creatures that lack control over their psychic abilities. Rather than focused mind blasts, they unleash waves of nauseating, mentally disruptive sensations. They use their viciously barbed tentacles to drain their victims’ mental energy.

Mind flayers loathe vampire mind flayers and view them as abominations. Nevertheless, they employ their warped brethren in desperate pursuits, such as preserving the elder brain of Bluetspur.

### Waxwork {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:Waxwork}

Murderous Wax Replacement

**Habitat:** Urban; **Treasure:** [Implements](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/dmg-2024/random-magic-items#implementstables)

Realistic humanoid sculptures come to life, waxworks seek to kill and replace those they’ve been crafted to resemble. These creatures typically believe they’re the original living beings rather than duplicates. Any waxwork confronted with evidence of its true nature flies into a rage until it or its double is destroyed.

In rare cases, a waxwork might live as if it were a person. Such individuals are typically callous and vain. Some seek to create more waxworks to replace more people.

### Weathermay-Foxgrove Twins {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:WeathermayFoxgroveTwins}

Adventurous Paranormal Investigators

Twins Gennifer and Laurie Weathermay-Foxgrove are monster hunters who’ve built a reputation as heroes in the domain of [Mordent](#rthw:mordent "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/mordent"), and their reputation is spreading in domains beyond. The daughters of the mayor of Mordentshire, Alice Weathermay, the twins can often be found at their home, Heather House, or at that of their adopted uncle, [**Doctor Rudolph van Richten**](#ref:monster:6491386-rudolph-van-richten "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491386-rudolph-van-richten").

In their youth, Gennifer and Laurie channeled their curiosity and propensity for troublemaking into solving local mysteries. The twins’ uncle—renowned monster hunter George Weathermay—returned to Mordent with his fiancée, Natalia Vhorishkova, just before the twins’ sixteenth birthday. The twins realized Natalia was manipulating their beloved uncle and eventually exposed her as a werewolf who was using George to pursue Rudolph van Richten. After the twins saved their uncle and the doctor from the werewolf, George and Rudolph encouraged the girls’ investigative instincts by training them as monster hunters.

Ever since, Gennifer and Laurie have aided Rudolph in his research and on adventurers across the Land of the Mists. Increasingly, the twins have struck out on their own, allying with heroes such as [**Ez d’Avenir**](#ref:monster:6491354-ez-davenir "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491354-ez-davenir") and Savra Sunstar to solve mysteries and hunt evil across domains.

#### Gennifer Weathermay-Foxgrove {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:GenniferWeathermayFoxgrove}

Gennifer learned a variety of medicinal and spiritual practices, both traditional and esoteric, from [**Rudolph van Richten**](#ref:monster:6491386-rudolph-van-richten "https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/6491386-rudolph-van-richten"). She has conducted in-depth studies of lycanthropy to help her and her sister pursue Natalia Vhorishkova, who remains at large. Secretly, Gennifer fears that she might have been infected with lycanthropy after their encounter with Natalia. She hasn’t shown signs of the curse yet, but she takes medication of her own concoction to ward off unwanted transformation. Gennifer quietly researches lycanthropy, searching for medicinal cures.

#### Laurie Weathermay-Foxgrove {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:LaurieWeathermayFoxgrove}

Laurie learned the ways of martial combat from her uncle George, training in techniques to combat the restless dead. She rarely travels without her canine companions, Joan and Tirran, the grown pups of her uncle’s foxhounds. She also wields her uncle’s magic sword, _Gossamer_, which, according to family legend, contains the soul of a heroic Weathermay ancestor. Laurie suspects that Gennifer is keeping something from her, but she won’t pry into her sister’s secrets.

### Wereraven {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:Wereraven}

Ominous Shape-Shifter

**Habitat:** Forest, Urban; **Treasure:** [Individual](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/dmg-2024/creating-adventures#individualtreasure)

Wereravens are secretive, cautious lycanthropes that seek to blend into society and subtly combat evil. To avoid the claws of the wicked forces that oppose them, and to protect those they hold dear, wereravens hide their identities and rarely reveal their hybrid forms. Nevertheless, folktales persist of eerie, raven-winged figures who appear prior to disasters, share mysterious prophecies, and aid hapless victims. Such stories are true in a way, as evil hunts wereravens wherever they go.

Because evil frequently travels in packs, wereravens flock together to battle such threats. They congregate in hard-to-reach aeries within or just outside urban settlements, such as atop bell towers, lighthouses, or ancient trees. Wereraven groups tend to be loosely organized, since members understand the importance of anonymity.

The [Keepers of the Feather](#rthw:ravenloft-adventures:keepersofthefeather "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/ravenloft-adventures#keepersofthefeather") (described in [chapter 3](#rthw:ravenloft-adventures "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/ravenloft-adventures")) is one example of a secret society of evil-opposing wereravens.

| WIS | 15  | +2  | +2   |
| CHA | 14  | +2  | +2   |

**Skills** [**Insight**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#skills) +4, [**Perception**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#skills) +6

**Gear** [**Shortbow**](#ref:equipment:17-shortbow "https://www.dndbeyond.com/equipment/17-shortbow")

**Senses** Passive Perception 16

**Languages** Common plus one other language

**Challenge** 2 (XP 450; PB +2)

#### Traits {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:Traits}

**_Mimicry._** The wereraven can mimic voices and animal sounds. A creature that hears this mimicry can tell it is an imitation only with a successful DC 12 Wisdom ([**Insight**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#skills)) check.

#### Actions {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:Actions}

**_Multiattack._** The wereraven makes two attacks, using Scratch or Shortbow in any combination. It can replace one attack with a Beak attack.

**_Beak (Raven or Hybrid Form Only)._** _Melee Attack Roll:_ +4, reach 5 ft. _Hit:_ 11 (2d8 + 2) Piercing damage. If the target is a Humanoid, it is subjected to the following effect. _Constitution Saving Throw:_ DC 10. _Failure:_ The target is [**cursed**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#curses). If the cursed target drops to 0 Hit Points, it instead becomes a **Wereraven** under the DM’s control and has 10 Hit Points. _Success:_ The target is immune to this wereraven’s curse for 24 hours.

**_Scratch._** _Melee Attack Roll:_ +4, reach 5 ft. _Hit:_ 7 (2d4 + 2) Slashing damage.

**_Shortbow (Humanoid or Hybrid Form Only)._** _Ranged Attack Roll:_ +4, range 80/320 ft. _Hit:_ 9 (2d6 + 2) Piercing damage.

#### Bonus Actions {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:BonusActions}

**_Shape-Shift._** The wereraven [**shape-shifts**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#shapeshifting) into a Medium raven-humanoid hybrid or a Small raven, or it returns to its true humanoid form. Its game statistics, other than its size, are the same in each form. Any equipment it is wearing or carrying isn’t transformed.

### Yithian {#rthw:denizens-of-the-mists:Yithian}

Fungous Alien Body Swapper

**Habitat:** Desert, Underdark, Urban; **Treasure:** [Arcana](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/dmg-2024/random-magic-items#arcanatables)

Yithians are cosmos-traveling scholars with distinctive, conical bodies and four limbs that end in pincers, sensory structures, and flute-like communication organs. They search for secrets to add to their vast libraries, conducting research by swapping minds with the inhabitants of other worlds—sometimes indefinitely. When a yithian swaps minds with a creature, it traps its victim’s mind in the yithian’s body, which it teleports to its unfathomable, alien home world.

**Senses** [**Truesight**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#truesight) 60 ft.; Passive Perception 14

**_Multiattack._** The yithian makes three Pincer attacks. It can replace one attack with a use of Sup.

**_Pincer._** _Melee Attack Roll:_ +9, reach 10 ft. _Hit:_ 18 (4d6 + 4) Piercing damage and the creature has the [**Grappled**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#grappledcondition) condition (escape DC 14).

**_Sup._** _Intelligence Saving Throw:_ DC 18, one creature within 10 feet that has the [**Grappled**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#grappledcondition), [**Incapacitated**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#incapacitatedcondition), or [**Restrained**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#restrainedcondition) condition. _Failure:_ 15 (3d6 + 5) Psychic damage. The target’s Hit Points maximum decreases by an amount equal to the damage taken, and the yithian regains Hit Points equal to that amount.

**_Mind Swap (Recharge 6)._** _Intelligence Saving Throw:_ DC 18, one Humanoid the yithian can see within 5 feet. _Failure:_ The target is possessed by the yithian; the yithian disappears, and the target has the [**Incapacitated**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#incapacitatedcondition) condition and loses control of its body. The yithian now controls the body; the target has no awareness of the yithian’s actions. The yithian can’t be targeted by any attack, spell, or other effect. The yithian’s game statistics are the same, except it uses the possessed target’s Speed and Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution modifiers. It knows everything the target knew.

The possession lasts until the body drops to 0 Hit Points or the yithian leaves as a Bonus Action. When the possession ends, the yithian returns to its body, which appears within 5 feet of the target. The target is [**Stunned**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#stunnedcondition) for 1 minute by alien memories, and it is immune to this yithian’s Mind Swap for 24 hours.

_Success:_ The target is immune to Mind Swap for 24 hours.

**_Eldritch Magic (2/Day)._** The yithian casts [**Clairvoyance**](#ref:spell:2618972-clairvoyance "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618972-clairvoyance"), [**Modify Memory**](#ref:spell:2619109-modify-memory "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619109-modify-memory"), [**Phantasmal Killer**](#ref:spell:2618857-phantasmal-killer "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618857-phantasmal-killer"), or [**Transport via Plants**](#ref:spell:2619196-transport-via-plants "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619196-transport-via-plants"), requiring no spell components and using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 18).

<CHAPTER id="rthw:tarokka-deck" title="Tarokka Deck">

# Appendix: Tarokka Deck {#rthw:tarokka-deck:AppendixTarokkaDeck}

## Appendix Tarokka Deck {#rthw:tarokka-deck:AppendixTarokkaDeck}

Tarokka fortune-telling cards originated among Vistani, who created these cards to guide their travels. Since Vistani entered the Mists, their cards have spread and gained renown as tools for divining the future and charting paths between the Domains of Dread. Now, diviners across many lands seek glimpses of what’s to come and answers to unknowable questions from the tarokka. Such diviners have a saying: “No secret is safe from the tarokka.”

The tarokka deck is a prop for creating mood-rich fortune-telling scenes in your adventures. It features prominently in the adventure [Curse of Strahd](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/cos), but you can use it to influence adventures of your own design as well.

[![(Artist: Pam Wishbow)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/23-001.raven-tarokka.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/23-001.raven-tarokka.png) [![](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/23-002.mists-tarokka.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/23-002.mists-tarokka.png)

## Composition {#rthw:tarokka-deck:Composition}

A tarokka deck has fifty-four cards, each of which has its own name. Forty of them compose the common deck, which is divided into four suits: coins, glyphs, stars, and swords.

Each suit contains cards numbered one through nine, plus a tenth card called the master of that suit. One can refer to a card by its suit designation or by its name. For instance, the six of stars is also known as the evoker, and the master of coins is the rogue.

The remaining fourteen cards make up the high deck and symbolize powerful and enigmatic forces.

All cards in the tarokka deck and what they represent are detailed at the end of [this appendix](#rthw:tarokka-deck:highdecktable "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/tarokka-deck#highdecktable").

> #### Digital Tarokka Deck {#rthw:tarokka-deck:composition:DigitalTarokkaDeck}
>
> An [interactive digital tarokka deck](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/taro/tarokka) is also available for creating mood-rich fortune-telling scenes. It was included with pre-orders for the _Ravenloft: The Horrors Within_ Ultimate Bundle and the Physical Tarokka Deck. It is currently available for purchase in the [marketplace](https://marketplace.dndbeyond.com/category/6019000?pid=D6019000).

### High Deck {#rthw:tarokka-deck:HighDeck}

The cards that make up the high deck aren’t considered one suit, although they all have a crown icon to mark their importance. Each card represents an important power. If one of these cards appears during a reading and contradicts the prediction of an earlier card, Vistani always assume this card takes precedence.

### Common Deck {#rthw:tarokka-deck:CommonDeck}

The four suits of the common deck are described below.

#### Coins {#rthw:tarokka-deck:Coins}

The suit of coins symbolizes desire for personal and material gain. It also represents gluttony, lust, and obsession. On the side of good, this suit can suggest the accumulation of wealth to benefit a charity or a just cause. On the side of evil, it embodies the worst aspects of greed.

#### Glyphs {#rthw:tarokka-deck:Glyphs}

The suit of glyphs symbolizes faith, spirituality, and inner strength. It is the suit of priests and those who devote themselves to the service of a deity, a higher power, or a heightened philosophy. It symbolizes health and healing, as well as illness and disease. On the side of good, this suit represents willpower and dedication. On the side of evil, it signifies weakness of character, self-doubt, and betrayal of one’s ideals or beliefs.

#### Stars {#rthw:tarokka-deck:Stars}

The suit of stars symbolizes the desire for personal power and control over things beyond mortal ken. It is the suit of mages, sages, and intellectuals. It also represents the triumph of magic, science, and reason over religion, mysticism, and superstition.

#### Swords {#rthw:tarokka-deck:Swords}

The suit of swords symbolizes aggression and violence. It is the suit of warriors, be they paladins, soldiers, or mercenaries. It also symbolizes the power of governments and leaders, whether noble or corrupt.

> #### Prop Tarokka Decks {#rthw:tarokka-deck:composition:commondeck:PropTarokkaDecks}
>
> Tarokka decks for use in your game are available separately, with each card featuring imagery to aid you in creating portentous fortunes. If you don’t have a tarokka deck, you can use a regular deck of playing cards instead. To do so, separate the numbered cards from the face cards and jokers, and treat them as two separate decks: the common deck (the numbered cards) and the high deck (the face cards and jokers).
>
> **_Common Deck._** Each suit in a regular deck of playing cards corresponds to a suit in the tarokka deck.
>
> - Hearts = Glyphs
> - Spades = Swords
> - Diamonds = Coins
> - Clubs = Stars
>
> An ace represents a one in the tarokka deck, while a ten in a regular deck represents a master card in the tarokka deck.
>
> **_High Deck._** Each jack, queen, king, and joker corresponds to a card in the tarokka high deck.
>
> | Playing Card      | Tarokka Card |
> | ----------------- | ------------ |
> | King of hearts    | Ghost        |
> | Queen of hearts   | Innocent     |
> | Jack of hearts    | Marionette   |
> | King of spades    | Darklord     |
> | Queen of spades   | Mists        |
> | Jack of spades    | Executioner  |
> | King of diamonds  | Broken One   |
> | Queen of diamonds | Tempter      |
> | Jack of diamonds  | Beast        |
> | King of clubs     | Donjon       |
> | Queen of clubs    | Raven        |
> | Jack of clubs     | Seer         |
> | Joker 1           | Artifact     |
> | Joker 2           | Horseman     |

## Tarokka Readings {#rthw:tarokka-deck:TarokkaReadings}

Tarokka decks aid fortune tellers in revealing information about specific individuals. The focus of a tarokka reading might be the individual having their fortune told or someone else. A fortune teller randomly selects or invites another to choose what tarokka card best represents the focus of the reading. To begin the tarokka reading, this card is laid face up in position 1 in the pattern below.

[![Image](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/23-003.tarokka-positions.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/23-003.tarokka-positions.png)

The fortune teller then draws four additional cards, laying one face down in each of the other numbered positions in the pattern. These positions each represent something about the focus:

**Position 1.** The focus of the reading and the lens through which the other cards are interpreted

**Position 2.** The past, something that might or might not be apparent to those other than the focus

**Position 3.** What opposes the focus, whether literal opponents or obstructing fortunes

**Position 4.** The future, an omen of what’s to come and a fate that might still be changed

**Position 5.** What aids the focus, whether literal allies or advantageous events

The reading proceeds with the fortune teller revealing the significance of each card’s position and what the card represents, as guided by the descriptions later in [this appendix](#rthw:tarokka-deck:highdecktable "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/tarokka-deck#highdecktable"). After a card is interpreted, the card in the next position is revealed. This continues until all five cards have been interpreted. The fortune teller might reveal more details (see the following section) or claim that the cards remain silent on certain points. The fortune teller and characters then might speculate about the reading’s broader meanings. Once you’re satisfied with what’s revealed, the reading ends.

## Tarokka Techniques {#rthw:tarokka-deck:TarokkaTechniques}

The tarokka deck is a prop for inspiring adventures and creating dramatic fortune-telling scenes. Through a mix of creative interpretation and card manipulation, a DM can influence what the tarokka reveals and the accuracy of its revelations. Consider the following techniques during tarokka readings.

### Stacking the Deck {#rthw:tarokka-deck:StackingtheDeck}

You can use sleight of hand tricks to ensure tarokka cards appear where you desire during a reading. Select the desired cards before the tarokka reading and put them in the order you want to draw them so you can produce them effortlessly and place them in the desired positions. Cards might be stacked on the top of the deck or drawn from the bottom. Stacking the deck is useful for ensuring specific results or creating patterns that appear repeatedly between readings. Avoid letting players notice you’re stacking the deck, as it undermines the mystery of that and future tarokka readings.

### Dramatic Interpretations {#rthw:tarokka-deck:DramaticInterpretations}

[![Orphir Brindletop, a member of the Keepers of the Feather, consults the tarokka (Artist: Irina Nordsol)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/23-004.orphir-brindletop.jpg)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/rthw/ogMxaVTj4GqgnUqr/23-004.orphir-brindletop.jpg)

When interpreting tarokka cards, you can elaborate on the card descriptions in [this appendix](#rthw:tarokka-deck:highdecktable "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/rthw/tarokka-deck#highdecktable"), reframing those details and adjusting them to better suit your adventure. Use these techniques to add onto and adjust the meanings of tarokka cards:

**Broad Interpretation.** Highlight broader card details, like the meanings of suits and the generalities they encompass, over card specifics.

**Card Imagery.** Focus on specifics in a card’s art, like the numbers of objects or the positions of figures, to suggest a deeper meaning.

**Contextual Meanings.** Suggest that multiple cards of the same suit or in specific relation to one another have greater or lesser meaning.

**Diviner Experience.** Reveal that a card arrangement has a specific meaning, or that the fortune teller has seen it in an ominous instance before.

**Foreshadowing.** Highlight details that align with impending events of which only you are aware.

**Leading Questions.** Have a fortune teller ask questions that lead characters to connect the reading with past events or their existing knowledge.

### Manipulating Fate {#rthw:tarokka-deck:ManipulatingFate}

You control fate in your adventures. If you don’t know what a tarokka card means during a reading, note that and fulfill its prophecy in the future. For example, if the four of glyphs appears in a reading, its imagery might appear later as a shepherd NPC, a hooked staff, a wandering sheep, four runes, or the like. You can then tell the players about the connection between the image and the reading.

Additionally, listen in on players’ speculations about the meaning of tarokka readings, then use those suggestions to influence future revelations in your adventures.

**High Deck**

| Name        | Meaning                                                                                                        |
| ----------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Artifact    | The importance of some physical object that must be obtained, protected, or destroyed at all costs             |
| Beast       | Great rage or passion; something bestial or malevolent hiding in plain sight or lurking just below the surface |
| Broken One  | Defeat, failure, and despair; the loss of something or someone important, without which one feels incomplete   |
| Darklord    | A powerful evil individual; one whose goals have enormous and far-reaching consequences                        |
| Donjon      | Isolation and imprisonment; a prisoner of their own beliefs                                                    |
| Ghost       | The looming past; the return of an old enemy or the discovery of a secret buried long ago                      |
| Executioner | The imminent death of one rightly or wrongly convicted of a crime; false accusations and unjust prosecution    |
| Horseman    | Death; disastrous loss of wealth or property, a horrible defeat, or the end of a bloodline                     |
| Innocent    | A being of great importance whose life is in danger (who might be helpless or simply unaware of the peril)     |
| Marionette  | The presence of a spy or a minion of some greater power; an encounter with a puppet or an underling            |
| Mists       | Something unexpected or mysterious that can’t be avoided; a great quest or journey that will try one’s spirit  |
| Raven       | A hidden source of information; a fortunate turn of events; a secret potential for good                        |
| Seer        | Inspiration and keen intellect; a future event, the outcome of which will hinge on a clever mind               |
| Tempter     | One who has been compromised or led astray by temptation or foolishness; one who tempts others for evil ends   |
